ruling: The TR bonus is as written: 1 TR. (The post's guess for the card bonus was struck through and corrected by TDaver to 2 M€.)
quote: TR is as written: 1TR.
author: njshaw2
heading: Venus track

question: What does the bot get for raising Venus to the 8% card-icon bonus?
ruling: The card bonus gives 2 M€ (not a card, not 1 M€), to be consistent with the heat production bonus on the temperature track. TR is 1 TR. Whether this applies when raised via the World Governing Intervention card is left open.
quote: Card is 2mcr, to be consistent with the heat production on temp track.
author: TDaver
heading: Venus track

question: Should the Venus Next track board be placed above or below the main MarsBot track board, given 'topmost track if tied' rules?
ruling: TDaver always plays with the Venus board at the bottom, below the main MarsBot track board.
quote: I've always played w Venus at the bottom
author: TDaver
heading: Venus track

question: What does MarsBot get when it reaches a space with a terraforming bonus on the Venus track (card draw, +1 M€) outside World Government Terraforming?
ruling: Njshaw2 is 99% sure the rulebook covers it; for an immediate ruling, give it the same as for the heat production bonus on the temperature track: 2 M€ instead of the bonus.
quote: give it the same as it would get for the heat production bonus on the temperature track, i.e. 2M€ instead of the bonus.
author: njshaw2
heading: Venus track

topic: Venus track as normal track for least advanced track
question: When MarsBot must advance the least advanced track, is the Venus track treated as a normal MarsBot track, placed at the very bottom?
ruling: Yes: place the Venus track at the very bottom and treat it as a normal MarsBot track when choosing the least advanced track (so it is topmost-if-tied only after the main tracks).
quote: Yup
author: TDaver
heading: Venus track

question: When the automa draws a card with two Venus tags, does its Venus track advance by two spaces?
ruling: Yes, once per Venus tag.
quote: Yes, once per tag.
author: njshaw2
heading: Venus track

question: Does MarsBot advance the Venus track once per Venus tag or once per card with a Venus icon (Chinese edition says per card)?
ruling: The English wording is ambiguously phrased, but the intent is an advance per tag, not per card.
quote: But the intent was an advance per tag, not per card.
author: njshaw2
heading: Venus track

question: What happens when the automa advances its Venus terraforming index onto the card-bonus and TR-bonus reward spaces?
ruling: On the card bonus space it gets 2 MC instead; on the TR bump space it gains 1 TR. This is stated as the intention, and they could not confirm the rulebook says so.
quote: Card bonus: Gets 2MC instead.
author: njshaw2
heading: Venus track

question: How does njshaw2's original Terraforming Mars solo Automa (MarsBot) work and what does it support?
ruling: The bot always plays 4 cards per era (2 per turn); the cards' tags move its markers along tracks and passing action icons triggers effects (TR, parameters, cities, greeneries, milestones, awards). The original version supports the base game and Prelude, Hellas and Elysium only in theory; Venus Next, Colonies and Turmoil were not yet supported. Normal difficulty targets roughly 100 VP.
quote: The basic method the bot plays by is by always playing 4 cards per era (2 per turn), where its actions are governed by the cards' tags, which move its markers along tracks matching the tags
author: njshaw2
heading: Versions of the Automa

question: Does the original free pre-published (print and play) MarsBot version support expansions or bot corporations?
ruling: No. The pre-published version supports no expansions and has no bot corporations, though it is close to the final published version.
quote: It doesn't support any expansions, and doesn't have bot corporations, but it's pretty close to the final published version.
author: njshaw2
heading: Versions of the Automa

question: Does a wild tag count as matching MarsBot's draft priority tags when drafting?
ruling: No. The Adding Corporations rulebook (p. 2) states the Wildcard tag is not considered matching the Draft Priority tag(s), because when played it advances the topmost furthest back track instead of matching.
quote: The Wildcard tag is not considered matching the Draft Priority tag(s) for this purpose.
author: njshaw2
heading: Wild tags

question: Does a wild tag count as a tag when MarsBot counts tags (e.g. Spire, Interface Hyperlink tiebreak, Sagitta)?
ruling: Yes, a wild tag is still a tag for things that count just 'tags'. It does not match a named draft priority tag, which looks for a specific tag.
quote: Yes, they're still tags.  The named draft priority tag match is different because it's looking for a *specific* tag
author: njshaw2
heading: Wild tags

question: Is it a misprint that an action shows an energy production decrease before the arrow while raising TR?
ruling: No. If an action has a cost it is shown before the arrow (e.g. pay 1 energy production to raise your terraform rating); costs are not shown with a minus sign, and the explanation text clarifies it.
quote: If an action has a cost, you see this cost before the arrow, for example pay 1 energy production to raise your terraform rating.
author: EagleEye80
heading: Action costs

question: Can you still add a resource with an action if you cannot or will not pay the cost of taking another player's resource?
ruling: No. The left-hand side of an action is a cost: paying is optional but without paying you do not get the effect. You can also take animals from your own cards, though that makes the card much weaker.
quote: The left hand side of an action is a cost. If the cost is not paid, you do not get the effect.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Action costs

question: Is a red-bordered resource cost of a blue card action optional?
ruling: No. Costs of an action (left of the red arrow) are always mandatory to perform the action, even for red-bordered resources (e.g. Ants removing 1 microbe to add one); the optional exception applies only to the immediate effects of playing a card.
quote: Costs of an action (on the left side of the red arrow) are always mandatory to perform the action, no matter what.
author: EagleEye80
heading: Action costs

question: Must the cost part of a blue card action (before the arrow) always be paid, even with a red-bordered resource?
ruling: Yes. Any cost for using a blue card action (before the red arrow) must be paid to get the reward, regardless of red borders. This applies to Ants and Predators, but it is not a requirement to play the card, only to use its action.
quote: Any cost for using an action on a blue card (before the red arrow) MUST be payed in order to get the reward (after the arrow). Regardless of red borders and such.
author: Fryxen
heading: Action costs

topic: Costs before the arrow have no minus sign
question: Why is a cost before the arrow on an action not written with a '-' sign?
ruling: Iconography convention: an effect is written with a minus, a cost is not (costs before the arrow have no minus).
quote: We had a heated discussion about this but concluded that an effect is written with a minus, but a cost isn't.
author: EagleEye80
heading: Action costs

question: Are resource removals that are costs (such as for Ants and Predators) mandatory?
ruling: Fryxen says that if it's a cost it's always mandatory, citing Ants and Predators. The terse reply does not spell out the surrounding discussion (the preceding post is cut off).
quote: Also, if it's a cost it's always mandatory. Ants and Predators.
author: Fryxen
heading: Action costs

question: Must Aerobraked Ammonia Asteroid place its microbes on an opponent's card if the player has none to receive them?
ruling: No. Only red-bordered icons can target opponents, so the microbes cannot be placed on another player's card.
quote: ONLY red-bordered icons can target opponents. So no, AAA can't place microbes on another player's card.
author: Fryxen
heading: Aerobraked Ammonia Asteroid

question: Can you use Ants if there is no microbe to take?
ruling: No, because removing a microbe is the action's cost. You could, however, remove an ant to gain an ant.
quote: You can not use Ants if there is no microbe to take because that is the cost for the action.
author: Fryxen
heading: Ants

topic: Solo: stealing from the neutral opponent with Ants/Predators
question: In solo play, where you can steal from the neutral opponent, can you use Ants and Predators?
ruling: Yes.
quote: Yes you can. :)
author: Fryxen
heading: Ants

question: Can you use an action like Ants or Predators (remove a resource from any card to add one to this card) when no card holds a suitable resource to remove?
ruling: No. Actions on blue cards must always be performed in full: you pay the cost (if any) and get the reward, without exceptions. So Ants or Predators can only be activated if some card (yours or another player's, because of the red border) holds the resource to remove.
quote: Actions on blue cards must always be performed in full, you perform the cost (if any) and you get the reward. No exeptions ever!
author: EagleEye80
heading: Ants

question: Can the Ants action be used when there is no microbe on any card to remove?
ruling: No. Actions (upper panel of a card) must always be performed in full with no exceptions, so Ants cannot be activated unless there is a microbe resource on one of your or your opponents' cards to remove. Removing red-bordered resources as a lower-panel effect is optional, but an action is not.
quote: Removing red-bordered resources as an EFFECT on a card (lower panel) is optional - but ACTIONS (upper panel) must always be performed in full with no exceptions.
author: EagleEye80
heading: Ants

question: Can Predators and Ants add a resource to themselves without having a resource to remove?
ruling: Official answer: the cost must be paid. The removal part of the action is a cost and cannot be skipped to gain the resource. Whether a card may pay the cost from its own resources is left open in the post.
quote: Official answer: the cost must be paid.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Ants

question: Can the Predators or Ants action be used when there is no animal/microbe on another card to remove, given that red-bordered resources are optional?
ruling: No. The animal (or microbe) removal before the arrow is a cost and must be done in full to get the effect after the arrow, so the action cannot be used if no resource is available to remove.
quote: Örjan is correct - the animal removal before the arrow is a cost, and must therefore be done in full in order to get the effect after the arrow.
author: Fryxen
heading: Ants

question: Is removal of red-bordered resources optional, as the rulebook says?
ruling: Per the user Örjan, endorsed with 'Örjan is correct': optionality of removing red-bordered resources applies when you play a card from your hand (red-bordered production removal is mandatory); the red border means any player including yourself, and the action on Predators and Ants removes a resource from any one card (any player) and adds it to itself.
quote: Örjan is correct
author: Fryxen
heading: Ants

question: When the end-of-generation variant raises ocean placement between generations, do ocean-triggered card effects still apply?
ruling: Yes. Arctic Algae still gives its plants because it does not matter who or what places the ocean. The official knew of no other cards triggering on global parameters in the base game (Aphrodite was mentioned as a future case).
quote: You still get bonuses from Arctic Algea because it doesn't matter who or what places the ocean.
author: EagleEye80
heading: Arctic Algae

question: Which card lets a Capital have more adjacent oceans than the reserved ocean areas allow?
ruling: Artificial Lake lets you place an ocean on an area NOT reserved for oceans.
quote: Artificial Lake lets you place an ocean on an area NOT reserved for oceans.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Artificial Lake

question: Is Mining Consortium's titanium production requirement there because it forces you to reduce someone's production?
ruling: No. The requirement is thematic: if you have no production of a resource it is hard to be part of a consortium on it. Other cards that lower any player's production do not necessarily have such a requirement.
quote: the requirement is a thematic one, that if you don't have any production of a resource, it is thematically hard to be part of a consortium on that resource.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Asteroid Mining Consortium

question: Why do Jovian cards have VPs, and is Asteroid Mining Consortium balanced for 2 players?
ruling: Jovian cards having VPs is intentional so that VP-icon multipliers sort in all Jovian cards, and it is why there are no Jovian events. Asteroid Mining Consortium is balanced for 3-4 players (it would cost 3-4 MC more for 2p); players are free to remove it from the deck.
quote: Jovians having VPs is intentional. Then you can sort out every card with VP symbol, and that'll include all jovians for when you have a multiplier.
author: Fryxen
heading: Asteroid Mining Consortium

question: Is a value of 0 still eligible for second place in an award?
ruling: There are no special rules: if all players tied for second place have 0, they all get 2 VP. If no player has anything counting, all share first place and get 5 VP.
quote: We don't have any special rules in this case. If all players on second place happens to have 0 in that category, then they all get some very cheap 2 VPs!
author: EagleEye80
heading: Awards

question: Is it acceptable to give no award VP to a player with zero in the category?
ruling: It is more thematic that a player with zero gets nothing; there is a strong case for a house rule, though the official rule has no such exception.
quote: It is more thematic, I agree, so you have a strong case for a houserule here.
author: EagleEye80
heading: Awards

question: Why do the Thermalist and Miner awards count leftover resources while Banker counts production?
ruling: Design intent: Thermalist and Miner count held heat, steel and titanium so those resources stay relevant at the end, while the Banker award keeps MC production relevant without over-rewarding TR.
quote: Also, in combination with the miner and thermalist awards, steel, titanium, and heat (and even energy) also stay relevant.
author: Fryxen
heading: Awards

question: How are awards scored when players tie for first or second place?
ruling: A tie for 1st place means no 2nd place: each tied winner gets 5 VP and the others none. If the tie is for 2nd place, the 1st place player gets 5 VP and each of the two 2nd place players gets 2 VP.
quote: Tie for 1st place -> no 2nd place. Ties are friendly, so that would be 5 VP each for the winners, none for the others.
author: Fryxen
heading: Awards

question: Does the Banker award count TR as part of MC production?
ruling: No. Banker only counts the specific MC production on the board, not including the TR.
quote: Banker only counts the specific MC production on the board, not including the TR.
author: Fryxen
heading: Banker (award)

question: What does the Banker award count?
ruling: Banker counts the MC production on your player board; it does not add any TR.
quote: Banker counts MC production on your player board, not adding any TR.
author: EagleEye80
heading: Banker (award)

question: Is the Beginner Corporation intended to be stronger at the start, and how many starting cards do players keep?
ruling: Intent: beginner corporations are better at the start because they have all their corporation value from the beginning; other corporations have ongoing effects, and all are calculated to have the same worth in the end. Also mentioned: the Planner milestone requires 16 cards in hand.
quote: Beginner corporations are better in the start because they have all their corporation worth from the beginning.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Beginner Corporation

question: What does a Beginner Corporation start with in solo?
ruling: With a Beginner Corporation in solo you still start at 0 production, but with 10 free cards and cash you don't have to spend on buying cards. They say you can house-rule it any way you like.
quote: If you use a beginner corporation, you would still start at 0 production, but with 10 free cards and cash that you don't have to spend on buying cards.
author: Fryxen
heading: Beginner Corporation

question: Why do Beginner Corporations draw their cards without choosing, and should new players use drafting?
ruling: Beginner Corporations simply draw their 10 cards to avoid putting new players in the hard position of choosing which to keep. Drafting is not for new players because it adds play time and they cannot choose informedly.
quote: This is why the Beginner Corporations just draw their cards without choosing, to avoid putting new players in that hard position.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Beginner Corporation

question: Are Beginner Corporations balanced against the unique corporations, and may they be mixed with them?
ruling: Beginner Corporations are balanced to have the same strength as the other corporations, so they can be mixed with unique corporations in the same game; they just make the start easier to digest.
quote: They ARE balanced to have the same strength as the other corporations, so you can mix.
author: Fryxen
heading: Beginner Corporation

question: Are beginner corporations balanced against standard corporations?
ruling: Beginner Corporations are designed to be a little bit better than the 12 standard corporations so new players can play on par, and are more luck-prone because the 10 starting cards may or may not synergize.
quote: Even without starting production though, the Beginner Corporations ARE a still little bit better than the 12 standard corporations
author: Fryxen
heading: Beginner Corporation

question: How does the Beginner Corporation differ from other corporations?
ruling: It is just like any other corporation: you start with what it says, you may choose it freely without drawing it, and there are 5 copies. It simply tells you to take the 10 starting cards for free instead of choosing and paying.
quote: Actually, they are just like ANY OTHER corporation. You start with what it says you start with, just like the others.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Beginner Corporation

topic: Mixing Beginner Corporation with other corporations
question: Can some players use the Beginner Corporation while others use advanced corporations?
ruling: Yes, some players could play with the Beginner Corporation at the same time as others play advanced corporations; they should be balanced against each other.
quote: some players could play with the Beginner Corporation at the same time as others play advanced corporations. They should be balanced against each other.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Beginner Corporation

question: Can a player decide to play the Beginner Corporation after seeing their 10 starting cards?
ruling: No. The choice to play a Beginner Corporation must be made beforehand, before seeing the 10 cards.
quote: A player can not choose to play Beginner Corporation after they've seen their 10 cards. That choice must be made beforehand.
author: Fryxen
heading: Beginner Corporation

question: How is the Beginner Corporation balanced relative to named corporations?
ruling: It is balanced to be slightly better than named corporations (playtested with experienced players) but much more luck dependent; the benefit is kept small enough that experienced players prefer named corporations. New players may still win or lose.
quote: The Beginner Corporation is balanced to be slightly better than the named corporations.
author: Fryxen
heading: Beginner Corporation

question: Is the Beginner Corporation allowed in the Solo Terraformer Challenge?
ruling: No. The Beginner Corporation is meant only for inexperienced players; it is more prone to luck and has a greater starting worth.
quote: No, Beginner Corporation is only meant to be played by inexperienced players.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Beginner Corporation

question: Are Beginner Corporations a variant, and does the draft apply to the starting 10 cards?
ruling: Beginner Corporations are not a variant; new players may use them in any variant (standard or CE) instead of choosing a corporation from 2 and a starting hand from 10. The draft may be used with any variant, but you do not draft the starting 10 cards, and draft is not used in solo play.
quote: You do not draft the starting 10 cards, and draft is not used in solo play.
author: Fryxen
heading: Beginner Corporation

question: What are the only differences between Beginner Corporations and the others, and what decides starting production?
ruling: Starting production depends only on whether Corporate Era cards are included. The Beginner Corporation differs only in that it is chosen before the 10 cards are dealt, keeps all 10 cards for free, and has no ongoing effect.
quote: Starting production only depends on the inclusion of the Corporate Era cards.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Beginner Corporation

question: Can you play solo with a Beginner Corporation?
ruling: It is OK but not recommended. Corporate Era should always be played in solo, since starting with 1 production and excluding 1/3 of the cards makes a very easy and boring challenge.
quote: Playing with a Beginner Corporation in solo is ok, but not recommended. In solo you have time to evaluate the cards without creating downtime for your friends.
author: Fryxen
heading: Beginner Corporation

question: With a Beginner Corporation you start with 10 project cards without paying, while with a normal corporation you are dealt 10 and buy the ones you keep at 3 MC each. Is this right?
ruling: Correct. With a Beginner Corporation the 10 starting project cards are kept for free; with a normal corporation you buy the starting cards you keep from your 10 at 3 MC each.
quote: Correct.
author: EagleEye80
heading: Beginner Corporation

question: Is playing with Beginner Corporations related to choosing the Standard game versus the Corporate Era?
ruling: No. Playing with Beginner corporations or normal corporations has nothing to do with the choice between the Standard game and the Corporate Era expansion.
quote: Please also note that playing with Beginner corps or normal corps has nothing to do with the choice of playing Standard game or playing the Corporate Era expansion.
author: EagleEye80
heading: Beginner Corporation

question: Can players in the same game use a mix of Beginner Corporations and normal corporations?
ruling: Yes. A mix of players with Beginner corporations and normal corporations is allowed.
quote: Also note that you may play with a mix of players with Beginner corps and normal corps.
author: EagleEye80
heading: Beginner Corporation

question: What are the solo setup rules regarding Corporate Era, starting production and the Beginner Corporation?
ruling: Solo is only played with Corporate Era cards and without the +1 starting production. You may still choose the Beginner Corporation and get the 10 cards for free, but only together with CE cards and rules (no extra start production).
quote: Solo game is only played with CE cards and without +1 production ... You can still choose to play beginner corp and get the 10 cards for free, but only in combination with CE cards and rules (no extra start prod).
author: EagleEye80
heading: Beginner Corporation

question: Are the Beginner Corporations intended as a handicap, and should experienced players use them?
ruling: The Beginner Corporations are balanced to be a little more powerful than the other corporations and should not be used by experienced players. They are more swingy (free cards may be very useful or mostly weak), which is boring for experienced players but good for beginners.
quote: The Beginner Corporations are balanced to be a little more powerful than the other corps (and thus should not be used by experienced players)
author: Fryxen
heading: Beginner Corporation

topic: Beginner Corporation chosen before seeing cards
question: Why must a Beginner Corporation be chosen before seeing the starting cards?
ruling: Design intent: the Beginner Corporation exists to eliminate the hard choice of which cards to keep for new players; choosing after seeing the cards would defeat the purpose. Experienced players who can fit the 10 cards to a corporation shouldn't use Beginner Corporations.
quote: The purpose of the Beginner Corporation is to eliminate the hard choice of which cards to keep for new players.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Beginner Corporation

question: How do beginner corporations fit into the game variants?
ruling: Beginner Corporations can be used in any variant and are given to new players instead of 2 normal corporations; experienced players can choose normal corporations at the same table. There is no separate 'beginner game' variant.
quote: Beginner Corporations can be used in any variant of the game, and is given to new players instead of 2 normal corps.
author: Fryxen
heading: Beginner Corporation

question: Can new players use beginner corporations while others use normal ones?
ruling: Yes. Normal corporations can be used at the same table as a new player's beginner corporation.
quote: And you can play with normal corps while the new players take a beginner corp in the same game.
author: Fryxen
heading: Beginner Corporation

question: How is the Beginner Corporation intended to be used?
ruling: It is designed for beginners only, for a first game: it is swingy because of free starting cards and it spares the player choosing starting cards. After the first play it should not be used again.
quote: Both of these features are designed to work for beginners only, so after your first play, you should never use it again.
author: Fryxen
heading: Beginner Corporation

question: How are corporations and starting hands chosen, and how does corporation production combine with the starting production?
ruling: First-time players take a Beginner Corporation (second-time players may too); all others are dealt 2 random unique corporations. Each player is dealt 10 project cards; Beginner Corporation players keep all 10 for free, the others choose a corporation and pay 3 MC for each card kept, revealing corporations in turn order. Corporation production is added on top of the starting 1 production in a standard game without CE.
quote: The players with Beginner Corporations keep all 10 card for free. The others will now have to choose which project cards and what corporation they want to keep.
author: Fryxen
heading: Beginner Corporation

question: May experienced players use Beginner Corporations?
ruling: Beginner Corporations are intended to teach new players and are not meant for players already familiar with the game; their wording is deliberately vague about how long to use them. They were designed at a slightly higher power level, but the difference is small. The rules (RAW) do allow flexibility, but in the designer's opinion the game host should not allow experienced players to take one. Vague rules must be agreed by all players on a single interpretation.
quote: But BC is not intended for people already familiar with the game.
author: Fryxen
heading: Beginner Corporation

question: Does the vague wording on who may use Beginner Corporations need an erratum?
ruling: No erratum is needed; the discussion was only about how to handle it and players are free to handle it as best they can.
quote: No, that was just a discussion of how to handle it. People are free to handle it after their best ability. No errata is needed.
author: Fryxen
heading: Beginner Corporation

question: Can the Beginner Corporation be used by non-beginners, and is it allowed in tournaments?
ruling: The rule is that a player unsure about the game can request a Beginner Corporation; otherwise they pick from 2 normal corporations. Beginner Corporations are slightly stronger but much swingier and are for teaching only, never allowed in tournaments.
quote: BCs are slightly stronger than normal corps, but much more swingy, resulting in more luck.
author: Fryxen
heading: Beginner Corporation

question: What are Beginner Corporations intended for?
ruling: They are meant to get the game going fast and easy for new players: when no one knows the game, or when you are new and don't want to bog down others. They are not intended for seasoned gamers or those wanting the full experience first time.
quote: They are not intended for seasoned gamers or people who want the full experience the first time and don't mind a 4-5 hour game.
author: Fryxen
heading: Beginner Corporation

question: Can a card with an action be used in the same round it is played?
ruling: Yes. Action cards may be used in the same round that you play them. Action cards are played upright and tipped sideways when their action is used, then tipped back in the production phase; each card's action can be used once per round.
quote: Actions cards should be allowed to be used on the same round that you play them.
author: Fryxen
heading: Blue card actions

topic: Actions versus effects on blue cards
question: Do all actions on a blue card trigger together, and how often can a blue card be used?
ruling: Blue cards have actions or effects. Effects always work. A card with an action (red arrow) may be used only once per generation, and if a card has more than one action you must choose which one action to perform that generation.
quote: A blue card with ACTION (red arrow) may only be used once per generation. If there are more than one action to choose from on a card, you must therefore choose which one action to perform that generation.
author: Isaac Fryxelius
heading: Blue card actions

question: Are actions on blue (active) cards optional, and how often can they be used?
ruling: Actions on blue cards are always optional and may be used only once per generation.
quote: Actions on blue cards are always optional, but may only be used once per generation.
author: EagleEye80
heading: Blue card actions

topic: Blue card actions once per generation
question: How often can actions be used: blue cards, corporations, converting heat/plants, standard projects?
ruling: Actions on blue cards (and corporations like UNMI) may be used only once per generation (mark with a player marker). All other actions, such as converting heat and plants, playing cards or standard projects, are unlimited.
quote: actions on blue cards (or corporations like UNMI) may only be used once per generation.
author: EagleEye80
heading: Blue card actions

question: Can both actions of a blue card with a choice of actions be used in one generation?
ruling: No. The card provides one action per generation; if it offers a choice (e.g. collect resources or spend them), you must choose one, never both.
quote: The card still only provide you ONE action per generation, so you cannot use both of them.
author: EagleEye80
heading: Blue card actions

question: Do the rules for playing a card (paying costs, performing all effects) also apply to using an action?
ruling: Using any action is similar to playing a card: you pay the cost and get the effect. If you cannot pay the cost you cannot use the action, and if you cannot perform the effects (with the same 3 exceptions as for playing cards) you cannot do the action either.
quote: Using any action is similar to playing a card (this answers most of Ken's questions). You pay the cost and get the effect.
author: Fryxen
heading: Blue card actions

question: How often can actions be used in a generation, in particular blue card actions?
ruling: Blue cards with actions can be used only once per generation; if a card gives 2 optional actions only one can be activated. All other actions (converting plants or heat, playing cards, standard projects, claiming milestones or awards) can be done many times, and blue card effects (not actions) can be activated any time.
quote: The only exception is the blue cards with actions on them - they can only be used once. If the card gives you 2 optional actions, then you can only activate one of them.
author: EagleEye80
heading: Blue card actions

question: How do actions on blue cards work: frequency, multiple actions, costs and effects?
ruling: Blue card actions can be used once per generation (mark with your player marker until production). If a card has more than one action, choose which one to use. Pay any cost before the arrow first, then perform the effect after the arrow with the same restrictions as playing a card: you must perform it in full, except raising an already maxed global parameter, removing opposing resources, or adding resources you can't collect. If you can't perform the effect or pay the cost, you can't take the action.
quote: Blue cards with actions can only be used once per generation (mark them as used with your player marker until the production phase).
author: Fryxen
heading: Blue card actions

topic: Playing and using blue card actions
question: Are playing a blue card and using its action separate actions, and must they happen in the same turn?
ruling: They are 2 separate actions. You do not have to play the card and activate it in the same turn.
quote: But you don't have to play the card and activate it on the same turn, though.
author: EagleEye80
heading: Blue card actions

topic: Which actions are limited to once per generation
question: Which actions are limited to once per generation?
ruling: All actions are shown with red arrows, but only actions on blue cards and corporations (UNMI, Viron, Celestic) can be activated once per generation. Other actions (standard actions on the board, exchanging heat or plants on the player board, claiming milestones/awards, playing cards) are not restricted.
quote: Other actions (Standard actions shown on the game board, exchanging heat or plants on the player board, claiming milestones/awards, or playing cards) are not restricted.
author: EagleEye80
heading: Blue card actions

topic: Blue card actions with no benefit
question: Can a blue card action be used when it gains nothing (e.g. Symbiotic Fungus with no microbe card, Martian Zoo with no animals)?
ruling: Yes. Per the FAQ, actions must be able to be performed in full except for raising an already maxed global parameter, removing opposing resources, or adding resources you cannot collect; the same applies to any action, including standard projects, converting plants or heat, and trading with a colony tile.
quote: Yes you can.
author: Fryxen
heading: Blue card actions

question: How many building tags does the Builder milestone require, given that the early board image posted online differs?
ruling: The Builder milestone requires only 8 building tags; the early pre-finalized board image that showed another number is wrong.
quote: Builder milestone only requires 8 building tags.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Builder (milestone)

question: Which cards place the Capital special tile?
ruling: The Capital tile is only placed by the Capital card, not by Noctis City, Phobos Space Haven or Ganymede Colony, which place normal city tiles. Capital is a special tile that counts as a city tile and scores adjacent oceans in addition to normal adjacent greenery scoring.
quote: This tile is only placed by the Capital card, not by Noctis City, Phobos Space Haven, or Ganymede colony.
author: Fryxen
heading: Capital

question: How should the 'VP / resource' icon on cards be read?
ruling: It means VP per resource, as in 'km/h': Livestock gives 1 VP for each animal on it and Herbivores gives 1 VP per 2 animals on it. Each card also carries a small text explaining the icons.
quote: "1 VP for each animal on this card." for Livestock, and "1 VP per 2 animals on this card." for Herbivores. This usage is consistent with daily use of language such as km/h = kilometers per hour.
author: Fryxen
heading: Card text and icons

question: A translated card's explanation text disagrees with its icons; which is authoritative?
ruling: All current and coming translations derive from the English original. Most people read the iconography correctly even if the explanation text is badly translated, and the errors should be corrected in the next print.
quote: All current and coming translations derives from the English original.
author: EagleEye80
heading: Card text and icons

question: The French Zone de Mohole text says energy production but the icon shows heat; which is right?
ruling: The icon is correct. Only the text is translated, icons are always the original and correct ones; English Mohole Area increases heat production.
quote: Only the text was translated; the icons are always original and correct, regardless of translation.
author: Fryxen
heading: Card text and icons

question: Why do some greenery cards say to raise oxygen in the text; is that an additional oxygen step?
ruling: No. The text is only explaining the icons and adds nothing not shown by icons; a second oxygen raise would have a second oxygen symbol on the card. The reminder exists because the greenery-raises-oxygen link is sometimes overlooked. Exceptions are cards marked with an asterisk.
quote: If the card would give you a second raise in oxygen there would have been an additional oxygen-symbol on the card.
author: EagleEye80
heading: Card text and icons

question: Is the iconography always sufficient, given cards like Mining Area versus Mining Rights?
ruling: Cards with an asterisk are an exception to the rule that icons are sufficient; for those the text must be read.
quote: Yes, cards with an asterisk are an exception.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Card text and icons

question: How do icon shapes map to game concepts?
ruling: As taught by Lord_Aethan: all square icons are resources; square icons on a brown background are production; all round icons are tags (except VP and oxygen); all hexagonal icons are tiles.
quote: 1. All square icons are resources 2. Square icons on brown background are production of resources. 3. All round icons are tags (except VP and Oxygen) 4. All hexagonal icons are tiles.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Card text and icons

question: Do card text mistranslations in other language editions change the card effects?
ruling: No: the icons are correct in all editions, so players should rely on the icons when a translated text is wrong. A later printing was expected to fix translation mistakes.
quote: I'm sorry to hear that. The icons are are correct though, so you should be fine anyway.
author: Fryxen
heading: Card text and icons

question: When the translated card text of a non-English edition contradicts the icon (e.g. text says increase M€ production but the icon shows -1), which is correct?
ruling: The icon is correct. Card and board iconography is identical in all language editions; only the black text differs, and some cards are mistranslated in non-English editions.
quote: Yes, because the card- and board iconography is the same for all language editions. The only difference is the black text.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Card text and icons

question: On a card where icons and text differ without an asterisk, which governs?
ruling: Icons are generally the stricter and clearer reading, while the text is looser and explains the function. If there is an asterisk or any question about the icons, read the text. It is a matter of whether they contradict each other without an asterisk.
quote: Ruleswise, the icons are often most clear, but if there is an asterisk or question about the icons, read the text.
author: Fryxen
heading: Card text and icons

question: Will the card icon/text conflicts be corrected?
ruling: The designers will add a few asterisks and change a couple of explanation texts in the next English printing; some of the reported conflicts are real, and some follow normal rules despite the wording.
quote: we're going to add a few asterisks and change a couple of explanation texts in the next english printing.
author: Fryxen
heading: Card text and icons

question: Which wins when a card's text and icons seem to differ?
ruling: An asterisk makes the card text authoritative; otherwise the text only helps explain the icons and does not replace them. If an interpretation conflicts with the icons or the text it is probably wrong.
quote: when there is an asterisk, text becomes authorative, like in this case. Otherwise, it is meant to help with understanding the icons, not replacing them.
author: Fryxen
heading: Card text and icons

question: How should card text and icons be read together?
ruling: The text is an explanation of the icons and can be imprecise; only an asterisk makes the text authoritative over the icons. If text and icons cannot be made to agree, the interpretation is probably wrong.
quote: Only an asterisk makes the text authoritative over the icons since they explain a deviation from the normal iconography. If you can't make the text and icons agree, they your interpretation is most probably wrong
author: Fryxen
heading: Card text and icons

question: How should card text and icons be interpreted when they seem to disagree on what a card does?
ruling: The icons and the text mean the same thing; the text is only an explanation and a reminder, not the rule. If the text is unclear, check the icons, and if the icons are unclear, check the text. Icon conventions (resources, production box, red border for affecting opponents, placement rules, oxygen for greenery, TR for raising parameters) come from the rulebook. Only an asterisk in the iconography means the effect deviates from the ordinary rules, as explained in the text.
quote: if you don't understand the text, check the icons, and if you don't understand the icons, check the text. [...] Only when there is an asterisk in the iconography does the effect deviate from ordinary rules, as explained in the text.
author: Fryxen
heading: Card text and icons

question: What do wild, rainbow and asterisked resource icons mean?
ruling: The wild resource icon (white with a question mark) means any standard resource. Non-standard resources are always specified with an asterisk. The rainbow resource means different types of resources, for example 1 heat and 1 microbe. Other deviations should have asterisks explaining the effect.
quote: The convention is to use the wild resource icon (white with question mark) as any standard resource. Non-standard resources are always specified with an asterisk.
author: Fryxen
heading: Card text and icons

question: How do card text, icons, asterisks and red borders relate?
ruling: Cards normally target only themselves and you; cards that put resources on other cards carry an asterisk, and interaction with opponents is always shown by a red border. The text is only an explanation and should follow the icons; deviations are noted with an asterisk and upper-case words in the text (e.g. Applied Science's resources on other cards that already have resources).
quote: So, in short, follow the icons. If you are unsure about the icons, read the text. If you are uncertain about the text, look at the icons; they should say the same.
author: Fryxen
heading: Card text and icons

question: When a card's text and icons disagree, which wins?
ruling: The icons should be trusted if in doubt, because text can be incomplete or misinterpreted. Only when there is an asterisk in the icons does the text win over the icons.
quote: so go with the icons if you have any doubt. Only when there is an asterisk in the icons will the text win over the icons.
author: Fryxen
heading: Card text and icons

question: How to interpret a card when icons and text seem to disagree?
ruling: Icons represent the actual effect, except where there is an asterisk or an obviously non-standard icon, in which case check the text. The text is only an explanation and may not cover every nuance; if unsure read the text, and if the text is unclear check the icons; if they disagree your interpretation is probably wrong.
quote: The icons represent the actual effect - except when there is an asterisk or a obviously non-standard icon.
author: Fryxen
heading: Card text and icons

topic: Tag triggers on the card itself
question: Does the same tag-trigger rule apply to Decomposers and Ecological Zone, and does Ecological Zone place 2 animals immediately for its own two matching tags?
ruling: Yes. Ecological Zone immediately places 2 animals on itself for its own two matching tags, and the same each-tag-triggers rule applies to Decomposers and Ecological Zone.
quote: Yes, that is right :)
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Cards triggering their own effects

question: Does Immigrant City's effect trigger on its own city tile?
ruling: Yes. All cards always trigger themselves, with no exceptions (like Insects counting its own microbe tag). Playing Immigrant City therefore first reduces MC production by 2 and then immediately increases it by 1 (as the post puts it), rather than making an exception.
quote: In Terraforming Mars, all cards always trigger themselves too. No exception.
author: EagleEye80
heading: Cards triggering their own effects

question: Can a card's own tags trigger its own effect while it is played?
ruling: Yes. A card's tags often trigger the card's own effect while being played; e.g. Decomposers adds a resource to itself when played because of its microbe tag.
quote: For example, Decomposers adds a resource to itself when being played because of its microbe tag triggering the card effect.
author: Fryxen
heading: Cards triggering their own effects

question: What does 'including this' / 'including these two' mean on tag-triggered effects such as Viral Enhancers and Ecological Zone?
ruling: The phrase reminds you that the card triggers its own effect: Viral Enhancers (science/microbe tags) triggers on its own tag, and Ecological Zone (plant/animal tags) triggers its effect twice for its own two tags. The wording is used consistently across all cards.
quote: the text "including this" reminds you that the card triggers its own effect. Ecological Zone has plant/animal tags so the text "including these two" reminds you that the card triggers its own effect twice.
author: EagleEye80
heading: Cards triggering their own effects

question: Why use Caretaker Contract (spend 8 heat to raise TR) when you can already spend 8 heat to raise temperature?
ruling: The card's action raises only TR, not temperature, so it is useful when temperature is already maxed and heat would otherwise be unusable.
quote: This card is not increasing the temperature, it's only increasing your TR. Therefore, this is a great card if temperature has maxed out already
author: EagleEye80
heading: Caretaker Contract

question: Can CEO's Favorite Project be played when no card in play can hold resources?
ruling: Yes. It falls under the exception for resources you cannot place: with no legal target for the resource you can still play the card.
quote: Actually, it does fall under the 3rd exception - you don't have a legal target to put the resource on. You can play the card.
author: Fryxen
heading: CEO's Favorite Project

topic: CEO's Favorite Project with no resource cards
question: Can CEO's Favorite Project be played if no card of yours has resources?
ruling: Yes. The card has no requirement and adding a resource you can't collect is one of the exceptions, so you just ignore that part. Only costs are mandatory, not rewards of that kind.
quote: So according to exception 3 you can play CEO's Favorite Project, yes.
author: Fryxen
heading: CEO's Favorite Project

question: What counts as a city, and are Ganymede Colony and Phobos Space Haven cities?
ruling: A city is a city tile (grey side of a greenery tile); the Capital special tile also counts as a city. All cities are on Mars except Ganymede Colony and Phobos Space Haven, hence the ON MARS restriction on some cards.
quote: A city in Terraforming Mars refers to city tiles, the grey ones on the back of every greenery tile. The Capital special tile is also considered a city
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Cities

topic: City counting: on Mars versus all
question: Which cards count all city tiles and which only city tiles on Mars?
ruling: The normal city icon counts all city tiles in play, on Mars or not (Energy Saving, Rover Construction, Immigrant City, Pets, Immigration Shuttles). Only cards with an asterisk at the city icon and capital-letter text count city tiles on Mars only (Zeppelins, Martian Rails, Tharsis Republic's MC production effect).
quote: the normal iconography indicates all city tiles in play, whether on Mars or not
author: Fryxen
heading: Cities

question: What is the generation marker on the terraforming rating chart for?
ruling: Its game-mechanic purpose is to know when the game ends in SOLO play (14 generations). In multiplayer it is only thematic.
quote: The main game-mechanic reason is to know when the game ends when playing SOLO(14 generations).For multiplayer it is just a nice thematic thought
author: Isaac Fryxelius
heading: Components

question: What to do when a color runs out of player cubes?
ruling: Use player markers of an unused color to mark production or blue card actions; the color only really matters on the game board. Do not use copper cubes, since they can get mixed with resources on the player board.
quote: I would use player markers of an un-used color to mark your production or actions taken on blue cards. The color is only really important on the game board.
author: Fryxen
heading: Components

question: Should a player's own colour cubes be used as resources on cards, and what are player markers on blue cards for?
ruling: No. Player markers are only placed on a blue action card to show the action was used this generation (removed after the generation). All resources, on player boards or on cards, are marked with the copper/silver/gold cubes.
quote: You are not supposed to use your player markers as resources on cards! You only put a player marker on a card to remember that you have used the action this turn
author: EagleEye80
heading: Components

question: What is the generation marker for?
ruling: It is a thematic add-on, necessary for solo play and good for tracking the direction of the draft.
quote: It is also necessary for the solo-play, and good to keep track on the direction of the draft.
author: EagleEye80
heading: Components

question: Does the generation marker matter for anything in the game?
ruling: It has a thematic function and helps remember the drafting direction and first player; it was included in the general rules instead of only for solo. The length of a generation is not defined.
quote: It has a thematic function, no doubt. [...] helps you to remember drafting direction and first player.
author: EagleEye80
heading: Components

question: Are there rules or card changes in the second printing?
ruling: The 2nd print has some rewording in the rules and on some cards, but nothing that actually changes the game, only clarifications. The insert is changed to a flat box-liner and promos are not included.
quote: 2nd print the insert is changed to a flat one (so called box-liner) and there are some re-wording in the rules and on some cards. Nothing that actually change the game - only clarifications.
author: EagleEye80
heading: Components

question: On the early board image posted online, is the card placement bonus in the southern hemisphere correct?
ruling: On the finalized board, the hex to the left of the southern-hemisphere hex with a card placement bonus also has a card as its placement bonus; the early image omits it.
quote: The hex to the left of the one with card placement bonus in the southern hemisphere should also have a card as placement bonus.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Components

question: What do you do if you run out of player cubes of your color (e.g. in a 2-player game)?
ruling: Each color has 40 cubes; 2-player games can use more than that. If you run out you can supplement with the unused colors. How to handle it is a matter of taste; only on the game board must you use your own color's markers, so other colors can be used on the production track or to mark used cards.
quote: We usually uses another colour for the production track or for marking used cards, because it's only important to use your own player markers on the game board.
author: EagleEye80
heading: Components

question: What happens when you run out of player cubes?
ruling: Running out normally only happens in a 2-player game. Use an unused player color to mark production and used cards, and your own color to mark tiles and TR.
quote: use an unused player color to mark production and used cards, and your own color to mark tiles and TR.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Components

question: Are the player cubes limited, and what happens if a player runs out?
ruling: Running out is usually due to misusing player markers as resources; in a 2-player game it can still happen. Then use cubes of another unused player colour: it only matters to tell tiles on the board apart, not to mark production on your own blue cards. Each colour has 40 markers and the count will not be increased.
quote: If that happens, you have each have 3 other player colors to choose from.
author: EagleEye80
heading: Components

question: How do you identify volcanic areas on the base game board?
ruling: Volcanic areas are marked on the board by bold text names (the base game has no separate concept or symbol for them). The post does not list which areas.
quote: We did make bold text names for them though.
author: Fryxen
heading: Components

question: Why does the game ask players to track generations?
ruling: Tracking generations is there for thematics and immersion (terraforming takes a very long time); it also has other uses.
quote: You track generations because of thematics.
author: Fryxen
heading: Components

question: What are the unlabelled art cards found at the top of decks and promo packs?
ruling: They are cover cards used to avoid mix-ups at the factory and to make each language edition clearly different; they have no playability.
quote: More precisely, they are cover cards to avoid mixups at the factory, to make each language edition clearly different from others.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Components

question: Conscription: does the discount apply to the next card played this generation only?
ruling: You only get the 16 M€ discount if you play another card this generation (the second action of the same turn or another turn in the same generation). The words 'this generation' apply.
quote: It means you only get the rebate if you play another card this generation. (It can be the second action of the same turn or in another turn the same generation).
author: Fryxen
heading: Conscription

question: Is Conscription's 'rebate' a discount or a kickback like Media Group?
ruling: It is a discount (as its own text says), not a kickback like Media Group; cost can never go below 0.
quote: Conscription is definitely a discount, as it details in its own text. Not a kickback like we see with cards such as Media Group.
author: Fryxen
heading: Conscription

question: Once temperature is at 8 or oxygen at 14%, can you still spend 8 heat to raise temperature or raise oxygen for TR?
ruling: No. When those parameters have reached their goal you cannot raise them further and you get no more TR from them (rules pages 3 and 5).
quote: No, the rules says that when those parameters have reached their goal you cannot raise them further, and you do not get more TR from them (rules page 3 and 5)
author: Isaac Fryxelius
heading: Converting plants and heat

question: Can you still convert plants to greenery when oxygen is maxed?
ruling: Yes, you can still convert plants into greenery tiles, though it is worth less because it gives no TR.
quote: It is worth noting that you can still convert plants to greeneries, even if it is then less worth because you don't get the TR.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Converting plants and heat

question: Can you convert heat when temperature is maxed?
ruling: Yes, you can convert heat into nothing if temperature is maxed.
quote: You can convert heat into nothing if temperature is maxed.
author: Fryxen
heading: Converting plants and heat

topic: Converting plants without space for a greenery
question: Can you convert plants into a greenery if the tile cannot be placed?
ruling: No. You cannot convert plants into a greenery tile if the tile cannot be placed (this will not occur if oxygen is not maxed out).
quote: You can not convert plants into a greenery tile if the tile can't be placed.
author: Fryxen
heading: Converting plants and heat

topic: Converting heat when temperature is maxed
question: If temperature is already maxed, can you spend 8 heat for no effect just to stay in the action phase instead of passing?
ruling: Yes. Converting heat can be done since raising a maxed parameter is allowed but ignored, per the card-play exceptions.
quote: Converting heat can be done since it will raise a maxed parameter, which is allowed but ignored as per the tree exceptions to card play.
author: Fryxen
heading: Converting plants and heat

question: Do the starting actions of Tharsis Republic and Inventrix use one of the actions of your first turn?
ruling: Yes. Actions are performed during your turn, not during setup, so the starting action is done as the first of your possible two actions on your first turn.
quote: actions is what you perform during your turn, not part of setup, so it is indeed done as the first of your possible two actions on your first turn.
author: Fryxen
heading: Corporations

question: When do you choose your corporation?
ruling: You choose your corporation at the same time as choosing your starting cards, so you can take the cards into account.
quote: You choose your corporation at the same time as choosing your starting cards, allowing you to take the cards into account when choosing corporation.
author: Fryxen
heading: Corporations

topic: Inventrix and Tharsis Republic first action
question: How does the pre-defined first action of Inventrix and Tharsis Republic interact with the two actions of the first turn?
ruling: The first of your two allowed actions on your first turn in the first action phase is used for this purpose. You may use the second action for that turn normally.
quote: the first of your two allowed actions on your first turn in the first action phase is used for this purpose.
author: Fryxen
heading: Corporations

question: Can a corporation with a mandatory first action delay it to generation 2 by passing on its very first turn?
ruling: Yes, a player could pass on the first turn and take the corporation's first action later, though Fryxen considers it most probably a very bad move.
quote: 2) Yes they could, but as you said it would most probably be a very bad move.
author: Fryxen
heading: Corporations

question: Can resources be added to or removed from a corporation as if it were a card?
ruling: Yes, corporations are cards: floaters can be added to Celestic and microbes to Recyclon. The only difference is that corporations are Corporation cards, not project cards, but no published effect depends on that yet.
quote: Yes, they are cards. Floaters can be added to Celestic and microbes can be added to Recyclon.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Corporations

topic: Corporations are played in player order
question: Do corporations count as played at game start in player order, so that Splice only triggers on microbe corporations revealed after it?
ruling: Yes. Players reveal their corporation in player order at the beginning and this counts as playing it, so Splice (and Saturn Systems with a future Jovian corporation) only triggers on corporations revealed after it. Player order also matters on the first turn (Immigrant City before Tharsis Republic's city) and for claiming Planner in generation 2.
quote: Yes, that's correct. The same will be true for Saturn Systems when we release another jovian corporation.
author: Fryxen
heading: Corporations

question: Why are corporations revealed in player order, and do players wait on each other when choosing?
ruling: Players choose corporation and project cards simultaneously but reveal consecutively in player order, for thematic reasons, because corporations play like ordinary projects where order sometimes matters, and to have rigid rules for tournaments.
quote: Players choose corp and project cards simultaneously, but reveal consecutively.
author: Fryxen
heading: Corporations

question: Are corporations revealed one after another, so that order can matter for effects like Saturn Systems' Jovian tag trigger?
ruling: Yes. Corporations are revealed (played) consecutively, so a player earlier in turn order may benefit from later corporations' tags and a later player may not; this is intended. Preludes are then played in turn order after all corporations are in play, so they have no turn-order bias.
quote: Yes, the corporations are revealed (played) consecutively, possibly resulting in a situation where player order matters and can give a player a small advantage/disadvantage.
author: Fryxen
heading: Corporations

question: Why are corporations not triggered simultaneously, and may players house-rule simultaneous setup?
ruling: The published game plays corporations consecutively, in the same way as project cards, for consistency and simplicity. Simultaneous setup is left to players as a house rule.
quote: we chose the consecutive variant where corporations work in the same way as the project cards.
author: Fryxen
heading: Corporations

question: How are corporations dealt with the 'Expansion Corps' rule?
ruling: Each player is dealt one corporation from each boxed expansion (Venus Next, Prelude, and later expansions) plus one more random corporation from the original and promo corporations.
quote: Expansion Corps. When dealing corporations, each player is dealt one from each boxed expansion (Venus Next, Prelude, and upcoming expansions), as well as one more random corp (from original + promo corps).
author: Fryxen
heading: Corporations

question: How many corporations are dealt to each player when several expansions are in play?
ruling: The official way is to choose from 2 random corporations, regardless of how many expansions are in the game.
quote: The official way is to choose from 2 random corps.
author: Fryxen
heading: Corporations

question: How does the Focus variant change corporation dealing?
ruling: The Focus variant lets you build a second pool of corporations from the expansions you want everyone to get a taste of; one of the corporations dealt is always drawn from this pool. The pool can contain corporations from several expansions.
quote: The 'Focus' variant allows you to create a second pool of corps from expansions you want everyone to get a taste of - 1 of the corps is always drawn from this pool.
author: Fryxen
heading: Corporations

question: Is there a way to stop the strongest corporations from always being chosen?
ruling: Fryxen suggests a variant: when a corporation wins, remove it from the corporation deck so it cannot be chosen again, optionally starting by removing corps that won recently, and reset the deck when too few corps remain.
quote: When a corp wins, remove it from the corp deck so it can't be chosen again.
author: Fryxen
heading: Corporations

question: Does CrediCor's refund depend on the printed cost, and does it apply to standard projects?
ruling: CrediCor refunds for any action costing 20 MC or more, including the City and Greenery standard projects. The basic (printed) cost counts, so discounts or paying with titanium do not remove the refund.
quote: It's the basic cost that counts: If you play a space card costing 21 MC, and you have -2 space discount, and then pay for the whole project with titanium - you still get your refund from CrediCor.
author: EagleEye80
heading: CrediCor

question: When does Credicor give its bonus M€ for playing a card (e.g. the Deimos Down space event)?
ruling: Confirmed: Credicor gives +4 M€ when its owner plays a card with a base cost of 20 or more (the poster's explanation, which the official confirmed with 'Yes, of course').
quote: Yes, of course. I forgot about that! Nice work!!
author: EagleEye80
heading: CrediCor

question: Does Diaspora Movement count its own Jovian tag despite the text not saying 'including this'?
ruling: Yes, in the normal way of these things; the text should have said 'including this' but it does not change how it works.
quote: Should have 'including this', but since that is the normal way of these things, it doesn't change how it works.
author: Fryxen
heading: Diaspora Movement

question: Can stacked discounts reduce a card's cost to zero?
ruling: Yes, the cost can be zero (Indentured Workers costs 0 from the start).
quote: The cost can be zero. In fact, there is one card in the game which costs 0 from the start: Indentured Workers.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Discounts and cumulative effects

question: Do effects stack?
ruling: Effects are cumulative: multiple discounts stack, a card can trigger several effects and trigger things with several of its tags, and raising a parameter 2 steps increases TR 2 steps.
quote: Effects are cumulative. So multiple discounts will be very useful together, and a card can trigger several effects and may trigger stuff with several of its tags.
author: Fryxen
heading: Discounts and cumulative effects

question: Are effects and discounts cumulative?
ruling: Effects are in general cumulative: a card can trigger several effects and each single effect of a card may trigger. Discounts are cumulative but a cost may not go below zero.
quote: Discounts are cumulative, but a cost may not go below zero.
author: Fryxen
heading: Discounts and cumulative effects

question: Can a card cost be negative after discounts?
ruling: No. A cost may never be negative; a 1 M€ card discounted by 2 costs 0 M€.
quote: A cost may never be negative.
author: Fryxen
heading: Discounts and cumulative effects

question: In which direction do players draft in the draft variant, and how does the generation marker help?
ruling: The generation marker is also used in the draft variant: on even generations you draft clockwise and on odd generations counter-clockwise.
quote: It is also used when playing the draft variant; even generation you draft clockwise, and on odd generations you draft counter-clockwise.
author: Fryxen
heading: Drafting

question: Did the designers try drafting the initial 10 cards?
ruling: Yes, during playtesting, and it was dropped: you need to choose freely among your cards and the two corporations to build a base; drafting at the game start increases luck instead of minimizing it.
quote: During playtesting, we have tried to draft the initial 10 cards also, but this is not good.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Drafting

question: Should the starting hand be drafted or mulliganed when a player has few playable cards?
ruling: The designers advise against drafting the starting hand or using a mulligan: picking from 10 cards and 2 corporations is a strategic moment that drafting or a re-draw would negate, and a poor hand is less bad than it looks (use standard projects, save M€, keep cards for later). The official draft variant does not apply to setup.
quote: I advice against drafting the starting hand or using mulligan.
author: Fryxen
heading: Drafting

question: Do you draft the 10 starting cards?
ruling: No. You do not draft the starting 10 cards; you are dealt them and choose which to buy.
quote: You do not draft the starting 10 cards.
author: Fryxen
heading: Drafting

question: Is drafting part of the default game?
ruling: Drafting is an optional rule: it increases game time and punishes players who do not know the game, so it is not the primary method, and Beginner Corporations are recommended for first-time players.
quote: so for the sake of beginners having a good experience, we put it as an optional rule.
author: Fryxen
heading: Drafting

question: Should the 10 starting cards be drafted?
ruling: No. The 10 starting cards are never drafted, because drafting before choosing a corporation makes the start random; only the 4 cards of the Research phase are drafted.
quote: For this (and other) reasons you never draft the 10 starting cards.
author: EagleEye80
heading: Drafting

question: Is drafting a standard rule, and what setup is recommended for first games?
ruling: Drafting is an optional variant, not part of the standard game. FryxGames recommend first games without the Corporate Era expansion and without draft, using the beginner corporation first.
quote: We still recommend starting your first games without Corporate Era Expansion and without draft. I would only play beginner corporation the first time
author: EagleEye80
heading: Drafting

question: In which direction should the card draft pass?
ruling: Draft direction should alternate between generations.
quote: you should alternate direction of the draft
author: EagleEye80
heading: Drafting

question: Should the draft always go the same direction?
ruling: Lord_Aethan discourages same-direction drafting: it allows same-strategy blocking by hate-drafting. Alternating drafting directions each generation prevents this.
quote: I would discourage same-direction drafting. [...] This is prevented by alternating drafting directions.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Drafting

question: Can the initial 10 cards be drafted?
ruling: They are not meant to be drafted. If a group insists on drafting them, Lord_Aethan suggests first keeping 5 of the 10 cards and then drafting the remaining 5 as usual.
quote: If you are determined to draft the 10 first cards, I would suggest you first keep 5 cards of your 10, then draft the remaining 5 as usual.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Drafting

question: How would the designers run a draft of the starting 10 cards?
ruling: Lord_Aethan's suggested variant: all players get 10 cards, each keeps 5, then the remaining 5 cards are drafted. This lets each player build a base from the starting draw while seeing more cards. Drafting starting hands was tried in development and removed.
quote: If I were to draft the starting 10 cards, I would do like this; 1. All players get 10 cards. 2. All players keep 5 of those. 3. Start a draft of the remaining 5 cards.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Drafting

question: Do the designers recommend drafting variants on the 10 starting cards?
ruling: No. They tried drafting variants of the starting 10 cards and found the outcome more random, not less, since players must pick cards before knowing which corporation they will play. Drafting in the research phase is not discouraged.
quote: Me and my brothers [b]do not recommend drafting variants on the 10 starting cards[/b] however.
author: EagleEye80
heading: Drafting

question: Is drafting an official part of the game or a variant?
ruling: Drafting is a variant (optional rule), because it has disadvantages even for experienced players, mainly a less smooth flow. The designer usually prefers to play without it but is willing to play with it.
quote: So I definitely think drafting is good, but it's still a variant because it also has disadvantages, even for experienced players.
author: Fryxen
heading: Drafting

topic: Draft variant: pick 5 then draft 5 of the starting hand
question: Is there an official-endorsed way to combine drafting with the starting 10 cards?
ruling: The official draft does not draft the starting 10. Fryxen describes an interesting compromise: pick 5 of your 10 cards, then draft the remaining 5, which lets you set up a combo and expand it. He does not see much overall benefit.
quote: There is an interesting compromise though, where you pick 5 cards out of your 10, and then draft the remaining 5.
author: Fryxen
heading: Drafting

question: Is the draft an official rule?
ruling: Drafting is an official variant, not part of the standard rules.
quote: That's why it is official and that's why it is a variant.
author: Fryxen
heading: Drafting

question: Is drafting the initial 10 cards part of the rules?
ruling: No. Drafting the initial 10 cards is not part of the game; the designers have concerns (not knowing which corporation to build toward, not knowing opponents' corporations, hate-drafting) but are open to trying it.
quote: I'm open to try a variant on this sometime.
author: EagleEye80
heading: Drafting

topic: Draft variant for the starting hand
question: Is there a recommended way to draft the starting hand?
ruling: Lord_Aethan would suggest, if drafting starting hands: first choose 5 of the 10 cards and one corporation, reveal corporations, then draft the other 5 cards. He notes that drafting all 10 is bad because you don't know your corporation and cannot hate-draft.
quote: First choose 5 of the cards AND one corporation. Reveal corporations. Then draft the other 5 cards.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Drafting

question: What initial draft would the designers suggest if players want one?
ruling: If an initial draft is wanted, a 2x5 draft, a 3-3-2-2 draft or similar might be best (rather than drafting 1x10); this is an opinion offered as an option, with the standard game having no initial draft.
quote: if you do want an initial draft, I think a 2x5 draft, a 3-3-2-2 draft or something similar might be best
author: Fryxen
heading: Drafting

question: Why is drafting optional rather than standard?
ruling: Drafting is an optional rule because the two alternatives have different benefits: drafting is more strategic, non-drafting is quicker and less fiddly. Non-drafting is the standard so new players are not overwhelmed.
quote: We wanted TM to be beginner-friendly and therefore chose non-drafting to be the standard so that new players would not be overwhelmed.
author: Fryxen
heading: Drafting

question: Why is there no official variant for drafting the starting 10 cards?
ruling: There is no official variant for drafting the starting cards, because at that point you have nothing yet to base the choice on; people's opinions differ and either way is fine.
quote: The reason we didn't consider a variant for drafting the starting 10 is because you don't yet have anything to base it on.
author: Fryxen
heading: Drafting

question: What happens when the project card deck runs out?
ruling: Reshuffle (the discards) when you need to draw a card and the deck is empty.
quote: Simply reshuffle when you need to draw a card if the deck is empty.
author: Fryxen
heading: Draw deck and drawing cards

question: When a card or tile placement lets you draw cards, do you pay 3 MC to keep each card?
ruling: No. Cards drawn by effects are simply added to your hand without paying anything.
quote: Simply draw them, paying nothing.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Draw deck and drawing cards

question: What happens if the draw deck does not have enough cards for the research phase?
ruling: There was no rule; Jacob's ruling: deal equally as much as you can (e.g. with 17 cards, each of 5 players is dealt 3).
quote: So I'll just make one up right now: Deal equally as much as you can, so if you had 17 cards, each of the 5 players would be dealt 3.
author: Fryxen
heading: Draw deck and drawing cards

question: When the draw deck runs out, are discards reshuffled, and how are the last cards dealt?
ruling: Yes, the discard pile is reshuffled (should be in the rules). When dealing the last cards, deal in turn order, 1 to each player until the deck runs out, then reshuffle the discard pile and continue dealing.
quote: I would deal 1 to each player intil the deck runs out, then reshuffle the discard pile and continue dealing.
author: Fryxen
heading: Draw deck and drawing cards

question: What happens when the draw deck runs out in a 5-player game?
ruling: With 5 players you sometimes have to reshuffle the draw deck once it is depleted, so discarded cards might reappear later.
quote: With 5 players, it sometimes happen that you'll have to reshuffle the draw deck once it gets depleted.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Draw deck and drawing cards

question: What happens when the draw pile is empty?
ruling: If the deck runs out, reshuffle the discard pile to form a new deck and continue play. This will be clarified in future prints.
quote: If the deck runs out, you reshuffle thediscard pile to form a new deck and continue play.
author: Fryxen
heading: Draw deck and drawing cards

question: What happens when the deck runs out?
ruling: The discard pile is reshuffled into a new deck if the deck has no cards when you need to draw.
quote: The discard is reshuffled into a new deck if the deck has no cards when you need to draw.
author: Fryxen
heading: Draw deck and drawing cards

question: What happens when the draw deck becomes empty?
ruling: The deck is reshuffled from the discard pile if it becomes empty.
quote: The deck is reshuffled from the discard pile if it becomes empty.
author: Fryxen
heading: Draw deck and drawing cards

topic: Reshuffle when the deck runs out
question: What happens when the deck runs out of cards?
ruling: Reshuffle the discard pile if the deck runs out.
quote: Reshuffle discard pile if the deck runs out.
author: Fryxen
heading: Draw deck and drawing cards

question: Is Ecoline's 7 plants for a greenery once per generation?
ruling: No. It replaces the usual action of converting plants into a greenery (standard 8 plants), so it can be used whenever the normal conversion could; the explaining text says 'always'.
quote: It isn't, this supplants the usual action of converting plants into greeneries. Thus, it says "always" in the explaining text.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Ecoline

question: Is Ecoline's plant discount an action limited to once per generation?
ruling: No. Ecoline's effect is not an action and may be used any number of times in a generation; it alters the plant conversion action on the player board, making it cheaper.
quote: Ecoline’s effect is not an action, and so may be used any number of times during the generation.
author: Fryxen
heading: Ecoline

question: Is Ecoline's ability an action limited to once per generation?
ruling: No. Ecoline's ability was always meant to supplant the normal plant conversion and can be used any number of times. It is shown as an effect because blue actions may only be performed once per generation, while the plant conversion is not limited.
quote: Ecoline's action was always supposed to supplant the normal plant conversion, and could always be used any number of times.
author: EagleEye80
heading: Ecoline

topic: Ecoline effect is not an action
question: Is Ecoline's plant conversion discount limited to once per generation?
ruling: No. Ecoline is not an action and is not restricted to once per turn; it is an effect that changes the plant conversion action on the player board, which is not limited.
quote: Ecoline is a special case because it's not an action in itself and it's not supposed to be restriced to only once per turn
author: EagleEye80
heading: Ecoline

question: How does Ecoline's ability to convert plants work, given the icons?
ruling: Ecoline's ability box is marked 'effect': it is not a card action but an alteration of the normal plant conversion standard action (the text is needed since icons do not portray this).
quote: this is not a card action, but an alteration of the normal plant conversion action.
author: Fryxen
heading: Ecoline

question: Does Ecological Zone require the greenery tile you have, and must the new tile be placed adjacent to your own greenery?
