ruling: You need a greenery tile of your own on the board to play it, but the new tile may be placed adjacent to any greenery tile, not only yours. Had it required any player's greenery, the tile icon would have a red border.
quote: Correct. If it required any greenery tile to be in play (for example an opponent's), there would have been a red border on the tile icon.
author: Fryxen
heading: Ecological Zone

question: When does a multiplayer game end versus a solo game?
ruling: In solo you have 14 generations to complete the terraforming; in multiplayer the game ends with the generation in which the terraforming is complete, so length can differ from game to game. Nothing prevents playing solo longer than 14 generations casually.
quote: In solo play you do it by yourself and have 14 generations to do it, but in multiplayer the game ends with the generation when the terraforming is complete.
author: Fryxen
heading: End of game

question: At the end of the game, how many times may plants be converted to greenery tiles (e.g. with 24 plants)?
ruling: Plants can be converted multiple times at the end of the game with no restriction. These tile placements also give placement bonuses, which can yield enough plants for yet another greenery.
quote: Plant can be converted multiple times at the end of the game; no restriction. These tile placements give placement bonuses too, and can result in the player getting enough plant for yet another greenery tile.
author: Fryxen
heading: End of game

topic: End of game: final greenery placement
question: Why can plants be converted to greenery after the last generation, and what does it affect?
ruling: The extra greenery placements make plant production relevant in the last generation and can affect the Landlord and Miner awards and the tie-breaker. Production of other resources can matter in the last generation for Miner, Banker and Thermalist and the tie-breaker. Greenery tiles must be placed next to your existing tile, so a player with no good spot may hold back.
quote: The main reason for the extra greenery placements is to make plant-producing cards relevant during the last generation. Also, this placement may affect the outcome for the awards Landlord and Miner, as well asthe tie-breaker
author: Fryxen
heading: End of game

question: At game end, may a player convert all their plants to greenery at once, or one greenery per round of players?
ruling: The player may do as much converting as possible on their turn: e.g. with 14 plants convert 8 into a greenery, and if the placement bonus gives plants to reach 8 again, convert another, then the next player may convert. Oxygen is already maxed so no TR is gained.
quote: The player may do as much converting as possible.
author: Fryxen
heading: End of game

question: Can the game stall endlessly if no player wants to raise the last global parameter, and should there be a forced end?
ruling: It is up to the players whether anyone wants to end the game; there is no forced end. Incentives to end include being in the lead, gaining least from continued play, grabbing TR, tile space running out, or running out of useful cards. No limit is set for when the deck runs out.
quote: Yes, it is up to the players if anyone wants to end the game (and if no one does - what's the problem?).
author: Fryxen
heading: End of game

question: Does the first player token move after the final production when greeneries are placed?
ruling: No. Do not shift the first player; there is no new generation.
quote: Do not shift 1st player. There is no new generation.
author: Fryxen
heading: End of game

question: After the final production, do players convert plants into greeneries one at a time or all at once in player order?
ruling: Each player may do as many plant conversions as they can before the next player goes. Collect placement bonuses for those greeneries; they may give enough resources to place yet another greenery, or win the Miner award or tie-breaker.
quote: Each player may do as many conversions as they can before the next player goes.
author: Fryxen
heading: End of game

question: How are greenery tiles placed from plants after the last production phase?
ruling: After the last production phase, players in the preserved player order may convert plants (8 each) into one or more greenery tiles, placed one at a time, triggering placement bonuses and other effects before the next tile. When that player can't place more, the next player goes; after everyone has had a chance, end game scoring begins.
quote: The greenery tiles are paid for (with 8 plants each) and placed one at a time, triggering placement bonuses and other effects before the next tile is placed.
author: Fryxen
heading: End of game

question: When placing greenery tiles at the end of the game, are blue card effects (e.g. bonus for placing greenery) still triggered?
ruling: Yes, effects from blue cards are triggered by the end-of-game greenery placements.
quote: Yes, that's exactly what I meant. :)
author: Fryxen
heading: End of game

topic: End of game: final production and greenery placement
question: Why do final production and final greenery placement happen at the end?
ruling: Design intent: together with placement bonuses and awards such as Landlord and Miner, they make many cards interesting to play even in the last generation and can decide the game. A streamlined version without them would make the end game less interesting.
quote: This, together with associated placement bonuses and the awards, makes a lot of cards interesting to play even on the last generation.
author: Fryxen
heading: End of game

topic: End of game greenery placement order
question: Does the first player place all their end-game greeneries at once or alternate with others?
ruling: Player 1 places as many greeneries as possible (can be more than 2), then the next player goes. Placement bonuses and other triggers still apply, which could give enough plants for another greenery or an award advantage.
quote: Player 1 places as many greeneries as possible (can even be more than 2), and then the next player goes.
author: Fryxen
heading: End of game

question: May a player who cannot win complete the last global parameter and end the game, even if it hands the win to another player?
ruling: Yes, they can do whatever they want; the designer notes it is a matter of politeness and kingmaking, and personally he would aim for the best placement for himself.
quote: They can of course do whatever they want.
author: Fryxen
heading: End of game

question: Does Energy Savings count city tiles not owned by you (including neutral and special cities)?
ruling: Yes for opponents' cities: the icon has a red border, which means opposing players' city tiles count too. The post does not separately address neutral or special-location city tiles.
quote: Look at the icons. Normal icons only affect yourself, but this icon has a red border, meaning you can count opposing city tiles as well.
author: Fryxen
heading: Energy Saving

question: Does "add 1 animal to any animal card" (with the asterisk and capitalized text) let or force you to put the animal on an opponent's card?
ruling: No. Capitalized words on a card only highlight the effect that the icons do not convey; they do not widen its scope. "ANY CARD" means a card other than the one being played, but still only among your own cards; targeting opponents' cards needs the red-border icon, which this effect does not have.
quote: "ANY CARD" is a special rule, because cards can normally only add resources to themselves. But this still only affects your own cards.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Eos Chasma National Park

question: Do victory points printed on played event cards still count, and when are they counted?
ruling: Yes. Event cards that carry VP still score them, but they are counted only at the end of the game.
quote: Correct! :)
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Event cards

question: Why are event cards red and why do tags on green cards count?
ruling: Red cards are events: thematically they happen once and have no further value, hence they are turned face down. Green cards are ongoing industries you own, which is why their tags keep counting; blue cards are like green but demand attention. Red is for theme, not because they attack other players; the aggressive effects of some events are tied to their concept.
quote: red cards are red for their theme, not for their in-game purposes.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Event cards

question: Why do played event cards go in a personal face-down pile instead of the common discard pile?
ruling: Played events are kept in the player's own face-down pile. Cards are unique and must not recycle into the deck after a reshuffle, and some score VP (Media Archives counts them).
quote: Each card in Terraforming Mars is unique (actually representing patents, which would explain why you buy them to your hand before being able to play them).
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Event cards

question: How does Factorum's "spend 3 MC to draw a building card" work?
ruling: It works like all other 'searchers': reveal and discard cards from the deck until you discard a card with the building tag, and take that card into your hand.
quote: It works like all previous 'searchers': reveal and discard card from the deck until you discard a card with that tag, and take that card into hand.
author: Fryxen
heading: Factorum

question: When Factorum finds a building card, must the card taken into hand be revealed?
ruling: Yes, the building card taken must be revealed, so everyone can see what is discarded, that you are not skipping a building card you don't want, and which building card you actually take.
quote: Revealed. The point is that everyone should be able to see
author: Fryxen
heading: Factorum

question: Can Factorum's actions be used for no effect?
ruling: No. Factorum cannot be used for no effect; the energy production action can only be chosen if you can perform it in full, which requires that you have no energy resources.
quote: Factorum cannot be used for no effect. The energy production action can only be chosen if you can perform that whole action (requires that you have no energy resources).
author: Fryxen
heading: Factorum

question: Why are VPs on Jovian cards counted separately in scoring?
ruling: Only for simplicity: it matters only with Jovian multiplier cards (3 in the game), which give 1 VP per played Jovian tag, so it is easier to count Jovian tags first.
quote: This actually only matters if you have a Jovian multiplier (of which there are 3 in the game).
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Final scoring

topic: Victory points on cards in hand
question: Do VPs on cards still in hand count at the end of the game?
ruling: No; only played cards score (implied: the designers consider it obvious that VPs on cards in hand are not counted).
quote: do we have to write in the rules that you don't count VPs on cards still in your hand???
author: EagleEye80
heading: Final scoring

question: Why is MC only used as a tiebreaker rather than scoring?
ruling: Design intent: money is only a tie-breaker so players do not hoard it and are better off using it for cards, awards and standard projects.
quote: Another incentive to speed the end of the game is making sure people don't hoard Money. That's why it's only used as a tie-breaker.
author: Fryxen
heading: Final scoring

question: In what order are milestones, awards and cards (including face-down events) counted in end-game scoring?
ruling: During end-game scoring, milestones and awards are counted before counting your cards, including your face-down event cards.
quote: Please note that during end game scoring, counting milestones and awards are done before counting your cards (including your face-down events).
author: EagleEye80
heading: Final scoring

question: What happens if two players tie on VP and M€ at the end of the game?
ruling: Take the last production after the final round, then place greeneries (optimal VP and, if possible, a few M€). If VP and M€ are still tied, the win is tied.
quote: If both VP and M€ are still tied, I would say the win is tied.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Final scoring

question: What should players do if they end on the same score and the same M€?
ruling: Accept a tie in the very unusual case of the same score and the same money.
quote: I think you should accept a tie in the VERY unusual case of ending on the same score and money.
author: EagleEye80
heading: Final scoring

question: Is the existing tiebreaker (M€) enough, and will further tiebreaker levels be added?
ruling: The existing tiebreaker should be enough. When results are so close that even that cannot tell the players apart, declaring a winner would be kind of weird.
quote: Yes, the existing tiebreaker should be enough.
author: Fryxen
heading: Final scoring

topic: Reducing production you cannot reduce (solo neutral opponent)
question: In solo, can you play a card such as Food Factory when you cannot reduce the production it requires, by letting the imaginary opponent take the reduction?
ruling: No. Production (or resources) without a red border must always be reduced by the player himself, so such a card cannot be played if the reduction cannot be performed. The neutral opponent only makes it possible to play cards with red-bordered effects without performing those effects.
quote: production without red borders must always be reduced by the player himself. Your imaginary opponent is only there to make it possible to play cards with red-bordered effects without performing those effects if you don't want to.
author: EagleEye80
heading: Food Factory

question: What are the bonuses for hitting certain temperatures and oxygen levels?
ruling: The heat-icon temperature bonus steps give 1 step of heat production. Reaching 0C lets you place an ocean tile (with its placement bonuses) and gain 1 TR step. Reaching 8% oxygen lets you raise temperature 1 step as a bonus (another TR step), which may itself hit a temperature bonus step.
quote: You get 1 step of heat production, as stated in the 'science' box on page 4 and indicated by the heat icon being in a brown box.
author: Fryxen
heading: Global parameters and terraform rating

topic: TR for multi-step global parameter raises
question: If an action raises a global parameter twice, do you gain TR twice?
ruling: Yes. Each step of a global parameter gives 1 TR. Giant Ice Asteroid (2 temperature steps and 2 oceans) gives 4 TR, unless a parameter is already maxed, in which case that step gives no TR.
quote: Each step of a global parameters results in 1 TR.
author: EagleEye80
heading: Global parameters and terraform rating

topic: TR for greenery and maxed oxygen
question: Is the TR gained when a greenery raises oxygen independent of the oxygen increase (does it still give TR when oxygen is maxed)?
ruling: The TR is not independent: the rules only remind you to increase TR because you increase oxygen. Only one card, Nitrogen-Rich Asteroid, gives TR and raises a parameter separately, and it is clearly marked as such.
quote: The rules only remind you to increase the TR because you increase O2. So it is not independent.
author: Fryxen
heading: Global parameters and terraform rating

topic: TR when a parameter is maxed
question: If oxygen or temperature is maxed, can a player still gain TR from other sources?
ruling: Yes: a maxed parameter gives no TR when raised, but you can still get TR from other parameters and from separate TR gains that some cards give (e.g. Magnetic Field Dome, Release of Inert Gases).
quote: But you can still get TR from other parameters, as well as separate TR, which some cards may give you (for example Magnetic Field Dome, Release of Inert Gases).
author: Fryxen
heading: Global parameters and terraform rating

question: Do global parameter steps and tile placements within one effect resolve one at a time, so that passed bonus steps and adjacency bonuses between them apply?
ruling: Yes. Execute all steps individually: one increase, then the next. For example when placing two ocean tiles, if the second is adjacent to the first you get the 2 MC adjacency bonus for it.
quote: Exactly. This is important for example for the placement bonuses when placing two ocean tiles. If you ölace the second one adjacent to the first, you should get 2 MC for that.
author: Fryxen
heading: Global parameters and terraform rating

question: Does TR increase for every raise of a global parameter, including multiple steps in one turn and the bonus steps on temperature and oxygen?
ruling: Yes. You always get 1 TR for each step a global parameter is raised, including several steps in the same turn and bonus steps. The thread's example of a card that places a greenery and also says 'increase your TR by one' was not answered explicitly beyond saying to read the icons.
quote: And yes, you always get 1 TR for each raise of the global parameters, including multiple steps the same turn and bonus steps.
author: Fryxen
heading: Global parameters and terraform rating

question: Can TR be reduced below 0?
ruling: No. You can't lose what you don't have, so you can't lower TR below 0.
quote: You can't lose what you don't have, so you can't lower TR below 0.
author: Fryxen
heading: Global parameters and terraform rating

question: Does Protected Valley's text "raise oxygen" mean oxygen goes up in addition to placing the greenery?
ruling: The icons say to place the greenery, and the text reminds you that this also means raising oxygen. So the card increases oxygen by 1 and your TR by 1.
quote: The icons tell you to place the greenery, and the text reminds you that that it also means to raise oxygen (some people tend to forget). So this card increases oxygen and your TR by 1.
author: Isaac Fryxelius
heading: Greenery placement

question: Why does the card text on greenery cards say to raise oxygen when the greenery already raises it, and why is TR not mentioned?
ruling: On all cards where a greenery icon is presented, the card text consistently says to raise oxygen. This is not the same as saying you should raise TR when raising a global parameter, which happens anyway.
quote: on all cards where a greenery icon is presented, it says in the card text to raise oxygen. Consistently.
author: Isaac Fryxelius
heading: Greenery placement

topic: Place greenery and raise oxygen text
question: If a card says place a greenery tile and raise oxygen, is oxygen raised twice?
ruling: No, only 1 step. The text describes that you get a greenery tile and what naturally follows from placing it. Look at the icons first; use the explanation text if they are unclear.
quote: Only increase 1 step. The text describes that you get a greenery tile and what naturally follows on placing that greenery tile.
author: Fryxen
heading: Greenery placement

question: When a card places a greenery as an effect, do you raise oxygen again?
ruling: You always raise oxygen (and TR) when placing a greenery, and there is never a double raise. The reminder text on the three cards that place greeneries only describes the icons; there is no separate oxygen icon.
quote: You always raise oxygen (and terraform rating) when placing a greenery, and there are never a double raise.
author: EagleEye80
heading: Greenery placement

topic: Plantation, Mangrove and Protected Valley placement
question: Where can the greeneries from Plantation, Mangrove and Protected Valley be placed?
ruling: Plantation is a normal (but cheaper) greenery that follows the normal greenery placement rules. Mangrove and Protected Valley may be placed on any available ocean-reserved area.
quote: Plantation is a normal (but cheaper) greenery that follows the normal placement rules for greeneries. Mangrove and Protected Valley on the other hand may be placed on any available ocean-reserved area.
author: EagleEye80
heading: Greenery placement

question: If you can't afford or are prohibited from placing a greenery on a free area next to your tile, may you place anywhere?
ruling: No. You may place anywhere only if there is no area available next to any of your tiles. Areas are unavailable only if reserved, already holding a tile, or non-existent.
quote: The only condition to place anywhere is that there is no area available next to any of your tiles.
author: Fryxen
heading: Greenery placement

topic: Greenery adjacent to a special tile
question: If your only tile is a special tile like Nuclear Zone, must the greenery be placed next to it?
ruling: Yes. The greenery must be placed next to an existing tile you own, so it must be next to the Nuclear Zone tile (unless that is surrounded).
quote: In this case, the greenery tile must be placed next to the Nuclear zone tile.
author: Fryxen
heading: Greenery placement

question: Does a card saying "place a greenery tile and raise oxygen 1 step" raise oxygen twice (once for the greenery and once for the text)?
ruling: No. The text only reminds you that placing a greenery raises oxygen by one; oxygen rises once. Oxygen rises without a greenery only if the card has an oxygen symbol (e.g. Steelworks).
quote: No, the explaining text reminds you to increase the oxygen for the placed greenery. Remember that the text always only explains the icons.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Greenery placement

question: Does a special tile such as Restricted Area count as a tile you own for the rule that greeneries must be placed next to your own tile if possible?
ruling: Yes, you own that tile, so the greenery adjacency requirement applies to it. It also means special tiles, like cities, can be used to open new locations for your greeneries.
quote: But this also means that you can use special tiles as well as cities to be able to put your greeneries in new locations...
author: EagleEye80
heading: Greenery placement

topic: Greenery placement next to any own tile
question: Must greeneries be placed next to your 'first' tile, and must cities be placed next to your own tiles?
ruling: Endorsed explanation: the greenery must be adjacent to any tile you own, not only your first tile; if you have none or no legal adjacent space, place it freely (respecting other restrictions). There is no rule requiring cities to be placed next to your own tiles.
quote: The rules are explained perfect by Bryan.
author: EagleEye80
heading: Greenery placement

question: If the only available greenery spaces next to your tiles are ones you cannot afford (e.g. a space with a 6 MC placement cost), may you place the greenery elsewhere?
ruling: No. 'Available' means the placement rules permit placing there; it does not refer to your current ability to afford it. A space you cannot afford is still available, so you cannot place elsewhere.
quote: Available means that the placement rules permit you to place there. It does not in any way refer to your current ability to place there, limited by other rules.
author: Fryxen
heading: Greenery placement

question: When a card says to place a greenery tile and raise oxygen, is oxygen raised twice (once for the tile, once for the text)?
ruling: No. Follow the icons; if there is no separate oxygen icon there is no separate oxygen increase, and the text only reminds you of the normal oxygen increase when placing a greenery tile.
quote: If there isn't any separate oxygen icon, then there is no separate oxygen increase - the text is only reminding you of the normal oxygen increase when placing greenery tiles.
author: Fryxen
heading: Greenery placement

question: Does Greenhouses count the cities of all players, or must you choose one player?
ruling: The red border means 'any, not just your own'. The effect is stated in text as 'for each city tile in play', so it counts all city tiles in play.
quote: Yes, red border means "any, not just your own". The effect of the card is also stated in text on the card, saying for each city tile in play.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Greenhouses

topic: Playing a prelude or corporation is not an action
question: Is playing a Prelude an action, so that Head Start's two actions could be used to play the second prelude?
ruling: No. Playing corporations and preludes works like playing project cards, but when you are allowed an action, they are never among the options.
quote: Playing corporations and preludes work like playing project cards, but when you are allowed an action, they are never part of the options.
author: Fryxen
heading: Head Start

question: Does Helion's heat count for the tie-breaker (as megacredits)?
ruling: No. Helion does not help the tie-breaker: their heat can be used as megacredits but is still heat.
quote: Helion does not help the tie-breaker. Their heat can be USED as megacredits, but the ARE still heat.
author: Fryxen
heading: Helion

question: Can Helion's heat count as MC for the Banker award or tie-breaking?
ruling: No. Helion's heat can be used as money but never becomes actual money, and heat resources are never moved to the MC box.
quote: Helion's heat can be used as money, but they never become actual money and you never move heat resources to the MC box.
author: EagleEye80
heading: Helion

question: Can Helion use heat as MC when MC is removed by a prelude, stolen by another player's card, or lost to a global event?
ruling: Helion can use heat for effects it is playing itself (e.g. Business Empire), but not when another player's card removes or steals MC (Hired Raiders) or when a Global Event (Riots) removes MC, because Helion is not doing anything then.
quote: Helion isn't doing anything when Hired Raider is being played against them. The player removes their resources and can't use Helion's ability
author: Fryxen
heading: Helion

question: Does Helion's unspent heat count as MC for the MC tiebreaker?
ruling: No. The tiebreaker counts actual MC; MC is not spent for the tiebreaker, so Helion cannot use its heat-as-MC ability.
quote: You don't spend MC for the tiebreaker, so Helion can't use its ability.
author: Fryxen
heading: Helion

question: Hired Raiders says steal but its icons show only red-bordered resources: do you gain the stolen resources?
ruling: The word STEAL is part of the iconography and is to be considered in combination with the icons, so the card steals (the player gains the resources) even though the icons are not fully consistent. Stealing, unlike removing opposing resources, requires actually stealing something.
quote: The word 'STEAL' is part of the iconography, so to speak. Since it is not part of an explaining paranthesis, it should be considered in combination with the icons.
author: Fryxen
heading: Hired Raiders

question: Hired Raiders says 'up to'; can you remove less than the maximum and gain only what you removed?
ruling: Yes: Hired Raiders lets you choose the amount, but you must gain exactly as many resources as you remove from the opponent.
quote: Well, in that case the card allows you to choose the amount, but you still have to remove the same amount that you gain.
author: Fryxen
heading: Hired Raiders

question: Can the Industrial Center special tile be placed adjacent to any city tile, including one belonging to the neutral player in solo?
ruling: Yes. Industrial Center may be placed adjacent to any city tile, including the neutral player's city.
quote: Yes sir! :)
author: Fryxen
heading: Industrial Center

question: Which tags can Interplanetary Trade count with a wild tag?
ruling: Interplanetary Trade can count all the normal tags, plus the event tag if the wild tag is set to event, plus Venus if playing with Venus Next.
quote: Interplanetary trade can benefit from all the normal tags + event if that is your wild tag + Venus if you play with that.
author: Fryxen
heading: Interplanetary Trade

question: Is the maximum MC production from Interplanetary Trade 12 rather than 11 with all official expansions (wild tag as event tag)?
ruling: Yes, confirmed: with the wild tag set to the event tag the maximum is 12 rather than 11.
quote: Yes.
author: Fryxen
heading: Interplanetary Trade

question: Does the action 'Look at the top card and either buy it or discard it' mean you play the card outright, or buy it into your hand?
ruling: You buy the looked-at card into your hand, paying 3 M€; you do not play it outright. (The alternative is to discard it.)
quote: Yes, you buy it to your hand, paying 3 M€.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Inventors' Guild

topic: Taking a card vs paying for it
question: What does 'take a card' mean, and do Inventors' Guild and Business Network require you to play the card immediately?
ruling: Effects that tell you to 'take' a card put it into hand without paying. Inventors' Guild and Business Network let you look at a card and either discard it or pay 3 M€ to put it in hand; nothing says you must play it immediately.
quote: All effects that just tell you to "take" a card means you take the cards into hand without paying for them.
author: EagleEye80
heading: Inventors' Guild

question: Can Inventors' Guild's action be used when you cannot afford to buy the card?
ruling: Yes. Looking at the top card and discarding it costs nothing, so the action can be taken even with less than 3 MC.
quote: Yes you can. Looking and discarding doesn't cost anything.
author: Fryxen
heading: Inventors' Guild

question: Will Inventrix's global requirement flexibility change?
ruling: Inventrix will be changed to +-2 on global requirements to make it more powerful.
quote: We will indeed change Inventrix to +-2 to make it more powerful.
author: Fryxen
heading: Inventrix

question: Can the requirement adjustments of Inventrix, Adaptation Technology and Special Design stack?
ruling: Yes, effects stack. The same goes for discounts.
quote: Effects stack, yes. :) The same goes for discounts, for example.
author: Fryxen
heading: Inventrix

question: Do Inventrix and Adaptation Technology requirement modifiers stack, and do discounts stack?
ruling: Yes, effects stack. Inventrix and Adaptation Technology together give +/-4 on global requirements, and discounts also stack (e.g. Anti-Gravity Technology, Earth Catapult and Research Outpost together make all cards 5 MC cheaper, with Space discounts on top).
quote: And yes, effects stack. This also applies to discounts, so 2 cards giving you a Space discount stacks to a greater discount.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Inventrix

question: Do effects that adjust global requirements (+/-2) and discounts stack?
ruling: Yes, all such effects stack, as do discounts (two space discounts of 2 make space cards 4 MC cheaper). Inventrix, Adaptation Technology and Special Design combined can change a global requirement by 6 steps.
quote: Yes, all those effects stack on top of each other. The same thing applies to discounts.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Inventrix

question: Does a +/-2 requirement modifier on temperature mean 2 steps or 2 degrees?
ruling: Modifiers are in steps. The temperature scale increases 2 degrees C per step, so one such effect shifts a temperature requirement by 4 degrees C; stacking all three shifts it by 12 degrees C.
quote: The temperature scale increases 2 degrees celcius (or Kelvin) for each step, so having one of these cards would allow you to change a temperature requirement by 4 degrees celsius.
author: Fryxen
heading: Inventrix

question: Do the effects of cards that change your global requirements (Adaptation Technology) stack?
ruling: There are 3 cards with this effect (Adaptation Technology, Special Design and Inventrix) and they stack.
quote: There are 3 cards with this effect, and they stack.
author: Fryxen
heading: Inventrix

question: Can Inventrix, Adaptation Technology and Special Design be combined to play Kelp Farming in the first generation?
ruling: Fryxen calls it a possible 'magic trick' to play Kelp Farming on the first turn using Inventrix, Adaptation Technology and Special Design together, implying their requirement modifiers stack.
quote: I've always wanted to do a first turn Kelp Farming using Inventrix, Adaptation Technology and Special Design.
author: Fryxen
heading: Inventrix

question: Do the +2/-2 global requirement cards (Inventrix, Special Design, Adaptation Technology) apply once or every time you play a card, and is the direction chosen once?
ruling: The effect applies every time you play a project card (it is not a one-time choice). Example: with a max 7% oxygen card you can play it at 9% oxygen, and with Inventrix or Adaptation Technology you can then immediately play a card requiring 11% oxygen because the effect applies to every card.
quote: This effect is the same as on Special Design and Adaptation Technology and applies every time you play a project card.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Inventrix

topic: Kelp Farming requirement with Inventrix / Special Design / Adaptation Technology
question: With the requirement-modifying cards, can Kelp Farming (requirement 6 ocean tiles) be played before oceans are placed?
ruling: With Inventrix, Special Design and Adaptation Technology all in effect (the three requirement-modifying effects together), Kelp Farming (requirement 6 ocean tiles) can be played before any oceans are placed. The effects are described in the thread as stacking (see the later official post in thread 1817225).
quote: With all three of these cards, Kelp Farming (req. 6 ocean tiles) can be played before any oceans are placed.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Inventrix

question: Is there an endorsed house rule to make Inventrix stronger?
ruling: The designers suggest, as an optional house rule, changing Inventrix's global requirement flexibility from +/-2 steps to +/-3 steps. It is not a printed rule.
quote: Suggestion for houserule: Change Inventix ability to +/-3 steps to make it more interesting.
author: EagleEye80
heading: Inventrix

question: Does Inventrix's requirement flexibility apply to tag-count requirements such as Anti-Gravity Technology's science tags?
ruling: No. Inventrix only affects global requirements (oxygen, temperature, oceans). Its own science tag counts toward tag requirements, so with Inventrix you need 6 more science tags for Anti-Gravity Technology.
quote: No, those are not global requirements. On the other hand, Inventrix does have a science tag, so you'll only need 6 more to be able to play Anti-Gravity.
author: Fryxen
heading: Inventrix

question: Do Inventrix's requirement flexibility, the blue card with the same effect and the red card for the next card played stack?
ruling: As quoted and endorsed by the official: they stack, so with Inventrix, the blue card and the red card the next card can be up to 6 steps from a requirement or maximum, e.g. Kelp Farming (requires 6 oceans) can be played in the first generation.
quote: ...and that's when you play Kelp Farming (requires 6 ocean!!) in the first generation. Powerful stuff! :p
author: EagleEye80
heading: Inventrix

question: What does "+2 or -2, your choice (in each case)" mean on requirement-modifying cards?
ruling: The wording is an explanation text only: you simply choose whichever direction suits you (+2 or -2), regardless of how you view negative temperature numbers. The reply does not restate whether the choice is per card played or once; the reply treats the plain reading as fine.
quote: With our wording you simply choose what fits you regardless of how you see the negative numbers.
author: Fryxen
heading: Inventrix

topic: Lake Marineris with oceans all placed
question: Can Lake Marineris be played for just its 2 VP when all oceans are placed?
ruling: Yes, because oceans are a global parameter exception.
quote: Yes, that's correct.
author: Fryxen
heading: Lake Marineris

question: Should Lake Marineris place a special extra ocean tile beyond the 9 oceans?
ruling: No. The designers will not give Lake Marineris a special tile. The card remains playable for its 2 VP even when all oceans are maxed out; an extra ocean tile would raise open questions (TR when the parameter is maxed, where to place it when ocean-reserved areas are used up).
quote: The card is still playable for 2 VPs, even when oceans are maxed out.
author: EagleEye80
heading: Lake Marineris

question: What happens when Lake Marineris is played with Arctic Algae in play and only 1 ocean tile remaining?
ruling: The first ocean is placed and its TR, adjacency, placement bonuses and Arctic Algae's 2 plants join the pool and may be resolved in any order. The second ocean can't be placed (a fulfilled parameter may still be pushed with no effect), so none of the triggers from a tile placement happen for it.
quote: The second ocean can't be placed, but falls under the exception that fulfilled parameters may still be 'pushed' but nothing happens.
author: Fryxen
heading: Lake Marineris

question: Does Lakefront Resorts give 5 MC per adjacent ocean or how does its text apply?
ruling: Read the text, not the icons: it alters the adjacency bonus for oceans rather than adding to it, and it should maybe have an asterisk.
quote: it should 'maybe' have an asterisk since it alters the adjacency bonus for oceans, rather than adds to it.
author: Fryxen
heading: Lakefront Resorts

question: Which areas count as reserved for Land Claim's 'non-reserved area' wording?
ruling: Reserved areas are the ocean areas and the city areas Noctis City, Ganymede Colony and Phobos Space Haven; an area claimed with Land Claim is considered reserved for that player. Whether the owner may then place a greenery without adjacency was not answered.
quote: the reserved areas are for ocean tiles and cities (Noctis City, Ganymede Colony, and Phobos Space Haven). And the Land-Claimed area would also be considered reserved for a certain player.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Land Claim

question: What does the Landlord award count?
ruling: It counts every tile owned by the players regardless of type. Ocean tiles are not owned by anyone and so do not count.
quote: The Landlords award count every tile owned by the players, regardless of type. Ocean tiles are not owned by anyone though.
author: Fryxen
heading: Landlord (award)

question: Do special tiles count as owned for the Landlord award?
ruling: Yes, you own your special tiles, as indicated on page 5 of the rules and by the square marker space on the tile, so they count for Landlord.
quote: Yes, you own your special tiles, as indicated on page 5 in the rules, and by the square marker space on the tile. So they do count for Landlord.
author: Fryxen
heading: Landlord (award)

question: What if all three Lava Flows locations are occupied?
ruling: You can't play it. Each increased temperature step is 1 TR, so the card gives 2 TR.
quote: If all those places are occupied, you can't play it. And each increased step is 1 TR. This card gives 2 TR.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Lava Flows

topic: Requirements: being able to perform a card's effects
question: Why can't Lava Flows be played when its tile can't be placed?
ruling: Being able to perform a card's effects is mandatory, except effects that raise a parameter already at its goal, add resources you can't collect, or remove resources from an opponent that you can't or don't want to (page 9 of the rules).
quote: Being able to perform a card's effects is mandatory except effects that * raise a parameter that has already reached its goal, * adds resources you can't collect, or * removes resources from an opponent
author: Fryxen
heading: Lava Flows

question: If one of the three Lava Flows locations is free, can you play it for only 1 temperature step, or is it all or nothing?
ruling: All or nothing.
quote: All or nothing.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Lava Flows

question: Can Lava Flows be played if a legal tile area exists but fewer than 2 temperature steps remain?
ruling: If there is a legal area for the tile you can place it and get the full effect; if only 1 temperature step is left you do that step and get 1 TR. If you can't place the tile you can't play the card at all.
quote: If there is an available legal area for the tile, you can place it there and get the full effect. ... But if you can't place the tile, you can't play the card at all.
author: Fryxen
heading: Lava Flows

topic: Requirements: tile placement must be possible
question: Does the rulebook sentence 'A tile must be placed if possible, but being unable to do so does not prevent you from playing the card' still apply?
ruling: No. Errata: remove that sentence from the rules. Tiles must be placed (so a card can't be played if its tile can't be placed), unless it is an ocean and all ocean tiles have already been placed.
quote: ERRATA: remove this sentence from the rules - tiles must be placed (unless it's an ocean and all ocean tiles have already been placed, per the exception rules on the previous page).
author: Fryxen
heading: Lava Flows

topic: Requirements: tile placement must be possible
question: Can you play a card if you can't place its tile?
ruling: No. You can't play the card if you can't place the tile.
quote: You can't play the card if you can't place the tile. Correct.
author: Fryxen
heading: Lava Flows

topic: Requirements: being able to perform a card's effects
question: What must be possible in order to play a card, and what are the exceptions?
ruling: To play a card you must be able to perform its functions, with 3 exceptions: (1) you may play a card that raises temperature, oxygen or oceans even if that parameter is already maxed out, ignoring the increase; (2) you may play a card that gives resources even if you cannot collect them (animals and microbes needing another card); (3) removing red-bordered (opposing) resources is optional.
quote: In order to play a card, you must be able to perform its functions. This has 3 friendly exceptions: 1) you may play a card that increases temperature, oxygen or ocean even if that parameter is already maxed out; just ignore increasing it.
author: Fryxen
heading: Mandatory effects and exceptions

question: Which effects of a card may be left unperformed when playing it?
ruling: Only three exceptions: you may play a card that (1) raises global parameters that have already reached their goal (no TR), (2) adds resources you can't collect (e.g. microbes with no microbe card to hold them), or (3) removes resources from any player (red-bordered resource icons) if you can't or don't wish to. All other effects must be performed or the card cannot be played.
quote: there are only 3 exceptions to this: You may play a card that 1. raises global parameters that have already reached their goal (you do not get TR for that) 2. adds resources that you can’t collect
author: Isaac Fryxelius
heading: Mandatory effects and exceptions

question: Do you need to be able to pay for a card's negative effects (e.g. have the energy production for a city)?
ruling: Yes, all effects of a card need to be performed; the designers regard it as both mechanically and thematically important that you cannot play a card without the required resources or production, e.g. a city without energy production or livestock without plant production.
quote: It would be very strange if it would suddenly become an advantage NOT to have the required resources or production!
author: EagleEye80
heading: Mandatory effects and exceptions

question: If a card says 'add up to X animals/resources', may you play it when you cannot add any?
ruling: Yes, you may still play the card and add 0 (for example if you have no animal card to add them to).
quote: If you do not have an animal card, you are still allowed to play this card, (putting 0 animals).
author: Isaac Fryxelius
heading: Mandatory effects and exceptions

question: What are the three exceptions to needing to perform all effects when playing a card (and using an action)?
ruling: The exceptions are: raising global parameters (oxygen, ocean, temperature) that are maxed; adding resources you cannot collect; removing resources you cannot or do not wish to. Fryxen confirmed this list.
quote: Yes, that's correct.
author: Fryxen
heading: Mandatory effects and exceptions

topic: Playing a card: requirements and the three exceptions
question: What must be true to play a card, and when can the direct effects be partially performed?
ruling: To play a card you must 1) fulfill any requirement, 2) be able to perform all its direct effects, and 3) pay for it. Three exceptions: it may raise an already maxed global parameter; remove resources from any player who doesn't have enough or you don't want to target; or add resources to a card when you have no card that can collect them. In those cases do as much as you can and disregard the rest.
quote: A card may be played even if it * raises a global parameter that is already maxed out, * removes resources from any player and they don’t have enough or you don’t want to target them, or it * adds resources
author: Fryxen
heading: Mandatory effects and exceptions

topic: Playing a card: mandatory effects and the three exceptions
question: Are the effects of a card with red-bordered icons optional, and which effects must be performed to play a card?
ruling: In general all effects must be performed to play a card. Three exceptions: you can ignore effects that raise a parameter already maxed, that give you resources you can't collect, or that remove opposing resources when opponents don't have enough to remove.
quote: The general rule is that all the effects have to be performed in order to play the card.
author: Fryxen
heading: Mandatory effects and exceptions

topic: Mandatory effects and the three exceptions
question: Which effects of a played card are mandatory?
ruling: Most rewards are mandatory, with 3 exceptions: you can play a card that 1) increases a maxed parameter (ignore that part, no TR), 2) removes opposing resources (not production, which stays mandatory), removing as much as you can and want, or 3) adds a resource you can't collect (ignore that part).
quote: Most rewards are also mandatory, with 3 exceptions.
author: Fryxen
heading: Mandatory effects and exceptions

topic: Must be able to perform all effects
question: Can you play a card if you cannot perform all of its effects?
ruling: No. If the player cannot somehow perform all effects, the card (or other action) cannot be played.
quote: If the player can't somehow perform all effects, the card (or other action) can't be played.
author: Fryxen
heading: Mandatory effects and exceptions

question: Which action effects may be skipped or fizzle if they cannot be performed?
ruling: In Terraforming Mars all effects of an action must be performed when you take it, with 3 exceptions (referring to the FAQ: raising an already maxed global parameter, removing opposing resources, adding resources you cannot collect). Anything else must be test-run and be legal before performing the action.
quote: In TM, only 3 things are allowed to fizzle
author: Fryxen
heading: Mandatory effects and exceptions

question: On a card with an OR, can you freely choose either option?
ruling: An OR means you can choose between the different options as long as your choice is playable.
quote: An OR means you can choose between different options as long as your choice is playable.
author: Fryxen
heading: Mandatory effects and exceptions

question: Which resources does Manutech gain, given its wild-resource icons?
ruling: No conflict: under the rules for wild resources, the text clarifies which resources apply.
quote: The rules for wild resources state that the text clarifies what resources apply.
author: Fryxen
heading: Manutech

question: Must you discard a card before drawing with Mars University?
ruling: Erratum: the card should have an asterisk and capital text to make clear that you have to discard a card first in order to draw a card.
quote: This card should have an asterisk and capital text to make it completely clear that you do indeed have to discard a card first in order to draw a card.
author: Fryxen
heading: Mars University

question: Can Mars University be played as your last card in hand?
ruling: Yes. Its whole effect is optional and triggered; discarding is not part of its direct effects, so it can still be played as the last card.
quote: Mars University can still be played as the last card though, because discarding is not part of its direct effects but is a trigger. Plus, it is optional.
author: Fryxen
heading: Mars University

question: Can a card be played as the last card if the effect it triggers cannot be performed?
ruling: Yes: playing a card does not require being able to perform the effect it triggers. Even if the trigger were mandatory, it would simply fizzle because part of it cannot be performed.
quote: So even if the trigger was mandatory, you could still play it as your last card, because playing it does not require you to be able to perform its triggering effect.
author: Fryxen
heading: Mars University

question: If a played card triggers both Mars University and a card draw such as Research, which resolves first?
ruling: The player chooses the order. Normally it is better to draw first so there is a better pool to discard from, but remember Mars University has you discard before you draw its new card.
quote: 3. You choose. And normally, it's better to draw cards first (Research) so you have a better pool of candidates to discard.
author: Fryxen
heading: Mars University

question: With Mars University, does Research let you discard a card to draw, then discard again (possibly the card just drawn) to draw another?
ruling: Yes. Confirmed: Research triggers Mars University twice, so you can discard a card to draw one and then discard another card to draw again; the second discarded card may be the one just drawn with the first science tag.
quote: All very correct. :)
author: Fryxen
heading: Mars University

question: Can you choose the order of Mars University's effect parts?
ruling: The order is fixed: iconography alone would let you choose the order, which was not intended, so the order is specified in the explanation text.
quote: Mars University is trickier, because iconography alone would let you choose order, which was not our intention.
author: Fryxen
heading: Mars University

question: Does Mars University's text (optional discard, fixed order) or its icons govern?
ruling: The text makes clear how it works; the card should have had an asterisk, but the distinction is not very important.
quote: Should have had an asterisk. It's not a very important distinction though, and the text still makes it clear how it works.
author: Fryxen
heading: Mars University

topic: Triggered effects that cannot be performed
question: Can a card or action be played when a required or triggered effect cannot be performed (for example a production decrease with none to decrease, or a triggered discard like Mars University)?
ruling: Failed triggers do invalidate the action: you must be able to perform all effects, including non-voluntary triggers. Example given: placing a tile on the south pole is only allowed if you can pay the triggered cost for placing a tile there.
quote: I think the point is that failed triggers DO in fact invalidate the action - you have to be able to do all effects, including triggers that are not expressly voluntary (like MU).
author: Fryxen
heading: Mars University

question: Does Mars University force an order of effects (discard then draw), and does it need an asterisk?
ruling: Mars University is intended to be played in the order of its text and icons, and strictly should carry an asterisk because it forces the order of effects. Fryxen only floated the idea of an erratum here.
quote: Strictly speaking, it should have an asterisk because it forces the order of effects. Maybe we have to make an errata in this case.
author: Fryxen
heading: Mars University

question: Must you discard before drawing with Mars University?
ruling: Yes. Mars University has been errata'd in the official FAQ on BGG to include an asterisk: you have to discard first, then draw.
quote: Mars University has been errata:ed to include an asterisk in the official FAQ here on BGG. You do have to discard first.
author: Fryxen
heading: Mars University

question: When does Media Group gain money relative to playing an event, given text saying 'after'?
ruling: 'After' is an older formulation but works as 'when': playing a card is when it is paid for and revealed and its effects and triggers go to the stack, so Media Group's effect triggers like any other.
quote: 'After' was an older formulation, but it works as well, since 'playing a card' is when you have payed for and revealed the card and its effects and triggers go to the 'stack'.
author: Fryxen
heading: Media Group

question: Can one player claim more than one milestone and fund more than one award?
ruling: Yes, there is no per-player limit other than the general limits (3 of 5 milestones claimed, 3 awards funded, each only once); one player can claim all 3 milestones and fund all 3 awards. This was an implicit confirmation: he did it once for 30 points at game end (3 players).
quote: I've actually achieved that once, earning me 30 points at game end (3-players). I won, by the way :)
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Milestones and awards

question: Does the Miner award count steel and titanium together?
ruling: Yes. Miner is the sum of steel plus titanium resource cubes at the end of the game, so the last production phase and placement bonuses matter.
quote: Miner is indeed the sum of steel plus titanium at the end of the game, so the last production phase and placement bonuses are important.
author: Fryxen
heading: Miner (award)

topic: Mining Area adjacency as first card
question: Can you play Mining Area as your first card when you have no tile to be adjacent to?
ruling: No. Mining Area must be placed adjacent to one of your own tiles, so with none you cannot play the card.
quote: Then you cannot play the card.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Mining Area

topic: Mining Area/Rights on Amazonis wild resource space
question: On Amazonis Planitia, can Mining Area or Mining Rights be placed on a space whose placement bonus is one standard (wild) resource, and what happens to the production?
ruling: Yes, if the player chooses steel or titanium as the wild resource gained from the space: that counts as getting a steel/titanium placement bonus, so the card can be placed there and gives the matching production. Mining Guild only triggers if you get that placement bonus, so you must choose steel or titanium.
quote: Correct, MG only gets its bonus if you get that placement bonus, so in this case you'd have to choose steel or titanium as your wild resource.
author: Fryxen
heading: Mining Area

topic: Mining Area/Rights on Amazonis wild resource space
question: If the wild resource space on Amazonis Planitia is taken as steel or titanium, can Mining Rights/Area be placed there and does the Mining Guild effect trigger?
ruling: Yes to both: choosing steel or titanium for the wild-resource placement bonus lets you place Mining Rights or Mining Area there, gaining the corresponding production, and also triggers the Mining Guild effect.
quote: Yes.
author: Fryxen
heading: Mining Area

question: Is Mining Expedition's removal of plants mandatory or 'up to'?
ruling: Up to: the old text formulation means 'up to', following the normal rule for red-bordered removal even if the text does not say it.
quote: Old text formulation. It means up to.
author: Fryxen
heading: Mining Expedition

question: Do tags printed on corporation cards count (e.g. Mining Guild's two building tags toward Builder)?
ruling: Yes, the tags count. Mining Guild has a good chance at the Builder milestone, but only if 3 other milestones are not yet claimed and no one else claims Builder first.
quote: Yes, the tags count.
author: Fryxen
heading: Mining Guild

question: Does Mining Guild give 2 steel production when covering a space with 2 steel?
ruling: No. Mining Guild gives only 1 step of steel production regardless of whether the placement bonus is 1 or 2 steel or titanium; to get more you must place more tiles on such areas.
quote: No, you only get 1 step of steel production, regardless of f you get 1 or 2 steel or 1 or 2 titanium as placement bonus.
author: Fryxen
heading: Mining Guild

question: Which tile placements trigger Mining Guild?
ruling: There are 10 areas on the board with steel or titanium bonuses, and Mining Guild triggers when you place any tile (city, greenery, ocean or special) on one of them.
quote: Mining Guild gets its effect when you place a tile (city / greenery / ocean / special) on one of them.
author: Fryxen
heading: Mining Guild

question: What exactly triggers Mining Guild's production bonus?
ruling: It triggers on the placing of a tile (on a steel or titanium placement bonus space), not on getting any steel or titanium. The 3rd printing (July 2017) added asterisks and changed the explanation text to make this clearer.
quote: It triggers on the placing of a tile, not on getting any steel or titanium, so we added the asterisks and changed the explanation text.
author: Fryxen
heading: Mining Guild

question: Should Mining Guild be read by the icons or text?
ruling: The icons are not to be taken strictly here; read the text, and the updated card has an asterisk.
quote: From the iconography (which I agree is not to be taken strict as is in this case) it is pretty clear that you should read the text
author: Fryxen
heading: Mining Guild

topic: Multi-step effects and 'if 1 or more' triggers
question: Can an effect such as 'lose 7 MC' or 'raise temperature 2 steps' be split into single steps to trigger things repeatedly?
ruling: Effects with several steps are separated into individual steps even though normally performed together, but an effect triggered by 'if 1 or more X' refers to the whole effect and does not trigger on each step. You cannot force Mons Insurance to pay out multiple times by splitting a 7 MC loss (Sabotage) into 7 packets.
quote: you can't force Mons to multiple payouts by for example separating 7 MC loss into 7 packets when playing Sabotage.
author: Fryxen
heading: Mons Insurance

question: With a card that makes an opponent lose up to X resources, can the target be chosen to lose 0 resources to trigger Mons Insurance's payout?
ruling: You may choose 0 for an 'up to X' removal like Asteroid's plants, but since the opponent lost nothing, Mons Insurance does not have to pay them.
quote: yes, you can choose 0, but since the then haven't lost anything, Mons doesn't have to pay them.
author: Fryxen
heading: Mons Insurance

question: Is reducing production, or removing your own resources, optional when playing a card?
ruling: Reducing production (e.g. animals cards) is mandatory since it is a cost to play the card, as is removing your own resources (Moss). Getting production that you can't increase would be ignorable, but no such case exists in the game.
quote: Reducing production (animals), on the other hand, is mandatory since that is obviously a cost to play the card, as is removing your own resources (Moss).
author: Fryxen
heading: Moss

question: Can Moss and Immigrant City be played when the effects only work in a particular order?
ruling: In the cases cited (Moss, Immigrant City) you can choose the order of the effects so that the plays are legal.
quote: In the cases cited above (Moss, Immigrant City) you can choose the order of the effects so that the plays are legal.
author: Fryxen
heading: Moss

question: Is losing a plant on Moss a requirement?
ruling: No. The wording on Moss clarifies that losing a plant is not optional; it is not a regular requirement, which is consistent with the rules.
quote: the wording on Moss was to clarify that losing a plant is not optional, not that it is a regular requirement.
author: Fryxen
heading: Moss

question: Can Moss be played with no plants if Viral Enhancers is in play?
ruling: Yes. Resolve the Viral Enhancers trigger first to gain a plant, then pay Moss's plant cost.
quote: You can play Moss without having any plants if you have Viral Enhancers in play. Choose to resolve the VE first to gain a plat and voila!
author: Fryxen
heading: Moss

question: May any tile other than the Noctis City card's city be placed on the reserved Noctis City hex?
ruling: No. No other tile than a city tile placed by the Noctis City project card may ever be placed on the Noctis City hex.
quote: You were right, no other tile than a city tile placed by the Noctis City project card may ever be placed there.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Noctis City

question: Where can Nuclear Zone's special tile be placed?
ruling: On any legal placement: areas reserved for oceans (blue) may not be used, and Noctis City's reserved space is also unavailable.
quote: Yes, any "legal" placement, that is. Blue areas are still reserved for oceans, and may thus not be used. Noctis City is also already reserved.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Nuclear Zone

question: Can Nuclear Zone be placed on an already occupied area, replacing the tile?
ruling: No. An area becomes unavailable when there is a tile on it.
quote: No. An area becomes unavailable when there is a tile on it.
author: Fryxen
heading: Nuclear Zone

question: Is Nuclear Zone owned by the player (an anchor for greenery adjacency and counted for Landlord)?
ruling: Yes: the tile is claimed with your color, can be a point (not necessarily the only one) to spread greeneries from, and counts for Landlord.
quote: Yes, the tile can be a point (not necessarily the only one) to spread greeneries from, and yes, it counts for Landlord.
author: Fryxen
heading: Nuclear Zone

question: Is placing a tile next to ocean tiles worth 2 MC a commonly missed rule?
ruling: Yes: the 2 MC for placing a tile next to ocean tiles is a rule people sometimes miss, but, unlike the action-phase misunderstanding, it does not have grave consequences for the game.
quote: Another rule that people sometimes miss is getting the 2 M€ from placing next to ocean tiles
author: Fryxen
heading: Ocean placement

question: If I place two oceans and the second lands next to the first, does the first ocean's adjacent-ocean MC bonus count the second ocean if I resolve it later?
ruling: No. The adjacency MC bonus is determined at the moment it is triggered (when the tile is placed), so the first ocean still gives 2 MC regardless of when you resolve the money or place the next ocean. Raising TR once for two oceans afterwards is fine.
quote: The money trigger is decided immediately when it is triggered, so it would give 2 MC regardless of what order you resolve it.
author: Fryxen
heading: Ocean placement

question: If I place an ocean tile next to another ocean tile, do I get the 2 MC adjacency bonus?
ruling: Yes. Placing an ocean next to an already placed ocean tile gives the 2 MC ocean adjacency bonus.
quote: 1) Yes.
author: Fryxen
heading: Ocean placement

question: With Olympus Conference, does Research let you add a science resource and immediately remove it to draw a card (or the reverse order)?
ruling: Yes. Confirmed: Research triggers Olympus Conference twice, so you can add a science resource and then remove it to draw a card, or remove one and then add one again.
quote: All very correct. :)
author: Fryxen
heading: Olympus Conference

question: Are played event cards, which are stored face down, hidden information?
ruling: Trackable information such as which events a player has played is in theory open, but it is deliberately semi-hidden to prevent analysis paralysis and kingmaking. Players may ask how many events or tags another player has, but stalling the game to survey opponents' cards should be called out.
quote: all trackable information is in theory open, so you could ask a player what events he/she has played, or how many VPs are on his/her cards. BUT such information is semi-hidden exactly to prevent AP and kingmaking
author: Fryxen
heading: Open and hidden information

question: Is final scoring information open?
ruling: Yes, scoring is open: players may state their points, and the designer says scoring is open information.
quote: SCORING IS OPEN!
author: Fryxen
heading: Open and hidden information

question: Are played cards, including face-down events and covered cards, open information?
ruling: Yes. All played cards are open information and everyone is entitled to know what has been played or done, even cards that are face down or covered, especially at end-game scoring, though repeatedly going through an opponent's cards to analyse is not appropriate.
quote: All played cards are open information; everyone is entitled to know what has been played/done in the game, even cards that are face down or covered.
author: Fryxen
heading: Open and hidden information

question: Is the identity of discarded cards (e.g. cards sold with Sell Patents or not bought in the research phase) public information?
ruling: No. Discarded cards are not public information. Whether sold cards must be placed face down was not answered.
quote: Discarded cards are not public information.
author: Fryxen
heading: Open and hidden information

question: Why are played events placed face down, and are they hidden information?
ruling: Events are placed face down to signal that their tags are only temporarily in effect and to discourage calculating exact scores; the information is still technically open and players may check it later. Rule 0 applies: asking is fine, stalling the whole game is not.
quote: This is why the information is technically open, even though hiding it from view helps the game along.
author: Fryxen
heading: Open and hidden information

question: Must a player reveal the number of cards in their hand when asked?
ruling: Yes, hand size is open information and should be told as soon as asked. Slow play is a matter of respecting others' time rather than an official ruling.
quote: Tell them what they ask for asap since it's open information.
author: Fryxen
heading: Open and hidden information

question: Who chooses the order when several effects or triggers happen at the same time?
ruling: The acting player chooses the order. If it is not in the action phase, the first player chooses the order.
quote: If several effects or triggers are to be performed at the same time, the acting player chooses the order. If it is not in the action phase, the first player chooses order.
author: Fryxen
heading: Order of effects

question: In what order is a card played: reveal, requirements, payment, effects?
ruling: First reveal and declare the card, confirm requirements and pay. It is now being played; all its effects and all effects triggered by playing it with its tags wait to be resolved in the order chosen by the active player. If the player can't perform all effects (apart from the exceptions), the whole action is taken back.
quote: When playing a card, you first reveal and declare that you're playing the card, then you confirm that you meet the requirements, and you pay for the card.
author: Fryxen
heading: Order of effects

question: In what order must a card's effects and the triggers they cause be resolved?
ruling: You may resolve effects and triggers in any order you like, as long as an effect is performed before the trigger it causes (and, e.g., a temperature step can be taken before placing the bonus ocean it triggers). Resolving triggers right away, or following the order printed on the card, is good habit but not a rule. Players should announce what they do.
quote: Performing triggers Before moving on to the next effect is good habit, but is not a rule. You choose triggers and effects in any order you choose (but must of course first perform an effect in order to get any trigger for it).
author: Fryxen
heading: Order of effects

question: Can you place a greenery, raise oxygen, raise temperature, place the bonus ocean and only then take the greenery's placement bonus?
ruling: Theoretically the sequence is maybe allowed as an extremely rare edge case, but the obvious thematic intent is to finish placing the greenery before resolving the triggers it caused.
quote: is an extremely rare edge case where the sequence would theoretically be allowed (maybe), but where the obvious thematic intent would be to finish with the greenery before resoving the triggers.
author: Fryxen
heading: Order of effects

topic: Payment first, then effects in any order
question: In what order are payment and effects resolved when playing a card such as Giant Ice Asteroid?
ruling: Pay first (titanium and discounts may be used, but not titanium gained from playing that card; any requirement box must be met before). Then perform the effects in any preferred order; effects triggered by an effect must be performed after that effect.
quote: Payment first, then the effects in any order (but effects triggered by effects mustbe performed after those effects, since they would otherwise not exist).
author: Fryxen
heading: Order of effects

question: How should the order of card effects, placement bonuses and triggers be understood?
ruling: Pay first. All effects of the card go individually into a pile of effects (a card raising temperature 2 steps is 2 effects). You may perform any available effect; effects it triggers (placement bonuses, other players' bonuses) are added to the pile. Perform each effect before the effects it adds; otherwise choose order freely.
quote: So there is just a very basic chain: * Pay first. * Perform an effect before any effects added by performing that effect.
author: Fryxen
heading: Order of effects

topic: Pile of effects: Subterranean Reservoir example
question: With Subterranean Reservoir, which effects can be performed before the ocean is placed?
ruling: After paying and revealing, the ocean placement and Media Group's +3 M€ are in the pile. Effects created by placing the ocean (printed placement bonuses including South Pole -6 M€, adjacency bonuses, TR, Arctic Algae) may not be performed before the ocean is actually placed. All waiting effects must be performed before another action can be taken.
quote: You may not perform any of those new effects before you actually place the ocean tile.
author: Fryxen
heading: Order of effects

topic: When a card counts as played
question: At what moment is a card considered played, and can Media Group's +3 M€ be taken before the event's own effects?
ruling: Order: 1) check requirements, 2) pay, 3) perform effects and triggered effects in any order, 4) place the card. A card/action is considered played the moment you've paid for it, so triggers on playing are among the card's own effects; Media Group's 3 M€ can be chosen before the event's own effects.
quote: A card/action is considered to be played the moment you've payed for it, so any trigger on that will be among the card's own effects.
author: Fryxen
heading: Order of effects

topic: Playing a card: cost and requirements first
question: When must a card's cost and requirements be satisfied relative to its effects?
ruling: The cost at the top left must be paid, and any requirement at the top of the card must be met, before any effects take place. For other actions the cost is stated before the red action arrow.
quote: The cost at the top left must be payed, and any requirement at the top of the card must be met before any effects take place.
author: Fryxen
heading: Order of effects

topic: Order of effects when playing a card
question: In what order are a played card's effects and the effects it triggers performed?
ruling: Effects can be performed in any order. A card's effects and the effects triggered by its tags form a pool that must be emptied; effects triggered by performing one effect are added to the pool only once that effect is performed, so they cannot be done before it.
quote: A, B, C, d, and e are now in a pool of options that must sooner or later be emptied
author: Fryxen
heading: Order of effects

topic: Order of effects in physical vs digital
question: Does the player choose the order of effects of a played card (e.g. Mars University before Research draws cards) in the physical game?
ruling: Yes, in the physical game the player chooses the order of effects; the digital version differs by not letting you choose the order. The designers are pushing the programmers to correct the order in cases where it matters.
quote: there is this small difference to the physical game that you can"t choose the order of effects.
author: Fryxen
heading: Order of effects

question: When playing a card, are triggers from other cards (e.g. Arctic Algae on ocean placement) resolved only after all of the played card's instructions, and what comes before effects?
ruling: Payment and requirements come first. After that the card's effects and the triggers they cause can be resolved in any order, as long as everything can be carried out.
quote: Completely correct. Payment and requirements first, then effects and triggers in any order, as long as everything can be carried out.
author: Fryxen
heading: Order of effects

topic: Order of effects: digital vs board game
question: Can the player choose the order of effects in the digital version?
ruling: In the board game players choose the order of effects; in the digital game they cannot, and the order is programmed to be most beneficial to the player.
quote: you can't choose the order of effects in the digital version.
author: Fryxen
heading: Order of effects

topic: Order of effects within an action
question: Within one action, in what order are its effects (tile placement, placement bonuses, triggered effects) resolved?
ruling: Effects that an action creates (oxygen from a greenery, placement bonuses, etc.) wait and are performed in the order the player chooses, but a cause always comes before its effect, so greenery -> oxygen -> TR is a chain. Multi-step effects (gain 5 M€, raise temperature 2 steps) split into single steps, yet a trigger worded 'if 1 or more X' sees the whole effect: Sabotage's 7 M€ loss pays Mons Insurance once, not 7 times.
quote: When effects are 'created' (oxygen from greenery, placement bonuses etc.), they wait to be performed in the order the player chooses.
author: Fryxen
heading: Order of effects

question: Are placing a greenery, raising oxygen and raising TR separable in time?
ruling: Greenery -> oxygen -> TR is a cause-effect chain and is treated as such. Effects that get 'created' (oxygen from a greenery, placement bonuses etc.) wait to be performed in whatever order the player chooses.
quote: Greenery -> oxygen -> TR is a cause-effect chain and is treated as such.
author: Fryxen
heading: Order of effects

topic: Being-played zone: when the played card reaches its destination
question: When does a card played leave to its final place, and when do its tags count?
ruling: The card leaves hand and enters a 'being played zone' where its tags count until all effects are done, then goes to its final destination (this is why tags on event cards count while being played). Tags are played at the same time as the card; effects triggering on tags are immediately added to the pile of effects.
quote: the card leaves hand and enters a 'being played zone' where its tags count until all is done and the cards go to its final destination.
author: Fryxen
heading: Order of effects

topic: Effects active when a card is played (Decomposers and Topsoil Contract)
question: If Decomposers is already in play when you play Topsoil Contract, do you get its effect right away from the played card's tags?
ruling: Correct: a card's effects turn on as it is played and then triggers fire, so you gain 1 M€ immediately. The being-played zone is a model to understand the rules, not an official rule.
quote: Correct. By the way, the BPZ is not an official rule, but rather a good model to understand the rules.
author: Fryxen
heading: Order of effects

question: Is gaining 2 steel divisible into gaining 1 steel and 1 steel as separate effects?
ruling: No. A given amount of one resource type is not divisible; most other things are.
quote: No. A given amount of one resource type is not divisible. Otherwise most things are.
author: Fryxen
heading: Order of effects

question: When a play triggers several effects, in what order are they resolved and can changed circumstances cancel a triggered effect?
ruling: As soon as an effect triggers it goes into a pool of pending effects. The active player chooses the order in which to resolve them; resolving one may change the situation but never removes another from the pool or removes the requirement to resolve it. If effects can't be resolved, the whole action has to be taken back (except the standard exceptions).
quote: As soon as an effect is triggered, it goes into a 'pool' of effects waiting to be resolved.
author: Fryxen
heading: Order of effects

question: When overspending with steel or titanium, do you get change back, and can cubes be exchanged?
ruling: You can overspend with steel and titanium (e.g. 6 steel for an 11 MC card) but the surplus value is lost, so it is usually more economical to pay 5 steel and 1 MC. The cubes only represent numbers of resources and can be exchanged with the bank at any time.
quote: The rule says that you can overspend with steel and titanium, but then surplus value is lost.
author: EagleEye80
heading: Paying with steel and titanium

topic: Paying for card actions with steel or titanium
question: Can steel or titanium be used to pay for an action (e.g. Space Mirrors) if the card has the matching tag?
ruling: No. You can pay with steel or titanium only if the action shows a steel/titanium symbol left of the red arrow; only Water Import From Europa and Aquifer Pumping allow it. Actions don't have tags, cards do, and when doing an action you pay for the action, not the card.
quote: there are only two cards which allows steel and titanium for action payment instead of M€, Water Import from Europa and Aquifer Pumping.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Paying with steel and titanium

question: Can plants pay for plant-tag cards or energy for power-tag cards like steel/titanium do?
ruling: No. Only steel and titanium have the special rule for paying for cards with building and space tags; plants and energy do not.
quote: a lot of people think you can pay with plants for plant tag cards, or energy for power tag cards. But those resources do not have that extra rule.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Paying with steel and titanium

question: Can you spend steel when building a city with the standard project?
ruling: No. Standard projects have no tags, so steel cannot be used. Helion never converts heat to money, but it may use heat as if it were money.
quote: Standard projects don't have tags, so no, you cannot use steel in this case.
author: EagleEye80
heading: Paying with steel and titanium

question: Can you pay with plant or energy resources when playing a plant-tagged or energy-tagged card?
ruling: No. The only building materials are steel (for cards with a building tag) and titanium (for cards with a space tag). Apart from those, cards can only be paid for with M€.
quote: The only building material in the game are steel (for cards with building tag) and titanium (for cards with space tag). There are no other way to pay for playing cards - except MegaCredits.
author: EagleEye80
heading: Paying with steel and titanium

question: Does Philares trigger on adjacency between its own tiles, or only your tile and an opponent's tile?
ruling: Read the text: the adjacency must be to an opponent's tile (the icons are ambiguous); an asterisk would be good but the corporation text is read anyway.
quote: Again, an asterisk would be good, but also again, the ambigous icon and the card being a corporation would prompt you to read it anyway
author: Fryxen
heading: Philares

question: What does the Phobos Space Haven city tile count for?
