ruling: The tile itself is worth no VP (playing the card is worth points), but it counts toward the Landlord award and the Mayor milestone, and it is a city for events/effects triggered by cities, except those that specify a city ON MARS.
quote: What DaveD said, plus it counts towards the Mayor Milestone.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Phobos Space Haven

question: Why does Phobos Space Haven place a city tile, and does its city tag matter?
ruling: The city tile is placed so it is visible that you built a city, so you do not miss the bonuses of triggering cards (Pets, Rover Construction, Immigration Shuttles). Standard city triggers use tiles, not tags. The city tag itself is not used for anything; it only reminds you the card places a city tile.
quote: Actually, the city tag itself is not used for anything at all, but it reminds you that the card places a city tile.
author: Fryxen
heading: Phobos Space Haven

question: If a card adds resources you cannot collect (no card to hold microbes), can you still play it, and must you give them to opponents?
ruling: Yes, you can still play the card and skip the part adding resources you can't collect; you are not forced to give resources to opponents.
quote: Correct.
author: Fryxen
heading: Placing resources on cards

question: Can resources be placed on any card?
ruling: Resources can only be placed on a card that defines what you can do with them. Decomposers can collect microbes (1 VP per 3 microbes); Viral Enhancers cannot since no function is attributed to microbes there. This avoids mixing resource types on one card.
quote: you can only place microbes on a card that defines what you can do with those microbes.
author: Fryxen
heading: Placing resources on cards

question: Which cards can collect resources such as microbes or animals?
ruling: Only cards that explicitly can use the resources on them (spend them in an action or score VP for them) may collect them. Viral Enhancers cannot, so the resource triggered by its microbe tag is a plant resource as stated on the card.
quote: Only cards that explicitly can use the resources on them may collect such resources.
author: Fryxen
heading: Placing resources on cards

topic: Adding resources to a card when no card can hold them
question: If you play a card that puts animal tokens on another card but you have no card that can hold animals, can you still play it?
ruling: Yes. You may play the card; if you have no project that can take care of the animals, they are lost. The post does not say whether the resources must or may go onto an opponent's card.
quote: You may also bring convoys with animals to Mars. But of course, if you don't have any project that can take care of your animals, they will die and you lose those resources.
author: EagleEye80
heading: Placing resources on cards

question: Do you need a card that can hold a resource to play a card that adds that resource to your own cards?
ruling: No. Placing resources on your own cards is optional: you may play a card that gives animals even with no animal card in play, ignore the resource, and perform the rest of the card effect as usual.
quote: Placing resources on your own cards are also optional - the rules says that you can play cards that give you animals, for example, even if you have no animal cards.
author: EagleEye80
heading: Placing resources on cards

question: Can a card without a red border place resources on another player's card?
ruling: No. You can never place resources on other players' cards unless the effect is red-bordered; resources and production without a red border only apply to the player himself.
quote: ...and you cannot ever place resources on other player's cards. Rules clearly states that resources and production without red-borders only apply to the player himself...
author: EagleEye80
heading: Placing resources on cards

question: On which cards can a microbe resource be placed?
ruling: Only cards that define a use for microbes can store microbe resources. These are often blue, but not all blue microbe cards can collect microbes (Viral Enhancers is an example that cannot).
quote: Only cards that define a use for microbes can store microbe resources.
author: Fryxen
heading: Placing resources on cards

topic: Playing a card that adds resources with no valid card
question: Can you play a card that tells you to add a microbe to another card if you have no card that can hold microbes?
ruling: Yes. This is one of the 3 allowed exceptions where you do not have to be able to do everything the card says.
quote: If you don't have such a card you can still play your card because this is one of the 3 allowed exceptions where you don't have to be able to do everything the card says.
author: Fryxen
heading: Placing resources on cards

topic: Placing resources on other players' cards
question: Can resources be placed on other players' cards when a card says to add them to another card?
ruling: No. You do not place resources on other players' cards unless the icon has a red border that allows targeting other players.
quote: You do not place resources on other players' cards, because you don't have the red border onthe icon that allows you to target other players' stuff.
author: Fryxen
heading: Placing resources on cards

topic: Placing resources on own cards not mandatory
question: Can you play a card that adds resources if you have nowhere to put them?
ruling: Yes. Placing resources on your own cards is not mandatory in order to play the card; if there is nowhere to put them, simply ignore them.
quote: Placing resources on your own cards is not mandatory in order to play the card. So you can play the card even without anywhere to put them.
author: Fryxen
heading: Placing resources on cards

question: Can a card with a microbe tag collect microbes?
ruling: No. Only cards that define a use for a certain resource can collect it; for example Viral Enhancers cannot collect microbes even though it is a microbe card.
quote: Only cards that define a use for certain resources can collect them. So Viral Enhancers for example, can't collect microbes even though it is a microbe card.
author: Fryxen
heading: Placing resources on cards

topic: Imported Nitrogen / adding resources is mandatory
question: Is adding microbes to another card optional for cards like Imported Nitrogen?
ruling: No. All effects must be performed; adding microbes is only omitted when they cannot be added to any card.
quote: No, you have to perform all effects. Adding microbes is not optional, it is only omitted when you can't add them to any card.
author: Fryxen
heading: Placing resources on cards

question: When a card says to add X resources to another/any card, can the resources be divided among multiple cards?
ruling: No. All resources from one effect go to a single card, and the same applies to resources gained from trading in Colonies. For Imported Nitrogen you choose one microbe card (for all 3 microbes) and one animal card (for both animals).
quote: You can not divide the resources to different cards, and the same is true when getting resources from trading in the Colonies expansion.
author: Fryxen
heading: Placing resources on cards

topic: Searching for tags with two required tags
question: Planetary Alliance says draw 1 Jovian card and 1 Venus card; can Cloud Tourism (Venus and Jovian tags) be taken as either the Venus or the Jovian card?
ruling: The Venus and Jovian draws are separate effects and the player may choose their order. So you can search for the Venus card first, take Cloud Tourism as that card (discarding the other revealed cards), and then search for a Jovian card. Taking the first card with either tag then searching for the other is the wrong procedure, though it rarely matters.
quote: Technically, those are separate effects, and you can choose the order.
author: Fryxen
heading: Planetary Alliance

question: How many cards must be in hand to claim the Planner milestone and where are they counted?
ruling: At this prerelease stage Planner required 18 cards in your hand (not on the table) when claimed.
quote: Planner requires that you have 18 cards in your hand (not on table) when you claim it.
author: Fryxen
heading: Planner (milestone)

question: How many cards in hand does the Planner milestone require, given that the early board image posted online differs?
ruling: The Planner milestone requires only 16 cards in hand; the early pre-finalized board image that showed another number is wrong.
quote: Planner milestone only requires 16 cards in hand.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Planner (milestone)

question: Does Poseidon's first-action colony placement happen immediately?
ruling: Corporations with a defined first action (like Poseidon) should strictly have an asterisk marking that the text departs from the icons, but one was not added since the corporation text is always read anyway. The post does not itself state when the colony is placed; the text governs.
quote: Corporations with a defined first action - do you really want to clutter down the cards with asterisks when you always read the corporation card text anyway
author: Fryxen
heading: Poseidon

topic: Edge-case guidelines for conflicting mandatory effects
question: What guideline applies when a mandatory corporation effect cannot be carried out within the normal rules (Poseidon colony, Vitor 4th award)?
ruling: Temporary rulings should: 1) not break the game (do not allow a 4th colony); 2) follow thematics (Poseidon should get a colony, doubling up is a last resort); 3) not punish the player too much nor reward them (fizzling the colony would be very punishing). A strict ruling would be to fizzle what cannot be performed while still letting the corp be played; the Vitor ruling (extra award) was made so as not to punish a fringe case where two rules clash.
quote: 1) Don't break the game. So don't allow a 4th colony. 2) Follow thematics. Poseidon should get a colony, but doubling up is a last resort
author: Fryxen
heading: Poseidon

question: Can Power Infrastructure's action be used to spend 0 energy for 0 MC just to take an action?
ruling: No. The card says 'spend' and spending 0 resources is not spending, so at least 1 energy must be spent.
quote: The card says 'spend', and you can't spend 0 resources - it wouldn't be spending. So no.
author: Fryxen
heading: Power Infrastructure

question: Can Predators remove an animal from another Predators card?
ruling: Yes, Predators can eat Predators.
quote: Predators can eat predators, yes.
author: Fryxen
heading: Predators

question: Is production capped at 10 on the production track?
ruling: No. Production has no limit for any resource: for 11, leave one player marker at 10 and start a new one at 1; for 22, use two markers at 10 and one at 2.
quote: it is important that there is no limit to how high your production is - for any resource.
author: Fryxen
heading: Production

question: Should MegaCredit production be allowed to exceed 10?
ruling: Yes; production can exceed 10 and the designers prefer it so players can specialise. Tharsis Republic would be handicapped if MegaCredit production could not exceed 10.
quote: As stated, Tharsis Republic will a bit handicapped if not allowed to exceed 10 MegaCredit production.
author: Fryxen
heading: Production

question: Can production exceed 10?
ruling: Yes, production can exceed 10.
quote: Production can exceed 10.
author: Fryxen
heading: Production

question: Is there a limit to how much M€ (or any resource) you can produce?
ruling: No: there is no limit to how much of anything you can produce. Use cubes near the '10' to mark sets of 10; for 50+ M€ production a silver cube can replace your player markers.
quote: That is correct. Leave cubes at or near the "10" on the track to show how many sets of 10 you have in production.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Production

question: What happens if your M€ production is negative enough that net income is below zero?
ruling: Left open: Fryxen is not sure and guesses you lose money if you have any; he doesn't feel a definitive answer is needed.
quote: I'm not actually sure what should happen if you end up with a net negative income. I guess you lose money if you have any.
author: Fryxen
heading: Production

question: Can you play a card that decreases your production by 2 or more steps if you have less production of that resource?
ruling: No. All production effects must be performed to play the card, so you need that production first. If the decrease targets opposing production (red border on the resource icon), someone must have that production to reduce, and you may choose to target yourself.
quote: All production effects MUST be performed in order to play the card, so yes, you need that production first.
author: Fryxen
heading: Production decreases

question: Why must a production decrease be possible before a card can be played?
ruling: A production decrease on a card usually represents the card's project converting that resource into another (e.g. energy into oxygen or steel, plants into animals, your money into someone else's money for Hackers). The decrease must be met because it simplifies doing the conversion manually every turn.
quote: So the production decrease must be met because it is a simplification from doing the conversion manually every turn.
author: Fryxen
heading: Production decreases

question: Can you play a card whose immediate effect would lower production below zero (or an already-zero track)?
ruling: No. You must fulfil the requirement and be able to perform the card's effects (rulebook pages 9 and 7). A card cannot be played if its production reduction would take your production below zero (below -5 for MC).
quote: No, you cannot play a card that lower production below zero (or below -5 for MC).
author: Isaac Fryxelius
heading: Production decreases

question: What if a card reduces any player's production (red-bordered production) and the opponent has none?
ruling: A red-bordered production reduction must be performed, so if the opponent does not have that production you must lower your own production or not play the card at all (rulebook page 15).
quote: A card effect that reduces production for any player (red-bordered production of a resource) must be performed, so if your opponent doesn’t have that production, then you must lower your own production or not play the card at all.
author: Isaac Fryxelius
heading: Production decreases

question: Is the summary 'production reduction is mandatory, red-bordered or not; red-bordered resource reduction is optional' correct?
ruling: Yes, a very good summary. Basically all effects of a card need to be performed; the exception is that you can still play asteroids and comets even if there are no plants to hit.
quote: Basically, all effects of a card needs to be performed. The exception is that you can still smash asteroids and comets to the surface even if you cannot find any plants to land them on.
author: EagleEye80
heading: Production decreases

topic: Playing a card that decreases production you lack
question: Can you play a card that decreases a production you don't have?
ruling: No. You must perform all effects on a card to play it (except the exceptions in the rules), so if the card lowers a production you can't lower, you can't play it.
quote: You always need to perform all effects on a card to be able to play it.
author: EagleEye80
heading: Production decreases

question: Can you play a card that makes you lose more production than you have (e.g. -2 energy production with 1)?
ruling: No.
quote: Haha, well, an easy question deserves an easy answer :)
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Production decreases

topic: Mandatory production and own resource reductions
question: Is reducing production, or one's own resources, on a card mandatory?
ruling: Yes. Reducing production (your own or a red-bordered target) is always mandatory, and if you cannot, you cannot play the card. Reducing your own (non red-bordered) resources is also mandatory. This is endorsed as correct.
quote: The basic rule is that you have to perform everything on the card
author: EagleEye80
heading: Production decreases

question: If a card would decrease a production you have at 0 (e.g. energy), can it be played?
ruling: No.
quote: No
author: EagleEye80
heading: Production decreases

topic: Production decreases are mandatory, resource removal is optional
question: Why must production decreases be performed (even red-bordered ones) while removing resources from opponents is optional?
ruling: A production decrease simulates a cost for the project and must be performed; a 'consortium' effect means someone else loses market share. One-time resource losses that can target opponents are not costs but optional effects, performed in full, in part, or not at all.
quote: If the production decrease simulates a cost for the project, it must of course be performed for the project to work.
author: Fryxen
heading: Production decreases

question: Can Protected Valley be played for just +2 MC production when there is nowhere to place the greenery?
ruling: No, because the greenery tile is not one of the exceptions.
quote: Yes, that's correct.
author: Fryxen
heading: Protected Valley

question: Do permanent effects on blue (active) cards affect everyone or only the owner?
ruling: An icon with a red border can target other players (here: trigger when other players act) as well as yourself. Example: Rover Construction gives YOU 2 M€ (no red border on the M€ icon) whenever ANYONE, including you, places a city tile (red border on the city icon).
quote: If an icon has a red border, it can target other players (in this case trigger when other players do stuff) as well as yourself.
author: Fryxen
heading: Red border icons

question: When a card adds animals/microbes, must you add them to other players' cards, and which icons can target other players?
ruling: An icon with a red border may target other players, but an icon without a red border always targets yourself. (In reply to the question, resources are placed only on cards you own.)
quote: An icon with a red border may target other players, but an icon without red border always targets yourself.
author: Isaac Fryxelius
heading: Red border icons

question: What does the red border on an icon mean (optional effect, reduction, target another player)?
ruling: The red border does not mean the effect is optional, does not mean something is reduced, and does not mean you must target another player. It simply means the effect can target any player (you or an opponent). Production decreases of red-bordered resources must still be performed, so you lower your own if no opponent has it, or do not play the card.
quote: The red border simply means that the effect can target ANY player.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Red border icons

question: What does a red border around an effect icon mean?
ruling: A red border means the effect has a greater scope than only your own play area, i.e. it can target other players and their cards. It does not mean the effect is negative.
quote: The iconography used to show that an effect can target other players and their cards is to put a red border around the icon.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Red border icons

topic: Red border on icons: who is targeted
question: Can an icon without a red border target another player's cards (e.g. Extreme Cold Fungus adding microbes)?
ruling: No. The absence of red borders always means you only target yourself; if the text says 'any card' but the icon has no red border it means any of your cards. A red border opens it up to other players and the text becomes more important.
quote: The absence of red borders always means that you only target yourself.
author: Fryxen
heading: Red border icons

question: Can a negative effect that removes resources be split between several players?
ruling: No. For simplicity each negative effect can only target one player. Iconography usually shows separate icons for up to three resources and a single icon with a number for higher values (exceptions for M€ and crowded cards).
quote: for simplicity, each negative effect can only target one player.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Removing and stealing resources

question: Do removed resources go back to the supply or are they stolen?
ruling: They return to the supply unless the card says 'steal' (as Hired Raiders does). Remove means no one gets them.
quote: Yes, unless it says "steal", as it does on for example "Hired Raiders". Remove means that no-one gets them.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Removing and stealing resources

topic: Attack cards: removal versus production decrease
question: Must attacking effects (removing resources, reducing production) be performed to play the card?
ruling: Effects that remove resources need not be performed; you may play the card and skip them (balance assumes that). Effects that reduce other players' production must be performed, though you may reduce your own production instead.
quote: You don't have to perform this effect in order to play the card. ... they have to be performed. You may reduce your own production instead
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Removing and stealing resources

question: Can a card that removes other players' resources target several players?
ruling: There is a special rule: cards that affect other players' resources can only target one player, yet any player, not just yourself.
quote: There is a special rule concerning cards that affect other players' resources. Such cards can only target one player, yet still any player, not just yourself.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Removing and stealing resources

question: Is removing red-bordered (anyone's) resources mandatory?
ruling: No: removing red-bordered resources is optional; you may remove a smaller amount or none, but if you remove any you must target a single player and cannot split the effect. This exception exists for thematic reasons (e.g. asteroids hitting plants).
quote: Therefore, we had to make an exception for removing red-bordered resources (usually asteroids killing plants).
author: EagleEye80
heading: Removing and stealing resources

question: Which resource removal effects are mandatory and which are optional?
ruling: Effects that remove your own resources are mandatory. Effects that remove resources from any player (red border around the icon) are voluntary and may be performed in full, in part or not at all. Only one player or card may be targeted at a time with the effects of a card. Removing production is always mandatory.
quote: Effects that remove your own resources are mandatory, while effects that remove resources from any player (marked by a red border around the resource icon) are voluntary
author: Fryxen
heading: Removing and stealing resources

question: A card that removes plants from an opponent shows two symbols: is it two effects, and can the targets differ?
ruling: Destroying plants is a single effect and specifically targets one opponent, so you cannot split the removal between opponents.
quote: Destroying plants is one effect and it specifically states that you target one opponent.
author: Fryxen
heading: Removing and stealing resources

question: Are take-that effects optional?
ruling: Removing resources from other players is always optional. Removing production is mandatory, but you may choose to remove your own production, so all take-that cards are technically optional.
quote: removing resources from other players is always optional, but removing production is mandatory. However, you could remove your own production
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Removing and stealing resources

topic: Red-bordered resource removal when playing a card
question: When playing a card, may you ignore removing red-bordered resources (for example when no one has any to remove)?
ruling: Effects that happen when you play a card must be performed in order to play it, but the rules state exceptions: you may ignore removing red-bordered resources.
quote: You may ignore removing red-bordered resources.
author: EagleEye80
heading: Removing and stealing resources

question: When a card says to take resources from another player, do you gain them or do they go to the supply?
ruling: The only time you take resources from another player and add them to your own is when the card specifically says STEAL. If it is just a red-bordered icon, the taken resources go to the supply. Predators and Ants are technically not stealing since the card also tells you to gain a resource; Asteroids do not steal plants, only destroy them.
quote: The ONLY time you take resources from another player and add them to your own is when the card specifically says 'STEAL'.
author: Fryxen
heading: Removing and stealing resources

question: Does protection against removing resources (e.g. plants) also block stealing them?
ruling: Yes. Stealing involves removing, so it is blocked by protection. Stealing is also a package deal: you cannot remove fewer resources and still gain the full amount, nor steal less than the stated amount.
quote: Stealing involves removing and is therefore blocked.
author: Fryxen
heading: Removing and stealing resources

topic: Requirements: whose tiles, production and tags count
question: When a card requires tiles, production or tags, do only your own count or everyone's?
ruling: Temperature, oxygen and ocean are global and owned by no one. For any other tile, production or tag requirement only YOUR tiles/production/tags count unless the icon has a red border, in which case everything in play counts. Both Interstellar Colony Ship and Lightning Harvest count only your own science tags.
quote: global parameters are the same for everyone, normal black-bordered icons counts only your stuff and red-bordered icons count all player's stuff.
author: Fryxen
heading: Requirements

question: Can a card use its own tags to meet its own tag requirement?
ruling: No. A card cannot use its own tags to meet its requirements.
quote: A card cannot use its own tags to meet its requirements.
author: Fryxen
heading: Requirements

question: How are minimum and maximum requirements shown on cards?
ruling: All maximum requirements have 'max' in the requirement box and a red background. All other requirements are minimum requirements and have a yellow background in the requirement box; 'min' is not printed because most requirements are minimum.
quote: All maximum requirements have a 'max' in the requirement box and have a red background color in the box. All other requirements are minimum requirements
author: Fryxen
heading: Requirements

question: Does a requirement like '3 oceans' mean exactly 3 or at least 3?
ruling: All requirements are minimum unless explicitly written otherwise. Tag requirements are the same. Temperature uses the warmer and colder wording to avoid confusion with negative numbers.
quote: All requirements are minimum unless explicitly written otherwise.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Requirements

topic: Max requirements only checked on play
question: Does a card with a Max requirement stop working once the parameter passes that value?
ruling: No. Requirements are only applied when a card is played; the card does not deactivate later (an early prototype did, but it was dropped as too fiddly).
quote: Requirements are only applied when a card is played.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Requirements

topic: Requirements apply only when playing a card
question: Can an already played card with a requirement (e.g. Search for Life's max oxygen) still be used after the parameter passes the requirement?
ruling: Yes. Requirements apply only when the card is played from hand; once the card is in play, ignore its requirements just as you ignore its cost.
quote: The rules state that the requirements (upper-left on the cards) only applies when you play the card from your hand.
author: EagleEye80
heading: Requirements

question: Is a requirement without 'max' a minimum or an exact requirement?
ruling: A requirement box that doesn't explicitly say 'max' is a minimum requirement; e.g. 'requires 3 oceans' means at least 3 oceans. There are no exact requirements.
quote: There are no ‘exact requirements’.
author: Fryxen
heading: Requirements

topic: Requirements apply only when playing from hand
question: Can you still use a card (e.g. a technology card) after its requirement has been exceeded?
ruling: Yes. Requirements only apply when you play the card from your hand; once the card is in play it stays in play.
quote: The requirements only apply when you play the card from your hand. Once the card is in play, it stays in play...
author: EagleEye80
heading: Requirements

question: If a card says 'requires X' without a max/min qualifier, can it only be played at exactly that parameter value?
ruling: No: there are no cards with exact requirements; all are either minimum or maximum requirements.
quote: So there are no cards in the game with exact requirements - all are either minimum or maximum requirements.
author: EagleEye80
heading: Requirements

question: Are requirements written as 'Requires 7% oxygen' exact values, unlike 'must be -18C or colder' or '7% or less'?
ruling: There are no exact requirements. If 'max' is not stated it is a minimum. On temperature, 'or colder' / 'or warmer' is added in parentheses because negative numbers make 'more' ambiguous.
quote: there are no exact requirements. If "max" is not stated, it is minimum.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Requirements

question: Is a printed global requirement (e.g. 2% oxygen, 4 oceans) a minimum or an exact value?
ruling: Per the rulebook, any requirement must be met to play the card: a global parameter must have reached the stated level, while cards marked as maximum (e.g. oxygen 9% or lower) can only be played while the parameter is still low. It is not an exact value.
quote: Any requirement must be met in order to play the card. Some cards require a global parameter to have reached a certain level, while others can only be played while the parameter is still low
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Requirements

question: Can tags played during the same action meet a card's requirements, and must all effects be doable before the action?
ruling: Requirements must be met before you begin the action, so tags played during the same action cannot satisfy them. This differs from effects: you do not need to be able to perform all effects before the action, but you must find a way to do them during the action (compare placing a tile on the south pole on Hellas).
quote: Requirements work a little differently, because it requires a certain condition to be met before you even begin the action, and so tags being played during the same action can't be used to meet requirements.
author: Fryxen
heading: Requirements

question: Do tag requirements on cards count only your own tags, or all players' tags?
ruling: Requirements count only your own tags (and anything you own). For a card to count other players' tags or anything they own, its icons have a red border; without the red border only your own are counted.
quote: These cards only count your own tags. For a card to count other people's tags , or indeed anything they own, the icons would have a red border.
author: Fryxen
heading: Requirements

question: Does Research's double science tag count twice for Scientist and science effects?
ruling: Yes. Research has double science tags to trigger science effects twice and count twice in the Scientist award.
quote: We even have double science tags on one card (Research) to trigger science effects twice, and count twice in the scientist award.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Research

question: Does Research count as playing two cards or take two actions?
ruling: No. The text only explains the icons unless an asterisk marks a special rule exception. Research's two science tags trigger twice on Mars University and Olympus Conference; there is no asterisk, so there is no special rule for playing it.
quote: the text is only explaining the icons, unless there is an asterisk to mark a special rules exception.
author: Fryxen
heading: Research

question: Does playing Research (two science tags) count as two actions?
ruling: No. Playing any card always counts as 1 action. The two science tags only mean the card may trigger other effects twice.
quote: Playing any card always counts as 1 action. The explanation text only points out that the card comes with 2 science tags and thus may trigger other effects twice.
author: EagleEye80
heading: Research

question: Why does Research have helper text saying it counts as two science tags?
ruling: Research is the only card with duplicate tags, so the helper text is there to avoid people wondering how it works or whether it is a misprint. It really counts as two science tags.
quote: Since no other card has duplicate tags, people are bound to wonder how it works and if it might even be a misprint.
author: Fryxen
heading: Research

question: Does Research count as two cards because of its two science tags?
ruling: No. Research is one card with two science tags; the text only clarifies how two identical tags work.
quote: It was less important to point out that it still obviously was just 1 card (how could anyone interpret it that way?). No conflict.
author: Fryxen
heading: Research

topic: Cards with two tags are not played twice
question: Do cards with two tags count as playing two cards, giving 'when you play a card' discounts (Earth Catapult, Research Outpost) twice or triggering Vitor twice?
ruling: No. Cards are not considered as playing two cards. Tag-based discounts say 'when you play a ... tag', not 'card'. Research's wording only emphasizes that its 2 science tags trigger twice for things like Valley Trust and Mars University.
quote: Cards are not considered as playing two cards.
author: Fryxen
heading: Research

question: Can special tiles be placed on reserved spaces (ocean or city) such as the ones Noctis City or Phobos use?
ruling: Reserved areas are reserved unless a card specifically states the tile can go there. There is no card that places a tile 'anywhere'.
quote: Correct. Reserved areas are reserved, unless a card specifically states it can go there. There is no card that places a tile 'anywhere'.
author: Fryxen
heading: Reserved areas

question: Which board spaces are reserved, and can anything other than oceans go on ocean spaces?
ruling: Noctis City, Phobos Space Haven and Ganymede Colony areas are reserved for the city tiles placed by the cards with those names. Blue areas are reserved for oceans, except that three cards place tiles there: Mohole Area, Protected Valley and Mangrove.
quote: Blue areas are reserved for oceans. However, 3 cards place tiles on blue areas anyway: Mohole Area, Protected Valley, and Mangrove.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Reserved areas

question: Can non-ocean tiles (e.g. Mining Rights) be placed on areas reserved for oceans, and what if all are used?
ruling: Only oceans may be placed on areas reserved for ocean; only three cards specifically allow an exception to this rule (not named in the post). Mining Rights may not be placed on an ocean-reserved area.
quote: The rules say only oceans may be placed on areas reserved for ocean, and only three cards specifically allow exception for this rule (as mentioned above).
author: Fryxen
heading: Reserved areas

question: How many areas are reserved and what can be placed there?
ruling: There are 12 blue areas reserved for oceans and 3 areas reserved for specific cities. No other tiles may be placed there unless specifically stated.
quote: There are 12 blue areas reserved for ocean and 3 areas reserved for specific cities.
author: Fryxen
heading: Reserved areas

topic: Robotic Workforce copies the production box
question: What exactly does Robotic Workforce copy from the targeted building card?
ruling: It copies only the production (brown) box of a building-tagged card, not other effects: copying Strip Mine gives -2 energy production, +2 steel production and +1 titanium production but does not raise oxygen or TR. Decreases in the box are copied too.
quote: As Carsten states, you copy only the brown box on another card.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Robotic Workforce

question: How does Robotic Workforce work on Mining Rights or Mining Area, whose production depends on the tile placement?
ruling: Robotic Workforce gives the same production that Mining Rights/Area originally gave, which depends on where its tile was placed (e.g. a tile on a titanium bonus gives another step of titanium production).
quote: If you use Robotic Workforce on for example Mining Rights, you get the same production that you originally got when playing Mining Rights, and thus depending on where that tile was placed.
author: Fryxen
heading: Robotic Workforce

question: Can Robotic Workforce copy the production box of an already played event card?
ruling: No: there are no building-tagged events, and tags on face-down cards don't count, so even a building event could not be copied.
quote: However, the tags on face-down cards don't count, so even if there were building events, it could not copy those production boxes.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Robotic Workforce

question: When Robotic Workforce duplicates Medical Lab, are the building tags counted at the time Medical Lab was played or at the time of duplicating?
ruling: Valid combo: duplicating the production box recalculates with your current building tags, not those you had when Medical Lab was played. It is probably the most powerful use of Robotic Workforce.
quote: It is a valid combo, and it's probably the most powerful one you can do with Robotic Workforce.
author: EagleEye80
heading: Robotic Workforce

question: Is duplicating Medical Lab's production with Robotic Workforce using your current building tags valid?
ruling: Yes, it is valid.
quote: Yes it is. Robotic Workforce can be very good :)
author: Fryxen
heading: Robotic Workforce

question: Does Robotic Workforce copy Soletta's production, and what triggers Optimal Aerobraking?
ruling: Robotic Workforce only works on cards with a building tag, so it cannot copy Soletta (space tag). Using Optimal Aerobraking with any event, or with any space OR event card, is listed as a misplay too; the card needs a played card that is both a space card and an event (implied).
quote: Yes, and Optimal Aerobraking with any event, or even worse, with any space OR event card.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Robotic Workforce

question: What can Robotic Workforce copy?
ruling: It can only target a card with the building tag and copies only that card's production box (any production decreases stated in the box must also be performed), not other effects. It cannot copy a production box that is part of an action or effect on the upper panel of a blue card; only a production box on the lower panel of a building-tag card.
quote: Can only target a card with the building tag, and it only copies that card's production box, not other effects.
author: Fryxen
heading: Robotic Workforce

topic: Robotic Workforce and action/effect production boxes
question: Can Robotic Workforce copy a production box that is part of an effect or action in the upper panel of a blue card (e.g. Underground Detonations)?
ruling: No. It can only copy a production box on the lower panel of a green or blue card, not production boxes that are part of an effect or action in the upper panel. The FAQ was updated accordingly.
quote: It can not copy production boxes that are part of an effect or action in the upper panel of a blue card; only a production box on the lower panel (on a green or blue card).
author: Fryxen
heading: Robotic Workforce

question: Can Robotic Workforce be used on a non-building card (the poster mentions Thorium Asteroid)?
ruling: No: Robotic Workforce must only be used on a building card (a card with a building tag).
quote: I hope you didn't use Robotic Workforce on Thorium Asteroid, it must only be used on a building card.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Robotic Workforce

topic: Robotic Workforce: which cards and what is copied
question: Can Robotic Workforce copy a blue or green card with a building tag, and what exactly is copied?
ruling: It can copy a blue or green card with a building tag, but only its brown production box (which changes your income, positive or negative), not that card's other advantages.
quote: Yes, but you can also copy the brown production box which changes your income (positive and negative). You don't copy any other advantages of that card.
author: EagleEye80
heading: Robotic Workforce

topic: Robotic Workforce copies the effect, not an amount
question: If Robotic Workforce copies Power Grid, does it copy the original amount or the current amount?
ruling: You copy the effect, not a specific amount. If the effect counts tags and you have more tags when you play Robotic Workforce, the effect is better. It only copies brown boxes and only works on cards with a building tag.
quote: You copy the effect - not a specific amount! If the effect counts tags and you have more tags when you play Robotic Workforce then the effect is better now.
author: EagleEye80
heading: Robotic Workforce

topic: Robotic Workforce target must be performable
question: Can Robotic Workforce target a card whose production decrease you cannot pay (e.g. Strip Mine with energy production 1)?
ruling: No. Card effects have the same requirements as playing cards: you must be able to perform the whole effect, with only 3 exceptions (ignore raising a maxed global parameter, ignore taking resources you can't collect, ignore destruction of resources caused by a red-bordered icon). Production must always be performed.
quote: Card effects have the same requirements and exceptions that playing cards have, so you must be able to perform the whole effect with only 3 exceptions
author: Fryxen
heading: Robotic Workforce

question: How does Robotic Workforce work, for example targeting Domed Crater?
ruling: The targeted card must be yours, in your tableau, and have a building tag. You pay 9 M€ for Robotic Workforce and state which card you target; you then apply only that card's production box (e.g. Domed Crater: energy production -1, M€ production +3). You get no tile placement, plants, or VP from the targeted card and need not meet its requirement.
quote: You do not get to place a city, you do not get the 3 plants, you do not get 1 VP, you do not have to meet the requirement of max 7% oxygen.
author: Isaac Fryxelius
heading: Robotic Workforce

question: When Robotic Workforce targets Mining Area, is the production a free choice or tied to the original tile placement?
ruling: Robotic Workforce copies the production box of the building; Mining Area's production depends on where its tile was placed, so you copy that production (e.g. titanium if it originally gave titanium). When in doubt, thematics is a good judge.
quote: If you choose to target Mining Area, that card's production depends on where the tile was placed, and so you copy that production.
author: Fryxen
heading: Robotic Workforce

topic: Robotic Workforce with Mining Rights / Mining Area
question: What does Robotic Workforce give when copying Mining Rights or Mining Area?
ruling: Robotic Workforce copies the production box, which references the tile placement bonus received from the mining tile placed by that card. If the tile gave a titanium bonus, you get titanium production; it does not place another tile. Even if both mining tiles are out, you reference the tile placed by the targeted card.
quote: If both mining tiles are out, you still reference the particular tile that was placed by the building card targeted by Robotic Workforce.
author: Fryxen
heading: Robotic Workforce

topic: Robotic Workforce needs a production box
question: Can you play Robotic Workforce if you have no building-tag card with a production box?
ruling: No. You can't play it if you can't perform its effect.
quote: Correct. You can't play it if you can't perform it.
author: Fryxen
heading: Robotic Workforce

topic: Robotic Workforce with a two-metal tile
question: On a fan board with an area giving both steel and titanium, does Robotic Workforce copying Mining Rights allow either metal, or must it repeat the earlier choice?
ruling: No official ruling given: official boards never have such an area, and he says only that they will handle the question if it comes up.
quote: we will not sell just any fanbased material, so we'll handle the question if it comes up.
author: Fryxen
heading: Robotic Workforce

question: If the rules do not forbid an action (e.g. placing the Lava Flow volcano on an occupied space), may players do it?
ruling: No: the rules describe every allowed move; players do not decide the rules, and silence is not permission. The official post does not itself answer the Lava Flow occupied-space question.
quote: Seriously, the rules tell you how to play the game, and describes every allowed move.
author: Fryxen
heading: Rules interpretation

question: What does 'including this' mean on Saturn Systems, since a corporation enters play when selected?
ruling: Yes, it is equivalent to starting with +1 MC production: the corporation enters play at the start of the game and its own Jovian tag triggers the increase. Saturn Systems has the best starting production of all the corporations.
quote: Yes. :) Saturn Systems has the best starting production of all the corporations.
author: Fryxen
heading: Saturn Systems

question: What happens to the card revealed by Search For Life: does it stay on top of the deck?
ruling: The revealed card is discarded. The intention is to keep the game free of deck manipulation.
quote: Search For Life discards the revealed card. It is our intention to keep TM clean from deck manipulation
author: Fryxen
heading: Search For Life

question: Is the card revealed by Search for Life put back or discarded?
ruling: It is discarded. The card should have said so; the designers wanted to avoid players knowing about the next card in the deck, which would complicate dealing and cause analysis paralysis.
quote: It is discarded. This should be made clearer in any new edition, though.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Search For Life

question: Where does the revealed Search for Life card go?
ruling: It is discarded; it should say so on the card but this slipped through proof-reading.
quote: It is discarded. It should say so on the card, but apparently this slipped through our proof-reading
author: Fryxen
heading: Search For Life

topic: Search for Life after finding life
question: After a science resource is on Search for Life, must or can you keep searching?
ruling: There is no need to search any more once you have found life: the card scores 3 VP if it has at least one science resource, and the wording was chosen to avoid reading that more resources give more than 3 VP.
quote: We didn't want people to misread that you could get more than 3 VPs. So, no, if you have found life, you don't have to search anymore...
author: EagleEye80
heading: Search For Life

question: What happens to the card revealed by Search for Life?
ruling: The revealed card is discarded.
quote: Search For Life: The revealed card is discarded.
author: Fryxen
heading: Search For Life

question: What is the correct text of Search For Life's action?
ruling: Erratum for the 1st edition: it should read 'Reveal and discard...'.
quote: Should read: “Reveal and discard...”
author: Fryxen
heading: Search For Life

topic: Search For Life: 3 VP and continued use
question: Why does Search For Life give VP for 'one or more' resources, and can you keep using the action after finding life?
ruling: The card gives either 3 VP or 0 VP; 'one or more' was chosen so nobody thinks more than 3 VP is possible. Because nothing stops the action after finding life, you can keep using it to stall or to collect more resources on cards (e.g. for the Excentric milestone).
quote: The easiest way was just to write 3VPs if you have one or more resource so noone would think you could get more than 3VPs.
author: EagleEye80
heading: Search For Life

question: Do resources on Self-Replicating Robots count as a resource type for Diversity Support?
ruling: No. Resources on Self-Replicating Robots have no type and so do not count for Diversity Support.
quote: They don't have any type, and so don't count for Diversity Support.
author: Fryxen
heading: Self-replicating Robots

question: Is a house rule limiting Sell Patents to once per generation, to stop stalling by selling one card at a time, acceptable?
ruling: No such limit exists in the base rules; he regards selling cards one at a time to stall as a costly but legitimate option. He says he understands the proposed once-per-generation house rule even though he would not use it.
quote: I understand that houserule even if I wouldn't use it myself...
author: EagleEye80
heading: Sell Patents

question: Is selling a card for its play cost instead of 1 MC an acceptable variant?
ruling: Not recommended: the rule is 1 MC per sold card. Selling for the card's cost would unbalance the game (always buy every card, expensive cards worth more thrown away, card-draw cards more valuable). Discarding is not meant as a reward.
quote: I would not recommend this game variant...
author: EagleEye80
heading: Sell Patents

question: How many cards can be sold in one action, and how many actions can you take in a generation?
ruling: One action sells any number of cards, each for 1 MC. The number of turns/actions in a generation is unlimited (you act until you pass).
quote: ...but you do know that you have UNLIMITED number of turns each generation, right? And that it is 1 action to sell any number of cards to get the same number of MC back (=1 per card discarded)?
author: EagleEye80
heading: Sell Patents

question: Which setup options exist besides standard/Corporate Era?
ruling: A player either takes a Beginner Corporation (10 cards free) or chooses between 2 regular corporations while looking at their 10 starting cards. The draft variant drafts the 4 cards of the Research phase and is never applied to the 10 starting cards. Solo is always played with the Corporate Era expansion (all cards, no extra production).
quote: You can play draft variant and draft the 4 cards in the Research Phase (draft is never applied on the 10 starting cards!).
author: EagleEye80
heading: Setup

topic: Setup: choosing starting cards and corporation
question: When do you choose your starting cards relative to your corporation, and when must a Beginner corporation be chosen?
ruling: Choose your starting cards at the same time as you choose your corporation. A Beginner corporation must be chosen before seeing the cards.
quote: Choose your starting cards at the same time as you choose your corporation card (Choosing a Beginner corporation must be done before seeing the cards though).
author: Fryxen
heading: Setup

question: At setup, do you choose a corporation first and only then see your 10 starting cards?
ruling: You are supposed to look at the corporation cards and the 10 starting project cards together and choose your corporation based on what is in your 10 cards. Stated with hedging ("I might be wrong here").
quote: you are supposed to watch both cards and corps together and make your choices from that - normally you would choose corporation based on what is on your 10 cards.
author: Isaac Fryxelius
heading: Setup

question: Who starts the very first game if nobody has played before?
ruling: Any method may be used to determine the starting player (random, age, experience, vote). The rule that the most recent winner starts is just a nice touch.
quote: You can use any method for determining starting player (random/age/experience/vote etc).
author: Fryxen
heading: Setup

question: How should the project deck be shuffled and dealt so that combos or stacked cards do not end up together?
ruling: Shuffle the cards after a game so they do not stay stacked; when dealing, deal one card at a time to each player in turn so stacked cards do not go to the same player (though they may still land in the same draft).
quote: Another way to avoid the problem is to deal cards one at a time, so that all players get their first card before anyone gets the second and so on.
author: Fryxen
heading: Setup

topic: Setup counts as part of generation 1
question: Does the setup count as part of generation 1 even without Prelude (relevant for e.g. Law Suit in generation 1)?
ruling: Yes. Setup is part of generation 1 whether or not Prelude is used; the base rulebook merely presented it separately because no cards depended on it.
quote: Setup is part of generation 1, regardless of if you use Prelude or not.
author: Fryxen
heading: Setup

question: How should a first game of Terraforming Mars be set up (Prelude, Corporate Era, corporations)?
ruling: For a group playing for the first time Fryxen recommends the Beginner Corporations in the standard game without Prelude and without Corporate Era cards: start with 1 production on each production track, everyone gets a Beginner Corporation card and 10 project cards to keep for free. Modules (unique corporations, Corporate Era, drafting, Prelude, TR solo, Hellas & Elysium, Venus Next, World Government Terraforming, Colonies, Turmoil) are added later; a new player can still use a Beginner Corporation while others pick unique corporations.
quote: I'd start with the Beginner Corporations, the standard game and without Prelude (Don't include corporate era cards or anything from Prelude, start with 1 production on each production track. Everyone gets a Beginner Corporation card and 10 project cards to keep for free, and go at it.)
author: Fryxen
heading: Setup

topic: Shortening the game via house rules
question: Can the game length be shortened by lowering global parameter targets?
ruling: House rules are allowed, but changing global parameters upsets card balance since card costs account for requirements. The standard game with starting production is designed as an epic 2-hour game for any player count; if 2-player Corporate Era drags, play the standard game.
quote: Of course you can houserule anything you want, but you should know that messing with global parameters also messes with the balance of the card requirement.
author: EagleEye80
heading: Shortening the game

question: Is there an official variant that shortens the game?
ruling: Suggested variant: at the end of each generation, before the new generation begins and before player order shifts, the current first player chooses 1 global parameter (ocean/oxygen/temperature) that is increased. The first player gets no TR or placement bonuses for this, and any bonus steps on the tracks are ignored.
quote: At the end of each generation, the current first player chooses 1 global parameter (ocean/oxygen/temp) that will be increased. This happens before the new generation begins and before player order shifts.
author: EagleEye80
heading: Shortening the game

question: Was the end-of-generation parameter-increase variant meant for the base game or for an expansion, and can it be used with Corporate Era?
ruling: The variant was intended for a later expansion, to compensate for the added game length expansions bring. There is no reason it cannot be used in a Corporate Era game if it feels too long.
quote: Actually, this variant was intended for an expansion later on. Expansions tend to add time to the game and so we came up with this mechanism to compensate for that.
author: EagleEye80
heading: Shortening the game

topic: Basic game as official shorter game
question: What is the official way to shorten a game?
ruling: The official shorter game is the basic game: start without the Corporate Era cards and with +1 on every production. Prelude was designed to roughly replace that production boost but can be added on top for a really short game.
quote: There is the official way to speed up the game, called the basic game: start without the corporate era cards and with +1 on every production.
author: Fryxen
heading: Shortening the game

question: Which official modular options shorten game time?
ruling: Any combination of: Prelude (fewer generations, about 15 min shorter), WGT / solar phase (fewer generations), Basic game (remove Corporate Era cards and start at +1 production of everything; about 1 h shorter), and not drafting (saves about 30 min). Solar phase was added to offset Venus lengthening play but can be used in any setting.
quote: Basic game (remove Corporate Era cards and start at +1 production of everything): fewer generations, ca 1 h shorter.
author: Fryxen
heading: Shortening the game

question: What is wrong with the printed Small Asteroid promo card?
ruling: There should be a minus before the plant icons (it decreases plants).
quote: Small Asteroid (promo): There should be a minus before the plant icons.
author: Fryxen
heading: Small Asteroid

question: Does Solar Probe's science tag count towards its own card draw?
ruling: Including tags being played is normal, so there is no conflict: the tags on the card being played count (the card is not an exception to the normal rules).
quote: Including tags being played is normal, so there is no conflict here.
author: Fryxen
heading: Solar Probe

question: Which time-saving solo adjustments does Jonathan use?
ruling: Personal preferences, not endorsed officially: take as many actions as you want per generation in solo; allow undo of actions as long as no cards have been drawn (undoing any bonuses they gave); sell back just-bought cards for 3 MC if no new cards were drawn; do not place owner markers except on neutral cities and greeneries. Only after about ten games.
quote: This is my personal preferences, not endorsed officially by FryxGames.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Solo challenges and variants

question: Which advanced time-saving solo adjustments does Jonathan use?
ruling: Personal preferences, not official: buy cards from the last research phase later in the generation only if you never had less than 3 MC to spare (safer: buy all 4 and sell back per the 3 MC rule); instead of taking 8 heat production, raise temperature 1 step right away (only after taking MC income), and likewise plants for greenery/oxygen, undoing them if new cards with requirements were drawn in research.
quote: The following rules can be added if you feel you are in good control of the game.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Solo challenges and variants

question: Is there an official-style solo campaign variant?
ruling: A variant the designers use: play normal rules, but at the start pick 2 corporations you want to choose from (not random) before drawing your 10 starting cards, then choose corporation and cards as normal; corporations you have won with stay in the box. Aim to win with all corporations in as few games as possible.
quote: You play the game following the normal rules. But in the beginning you pick out 2 corporations you want to choose from (you don't draw random!).
author: EagleEye80
heading: Solo challenges and variants

question: Is counting out 52 cards for research phases a good way to track generations in solo?
ruling: Endorsed tip: after setup count out 52 cards and use that stack only for the research phase, drawing all other cards from the rest of the deck; when the stack is gone you have played your 14 generations.
quote: That's a really smart thing to do! I will probably start doing this myself
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Solo challenges and variants

question: What must a solo game use to be a valid highscore game?
ruling: Start with 14 TR instead of 20, 0 starting production of each resource, 2 neutral cities and greeneries, and no drafting variant.
quote: Did you start with 14TR instead of 20, with 0 starting production of each resource, 2 neutral cities and greeneries, and no drafting variant?
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Solo challenges and variants

question: What conditions does a solo game need to meet for the Solo Terraformer Challenge?
ruling: Completed solo game per the written rules: all three tracks finished before the end of the 14th generation, start at 14 TR, 2 neutral cities and greeneries at start, no drafting, no milestones or awards, all Corporate Era cards included, 0 (not 1) production of all 6 resources. Only the Corporate Era expansion may be used (promo cards allowed).
quote: You completed all three terraforming tracks (oxygen, temperature, and oceans) before the end of the 14th generation.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Solo challenges and variants

question: May a player choose which two corporations they are dealt in the Solo Terraformer Challenge?
ruling: Yes. You may select exactly which 2 corporations you choose from at the start of the game, if you select them before revealing the 10 starting cards.
quote: any player may choose their corporations freely if they do so before the 10 starting cards are revealed.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Solo challenges and variants

question: What are the solo game conditions for the Solo Terraformer Challenge?
ruling: Challenge scores require the solo game per the written rules: all three tracks completed before the end of generation 14, start at 14 TR, place 2 neutral cities and greeneries at the start, no drafting variant, no milestones or awards. Only the Corporate Era expansion (and promo cards) may be used.
quote: You started at 14 TR. * You placed 2 neutral cities and greeneries at the start of the game. * You did not use any drafting variant.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Solo challenges and variants

question: What production does a solo Corporate Era challenge game start with?
ruling: The challenge requires including all Corporate Era cards and starting with 0 (not 1) production of all 6 resources.
quote: You included all Corporate Era cards. * You started with 0 - not 1 - production of all 6 resources.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Solo challenges and variants

question: How can you avoid miscounting generations in solo?
ruling: Recommended practice: count out 52 cards (4*13) for the research phases and use them only for research phases (the first generation has no research phase), drawing all other cards from the main deck. When the last of those cards are drawn, you are in the last generation.
quote: please count out 52 cards (4*13) to use for the research phases throughout the game (the first generation has no research phase).
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Solo challenges and variants

question: For the Solo Challenge Breeder and Colonizer milestones, what counts as animals and cities?
ruling: Breeder counts 20 animal tokens (not animal points). Colonizer counts 10 city tiles, including space cities and the capital but not neutral cities.
quote: 20 animal tokens, 10 city tiles (including space cities and capital, but not neutral cities).
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Solo challenges and variants

question: Is the fan solo variant 'Terraform Mars in 12 generations using all 12 corporations' acceptable?
ruling: Endorsed as a fun but hard play mode for experienced players. Variant as posted: solo, 12 generations; after seeing the 10 starting cards pick any of the 12 corporations for the first generation; each following generation pick a new unused corporation, ignoring its starting resources/production/cards but using its passive effect (Saturn Systems still gives its 1 MC production) for that generation only; the game ends after all 12 corporations were used, with the normal final plant production and greenery placement.
quote: I can recommend this play mode to experienced players...
author: EagleEye80
heading: Solo challenges and variants

question: Is there an official solo challenge variant?
ruling: Challenge suggested by EagleEye80: try to win with every one of the 12 corporations in fewer than 20 games; each game you choose which 2 corporations to pick from before looking at your 10 starting cards, and once you win with a corporation you put it back in the box.
quote: In this challange you get to choose which 2 corps you want to pick from - before you look at the 10 starting cards, of course.
author: EagleEye80
heading: Solo challenges and variants

question: Is there a way to score a lost solo game fairly?
ruling: The score is pointless if you lose. If you really want to score a loss, lose about 5 VP for each lacking terraforming step, though the designer does not recommend it as it removes tension.
quote: One thing you could do if you really want to score a loss is for each lacking step of terraforming to lose you 5 VP or so.
author: Fryxen
heading: Solo challenges and variants

question: Do solo players get the extra starting production of the base game?
ruling: No. In solo you are not allowed the extra base-game starting production, even if you play the base game.
quote: In solo, you are not allowed the extra base game production, even if you play the base game.
author: Fryxen
heading: Solo game

topic: Solo game: cards useless in solo
question: Should cards that are useless in solo be removed from the deck?
ruling: No special rule: leave them in the deck and simply do not buy them, so no deck changes or extra rules are needed.
quote: The easiest 'solution' is to just let them be in the deck and be cards that you don't buy.
author: Fryxen
heading: Solo game

question: How is the solo game set up and what is the goal?
ruling: Solo starts with TR 14 and 14 generations to complete terraforming (temperature -30C to +8C, oxygen 0% to 14%, 9 ocean tiles: 42 steps). Two neutral cities are placed, each with one greenery tile, positioned by the cost of 4 randomly drawn cards; these neutral greenery tiles do not raise the oxygen level. Awards and milestones are not used in solo play.
quote: When soloing, 2 neutral cities are placed, with one greenery tile each ... These greenery tiles do not raise the oxygen level. Awards and milestones are not used in solo play.
author: Fryxen
heading: Solo game

question: Can card effects that steal resources or production target someone in the solo game?
ruling: Yes. As a last-minute improvement the solo game has a passive, silent opponent that can be targeted by card effects such as stealing resources or production, so almost all cards work in solo.
quote: you now have a passive, silent opponent that can be targeted by card effects such as stealing resources or production.
author: EagleEye80
heading: Solo game

question: Must Corporate Era cards and corporations be included in the solo game?
ruling: Yes. The Corporate Era cards (including corporations) should be added in the solo version; the solo game is balanced with them.
quote: Yes, the CE cards (including corps) should be added in the solo version.
author: Fryxen
heading: Solo game

question: In the solo game, do you set production to 0 and do corporations still give their production and resources?
ruling: Starting without the standard game's extra production is part of playing Corporate Era, not the standard game. All corporation effects, tags, resources and production remain valid in solo, and a Beginner Corporation can be used in solo (not weaker than unique corporations, just simpler). So start at 0 production plus whatever the corporation gives.
quote: Starting without extra production is an included feature of playing Corporate Era as opposed to playing the standard game (without CE). All corporation effects, tags, resources and production are still valid in the solo game.
author: Fryxen
heading: Solo game

question: What counts as a valid win for the 2016 Solo Highscore list?
ruling: Only wins count: completing terraforming before the end of the 14th generation with the base game plus Corporate Era cards; promo cards are allowed, but not (prototype) expansions.
quote: Only submit your score if you won the solo game (that is, completed terraforming before the end of the 14th generation) with the base game + Corporate Era cards. Promo cards are allowed, but no expansions (prototypes).
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Solo game

question: What starting resources and production does the neutral opponent have in solo, and how do steal/decrease effects work?
ruling: The abstract neutral opponent has endless production and resources to steal or reduce. The rule exists so that more cards can be played in solo, since otherwise cards could not be played because all effects must be performed.
quote: The abstract opponent have endless production and resources to steal or reduce.
author: EagleEye80
heading: Solo game

question: Is there a way to finish the solo game early if all parameters are done by generation 13?
ruling: No. You always play 14 generations in solo; with 1 generation left you use it to get as many points as possible.
quote: You always play 14 generations in the solo game. If you have 1 generation left, you use it to get as many points as possible.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Solo game

question: In solo, should you wait to max the parameters until generation 14?
ruling: No need to wait: per rulebook page 13 you ALWAYS play 14 generations in solo, even if all global parameters are maxed out earlier, and can spend the last turns only on points.
quote: Patrick, as seen on page 13 of the rulebook, you ALWAYS play 14 generations in solo, even if all global parameters are maxed out before then.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Solo game

question: What is the point of the neutral cities and greeneries in solo setup?
ruling: The random placement of the neutral cities makes the map options different between plays, and they remind you that you have an imaginary opponent you can target with your cards.
quote: The random placement of the neutral cities ensures that the options on the map is different between plays.
author: EagleEye80
heading: Solo game

question: In solo, can you score points from the neutral player's cities?
ruling: No: neutral cities score for the neutral player, not you. Placing your own cities next to neutral greeneries does increase your own city's worth.
quote: You cannot get points for the neutral cities, because they would score points for the neutral player, not you.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Solo game

question: How many generations does the (base) solo game last?
ruling: 14 generations (rounds are called generations).
quote: Except it is 14 rounds (called generations, that's how epic this is)
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Solo game

question: Do neutral cities and greeneries count as the player's own in solo?
ruling: Implied no: the neutral cities and greeneries are not the player's and must not be counted as yours when scoring.
quote: I can't see the neutral cities and greeneries in this picture. You didn't count them as yours, did you? ;)
author: Fryxen
heading: Solo game

question: What are the solo game startup rules?
ruling: The solo startup is: no starting production of any resource (only what the corporation gives) and only 14 TR.
quote: are you sure you are playing by the solo game startup rules (no starting production of any resource, and only 14 TR)?
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Solo game

question: What starting production applies in solo with a beginner corporation?
ruling: Solo always uses Corporate Era, so you start without base production, except for production granted by your corporation; a Beginner Corporation does not change this.
quote: For solo, you always use Corporate Era, and thus always start the solo version without production
author: Fryxen
heading: Solo game

question: Is solo played with Corporate Era, and what is base production?
ruling: Solo play is always played with Corporate Era, so basic production is 0.
quote: Solo play is always played with Corporate Era, so basic production is 0.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Solo game

question: Can all cards be played in the solo game, including cards that target an opponent?
ruling: Yes, all cards can be played in solo. Virus, Land Claim and Sabotage are mostly useless there (their effects are pointless without opponents) unless combined with cards such as Interplanetary Cinematics and Media Group.
quote: Yes, all cards can be played.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Solo game

question: What production does the solo player start with, and may a corporation be chosen after seeing the starting cards in the solo campaign variant?
ruling: In solo you start with no production except what is on your corporation. In the campaign variant, choosing a corporation to fit your starting hand would make it much easier, so the corporations are picked before drawing.
quote: Don't forget that you start with all cards and no production in solo - only what's on your corporation.
author: EagleEye80
heading: Solo game

question: What does 'start with all cards and no production in solo' mean?
ruling: In solo you play with all the cards in the box, including Corporate Era, and you do not start with the extra +1 production of each resource that the basic-game setup describes.
quote: I meant that you always play solo-game with all the cards in the box, including Corporate Era, and that you don't start with the extra production of each reasource described in setup for the basic game.
author: EagleEye80
heading: Solo game

question: Is there an official solo variant for the standard game without Corporate Era?
ruling: No. The official solo variant is only for Corporate Era, because a solo game with only the standard cards would be one-dimensional.
quote: The reason for only having a solo version with Corporate Era is that the standard game basically is all about terraforming
author: Fryxen
heading: Solo game

question: Can the solo game be played without Corporate Era?
ruling: No. The solo game is only defined for Corporate Era; there is no official solo version without it (one comparable version for scores, more strategy, and theme in place of milestones and awards).
quote: Solo game is only defined for Corporate Era. There is no solo version without it, for several reasons.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Solo game

topic: Solo setup: Indentured Workers as neutral tile placement card
question: In solo setup, what if the revealed card for placing neutral tiles has cost 0 (Indentured Workers)?
ruling: Lord_Aethan would draw another card. Treating 0 as an illegal placement and moving on to 1 is closest to the rules in his view, but he says it is not an obvious reading.
quote: I would tend to treat 0 as an illegal placement, moving on to the next, which is 1. This is in no way an obvious way to do it, though, which is why I always draw a new card instead.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Solo game

question: How should a 0-cost card be handled when placing neutral tiles in solo setup?
ruling: It does not matter much how you resolve it. The neutral cities and greeneries exist to vary the map setup so tiles are not always placed in the same favourite places, and to make cards such as Tharsis Republic, Zeppelins and Martian Rails more viable in solo.
quote: Because the exact placement is not actually important, I doesn't really matter how you resolve it.
author: Fryxen
heading: Solo game

question: Which variant and setup does solo play use?
ruling: Solo always uses the Corporate Era variant (CE cards added, 0 production plus what the corporation gives); no Beginner Corporations or draft. Setup: randomly place 2 neutral cities and greeneries, and Terraform rating starts at 14 instead of 20.
quote: Solo play always uses the CE variant, so the CE cards are added to the game, and you start with 0 production, plus what the chosen corporation gives you.
author: Fryxen
heading: Solo game

question: When does a solo game end and when is it scored?
ruling: The game ends after 14 full generations. To win you must finish the terraforming before the extra round of converting plants into greenery tiles. Only games you win are scored (after the extra placement of greenery tiles).
quote: The game ends after 14 full generations. In order to win you must finish the terraforming before the extra round of converting plants into greenery tiles.
author: Fryxen
heading: Solo game

question: What is the starting production when playing solo without Corporate Era?
ruling: There is no official solo variant without Corporate Era; players must make their own rules. A solo game played with +1 starting production and without CE cannot have its score posted on the highscore lists.
quote: There is no solo variant without CE. If you would play solo with +1 production and without CE anyway, you cannot post scores on the highscore lists!
author: EagleEye80
heading: Solo game

question: Is drafting allowed in the solo game?
ruling: Drafting in solo is not officially allowed since it makes the game easier and gives higher scores. It could be fun to do unofficially.
quote: It's not officially allowed since it makes the game easier and thus gives higher scores. Could be fun to do unofficially though, even if it takes away some of the challenge.
author: Fryxen
heading: Solo game

question: In the solo setup, does the initial placement of greenery/city tiles raise the oxygen level or TR?
ruling: Confirmed: the initial solo placement is only there to add variation because of the static map, so it does not increase the oxygen level or TR. It also affects Tharsis Republic and makes city-dependent cards more playable in solo.
quote: Yes, variation is needed because of the static map, forcing players to adjust their tile laying from game to game.
author: Fryxen
heading: Solo game

question: In solo play, where do resources come from when a card says to steal from the neutral opponent?
ruling: From the bank. The neutral player exists so (almost) all cards are playable in solo: cards work as in multiplayer, but instead of removing resources or lowering production from a player, it is taken from the bank.
quote: The cards work just as they would in multiplayer, but instead of removing resources (or lowering production) from a player, this is taken from the bank instead.
author: EagleEye80
heading: Solo game

question: In solo, do you gain resources when a card says 'remove' rather than 'steal'?
ruling: Confirmed: only 'steal' cards let you take resources from the neutral player (from the bank). Removing resources or production from another player has no effect at all in solo.
quote: Exactly. Removing would have no effect at all in solo...
author: EagleEye80
heading: Solo game

topic: Solo neutral city and greenery placement
question: In solo setup, what if the card revealed for placing a neutral tile has cost 0 (e.g. Indentured Workers)?
ruling: The system is just a way to place neutral cities and greeneries randomly. If you draw the only 0 cost card, solve it as you like (redraw or go back one step). The important point is that placement is random and not chosen by the player.
quote: The important thing is that the setup is random and not decided by the player.
author: EagleEye80
heading: Solo game

question: What are the solo game rules and how do variants apply?
ruling: Solo is always Corporate Era: start with 0 production and CE cards, TR 14, fully terraform Mars in 14 generations. Draft may not be used; Hellas & Elysium may be used normally; the expansion corps rule may be used.
quote: The solo game is ALWAYS Corporate Era, so you always begin with 0 production and include the Corporate Era cards. Fully terraform Mars in 14 generations, starting with a TR of 14.
author: Fryxen
heading: Solo game

question: How long is a solo game and what happens if terraforming is not completed?
ruling: The solo game is always 14 generations (12 with Prelude). Terraforming must be completed in that time; if not, you have failed and get no score. If you succeed, continue with final scoring.
