quote: The solo game is always 14 generations (or 12 if you play with the Prelude expansion). In that time, you need to complete the terraforming. If you don't, you've failed and don't get a score at all.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Solo game

question: In solo, can a player win by placing greeneries after the last generation to complete the oxygen parameter?
ruling: No. Win conditions are checked before the final greenery conversion.
quote: Win conditions are checked before final greenery conversion, so no.
author: Fryxen
heading: Solo game

question: How should the solo 'neutral player' and neutral delegates be understood?
ruling: The neutral player represents every faction and power outside the played corporations (World Government, unplayed corporations, political entities, civilians) and is treated as one neutral player with limited, automated actions. Neutral delegates do not necessarily thematically belong to one single player.
quote: The 'neutral player' represents every faction and power outside the currently played corporations.
author: Fryxen
heading: Solo game

topic: Solo setup tile placement by card cost
question: In the solo setup the first revealed project's cost is counted onto the board; what if that cost is 0 or counts off the board?
ruling: The rulebook deliberately omits these rare scenarios; exactly how it is handled does not matter much because the point is just randomness. He personally redraws if the card gives 0 or too high a number.
quote: We opted for less text in the rulebook, even if it omits a couple of rare scenarios. Personally, I just redraw if the card gives me a 0 or too high a number.
author: Fryxen
heading: Solo game

topic: Solo mode: milestones, awards and card exclusion
question: Why does the solo mode have no milestones/awards and no list of cards to exclude?
ruling: By design: milestones and awards are interactive and do not make sense without an opponent, and no list of cards to exclude was added to keep setup short and switching between solo and multiplayer easy.
quote: We didn't include milestones and awards since these are mainly interactive and don't make much sense without an opponent.
author: Fryxen
heading: Solo game

question: May a solo player remove cards that do little in solo (Virus, Toll Station, Land Claim, Sabotage, Protected Habitats)?
ruling: Yes, you can remove them, but he sees little point: there is no official list, and the cards can still be useful in rare cases (e.g. events with rebates).
quote: So, yes, you can remove those cards, but I don't actually see much point in doing it.
author: Fryxen
heading: Solo game

question: Is there an official VP-based solo variant, and does the official solo only care about terraforming?
ruling: There is no official VP-based solo variant. The Prelude expansion adds a TR solo variant where the aim is 63 TR. The official solo game includes scoring, so the goal is to succeed at terraforming while getting a good score.
quote: There is no official VP variant. There is a TR variant from Prelude though, where you aim for 63 TR, making a few more cards viable. The official solo includes scoring
author: Fryxen
heading: Solo game

question: What are the recommended solo-game setup rules without the Automa?
ruling: Always start at 14 TR; always 12 generations if using preludes; always -2 MC production if using Colonies; always use World Government Terraforming if using Venus Next, in which case terraforming all also includes the Venus scale. Use any promos you like.
quote: Always start at 14 TR. Always 12 generations if using preludes. Always -2 MC production if using Colonies. Always use World Government Terraforming if using Venus Next.
author: Fryxen
heading: Solo game

question: What goal and which maps are valid in the solo game?
ruling: Choose either terraform all parameters or reach TR 63 (Jacob prefers TR63). Any map may be used except Amazonis Planitia.
quote: Choose: Terraform all or TR63. ... Choose: any map except Amazonis Planitia.
author: Fryxen
heading: Solo game

question: Can you discard 0 cards for an effect that lets you discard cards?
ruling: No. It is impossible to discard 0 cards: if no card leaves your hand to the discard pile, you are not discarding.
quote: it is impossible to discard 0 cards. If no card leaves your hand to the discard pile, you're not discarding.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Spending or discarding zero

question: Is there a difference between 'pay' and 'spend', and can you pay or spend zero?
ruling: There is no in-game difference between 'pay' and 'spend'. Paying or spending zero is not paying or spending; thematically you cannot pay zero. Allowed exceptions like spending 8 heat at maxed temperature or using Symbiotic Fungus without taking the microbe are accepted despite this.
quote: There is no in-game difference between 'pay' and 'spend'.
author: Fryxen
heading: Spending or discarding zero

question: Can 'X' in 'spend any number of' actions (e.g. Power Infrastructure) be zero?
ruling: No. X is always a positive number. A determined effect with a count (such as 'pay 1 per Z', Insects without plant tags, or Turmoil payouts) may evaluate to zero.
quote: So, to summarize, 'X' is always a positive number.
author: Fryxen
heading: Spending or discarding zero

question: Can Sponsored Academies be played when you have no other card in hand to discard?
ruling: No. You must be able to perform the whole effect (discard a card, then draw 3 and opponents draw 1), so Sponsored Academies cannot be played as your last card.
quote: And if you can't perform the effect, then you can't play the card. So you can't play Sponsored Academies as your last card.
author: Fryxen
heading: Sponsored Academies

topic: Basic game structure: starting production and actions per turn
question: Which beta-test suggestions made it into the final rules about starting production and turn structure?
ruling: In the final rules, in the basic game all players start with 1 production of all 6 resources, and during the Action Phase players take turns doing 1 or 2 actions at a time until all players have passed.
quote: 1. In basic game, all players start with 1 production of all 6 different resources. 2. During Action Phase, the players take turns doing 1 or 2 actions at a time, until all players have passed.
author: EagleEye80
heading: Standard game and Corporate Era

question: Is a corporation's starting production added to the standard game's 1 production of each resource or instead of it?
ruling: Added. The extra production in the basic game is added to whatever start bonuses the corporation gives (Thorgate starts with 2 energy production). It is used only in the basic game (not solo and not with Corporate Era).
quote: Yes, the extra production in the basic game is [b]added[/b] to whatever start bonuses your corporation might have. In this case Thorgate starts with 2 energy production.
author: EagleEye80
heading: Standard game and Corporate Era

topic: Starting production in standard vs Corporate Era game
question: Does the starting 1 production of each resource depend on beginner corporations or on the game version?
ruling: The 1 production of each resource at start belongs to the standard game (without Corporate Era cards), not to beginner corporations. A beginner corporation can be played with Corporate Era (no starting production), and a regular corporation in the standard game gets 1 production of each plus its own bonuses.
quote: the starting production of 1 for each resource is connected to the standard game (i.e. not using the Corporate Era version).
author: Fryxen
heading: Standard game and Corporate Era

topic: Basic vs extended game, corporation choice
question: How do the basic game and Corporate Era game differ in starting production, and can beginner and normal corporations be mixed?
ruling: Basic (short) game: no Corporate Era cards, everyone starts with 1 extra production of each resource, plus corporation bonuses (Thorgate gets 1+1 energy production). Extended game (Corporate Era): all cards, no extra production beyond corporation bonuses. Either corporation type can be used in both, and beginner and normal corporations can be mixed between players.
quote: Basic game (short game): Play without the CE-cards and everybody starts with 1 (extra) production of each resource.
author: EagleEye80
heading: Standard game and Corporate Era

question: Is the 1 production of each resource linked to the Beginner Corporation?
ruling: No. It is linked to the standard game; in every game either all players have it or none. The Beginner Corporation's advantage is lots of money and not having to choose which cards to keep.
quote: The 1 production per resource is NOT linked to the Beginner Corporation, but to the STANDARD GAME. In every game, either all players have it or none.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Standard game and Corporate Era

question: What production do players start with in the standard game versus the Corporate Era?
ruling: All players, whatever corporation, start with 1 production of each resource in the standard game (without Corporate Era cards) and with 0 production of each resource in a Corporate Era game. Then the corporation card's starting production is added.
quote: ALL players, no matter what corporation they are playing, start with 1 production of each resource in the standard game (WITHOUT corporate era cards), and ALL players start with 0 production of resources in a Corporate Era game.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Standard game and Corporate Era

question: In the standard game, does Thorgate start with 2 energy production and Helion with 4 heat production?
ruling: Yes: the default 1 production is added to the corporation's, so Thorgate starts with a total of 2 energy production and Helion with 4 heat production.
quote: Yes, that is correct :)
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Standard game and Corporate Era

question: How do the standard game and the Corporate Era expansion differ in starting production?
ruling: Standard game: start with 1 extra production of everything plus corporation starting bonuses. Corporate Era (extended game): no extra production (only corporation bonuses) and all CE cards (red triangle) are added. This applies to all players regardless of whether they use the Beginner Corporation or a regular one.
quote: Playing with or without extra production affects all players, no matter if they play with Beginner corporation or (regular) corporation!
author: EagleEye80
heading: Standard game and Corporate Era

topic: Standard game vs Corporate Era setup
question: What is the difference in setup between the Standard Game and the Corporate Era Game?
ruling: Standard Game: start with 1 production of each resource plus whatever the corporation gives, and remove all Corporate Era cards from the deck. Corporate Era Game: start with 0 production of each resource plus the corporation's, and add all Corporate Era cards to the deck. The standard game is the shorter one. (The second question, whether cities always give 1 income production, was not answered.)
quote: Standard Game: You start with 1 production of each resource, adding whatever you get from your corporation card. Remove all Corporate Era cards from the deck. [...] Corporate Era Game: You start with 0 production of each resource
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Standard game and Corporate Era

question: Which setup is the 'real' Terraforming Mars: standard or Corporate Era?
ruling: The intended game is Corporate Era without drafting. The standard game is a shorter, more focused variant (hence its arbitrary 1 production of each resource); drafting was added for control, combos and interaction but adds game time and the designer usually prefers playing without it.
quote: Actually, it's Corporate Era without drafting.
author: Fryxen
heading: Standard game and Corporate Era

question: Does choosing normal corporations mean you must use Corporate Era (0 production and extra cards)?
ruling: No. Corporate Era is unrelated to the choice of normal or beginner corporations. Regardless of corporations, you choose either the basic game (basic deck, 1 production of each) or Corporate Era (shuffle basic and CE cards together, start without extra production). Players with beginner and normal corporations can be mixed.
quote: Corporate Era has no connection to the choice of normal corporations or beginner corporations.
author: EagleEye80
heading: Standard game and Corporate Era

question: What is the difference between the standard game and the Corporate Era variant?
ruling: The standard variant does not use Corporate Era [CE] cards and players start with 1 production of each resource plus what the corporation gives. The Corporate Era variant adds all [CE] corporations and project cards and players start with 0 production of each resource plus what the corporation gives.
quote: The Corporate Era (CE) variant adds all [CE] corporations and project cards to the game, and players start with 0 production of each resource, plus what the chosen corporation gives.
author: Fryxen
heading: Standard game and Corporate Era

question: Is the +1 production of each resource that players start with separate from the production a corporation gives?
ruling: Yes. The 1 production of each resource every player starts with is in addition to whatever the corporation gives, which is why the rulebook calls it 'extra'. Whether you start with it matters for balance (e.g. everyone having titanium or energy production at the start weakens Phobolog and Thorgate).
quote: This is the reason that we emphasize that the +1 production is [b]extra[/b], so people understand that whatever their corps are giving them is added on top of this.
author: EagleEye80
heading: Standard game and Corporate Era

question: Is starting with 1 production of each resource combined with Corporate Era cards an official variant?
ruling: The +1 starting production in the standard (non-Corporate Era) base game is there to speed things up. Using +1 starting production with a Corporate Era game is not an official variant.
quote: It works the same when you use +1 production in the base game or with a CE game (which is not an official variant).
author: EagleEye80
heading: Standard game and Corporate Era

topic: Standard game vs Corporate Era card selection
question: Why are some cards marked Corporate Era and which cards stay in the standard game?
ruling: The standard game is built to need as few actions as possible to make the 42 terraforming steps, so cards that neither terraform nor give heat/plant production were moved to Corporate Era. Cards kept in the standard game include the city block, most cards with global requirements (animals and many bio cards but not Tardigrades), a few steel/titanium and Jovian cards, energy production, and enough cards so all awards and milestones are playable.
quote: The CE cards were separated mostly on the principle that terraforming the necessary 42 steps should take as few actions as possible, because game length is primarily dependent on the number of actions taken.
author: Fryxen
heading: Standard game and Corporate Era

question: What starting production applies in the standard game, Corporate Era and solo (e.g. for Helion)?
ruling: Confirmed: the standard game starts all six productions at 1 (Beginner and other corporations), so Helion has heat production 1+3 and the other productions at 1; the Corporate Era game and solo start with no production except what the corporation provides, and Beginner Corporation gets none in Corporate Era.
quote: Yes, if you change "energy" for "heat" on the Helion example, your examples are correct.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Standard game and Corporate Era

question: What do the standard game and Corporate Era mean, and can they be combined with other variants?
ruling: Standard game (rulebook default): +1 production of all 6 resources and Corporate Era cards excluded; it can be combined with any official variant or expansion, though always including Corporate Era is recommended because the game is balanced around it. Corporate Era: 0 starting production and Corporate Era cards included.
quote: Corporate Era. 0 starting production instead of +1, and the Corporate Era cards are included.
author: Fryxen
heading: Standard game and Corporate Era

question: Is the standard game's +1 production of each resource related to Beginner Corporations, and may a beginner (10 free cards) and an experienced player (choose 10 cards, pay 3 MC each, pick one of 2 corporations) mix in one game?
ruling: Starting with 1 production of each resource is tied to playing the standard game without the Corporate Era cards, not to using Beginner Corporations. Mixing is confirmed: the beginner gets the Beginner Corporation with 10 free cards, the experienced player chooses cards and a corporation of 2 and pays for the cards kept.
quote: 1) Starting with +1 production is coupled to playing the standard game without the Corporate Era cards as well. It has nothing to do with using Beginner Corporations.
author: Fryxen
heading: Standard game and Corporate Era

question: How do you choose between a Corporate Era game and a standard game and what production do players start with?
ruling: Corporate Era means every player starts at 0 production and the CE cards and corporations are mixed in. A standard game means production starts at 1 for every resource and the CE cards are not in the game.
quote: Corporate Era means every player starts their board at 0 production and the CE cards and corporations are mixed in. Standard game means that productions start at 1 and that the CE cards are not in the game.
author: Fryxen
heading: Standard game and Corporate Era

question: What differs between the basic (standard) game and Corporate Era, and how does Prelude relate?
ruling: The basic game removes the Corporate Era cards and adds +1 of each production. Prelude was designed to replace the extra production part of the basic game and make it more interesting. Beginner corporations are something else: purely a way to introduce first-timers, with any combination of variants or expansions.
quote: the basic game removes the CE cards but also adds +1 of each production.
author: Fryxen
heading: Standard game and Corporate Era

question: Why does the standard game have fewer cards than Corporate Era?
ruling: The standard game was designed as a shorter variant: initial production added to cut generations, and cards not directly related to moving the parameters (Earth, Jovian, science, steel, titanium strategies, complex cards such as Viral Enhancers and Robotic Workforce) were scaled back to cut actions. Animals were kept for their relevance to the parameters. The original design included Corporate Era.
quote: The original design included corporate era, but we needed a shorter variant for people to get into the game more easily.
author: Fryxen
heading: Standard game and Corporate Era

question: Why is the non-Corporate-Era game presented as the default/standard game?
ruling: The standard game is meant as a quick, easy way in, especially when learning, so it is the default; otherwise many would start with Corporate Era and have an overly long first game. The same reasoning applies to Beginner Corporations; experienced players can skip both.
quote: Since the standard game is meant to give everyone a quick and easy way into the game (especially when learning), we wanted it as the default.
author: Fryxen
heading: Standard game and Corporate Era

question: Where does the +1 MC production of the City standard project come from?
ruling: Page 10 of the rulebook: for 25 M€ the City standard project places a city tile (collecting placement bonus, with a player marker) and increases M€ production 1 step; the icon is on the game board's standard projects panel.
quote: 6) City: For 25 M€ you get to place a city tile (collect any placement bonus for the tile, and place a player marker on it). You also get to increase your M€ production 1 step.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Standard projects

question: Do standard projects share a generic city effect with cards that place cities?
ruling: No. Standard projects are effects of their own, like simple cards you can play over and over, and do not affect other card effects. What all city tiles share is that they can't be adjacent to other cities (unless a card says otherwise) and score 1 VP per adjacent greenery.
quote: You should treat the standard projects as if they were simple cards that you can play over and over again. They do not affect other card effects in any way.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Standard projects

question: Does placing a city tile from a card increase M€ production by 1 like the City standard project does?
ruling: No. You get no extra M€ production for placing a city tile; the +1 M€ production comes from performing the 'City' standard project. The 'see page 5' reference in the rulebook is misplaced.
quote: You do not get any extra M€ production for placing a city tile - you get it from performing the 'standard action city'.
author: Isaac Fryxelius
heading: Standard projects

question: Can standard projects printed on the board be used several times per generation?
ruling: Yes, standard projects printed on the board may be used several times. The post cites spending 8 heat to raise temperature as an example, but the same author's next post says standard projects are only the actions printed on the board.
quote: Standard projects (printed on the board) may be used several times, for example spending 8 heat to raise temperature if possible (and get TR).
author: EagleEye80
heading: Standard projects

question: Do cities placed by cards give the extra MC production that the City standard project gives?
ruling: No. The extra MC production is only for building a city as the standard project (action), not for cities from cards.
quote: The extra MC-production for doing the standard action city is only for building a city as a standard action. You DONT get extra MC-production for building cities from cards.
author: EagleEye80
heading: Standard projects

topic: City standard project without legal placement
question: Can MC be spent on the City standard project when there are no legal placements left?
ruling: No. The City standard project cannot be used when there is no legal space to place the city.
quote: Not if there are no more legal placements.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Standard projects

question: Can you use the City standard project for the income if you cannot place the tile?
ruling: No. You cannot do a standard city project if you cannot place the tile.
quote: You can not do a standard city to get the income if you can't place the tile.
author: Fryxen
heading: Standard projects

topic: Aquifer standard project with oceans maxed
question: Can you pay for the Aquifer standard project when all oceans are placed?
ruling: Yes, you can pay 18 for the standard Aquifer even if oceans are maxed, but you get nothing.
quote: You can pay 18 for a standard Aquifer even if ocean is maxed, but you get nothing.
author: Fryxen
heading: Standard projects

topic: Standard project city: +1 M€ production only for the standard project
question: Do cards that place a city also give the +1 M€ production the city standard project gives?
ruling: No. The +1 M€ production is not a general rule for placing cities; it only happens when you use the standard project to place a city. For a card that places a city, read the card effect.
quote: Getting +1 MC production is not a general rule for placing cities - it's just an effect that happens when you use the STANDARD PROJECT to place a city!
author: EagleEye80
heading: Standard projects

topic: Standard project city with no legal tile placement
question: Can you pay for the city standard project just to raise M€ production when no city can be placed?
ruling: No. Effects on cards, standard projects, card actions etc. are mandatory except maxed global parameters, resources you can't collect, and opposing resources. There is no exception for tiles other than maxed ocean tiles.
quote: Effects on cards, standard Projects, card actions etc. are mandatory, except for * maxed global parameters, * resources you can't collect, and * opposing resources. No exception for tiles other than maxed ocean tiles.
author: Fryxen
heading: Standard projects

topic: Standard projects follow the same sequence as card play
question: When are standard project effects resolved, and when is a standard project considered played (relevant to Thorgate's discount)?
ruling: Standard projects work like every other action: check requirements, pay the cost, then perform the effects and triggered effects in any order. The same applies to converting plants, claiming a milestone, or using a blue card action. A standard project, like a card, is not considered played until paid for.
quote: all actions work the same way: Check the requirements, pay the cost (if any), and perform the effects and triggered effects in any order.
author: Fryxen
heading: Standard projects

question: Does Standard Technology refund actions such as spending 8 heat or 8 plants, or blue card actions?
ruling: Standard projects are only the actions printed on the board, so Standard Technology gives no refund for blue card actions. Asked whether spending 8 heat or 8 plants triggers it, Enoch answered only with that definition and did not name heat or plants.
quote: Standard projects are only the actions printed on the board. It would be really crazy if "Standard Technology" would give you refunds for actions on blue cards too!!
author: EagleEye80
heading: Standard Technology

question: Can you use Steelworks when oxygen is maxed?
ruling: Yes; you ignore the oxygen part and get the steel.
quote: So you can use Steelworks even if the O2 is maxed out; you just ignore that part and get the steel.
author: Fryxen
heading: Steelworks

question: Can the Steelworks action be used if oxygen is maxed?
ruling: Yes, to get the 2 steel for 4 energy.
quote: And actions such as the one on Steelworks can be used even if oxygen is maxed out, just to get the 2 steel for 4 energy.
author: Fryxen
heading: Steelworks

question: Which null actions are allowed for stalling?
ruling: Symbiotic Fungus can be used to stall since adding microbes is one of the three exceptions, and raising a maxed temperature by spending 8 heat can also stall for the same reason.
quote: Symbiotic fungus can stall since adding microbes is one of the 3 exceptions.
author: Fryxen
heading: Symbiotic Fungus

question: When do tags (including those on corporations) count?
ruling: Tags count for card effects based on existing tags (examples given: Satellites, Medical Lab, Cartel, Miranda Resort), for card tag requirements (usually science), and for the Builder milestone and Scientist award.
quote: Some cards have effects based on existing tags. That's when they count. Examples: satellites, medical lab, cartel, Miranda resort.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Tags

question: If you play Advanced Ecosystems (animal, plant and microbe tags) with Decomposers in play, do you add 3 microbes?
ruling: Yes. Each tag is counted separately: effects trigger on playing a tag, not a card, and one card with several tags plays each tag.
quote: Each tag is indeed counted separately, that is why refer to playing a tag instead of playing a card
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Tags

question: Do tags have rules of their own, and are there steel or titanium tags?
ruling: Tags (round icons except oxygen) are keywords with no rules of their own; they only matter when referenced by other effects. There are no steel or titanium tags: the building tag lets steel pay for part or all of a card (each steel substitutes 2 MC) and the space tag likewise for titanium. Resources are square icons, tags round, tiles hexagon, red-bordered resources can affect any player, and a brown box means production.
quote: Tags have NO RULES applied to them. They do nothing on their own. They are only referenced by other effects.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Tags

question: What does a card with a Microbe tag let you do; do tags have rules?
ruling: Tags have no rules applied to them; they are thematic keywords that other cards or effects (or the player board, e.g. steel for building tags) may reference. A Microbe tag does not let you pay with microbes.
quote: Tags have no rules at all applied to them. That's why you won't find anything about them in the rulebook.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Tags

question: When a card has several matching tags (Advanced Ecosystems with GMO Contract; Research with Valley Trust), does each tag trigger the effect?
ruling: Yes. Each tag triggers the effect and effects are generally cumulative: Valley Trust plays Research for 4 MC less, and Advanced Ecosystems with Viral Enhancers in play gives 3 plants (so GMO Contract would give 2 MC per tag).
quote: Each tag triggers the effect, and effects are generally cumulative, so that Valley Trust can play Research for 4 mc less.
author: Fryxen
heading: Tags

question: Can a wild tag be designated as an event tag?
ruling: Yes. A wild tag can be an event tag or any other valid tag, including Venus if playing with Venus Next. A tag is only valid if at least 1 other card in the deck has it.
quote: Yes, it can be an event tag. Or any other valid tag, including Venus if you play with that. At least 1 ither card in the deck needs to have the tag for it to be valid.
author: Fryxen
heading: Tags

question: Do Media Group and Media Archives work with a wild tag set to the event tag?
ruling: Media Group does not trigger since the tag is not played. Media Archives counts cards in the event pile, not tags, so a wild tag doesn't help it; the event icon was only reused for simplicity.
quote: Media Group doesn't trigger since the tag is not played. Media Archives counts cards in the event pile, not tags since those tags are not in play.
author: Fryxen
heading: Tags

question: Can a wild tag be chosen to be a wild tag, and what is its state if no choice is made?
ruling: No: a wild tag is not itself a tag, so it can't be chosen as a wild tag. If you don't choose anything it counts as no tag, which is also the state it reverts to at the end of each action.
quote: A wild tag is not itself a tag so you can't choose a wild tag to be a wild tag, and if you don't choose anything for it, it counts as no tag.
author: Fryxen
heading: Tags

question: Do tags on event cards trigger effects?
ruling: Yes, all tags on all events can trigger effects when the event is played: building and space tags allow paying with steel/titanium (no building events exist), microbe tags trigger Decomposers and Viral Enhancers, science tags trigger Olympus Conference and Mars University, Earth tags get a discount from Earth Office and Teractor.
quote: All tags on all events can trigger some effect.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Tags on event cards

question: Do the science tags on red event cards count for the end-of-game award for most science tags?
ruling: No. Tags on events only matter when the event is played (combos, discounts, effect triggers); afterwards they do not count.
quote: Tags on events only allow for combos when they are played, discounts and effect triggers.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Tags on event cards

question: Do science tags on a played event count for the Scientist award or science requirements, or trigger Mars University and Olympus Conference?
ruling: Events are turned face down after being played and their tags only apply when being played. They do not count for the Scientist award or science tag requirements, but they do trigger Mars University and Olympus Conference.
quote: So they would not count for the Scientist Award or science tag requirements, but they do trigger Mars University and Olympus Conference.
author: Fryxen
heading: Tags on event cards

question: Does playing an event with a Jovian tag count as putting a Jovian tag into play for Saturn Systems?
ruling: Tags on event cards do not enter play; they are only triggered while the card is being played. Event science tags therefore do not count for requirements or the Scientist award, though they trigger Mars University and Olympus Conference when played. (There are no Jovian events.)
quote: Tags on event cards do not enter play, but are only triggered while playing the card.
author: Fryxen
heading: Tags on event cards

topic: Tags on events and end-game scoring
question: Do tags on played event cards count for tag requirements and end-game scoring?
ruling: No. Tags on events are played, triggering effects at that moment (science tags trigger Olympus Conference and Mars University), but the events never really enter play, so they do not count towards tag requirements or end-game scoring; e.g. Invention Contest's science tag does not count toward the Scientist award.
quote: Tags on events do NOT count for end-game scoring.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Tags on event cards

question: Do tags on event cards count after the event is played?
ruling: Tags on event cards are only active when you play it, not after you have placed it face down, and not even during scoring when potential VPs are considered.
quote: The tags on event cards (red cards) are only active when you play it, not after you've placed it face down. Not even during scoring when their potential VPs are considered.
author: Fryxen
heading: Tags on event cards

question: Do tags on event cards count?
ruling: They are active and may trigger effects while the event is being played, but are not counted afterwards, neither during the game nor at end game scoring (they may still give end game VP if they have a VP icon).
quote: They are active and may trigger effects while being played, but are not counted after this
author: Fryxen
heading: Tags on event cards

topic: Event cards tags and end-game scoring
question: Do tags on event cards count after the event has been played, for example for end-game VP cards such as Jovian-tag scoring?
ruling: Event cards only apply their tags while being played, then are turned face down. Afterwards events are only considered for their own additional VP (or negative VP) in end-game scoring, nothing else, so their tags do not count for tag-based scoring.
quote: Eventcards only apply their tags while being played. Then they are turned face down.
author: EagleEye80
heading: Tags on event cards

topic: Tags on event cards at final scoring
question: Do tags on event cards count at final scoring (e.g. for cards giving VP per Jovian tag, or the Scientist award)?
ruling: No. Tags on event cards do not count during final scoring; e.g. science tags on events do not count towards the Scientist award. There are no Jovian events, and all Jovian cards also have VPs.
quote: tags on event cards do not count during final scoring. Science tags on events (those do exist) do not count towards the Scientist award, for example.
author: Fryxen
heading: Tags on event cards

question: Do the tags of face-down (played) red Event cards count for requirements and end-game scoring?
ruling: No. Event cards are turned face down because they represent something that happened and is not a continuing part of your corporation (its tags, productions and abilities); their tags therefore do not count. The face-down convention has a thematic, not mechanical, origin.
quote: They are face down because they represent something that happened and is not a continuing part of your corporation (represented by its tags, productions, and abilities). Their tags don't count for the exact same reason
author: Fryxen
heading: Tags on event cards

question: Is the event symbol a tag, e.g. for Sagitta and Spire counting tags?
ruling: Yes. The event tag is just like other tags; it happens to be on red cards that go face down in your event pile after being played. Their tags count while the card is being played. Fryxen calls the older ruling bad, at least the part about a wild tag not being able to be an event tag.
quote: The event tag is just like other tags, they just happen to be on red cards that rule that they are placed face down in your event pile after they have been played. Their tags count while the card is being played.
author: Fryxen
heading: Tags on event cards

question: Do tags on played event cards count for requirements such as 'you need 2 science tags'?
ruling: Event cards keep their tags, but those tags are only relevant while the event is being played. Events represent things that happen and are done, unlike ongoing projects. (The answer to later requirement checks is implied: they don't count.)
quote: When you play an event, it is still relevant whether it involves space, microbes, science etc, so they can have those tags, but they are only relevant while playing the card.
author: Fryxen
heading: Tags on event cards

question: How much take-that is in the game and which cards could be removed to reduce it?
ruling: In total 25 of 208 cards can decrease other players' resources or production, half of them targeting plants. Suggested variant: remove all 25 (not recommended), or only the 10 most evil: Deimos Down, Giant Ice Asteroid, Energy Tapping, Heat Trapping, Hackers, Sabotage, Virus, Asteroid Mining Consortium, Great Escarpment Consortium, Power Supply Consortium (maybe also Hired Raiders).
quote: In total, 25 cards can decrease other players' resources or production, out of 208 cards.
author: Fryxen
heading: Take-that cards

question: Can you play without red 'take-that' cards?
ruling: Removing all of them would be a mistake (asteroid and animal categories would disappear). If the take-that is too much, only remove the 10-11 most aggressive cards (the game owner may house-rule it).
quote: I'd suggest first playing the game as it is, and if you still think the take-that is too much, then remove only the 10-11 most evil cards, not more.
author: Fryxen
heading: Take-that cards

question: Is Teractor's discount per Earth tag as the icons suggest or limited by the text?
ruling: No conflict according to the designer: the text is an explanation covering 99% of situations and does not replace the icons.
quote: No conflict. Again, the text is an explanation (that covers 99% of situations) and does not replace the icons.
author: Fryxen
heading: Teractor

question: Does Terralabs Research gain 1 MC whenever you gain a card in hand?
ruling: No; the text applies. The designer agrees that an asterisk is in order, but the corporation ability is always read anyway.
quote: Correct, an asterisk is in order.
author: Fryxen
heading: TerraLabs Research

question: How do corporations that change the cost of buying cards combine?
ruling: Buying cost alterations are modifiers: Terralabs Research makes cards cost -2 to purchase and Polyphemos +2, cancelling out. Fan-made cards with similar effects should follow the same logic.
quote: In the case of buying cost alterations, they are considered modifiers, so Terralabs make cards cost -2 to purchase while Polyphemos make them cost +2, cancelling each other out.
author: Fryxen
heading: TerraLabs Research

topic: Terralabs Research and Polyphemos vs Factorum
question: Do Polyphemos' (and Terralabs Research's) card cost changes apply to Factorum's action that draws a building card?
ruling: No. Terralabs Research and Polyphemos only affect when you buy cards, such as in the research phase and when using Inventors' Guild or Business Network. Factorum's action is not defined as buying, so the cost change does not apply.
quote: Terralabs and Polyphemos only affect when you buy cards, such as during research phase and when using Inventor Guild or Business Network. Factorum's action is not defined as buying, and so it doesn't apply.
author: Fryxen
heading: TerraLabs Research

question: When do you place the city tile that Tharsis Republic gives?
ruling: As your first action in the game (option 3 of: before anyone acts, at start of turn, as your first action). The timing was clarified to placement as the first action so that it follows normal placement rules and triggers Tharsis Republic's effects.
quote: Option 3 is correct.
author: Fryxen
heading: Tharsis Republic

question: Do you pay for the initial Tharsis Republic city and does it trigger the corporation effect?
ruling: No payment: it forces you to place a city tile for free. Normal placement rules apply, so you get the placement bonus, and it triggers the corporation ability, raising MC production 1 step and giving you 3 MC.
quote: it forces you to place a city tile for free. Normal placement rules apply, so get placement bonus as well. Furthermore, this will trigger the ability
author: Fryxen
heading: Tharsis Republic

topic: Tharsis Republic 3 MC for city placement
question: Is Tharsis Republic's 3 MC bonus for placing a city restricted to cities on Mars?
ruling: No. The 3 MC bonus for placing city tiles is not restricted to Mars because the card does not say so.
quote: this 3 MC bonus is NOT restricted to cities on Mars (since it doesn't say so).
author: Fryxen
heading: Tharsis Republic

question: What does the solo game start with and how does Tharsis Republic work?
ruling: The solo version is basically the Corporate Era game: you start with no production on your player board, only what the corporation gives. For Tharsis Republic he thinks the solo rules treat it as a special case: MC production from the 2 neutral cities, so it starts at 2 MC production and gets 1 more when it places its free city on the first turn.
quote: The solo version is basically the Corporate Era expansion game, which means you start with no production on your player board, only what your corporation gives you.
author: EagleEye80
heading: Tharsis Republic

question: Does Tharsis Republic gain both 3 MC and 1 MC production for its own city, including its free first-turn city?
ruling: All effects are cumulative. When any player places a city, Tharsis Republic gets 1 MC production; when Tharsis Republic places a city it gets 3 MC and 1 MC production plus any placement bonuses. Its free first city gives 3 MC and 1 MC production only.
quote: If TRep place a city - he gets 3 MC and 1 MC-prod + any bonuses he got from placing the city in the first place.
author: EagleEye80
heading: Tharsis Republic

topic: Tharsis Republic city via standard project
question: What does Tharsis Republic get from a city built by standard project versus by card?
ruling: Standard project city: the standard project's 1 MC production plus 3 MC and 1 MC production, i.e. 3 MC and 2 MC production; a city card gives the production on the card plus 3 MC and 1 MC production. The extra 1 MC production applies only to the city standard project, not to cities placed by cards.
quote: the extra 1 MC-prod you get for placing a city by a standard project, only applies when building a city by this standard project - not for building cities by cards!
author: EagleEye80
heading: Tharsis Republic

topic: Cities off Mars and Tharsis Republic
question: Why do cities placed off Mars (Ganymede) not trigger some city effects while the owner still gets 3 MC for them?
ruling: Fryxen gives a thematic explanation: the corporation is good at organizing and building cities, but as a republic can only tax the Martian ones. This is left as a thematic quirk; the exact wording of the card effects decides which cities count.
quote: They are good at organizing/building cities, but as a republic can only tax the Martian ones. Those quirks are all thematic and add a little flavor to the game, as well as uniqueness to the cards.
author: Fryxen
heading: Tharsis Republic

question: In solo, does Tharsis Republic get its production bonus for the neutral cities placed during setup?
ruling: Yes. Tharsis Republic gets its city production bonus (MC production) for the neutral cities as well; this exception is stated in the solo rules.
quote: You seem to have forgotten to take the production bonus for the 2 neutral cities (this Tharsis Republic exception is stated in the solo rules).
author: Fryxen
heading: Tharsis Republic

question: Why does Thermalist count heat resources rather than heat production?
ruling: Design intent: heat production depends on the cards drawn (tactics and luck), while heat resources reflect long-term choices, and for a 5 VP award they prefer the winner to be decided by strategy.
quote: heat production is only based on the cards you get (tactical choices and luck), while heat resources are affected by your long-term choices (strategy).
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Thermalist (award)

question: Which version of the ThorGate card is correct?
ruling: The version with the discount is correct and the other is an old version. The new version also lets the discount apply to the Power Plant standard project.
quote: The first ThorGate with discount is correct, the second is an old version. ... you can use it also on the standard project Power Plant.
author: Fryxen
heading: ThorGate

topic: Tile placement: cards that override normal placement rules
question: Do cards always follow the normal tile placement rules?
ruling: No. Many cards disregard normal placement rules, e.g. Moholes places a tile that must be placed on an area reserved for ocean, and Urbanized Area places a city tile that has to be adjacent to 2 other cities.
quote: many cards disregard normal placement rules to allow for a more thematic gameplay, such as the card Moholes, which places a tile that must be placed on an area reserved for ocean, or Urbanized Area, which places a city tile which has to be adjacent to 2 other cities.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Tile placement

topic: Requirements: tile placement must be possible
question: Can you play a card that places a tile when there is no legal placement for it?
ruling: No. Errata to the rulebook: any tiles placed by the card must have legal placements, or you cannot play the card. The exception is ocean tiles after they run out, since effects raising the ocean parameter can be ignored when it is maxed.
quote: ERRATA: Any tiles placed by the card must have legal placements, or you can't play the card.
author: Fryxen
heading: Tile placement

question: Do special tiles act like greenery or have functions of their own?
ruling: Special tiles are completely without function or special rules (except Capital counts as a city). They are not cities, oceans or greeneries, have no placement restrictions, give no VP, TR or other bonuses, only the placement bonuses of the space; special rules are on the card that placed them.
quote: Special tiles are tiles completely without function or special rules (except Capital counts as a city). They are not cities, oceans or greeneries.
author: Fryxen
heading: Tile placement

topic: Tile cards that cannot place a tile
question: Can you play a card that places a tile when you cannot place the tile?
ruling: No. You cannot play a card that places a tile if you actually cannot place the tile.
quote: you can't play a card that places a tile if you actually can't place the tile.
author: Fryxen
heading: Tile placement

question: Does a card need to be able to place its stated tile to be played (rulebook p. 10 1st edition)?
ruling: Erratum: the rulebook p. 10 exception that you don't need to be able to place a stated tile is wrong. Any tile placed by the card must be placed, unless it is an ocean tile and all oceans are already placed.
quote: Page 10 in the rulebook states another exception; that you don’t need to be able to place a stated tile. This is wrong
author: Fryxen
heading: Tile placement

question: Can a tile be placed on top of another tile?
ruling: No. A tile can never be placed on top of another tile.
quote: A tile can never be placed on top of another tile.
author: Fryxen
heading: Tile placement

question: When a card lets you place two tiles (e.g. two oceans), are they placed one after another or simultaneously, and can you see a drawn card before placing the second?
ruling: Every icon is a separate effect. The tiles are placed one after the other, so the second ocean can be adjacent to the first and score its adjacency bonus, and you may see cards drawn from the first tile's placement bonus before placing the second.
quote: All icons are separate effects, so you Place the first ocean tile, then the next and so forth.
author: Fryxen
heading: Tile placement

question: What are the basic tile placement rules for cities, greeneries and oceans?
ruling: Cities cannot be placed next to other cities. Greeneries must be placed next to another tile you own, if possible. Oceans must be placed on areas reserved for oceans, and non-ocean tiles may not be placed there. Noctis City, Ganymede Colony and Phobos Space Haven have their own appointed spaces where only those tiles may be placed.
quote: Greeneries must be placed next to another tile that you own, if possible.
author: EagleEye80
heading: Tile placement

question: Can a card be played when some of its tiles cannot be placed (Artificial Lake with all oceans placed, Space Port with no city space)?
ruling: Fryxen says an earlier rule that allowed plays placing tiles that couldn't be placed (for thematic reasons) was removed, because it was unnecessary and created unwanted rules questions, especially for Mining Rights. The post does not state a verdict for Artificial Lake or Space Port specifically.
quote: But we removed the rule for 2 reasons. First, it was an unnecessary rule. More importantly, it created unwanted rules questions, especially for Mining Rights and the like.
author: Fryxen
heading: Tile placement

question: If all city and greenery tiles are used, is placing more cities or greeneries (or playing Phobos/Ganymede cards) illegal?
ruling: The tiles are not supposed to run out; use replacements if you need.
quote: The tiles are not supposed to run out. Use replacements if you need.
author: Fryxen
heading: Tile placement

question: Does Toll Station count the space tags of all opponents together or of a single opponent?
ruling: It counts the space tags of all opponents added together.
quote: Yes and yes :) It counts all opponents.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Toll Station

question: In the solo game can Toll Station count your own space tags?
ruling: No: Toll Station is about opponents' space projects; in solo it is simply useless unless combined with something. Satellites is the card that counts your own tags.
quote: Theme dictates the effects. Why would a toll station give money for your own space projects? There is another card doing exactly that, though: Satellites.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Toll Station

question: How should a tournament be structured (scoring, setup, time limits)?
ruling: Suggested, not official: score winner 3, within 5 VP 2, within 10 VP 1 (a max 5/10 VP difference was proposed); first game standard (+1 production, no Corporate Era, no draft) with Beginner Corporations for new players; time limit 2h standard and 3h Corporate Era; unfinished games finish the generation with one point less; optional timers disallowing new actions after 1 minute.
quote: Maybe a maximum of 5 VP difference for 2 points and 10 for 1 points would be better because otherwise it might be too easy to get 2 points.
author: Fryxen
heading: Tournament play

question: Should tournaments use initial drafting and modified or banned cards such as buffed UNMI, Inventrix and nerfed CrediCor?
ruling: The designer would play the game as it is: no initial draft and no modified or banned cards. The earlier suggested house rules for UNMI/Inventrix/Credicor are not official, only one brother's personal opinion.
quote: I'd go with the game as it is. That's how people are used to playing it: No initial draft, and no modified/banned cards.
author: Fryxen
heading: Tournament play

question: How can expansions be worked into a multi-round tournament?
ruling: Suggested format: first game base with Corporate Era only, second with Hellas or Elysium, third with the other map side plus Venus Next. A time limit and pairing similar-skill players after round one are called the most important issues.
quote: Expansions could be worked in if you play several rounds of games: 1st round only Base game Corporate Era, 2nd game with Hellas/Elysium, 3rd game with the other side + Venus Next.
author: Fryxen
heading: Tournament play

question: What format did the Swedish Terraformer Championship use?
ruling: Example event format: points by VP distance from the table winner (4/3/2/1 for winner, within 5, 10, 15 VP); three matches (no CE; CE with Hellas or Elysium by vote; CE with Venus Next), draft only in the final, latest Prelude used in all matches.
quote: Draft only in final. For all matches, we played with the latest version of the Prelude expansion.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Tournament play

question: Is there an official competitive setup or an official variant with an initial draft?
ruling: There is no definitive competitive setup, and Terraforming Mars has no official variant with an initial draft (of the starting hand).
quote: TM has no official variant with initial draft.
author: Fryxen
heading: Tournament play

question: Can the animals from the comet card be added to an opponent's card (the poster's 'consensus' being that you cannot)?
ruling: Confirmed: you cannot. To do something to an opponent or their cards the icon needs the red border, and Towing a Comet's icon does not have it.
quote: Correct. In order to do something to your opponent, you need that red border on the icon. Towing A Comet doesn't have that.
author: Fryxen
heading: Towing A Comet

question: Are triggered card effects, such as Ecological Zone adding an animal when you play a plant or animal tag, mandatory?
ruling: Intent: effects should always trigger when possible, and any player may invoke your triggers, so they should be considered mandatory, but only if someone remembers them. Mars University is optional ("may"). Cards generally have only positive effects so it is in your interest to trigger.
quote: But I would say that any player may invoke your triggers whenever applicable, so they should be considered mandatory, but only if someone remembers them (and nice people should help each other remember).
author: Fryxen
heading: Triggered effects

question: Are triggered effects mandatory, and is forgetting one a rules violation?
ruling: Triggers are not mandatory but may be invoked by anyone, so forgetting one is not a violation and cannot invalidate a game; since it is always in someone's interest they should normally be performed and players should help each other remember.
quote: Triggers are not mandatory, but may be invoked by anyone. Thus there can be no cheating or invalidating.
author: Fryxen
heading: Triggered effects

question: Are triggered effects of blue cards mandatory, and must other players remind someone who forgets one?
ruling: All triggers are automatic. Most are beneficial and the rare harmful ones are usually emphasised with 'must'. Officially any player can enforce any effect by reminding the owner and nobody has a formal duty to do so. Forgetting a trigger is a rules mistake; players are encouraged to help each other remember (rulebook page 12), even retroactively if it can still be done.
quote: Basically, all triggers are automatic. [...] the official procedure is that any player can enforce any effect by reminding each other (no-one has any official 'duty').
author: Fryxen
heading: Triggered effects

question: May a player apply a forgotten effect retroactively if that hurts another player's plan, for example a milestone claim?
ruling: Fryxen says players are free to decide for themselves, but he would allow the retroactive effect: it was a bonus the player should have had and others could have reminded them earlier. A player cannot be 100 percent sure nobody can get extra MC, so holding off on a milestone is risky.
quote: You're of course free to do as you wish, but I'd allow it. It was a bonus they should have had, and you were free to remind them of it earlier.
author: Fryxen
heading: Triggered effects

question: Are takebacks allowed after a player's turn is over?
ruling: Retroactive bonuses and takebacks are different things. The only takeback Fryxen would allow beyond the player's own turn is when they passed while still having obvious actions to take, such as adding an animal or converting heat.
quote: The only takeback I would allow beyond the player's turn is if they passed while still having obvious actions to take, like adding an animal or maybe converting heat.
author: Fryxen
heading: Triggered effects

question: How should a forgotten triggered bonus (such as Tharsis Republic production) be handled after the fact?
ruling: In casual play the rulebook says players should help each other remember triggered bonuses, and Fryxen often lets a player take what they missed as far back as all players agree. There is no strict casual rule.
quote: I often even let player get resources they should have had from that production as far as all the players can agree how long it has been.
author: Fryxen
heading: Triggered effects

question: What is the strict rule for forgotten triggers in tournament play?
ruling: In tournament play any player may point out and enforce any trigger, but only during the same turn.
quote: The strict rule is that any player may point out and enforce any trigger but only during the same turn.
author: Fryxen
heading: Triggered effects

question: What happens when you pass during the action phase?
ruling: If you pass, you are out of the round (you do not get to act again that generation).
quote: If you pass, you're out of the round.
author: Fryxen
heading: Turn structure and actions

question: What can a player do during the play phase of their turn?
ruling: During the play phase you can do everything except research and production (which have their own simultaneous phases): play a card, convert plants into a greenery tile, convert heat into a temperature increase, discard a card for 1 MC, use a standard project, claim a milestone, fund an award, or use an action on a card in play, as many times as you can afford and in any order. Card actions can only be done once per round.
quote: During the play phase you can do Everything except research and production, which still have their own phases that you perform simultaneously.
author: Fryxen
heading: Turn structure and actions

question: How many production phases happen in a generation with two players, and when do you produce?
ruling: Players go round and round taking one or two actions until everyone passes (takes no action), and only then is production performed. You usually spend most resources before passing, then get new resources once all have passed.
quote: go round and round, taking one or two actions intil everyone PASS (take no action). This means that you usually spend all or most of your resources before you pass, THEN you get new resources
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Turn structure and actions

question: Is there a limit on the number of actions in a generation?
ruling: No. In one generation you may essentially perform any number of actions, but only 1 or 2 at a time before the next player.
quote: In one generation you may essentially perform any number of actions, but only 1 or 2 at a time.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Turn structure and actions

question: Is the number of actions limited per generation in solo?
ruling: No. In both solo and multiplayer the number of actions is unlimited; resources are the limit.
quote: In both solo and multiplayer, the amount of actions is unlimited, but the resources are what limits you.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Turn structure and actions

question: Do players draw cards each turn, and how many turns can a player take per generation?
ruling: Per rulebook page 8: you take 1 or 2 actions each turn, or pass; play proceeds clockwise until all players have passed, so you get as many turns as you like per generation as long as you do not pass. Cards are bought only at the start of each generation.
quote: Page 8 in the rulebook says that "you take 1 or 2 actions each turn, or pass. play proceeds clockise around the table until all players have passed"
author: Isaac Fryxelius
heading: Turn structure and actions

question: How many turns do you get in the action phase when you hold a lot of M€?
ruling: You get as many turns as you like during the action phase, with 1 or 2 actions per turn, so spend your M€; only afterwards comes the production phase that pays new income.
quote: you get as many turns as you like during the action phase, with 1 or 2 actions per turn.
author: Isaac Fryxelius
heading: Turn structure and actions

question: Is there a limit to the number of actions a player can take per generation, and when does the generation end?
ruling: The turn goes around the table repeatedly until everyone has passed; each turn is 1 or 2 actions. As long as you do at least 1 action it will be your turn again after the others. If all others have passed you can keep taking turns until you pass too. The total number of actions per generation is unlimited.
quote: The total number of actions per generation is unlimited.
author: EagleEye80
heading: Turn structure and actions

topic: Action phase: going around the table
question: In the Action phase, does each player take only one turn of 1-2 actions per generation?
ruling: No. Players take turns doing 1 or 2 actions, going around the table repeatedly until everyone has passed; taking 2 actions and then passing is a misreading. The rulebook wording was to be clarified in the next print.
quote: I agree with you all :) and we will have it much clearer in the next print.
author: Fryxen
heading: Turn structure and actions

topic: Actions per turn versus per generation
question: Is a player limited to 2 actions per generation?
ruling: No. The rules allow 1-2 actions per turn but any number of turns per generation; limiting to 2 actions per generation is a misconception that adds game time.
quote: The rules say you can play 1-2 actions per turn, but any number of turns per generation.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Turn structure and actions

question: How many actions can a player take in a generation?
ruling: Actions per generation are unlimited. The rules (to be rephrased in the next reprint) mean players take turns doing a limited number of actions at a time and keep going until they pass.
quote: Yes, we will refrase and emphasize that you have unlimited actions in the next reprint.
author: EagleEye80
heading: Turn structure and actions

topic: Doing more than two actions in a generation
question: How can a player perform more than two actions per generation?
ruling: Go around the table doing 1-2 actions each time until every player has passed; you can do as many actions as you like in a generation, but only 1-2 at a time.
quote: You go around the table doing 1-2 actions until every player has passed.
author: EagleEye80
heading: Turn structure and actions

question: How many actions can a player take per generation, and what is limited to 1-2?
ruling: The number of actions per generation is unlimited. The only limit is 1-2 actions at a time before the next player's turn; players go around the table until they choose to pass.
quote: The number of actions per generation is unlimited! The only limitation is that can only do 1-2 actions at a time before it is the next players turn.
author: EagleEye80
heading: Turn structure and actions

question: How many actions can a player take?
ruling: 1-2 actions per turn, with unlimited actions per generation.
quote: 1-2 actions per turn, unlimited actions per generation.
author: Fryxen
heading: Turn structure and actions

question: How many actions does a player get in the action phase of a generation?
ruling: Players have an unlimited number of actions each generation. They go around the table taking turns of 1-2 actions until everyone has passed.
quote: Did you understand that all players have unlimited number of actions every generation? [...] You go around and around and around the table doing 1-2 actions at a time until everyone has passed
author: EagleEye80
heading: Turn structure and actions

question: Was the rule about actions per generation reworded?
ruling: Yes, the rulebook text was re-formulated to make clear you have unlimited actions each generation (1-2 actions per turn, many turns).
quote: Yes, we have re-formulated this part of the rules to make it clear that you have unlimited actions each generation.
author: EagleEye80
heading: Turn structure and actions

question: How many actions does a player take in a generation and when are they out of the action phase?
ruling: You have an unlimited number of actions each generation but may only take 1 or 2 at a time (your turn). After the other players' turns you get a new turn. Only if you passed (did no action on your turn) are you out for the rest of that action phase.
quote: You have an unlimited number of actions each generation, but may only take 1 or 2 at a time (your turn).
author: Fryxen
heading: Turn structure and actions

question: Is there a limit to how many cards a player can play in a generation?
ruling: No. You have an unlimited number of actions each generation, so you can play as many cards as your resources allow.
quote: This means that you can play as many cards as your resources allow.
author: EagleEye80
heading: Turn structure and actions

question: After all other players pass, does the remaining player have unlimited actions?
ruling: Yes. The number of turns is unlimited: if you are the only player who has not passed, you keep taking turns until you choose to pass.
quote: Yes, the number of turns are unlimited. If you are the only one that have not passed on your turn, you can continue to take turns until you choose to pass.
author: EagleEye80
heading: Turn structure and actions

question: How do turns and generations relate in the action phase?
ruling: Every player has as many turns as they like each generation until they pass on their turn, but only 1-2 actions each turn; the turn then proceeds around the table until it is your turn again. A turn is not a generation.
quote: Every player has as many turns as they like each generation until they choose to pass on their turn. BUT - only 1-2 actions each turn
author: EagleEye80
heading: Turn structure and actions

question: How many turns can a player take in a generation?
ruling: You may take as many turns as you like in a generation until you pass. The second printing's rulebook and reference cards state this more clearly.
quote: the rulebook and reference cards are a little more clear on your right to take as many turns as you like in a generation, until you pass
author: Isaac Fryxelius
heading: Turn structure and actions

question: Why is there no player-influenced turn order (e.g. first to pass goes first next generation)?
ruling: Design intent: turn order is fixed (rotating first player) so it is fair, predictable and easy; a turn order track was rejected as it complicates play, makes the state harder to overview, and risks a static turn order where one player goes first almost every generation.
quote: So we opted for a turn order that would be fair, predictable and easy.
author: Fryxen
heading: Turn structure and actions

topic: Attacking a player who has passed
question: Can an attack card be played against a player who has already passed for the generation?
ruling: Yes. There is no rule protecting passed players; a player who passes only forfeits the ability to respond.
quote: No such rule. If your buddy passes, he forfeits his ability to respond. You can still play the card to affect him.
author: Fryxen
heading: Turn structure and actions

question: How does the action phase proceed and when does it end?
ruling: The first player takes 1 or 2 actions (some corporations have a fixed first action, after which they may take a second action or not). Turns pass clockwise with 1 or 2 actions at a time until everyone has passed (taken no action on their turn), so the turn can go several laps and you get another turn as long as you take at least 1 action on your turn.
quote: The turn passes clockwise with players taking 1 or 2 actions at a time until everyone has passed (=taken no action on their turn).
author: Fryxen
heading: Turn structure and actions

question: What does UNMI's action condition mean: 'if you have increased your TR this generation'?
ruling: It is about TR (Terraforming Rating), not VP. In normal cases you can take the action if you have increased a global parameter or placed an ocean this generation; some special cards also give TR.
quote: Please note that this is TR (Terraforming Rating), not any VP.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: United Nations Mars Initiative

question: How often can the UNMI corporation action be used?
ruling: UNMI works exactly like a blue card with an action; it may be used only once per generation.
quote: UNMI works exactly like a blue card with an action; it may be used only once per generation.
author: Fryxen
heading: United Nations Mars Initiative

question: Is there an endorsed house rule to make UNMI stronger?
ruling: The designers suggest, as an optional house rule, making the UNMI TR-raising effect cost 1 MC to use. It is not a printed rule.
quote: Suggestion for houserule: Make the effect cost 1 to use to make UNMI better.
author: EagleEye80
heading: United Nations Mars Initiative

topic: Fan variant: choose corporation and two cards
question: Are a UNMI activation cost of 1 M€ and an Inventrix modification official mods?
ruling: No: the described UNMI (1 M€ to activate) and Inventrix (+-3 steps, cards at 2 M€ after round 1) changes are definitely not official mods.
quote: Interesting variant, but those are definitely not official mods...
author: Fryxen
heading: United Nations Mars Initiative

question: Are the suggested tweaks to UNMI (cost 1 to use effect) and Inventrix (+/- 3) official?
ruling: No. Those earlier comments were not official suggestions; the corporations are played as printed, and the designers do not patch slightly-below-average corporations.
quote: Thoze earlier comments were not really suggestions or official. If we starr patching anything slightly below average it will be difficult to draw the line.
author: Fryxen
heading: United Nations Mars Initiative

topic: UNMI cannot be used to stall
question: Can UNMI's action be taken as a stalling move when TR has not been raised this generation or when doing nothing?
ruling: No. The condition (TR raised this generation) is a prerequisite for taking the action, not only for the effect, so you must be able to pay 3 MC and raise TR to take it.
quote: Official answer: No, you can't stall with UNMI.
author: Fryxen
heading: United Nations Mars Initiative

topic: Icons vs explanation text on actions
question: Does the printed text or the iconography govern UNMI's action?
ruling: The ruling is based on the iconography, the 'function bearer' of a card; the explanation text only explains it. Null actions exist only under the 3 exceptions (e.g. Symbiotic Fungus with no microbe card, converting heat when temperature is maxed); UNMI does not fall under them.
quote: The ruling is based on the iconography, because that's the basic 'function bearer' of a card in TM.
author: Fryxen
heading: United Nations Mars Initiative

question: Can UNMI's action be used as a null action if you have not raised TR yet this generation?
ruling: No. The iconography tells you to gain a TR, which you cannot under those circumstances; a null option would need to be shown with an 'OR' or a bare red arrow.
quote: You can't use it as a null action because the iconography tells you to gain a TR, and you can't under the given circumstances.
author: Fryxen
heading: United Nations Mars Initiative

question: What counts as a generation for the UNMI action, and does the TR gain have to be just before it?
ruling: A generation consists of turn order, research, actions, production and the solar phase; generation 1 includes setup. So TR from preludes and corporation plays counts in generation 1, as does any TR gained during the action phase. The TR doesn't have to be gained just before the UNMI action; it is enough to remember how you got it.
quote: It doesn't have to be just before the UNMI action. It's enough to remember and refer to how you got the TR.
author: Fryxen
heading: United Nations Mars Initiative

question: Can Terraforming Mars be played with 6 players?
ruling: Nothing technically prevents it (answer 'Technically, no' to 'is there any reason we can't play with 6'). Balance issues may arise, especially for effects affecting all players, and the Terraformer milestone should probably be lowered to about 30 TR instead of 35 to stand a chance of being taken.
quote: Technically, no. Some balance issues might arise, especially for effects affecting all players. Also, the Terraformer milestone should probably be lowered to about 30 TR instead of 35 to stand a chance of being taken.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Variants and house rules

question: Does EagleEye80 recommend a sixth player?
ruling: The game works at 1 to 5 players. He would not recommend adding a 6th player (they have tried it): downtime, needing a very large table, no chance to follow opponents.
quote: I think the game works on all player counts from 1-5 [...] I would not recommend adding a 6th player. (yes, we have tried it)
author: EagleEye80
heading: Variants and house rules

question: Is a card-market variant (face-up market replacing the starting deal/draft) workable, and what market size is suggested?
ruling: Lord_Aethan encouraged trying it and suggested a fixed-size market of 3*2 or 4*2 cards regardless of player count, rather than a size scaling with player count.
quote: I do believe it would be better to have a fixed-sized market, though. I would suggest 3*2 or 4*2 cards regardless of player count.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Variants and house rules

question: Should players be allowed to trade resources with each other as a house rule?
ruling: The designers advise against it: trading would make the game much longer, would undermine the importance of the resources and productions you choose to build, and would favour players good at negotiating. Having too much steel, heat or titanium is part of the game; use the Miner and Thermalist awards.
quote: It would take away the importance of which resources and productions you choose to build. If you play poorly you may end up with more resourses than you need, yes, and that's part of the game.
author: EagleEye80
heading: Variants and house rules

question: Should there be a standard action to buy cards from the deck for M€ (house rule)?
ruling: The designers advise against it: allowing cards to be bought for money makes money too powerful, so the game would always be about who has the most money, whereas now lacking cards limits what money can do.
quote: If you can buy cards for money, then that will make money too powerful, and the game would essentially always be about who has the most money.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Variants and house rules

question: How could a variant where players have two corporations be balanced?
ruling: Fryxen suggests costing the extra corporation at 65 (corporation baseline value) minus its starting MC, e.g. Teractor 5 MC, PhoboLog 41 MC (giving 10 titanium and the titanium boost); alternatively discarded corporations could form a first-come-first-served market set up before the first action phase. Not tested.
quote: The most straight-forward way to implement it would be cost them at 65 (Corporation base line value) minus their starting Money.
author: Fryxen
heading: Variants and house rules

question: What does FryxGames ask of people making and sharing fan-made cards?
ruling: Fan-made cards must be marked 'fan made' to distinguish them from official content, should avoid copyrighted artwork, and may not be used commercially. Cards are game content while cubes, tiles and similar items are alternative accessories.
quote: please mark all cards 'fan made' so there is a clear distinction between official and non-official content.
author: Fryxen
heading: Variants and house rules

question: Is the Moon expansion an authorized FryxGames product?
ruling: There is no official Moon expansion; it is fan made and FryxGames is not involved, so using it is not authorized, though players can play any way they like.
quote: There is no official Moon expansion. It is fan made and FryxGames is not involved in any way.
author: Fryxen
heading: Variants and house rules

question: Is advising or negotiating about attack targets (e.g. who has plants to remove) part of the game?
ruling: Fryxen likes keeping negotiation about attack targets in his games; helping players see their options is fine especially when teaching, but beyond some point it stops being good. It depends on the group; no formal rule.
quote: Negotiating targets of an attack is a spice I'd rather keep in my games. :)
author: Fryxen
heading: Variants and house rules

question: How can engine building be toned down while keeping the game interesting?
ruling: Fryxen suggests removing all card-drawing cards: engine builders need access to many cards, so less access makes the strategy harder. The base game itself was designed with higher baseline production and fewer engine cards.
quote: If you want to nerf engine building a little while still keeping it interesting, try removing all card-drawing cards.
author: Fryxen
heading: Variants and house rules

question: Is there an official team mode?
ruling: An official 2v2 expansion for Terraforming Mars released on the Gamefound campaign for The Legacy Of Mars: two teams of two, sending cards and resources to your team-mate, with new milestones and awards adjusted for it.
quote: In the 2v2 version, you team up against each other, send cards and resources to your team-mate, and enjoy a combo-filled night with new milestones and awards adjusted just for this experience.
author: Fryxen
heading: Variants and house rules

question: Does the 2v2 product add new project cards or corporations?
ruling: No. It is a very simple product with the 2v2 rules and 2 sets of milestones and awards; some of those are mechanically linked to team play. It adds no new content applicable to normal play.
quote: No, it's a very simple product with 2v2 rules and 2 sets of milestones and awards adjusted to a gameplay where it will be easier to go bananas with your strategies
author: Fryxen
heading: Variants and house rules

question: Does each tag played trigger effects such as Viral Enhancers, and who chooses the trigger order?
ruling: Yes: each tag played can trigger effects, and per the rules you choose the order in which they trigger.
quote: Yes. Each tag played can trigger effects, and per the rules, you choose the order in which they trigger.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Viral Enhancers

question: If I play a microbe-tag card with Viral Enhancers in play, can I take a plant resource, and does it apply when playing Viral Enhancers itself?
ruling: Yes to both: you are not forced to match the tag. Microbe cards that collect microbes can add a microbe to the card or gain 1 plant instead; microbe cards that do not collect microbes always give the plant. It also triggers when you play Viral Enhancers itself.
quote: Yes, and that includes when you play Viral Enhancers itself.
author: Fryxen
heading: Viral Enhancers

question: With Viral Enhancers, when you play a plant, microbe or animal tag, what can you take?
ruling: You choose: put a resource cube on the card you just played (if it can hold one) or take a plant resource on your player board. Each tag counts, so Advanced Ecosystems gives 3 plant resources (it cannot hold resources itself).
