quote: When you play a card with plant/microbe/animal tags, you choose: - put a resource cube on the card you just played (if possible) - or take a plant resource on your player board
author: EagleEye80
heading: Viral Enhancers

question: If you have Viral Enhancers and no plants, can you play a plant-tagged card that requires paying a plant, using the plant Viral Enhancers gives you?
ruling: No. Viral Enhancers gives a plant when you play a plant-tagged card, but you cannot play a card that requires you to pay a plant if you do not already have a plant before you play it.
quote: Viral enhancers gives you a plant if you play a card with a plant tag - but you can not play that card you described if you do not have a plant before you play it.
author: Isaac Fryxelius
heading: Viral Enhancers

question: How do Viral Enhancers' triggers work when a card has multiple matching tags, e.g. Decomposers (plant and microbe)?
ruling: Each tag is counted when you play a card, so Viral Enhancers triggers per matching tag: Decomposers gives 2 microbes on itself, or 1 microbe plus a plant. Explanation text may differ from the icons, but icon meaning is used unless there is an asterisk.
quote: Viral Enhaners then Decomposers will give 2 microbes on Decomposers, or 1 microbe plus a plant.
author: Fryxen
heading: Viral Enhancers

topic: Viral Enhancers always allows a plant
question: Can you take a plant with Viral Enhancers if the played card can hold animal or microbe resources?
ruling: Yes. When Viral Enhancers triggers you always have the option to take a plant for the triggering tag(s).
quote: When Viral Enhancers triggers, you always have the option to take a plant for the triggering tag(s).
author: Fryxen
heading: Viral Enhancers

topic: Interacting with other players' cards requires red border
question: Can Viron's effect interact with other players' action cards?
ruling: No. The only way you can ever interact with other players via card effects is if the icons have a red border; Viron's effect has no red border, so it cannot use other players' cards.
quote: The ONLY way you can EVER interact with other players via card effects is if the icons have a RED BORDER.
author: Fryxen
heading: Viron

question: When Viron repeats an action card with an 'OR' between options, can it use either option, and both?
ruling: Viron can use either option on the action card regardless of which option was chosen with the normal use of that card, but never both: 'OR' means 'either X or Y'.
quote: Viron can indeed use either option on an action card, regardless of which option you chose with the normal use of that card. But in neither case do you get to do both options.
author: Fryxen
heading: Viron

topic: Water Splitting Plant with oxygen maxed
question: Can you use Water Splitting when oxygen is maxed?
ruling: Yes, you can spend 3 energy to get nothing.
quote: You can even use Water Splitting when O2 is maxed, spending 3 energy to get nothing.
author: Fryxen
heading: Water Splitting Plant

question: Do the three Big Box replacement cards have to be used, and with which expansions?
ruling: Using them is optional; they add special tiles to the game and can be used in any combination of expansions. Cardboard tiles for them come with the Big Box or can be printed from FryxGames' PDF.
quote: You don't need to use them at all, but they will make the game a notch more fun. They can be used in any combination of expansions.
author: Fryxen
heading: Big Box replacement cards

question: What extra special tiles and cards does the Big Box contain compared with the base game and expansions?
ruling: The Big Box includes 3 new special tiles and 3 alternate cards that place them, which are replacement cards for Deimos Down, Great Dam and Magnetic Field Generators. The cards are also in the Big Box promo pack but without the tiles; the tiles can be printed from the FryxGames website. The expansions otherwise add no tiles.
quote: The only exception is that the Big Box also includes 3 new special tiles and 3 alternate cards that place them. These are replacement cards for Deimos Down, Great Dam, and Magnetic Field Generators.
author: Fryxen
heading: Big Box replacement cards

question: Does the Big Box version of Magnetic Field Generators differ from the base game card?
ruling: The Magnetic Field Generators card in Terraforming Mars: Big Box instructs you to place a special tile (the 3D Magnetic Field Generators tile) and is meant to replace the base game card. The base card did not specify placing a special tile.
quote: the card that comes inside Terraforming Mars: Big Box will instruct you to place this tile. This card is meant to replace the card in the base game.
author: evilone
heading: Magnetic Field Generators

question: Do tags on event cards, multiple tags on a card, or a wild tag trigger Aridor's new-tag production bonus?
ruling: Tags on event cards do not count for Aridor, not even the event tag, because events are not put in play. A card with two new tags (e.g. Vesta Shipyard) might give 2 bumps if you had neither before. A wild tag does not count: it is not a tag when put into play and is not 'put into play' when applied during an action.
quote: Tags on event cards do not count for Aridor, even the even tag itself.
author: Fryxen
heading: Aridor

question: Playing Sister Planet Support with a wild tag set as Venus to meet its requirement, does that trigger Aridor?
ruling: The wild tag can satisfy the Venus requirement but does not trigger Aridor (it is not a new permanent tag). Playing Sister Planet Support does trigger Aridor because it brings its own permanent Venus tag into play. Outside your own action and while being played the wild tag is no tag.
quote: The wild tag can be used to fulfill the venus tag requirement for playing Sister Planet Support, but it will not trigger Aridor (because it's not a new permanent tag).
author: Fryxen
heading: Aridor

question: Why can't the wild tag trigger Aridor?
ruling: Aridor triggers on permanent tags and the wild tag is not a permanent tag; 'wild' is not a tag type but a rule/effect. The wild tag counts as no tag at all when undecided, to remove rules ambiguities.
quote: Aridor triggers on permanent tags, and the wild tag is not a permanent tag; it changes.
author: Fryxen
heading: Aridor

question: Does setting a wild tag to a building tag while playing a building prevent an Aridor trigger, versus Sister Planet Support triggering Aridor anyway?
ruling: Aridor should trigger on Sister Planet Support as previously said, because it brings a new permanent tag type; the wild tag is not permanent. He withdraws the idea that a wild tag can prevent your own Aridor trigger, and says he might change his mind about the wild tag.
quote: Aridor should trigger on SPS like I said because it does bring a new permanent tag type. The wild tag is not permanent.
author: Fryxen
heading: Aridor

question: Does Aridor get its bonus from playing event cards with new tags?
ruling: No. Aridor doesn't get its bonus from event cards because event tags don't stay in play.
quote: Aridor doesn't get its bonus from event cards, because those tags don't stay in play.
author: Fryxen
heading: Aridor

question: How do Beginner Corporations work in any setup?
ruling: In any game setup, a first-time player can be dealt 1 Beginner Corporation and 10 free cards instead of choosing from 2 corporations and buying cards. Beginner Corporations are not dealt to all players unless they are all beginners.
quote: In ANY game setup and combination of variants and expansions, a 1st time player can join and be dealt 1 Beginner Corporation and 10 free cards
author: Fryxen
heading: Beginner corporations

question: How do Beginner Corporations work together with Prelude?
ruling: A Beginner Corporation player gets the 10 free cards and then chooses 2 out of 4 Prelude cards just like the others.
quote: if you play Beginner Coroporation with Prelude, you are supposed to get your 10 free cards and then choose 2 out of 4 Prelude cards just like the others.
author: Fryxen
heading: Beginner corporations

question: May floaters from a colony effect be split among several floater cards?
ruling: No. Each effect adds only to one card, like Large Convoy. Colony bonuses are separate effects and can be directed to other cards (e.g. placement bonus on one card, trade income on another, each colony's bonus on different cards).
quote: Each effect should only add to one card, just like similar card effects like Large Convoy.
author: Fryxen
heading: Colony bonuses and trade income

question: If you have a colony on a tile and trade with it, do you get both trade income and the colony bonus?
ruling: Yes, but they are separate effects, so for Titan the trade income floaters can go on one card and the colony bonus floater on another.
quote: Yes, but they are separate effects, so in the case of Titan you can place the trade income floaters on one card and the colony bonus floater on another card if you like.
author: Fryxen
heading: Colony bonuses and trade income

question: Can resources gained from a colony be split between several cards?
ruling: The trade income must go to only one card, but colonies there have their trading bonus (and placement bonus) which can go to different cards since those are separate effects.
quote: The trade income must go to only one card, but if you have colonies there, their trading bonus (and placement bonus) can go to different cards since those are separate effects.
author: Fryxen
heading: Colony bonuses and trade income

topic: Trade income and colony bonus order
question: Is there a required order for collecting trade income and colony bonuses?
ruling: No fixed order: treat them as independent effects and the active player chooses the order.
quote: Number 2) is right. The active player chooses order.
author: Fryxen
heading: Colony bonuses and trade income

question: Are colony bonuses mandatory or optional (e.g. a microbe that an opponent with Ants would eat)?
ruling: All effects are generally mandatory. Three exceptions: microbes (card resources) must be taken if possible but can be ignored if you can't take them; parameter raises may be ignored if maxed; red-bordered resource destruction may be ignored wholly or partly. If you can't perform all effects, you can't take the action.
quote: All effects are generally mandatory, regardless of if you play a card, use a standard action, use a blue card action or something else.
author: Fryxen
heading: Colony bonuses and trade income

question: Can a player choose not to take their colony bonus (e.g. microbes that an opponent with Ants would eat)?
ruling: Official answer: No. Effects are generally mandatory, with exceptions: card resources must be taken if possible but may be ignored if you can't take them; parameter raises may be ignored if maxed; red-bordered resource destruction may be ignored. So if you trade to get microbes, or get them as colony bonuses, you must take them if you can.
quote: So if you trade to get microbes, or get them as colony bonuses, you must take them if you can.
author: Fryxen
heading: Colony bonuses and trade income

question: Does Community Services count the corporation and Preludes, and event cards?
ruling: Green and blue cards count, as well as the corporation and Preludes. Events do not count because they are face down (not in play).
quote: Green and blue cards count, as well as corporation and preludes. Events do not count because they are face down (not in play).
author: Fryxen
heading: Community Services

question: Does Cryo-Sleep's 'pay 1 less resource' trading discount apply when paying with M€?
ruling: Yes: M€ is a resource, just like energy or titanium, so paying with M€ costs 1 less (8 M€).
quote: M€ is a resource, just like energy or titanium.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Cryo-Sleep

topic: Factorum action with no building cards
question: Can Factorum's action (pay 3 M€ to draw a building card) be taken if no building-tag card is left in the deck and discard?
ruling: No: not finding the right card is not one of the 3 exceptions, so the action is cancelled. This is one of the few cases where an action is started and then cancelled, because the search revealed information. No errata exists; a suggested house rule is to discard cards from the deck until it runs out or a building card is found, then take it.
quote: Not finding the right card is not one of the 3 exceptions. If the action tells you to get a certain card and you can't, then the action is cancelled.
author: Fryxen
heading: Factorum

question: Why does the Colonies printing of the Lanterns card have no space tag compared to the promo?
ruling: Intentional: tags were removed from cards where unnecessary because space and Jovian strategies were already boosted in Colonies. Thematically the Lanterns are located in the atmosphere, not in space.
quote: Thematically, the Lanterns are located in the atmosphere, not in space.
author: Fryxen
heading: Jovian Lanterns

question: Which version of Jovian Lanterns is correct, the promo with a space tag (cost 21) or the Colonies card without it (cost 20)?
ruling: The space tag was removed, and the cost reduced accordingly, because Jovian Lanterns is situated in Jupiter's atmosphere, not in space; the version without the space tag is the intended one.
quote: The reason we removed the space tag (and therefore reduced the cost) is that Jovian Lanterns is a project situated in Jupiter's atmosphere, not in space.
author: Fryxen
heading: Jovian Lanterns

question: Is the maximum of 4 on the Jupiter Floating Station a limit on floaters on the card or on the MC gained?
ruling: There is no limit to adding floaters; the limit applies only to how many credits you can get in that action. Alternatively it can be read as how many of your floaters you may count, which amounts to the same thing.
quote: There is no limit to adding resources, only in how many credits you can get in that action.
author: Fryxen
heading: Jupiter Floating Station

question: May Jupiter Floating Station hold more than 4 floaters, or is 4 only the cap on MC gained?
ruling: As many floaters as you like; the 'max 4' only restricts the second action of getting money for floaters.
quote: As many as you like. The "max 4" is clearly a restriction only for the second possible action of getting money for floaters.
author: Fryxen
heading: Jupiter Floating Station

question: Does Lunar Mining count its own Earth tag even though the card lacks 'including this'?
ruling: Yes. The rule is that every card triggers off its own tags; the 'including this' explanation text only reflects it. Unless a card has an asterisk and explicit instruction not to count itself, it counts its own tags.
quote: The rule is that every card triggers off its own tags.
author: Fryxen
heading: Lunar Mining

question: If a card requires placing a colony but there is no valid position, can the card still be played?
ruling: No. A colony is not a resource and the colony tile is not a card, so the exception for resources and tiles that cannot be placed does not apply; you must place the colony to play the card.
quote: A colony is not a resource, and the colony tile is not a card, so that exception does not apply. You have to place the colony in order to play the card.
author: Fryxen
heading: Placing colonies

topic: Placing a colony on a tile with unstorable resources
question: Can you build a colony on a colony tile whose resources you cannot store (to block it or collect the bonus)?
ruling: Yes, for the same reasons: card-resources you cannot store can be ignored and the rest of the effect applied.
quote: Yes, for the same reasons as above.
author: Fryxen
heading: Placing colonies

topic: Placing a colony without a card to collect the bonus
question: Can you place a colony on a tile (e.g. Titan) when you have no card that can collect the placement bonus resource?
ruling: Yes. It raises the level the marker drops back to after trades, and later your resource cards can receive resources from colony bonus and trade income once you have cards that can collect them. Normally not a good play.
quote: You can place a colony on Titan without having a floater cards to put the placement bonus on.
author: Fryxen
heading: Placing colonies

question: Is Pluto's colony bonus draw a card and then discard a card, in that order?
ruling: Yes: the effect is specifically a draw then a discard, so the active player decides only who draws/discards first and can take trade income before their own colony bonuses.
quote: That's how it works, yes.
author: Fryxen
heading: Pluto

question: If several players have a colony on Pluto, in which order do they get their colony bonuses when someone trades there?
ruling: The active player determines the order of effects.
quote: The active player determines the order of effects.
author: Fryxen
heading: Pluto

topic: Corporation order with Prelude (Stormcraft, Saturn Systems)
question: If a corporation goes first, does its Jovian tag trigger a later Saturn Systems, and how does Prelude change that?
ruling: With Prelude, preludes are played after all corporations, so a Jovian prelude of the first player's Stormcraft would trigger Saturn Systems even though Stormcraft goes first. Corporation tags alone depend on reveal order.
quote: If you use Prelude, though, they are all played after all corporations. So if Stormcraft has a jovian prelude, it would trigger Saturn Systems even though Stormcraft goes first.
author: Fryxen
heading: Saturn Systems

question: When playing the standard game plus Colonies without Corporate Era cards, does everyone start with +1 production of each resource?
ruling: Yes. Exclude the Corporate Era cards, add the Colonies cards and colony tiles, and everyone starts with +1 production of each resource. Prelude can be added too (2 Prelude cards per player) and +1 production is still kept.
quote: If you want to play standard game + Colonies, you exclude the CE cards, add the Colonies cards and colony tiles, and everyone starts with +1 production of each resource.
author: Fryxen
heading: Setup and deck composition

topic: Colonies promo cards are single copies
question: May both the promo copies and the Colonies copies of Lunar Exports, Atmo Collectors and Jovian Lanterns be put in the deck?
ruling: No. Each card exists in only one copy in the project deck (they are patents); the promos are pre-releases of the Colonies cards, so only 1 of each card is used.
quote: Each card is only supposed to exist in 1 copy in the deck, as they are thematically called "patents".
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Setup and deck composition

question: In a solo game, when do you select which colony tiles to keep, and is the extra Aridor colony tile random?
ruling: In solo, you choose colony tiles at the same time as choosing cards and corporation; in multiplayer, the tiles are drawn before choosing cards and corporation. Aridor can choose the discarded colony tile in a solo game; it is not random, and Aridor should choose a tile that goes well with the starting hand.
quote: In solo, you choose colony tiles at the same time as choosing cards and corp. For multiplayer, the tiles are drawn before choosing cards and corp.
author: Fryxen
heading: Setup and deck composition

question: Can Colonies be played solo?
ruling: Yes, you can definitely play solo with Colonies.
quote: Yes,you can definitely solo with Colonies.
author: Fryxen
heading: Solo game

topic: Solo with Colonies lowers MC production
question: In solo with Colonies, is the starting TR lowered?
ruling: No. Colonies lowers the starting MC production by 2 steps, not the TR; this is relevant for TR solo.
quote: Colonies lowers the MC production 2 steps, not the TR. Relevant for TR solo.
author: Fryxen
heading: Solo game

question: Can Stormcraft's floaters (usable as heat) count as heat for the Thermalist award?
ruling: No. They are still floaters, not heat, and the award doesn't use heat, it only counts it.
quote: No. Because they are still floaters, not heat. And the award doesn't use heat, it only counts it.
author: Fryxen
heading: Stormcraft Incorporated

question: What does the action of Stormcraft Incorporated do?
ruling: The action adds a floater to any of your cards that define a use for those floaters, and can be used once per generation.
quote: An action to add a floater to any of your cards that define a use for those floaters. This action can be used once per generation.
author: Fryxen
heading: Stormcraft Incorporated

question: Is the Stormcraft Incorporated effect only triggered when its action is taken?
ruling: No. The effect is separate from the action: floaters on Stormcraft can always be spent as if they were 2 heat each, whenever you would spend heat (analogous to Helion).
quote: An effect that allows you to spend floaters from Stormcraft as if they were 2 heat each. This effect is always active and allows you to use these floaters whenever you would spend heat.
author: Fryxen
heading: Stormcraft Incorporated

question: How does the white colony marker on a colony tile move, so the board state can be recreated after a bump?
ruling: The white colony marker goes down as far as it can whenever the colony tile is traded with, and goes up one step in the solar phase. If there is a trade fleet there, the white marker should be at the bottom of the track. Building colonies blocks spaces at the bottom so the white marker doesn't go down as far.
quote: the white colony marker goes down as far as it can whenever the colony tile is traded with, and goes up one step in the solar phase.
author: Fryxen
heading: Trading

topic: Trading with a colony that has unstorable resources
question: When you trade with a colony tile whose resources you cannot store, does the scale still reset?
ruling: The scale resets as normal. Taking card-resources when you don't have anywhere to store them can be ignored and the rest of the effect applied, as per normal rules for playing cards. It also does not stop colonies on that tile from collecting their colony bonus.
quote: The scale resets as normal.
author: Fryxen
heading: Trading

question: Can the trade cost be paid with a mix of MC, energy and titanium (e.g. 6 MC and 1 titanium)?
ruling: No, you cannot mix payment types for trading.
quote: You can not mix, no.
author: Fryxen
heading: Trading

question: Can you trade with multiple colonies in one generation?
ruling: Yes, if you have more trade fleets. Trade fleets move from the trade fleets tile and only return in the solar phase, so each trade fleet can trade only once per generation.
quote: The trade fleets always move from the trade fleets tile, and only go back there in the solar phase, so each trade fleet can only trade once during the generation.
author: Fryxen
heading: Trading

topic: Trading with colonies without being able to collect
question: Can you trade with Miranda, Titan or Enceladus if you have no cards that can collect animals, floaters or microbes?
ruling: Yes. Every action works along the same lines as playing a card, with the same exceptions, so you can trade and just ignore the part of the effect you can't collect.
quote: Every action works along the same lines as playing a card, and with the same exceptions.
author: Fryxen
heading: Trading

topic: Trading with a colony tile without colonies
question: Can you trade with a colony tile that has no colonies on it?
ruling: Yes, you can trade without any player colonies; there are 7 independent colonies in the background producing stuff to trade.
quote: You can trade without any player colonies.
author: Fryxen
heading: Trading

question: Does a card with a wild tag count towards the number of cards with no tags?
ruling: A wild tag is no tag at all until you choose it to be one of the defined tags during an action, so a card with a wild tag counts as a card with no tag outside that moment.
quote: It is no tag at all until you choose it to be one of the ones defined in the rules during an action.
author: Fryxen
heading: Wild tag

question: Confirming that a wild tag counts as no tag for Community Services but not as a tag for Aridor, what else is a wild tag useful for?
ruling: Right: a wild tag counts as no tag for Community Services and does not count as a tag for Aridor.
quote: Right.
author: Fryxen
heading: Wild tag

question: Does a wild tag boost cards that give something per tag when played?
ruling: Yes, a wild tag in play enhances cards like Satellites and Insects that give something per tag when you play them (not when you play the wild tag card itself).
quote: Another use for the wild tag is of course to enhance cards like Satellites, Insects etc. that give something per tag when you play them (not when you play the wild tag).
author: Fryxen
heading: Wild tag

question: For Aridor and Community Services, is the wild tag a tag?
ruling: The wild tag is NOT a tag for Aridor (no production bump) but would give Community Services a bump. The wild tag is only ever an actual tag during one of your actions when you decide it to be a certain tag.
quote: The wild tag is only ever an actual tag during one of your actions when you decide for it to be a certain tag.
author: Fryxen
heading: Wild tag

question: What can a wild tag be used for?
ruling: Allowed: satisfying tag requirements for playing cards (Gene Repair, Fusion Power), fulfilling milestone requirements (Diversifier, Builder), boosting cards that count tags when played (Insects, Worms, Terraforming Ganymede). Forbidden: triggers when you play the wild tag (Space Station, Aerobraking), Jovian scoring (Ganymede Colony), award competition (Scientist), opponents targeting it (Toll Station), and Aridor.
quote: Satisfying tag requirements for playing cards (Gene Repair, Fusion Power)
author: Fryxen
heading: Wild tag

question: Does a wild tag count for Community Services, and does it trigger Aridor?
ruling: Yes, it counts for Community Services and does not trigger Aridor. The wild tag is only the tag you want it to be during one of your actions; at all other times it is no tag. Anyone is free to houserule.
quote: Yes, it counts for Community Services, and will not trigger Aridor.
author: Fryxen
heading: Wild tag

question: Why is a wild tag considered no tag while events count as having an event tag?
ruling: Design intent: the wild tag is not a tag when played; events are thematically one-time and thus have a meaningful tag.
quote: Events are thematically one time eventuellt and thus have a meaningful tag.
author: Fryxen
heading: Wild tag

question: Is 'Claimer's Price' on the Hellas/Elysium board a typo, and is 'Excentric' a typo?
ruling: Isaac Fryxelius confirmed 'Claimer's Price' is a typo that carried over from the main game board to both Hellas and Elysium. 'Excentric' is not a typo.
quote: yes, definitly a typo (that really came as chock when we realized it, and it actually survived from the main game to both Hellas and Elysium :cry:)
author: Isaac Fryxelius
heading: Board typos

question: The Elysium Ecologist milestone shows 4 on the map but 6 in the (French) rules; which is right?
ruling: Fryxen answered only that the iconography on the board can be trusted because it is not changed in translation, which points to the number shown on the map (4); he did not state the number explicitly.
quote: you can trust the iconography because that is not changed in translation.
author: Fryxen
heading: Ecologist (milestone)

question: Does the Ecologist milestone count cards or tags, and must all of plant, animal and microbe types be present?
ruling: It counts 4 tags, not 4 cards, so a card with both a plant tag and an animal tag counts as two of the four.
quote: It is 4 tags, not 4 cards. If you have a card with both plant tag and animal tag, you're halfway there :)
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Ecologist (milestone)

topic: Space Baron / Celebrity awards and event cards
question: Do cards in the discard pile (events) count towards the Space Baron and Celebrity awards?
ruling: No. Event cards do not contribute to these awards.
quote: Not. The rules clearly state that event cards do not contribute to these Awards.
author: Fryxen
heading: Event cards and awards

topic: Event cards are not in play
question: Are played event cards still 'in play' for the Hellas & Elysium awards that count cards in play?
ruling: No. Event cards are not in play after you have played them.
quote: Event cards are not in play after you've played them.
author: Fryxen
heading: Event cards and awards

topic: Self-Replicating Robots and the Excentric award
question: Do resources on cards placed on Self-Replicating Robots count toward the Excentric award on Hellas?
ruling: No. The cards on SRR are not yet in play, so resources on them do not count towards Excentric. The resources are still resources, and other cards can add resources to it as long as they don't specify cards in play (which Excentric does).
quote: The cards on SRR are not yet in play, and so the resources on them do not contribute towards the Excentric Award on the Hellas map.
author: Fryxen
heading: Excentric (award)

question: Do resources on cards placed on Self-Replicating Robots count towards the Excentric award?
ruling: No. The Excentric award counts resources on cards in play, including corporations. Cards held on Self-Replicating Robots are not in play, so their resources do not count.
quote: Errata: The Excentric Award Counts Resources on cards in play (including Corporations).
author: Fryxen
heading: Excentric (award)

question: Do microbes, animals and other special resources on cards count as 'resources' for the Excentric award?
ruling: Yes. All square icons are resources, shown by metallic cubes. The six basic resources are on the player board, and there are several non-standard resources such as microbes, animals and science.
quote: In essence, all square icons are always resources, and they are represented by the metallic cubes.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Excentric (award)

question: What exactly does the Generalist milestone require?
ruling: Official answer: in a standard game, 2 production of each of the 6 standard resources; in a Corporate Era game, 1 production of each.
quote: Official answer: Standard game: 2 production of each the 6 standard resources. Corporate Era game: 1 production of each.
author: Fryxen
heading: Generalist (milestone)

question: Do production bonuses from Prelude cards count towards the Elysium Generalist milestone?
ruling: Yes. Prelude production and tags count just like those from corporations and project cards. The 'extra' production in the Elysium rule refers only to the +1 on all production in the standard game.
quote: The prelude production and tags count, just as corporations and project cards. The 'extra' production refers to the +1 on all production in the standard game, nothing else.
author: Fryxen
heading: Generalist (milestone)

topic: South Pole 6 M€ is an effect, not a cost
question: Can the 6 M€ for placing on the Hellas South Pole be paid with M€ gained from other placement effects of the same action?
ruling: Yes. The 6 M€ at the South Pole is part of the effect, not the card's cost, so you can perform it in your preferred order and use M€ you gain from other effects (like Moss with Viral Enhancers). An actual cost must be paid first and cannot be paid from resources gained by the effects.
quote: The same goes for the south pole - it requires you to lose 6MC, but it is actually part of the effect, not the cost, so you can perform it in your preferred order and get away with it!
author: Fryxen
heading: Hellas South Pole

topic: South Pole 6 M€ payable later in the action
question: Can the -6 M€ on the Hellas South Pole be paid later in the action, like the plants on Moss?
ruling: Yes. It can be paid later during the action, as with the -1/-2 plants on the Moss cards, as long as you are able to finish the complete action with all its effects.
quote: The -6 MC on the South Pole can be payed for later during the action, just as the -1/-2 plants on the Moss cards, as long as you are able to finish the complete action with all its effects.
author: Fryxen
heading: Hellas South Pole

topic: South Pole 6 M€ with no oceans left
question: On the Hellas South Pole, is the 6 M€ still required if there are no oceans left to place?
ruling: Yes. Placing the ocean is ignored if oceans are maxed, but losing 6 M€ is not ignored and must be performed for the action to be taken.
quote: In the same way, placing an ocean tile is ignored if maxed, while losing 6 MC is not, and so has to be performed in order for the action to be taken.
author: Fryxen
heading: Hellas South Pole

question: Where can Lava Flows be placed on the Elysium and Hellas maps?
ruling: On the Elysium map Lava Flows has four new target sites. On the Hellas map it is playable without its printed placement restrictions, so it can be placed 'anywhere'. The restrictions are removed so players need not take cards out when switching maps.
quote: Lava Flows has four new target sites on the Elysium map. On the Hellas map, it will instead be playable without its printed restrictions, so it can be placed 'anywhere'.
author: Fryxen
heading: Lava Flows

question: On which of the new map sides does Lava Flows have designated target spaces?
ruling: On one of the two new sides the allowed Lava Flows spaces are marked in bold, as on the main board. (Per the other Hellas rulings, on the other side it can go anywhere.)
quote: One of the sides has marked in bold where it can go, just as on the main board
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Lava Flows

question: Can the Hellas & Elysium maps be used for solo play, and are their milestones and awards used?
ruling: The Hellas & Elysium maps are for 1-5 players. In solo play the maps' new placement bonuses and ocean configuration apply, but the new milestones and awards are not used.
quote: The new milestones and awards are not used in solo play though.
author: Fryxen
heading: Map contents and solo play

question: What does the Hellas & Elysium expansion add to play?
ruling: It is only a double-sided map with no new cards. Each side has 5 new milestones, 5 new awards, a new ocean placement configuration and many new placement bonuses; otherwise play is the same.
quote: Each side contains 5 new milestones and 5 new awards, a new configuration of ocean placements and a lot of new placement bonuses. However, the play is the same, just varied.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Map contents and solo play

question: Why do milestones and awards come in fixed sets per map rather than being randomized?
ruling: Sets can be designed for specific maps, are easier to balance, avoid overlapping milestones/awards, and are hard to expand with new balanced ones. Randomized milestones and awards give variation but do not improve the game; this is the designers' stated reason, not a ban on the variant.
quote: Using randomized M&As provides interesting variation, but it does not improve the game.
author: Fryxen
heading: Milestones and awards sets

question: Where may Noctis City be placed on the Hellas and Elysium maps, which lack the Noctis Labyrinthus spot?
ruling: On the new maps Noctis City can be placed anywhere (it loses its old reserved spot but is fully playable). Fryxen later clarified in another thread that it is placed like a normal city, see the 2017-08-24 ruling.
quote: Therefore, Noctis City can be placed anywhere, and will miss its old sweet spot, but be fully playable.
author: Fryxen
heading: Noctis City

question: On the Hellas/Elysium maps (where the rules insert says Noctis City may be placed on any non-ocean area), does the normal city restriction of not being adjacent to another city apply?
ruling: Yes. The map rules override Noctis City's exception, so it is placed just like a normal city: not on ocean areas and not beside other cities.
quote: The rules override the Noctis City exception, so it is placed just like a normal city (i.e. not on ocean areas, and not beside other cities).
author: Fryxen
heading: Noctis City

topic: Noctis City and Lava Flows placement
question: Where can Noctis City (and Lava Flows) be placed on the Hellas and Elysium maps; is the usual city-adjacency restriction dropped?
ruling: On the Hellas map, Lava Flows and Noctis City may be placed on any non-ocean area. On the Elysium map, Lava Flows must be placed on one of the 4 volcanoes (names in bold on the board) and Noctis City can be placed anywhere.
quote: On the Hellas map you may place Lava Flows and Noctic City on any non-ocean area. On the Elysium map you must place the Lava Flows on any of the 4 volcanos
author: EagleEye80
heading: Noctis City

topic: Noctis City and Lava Flows restrictions on Hellas & Elysium
question: Why do Noctis City and Lava Flows have no special locations on the Hellas & Elysium maps?
ruling: Thematic reasons: neither map has the Noctis region, and only Elysium has volcanos. Rather than requiring removal of those cards from the deck, the placement restrictions were removed for these maps.
quote: neither map has the Noctis region, and only Elysium has volcanos. Rather than demanding their removal from the deck we thought it simpler to remove their restrictions.
author: Fryxen
heading: Noctis City

topic: Noctis City and Lava restrictions on Hellas
question: Why not officially ban Noctis City, Lava Flows (140) and Lava Tube Settlement (P37) on Hellas instead of removing their placement restrictions?
ruling: The official map rules remove the placement restrictions of these cards rather than banning them, because sorting them out of the deck when changing maps is more effort and the rule makes switching maps easy.
quote: Because it is a bigger effort to sort them out from the huge deck than to just remove their restrictions. Makes it easy to switch maps as you like.
author: Fryxen
heading: Noctis City

topic: Noctis City and Lava restrictions on Hellas
question: Why are volcanic-area cards restricted on Elysium but unrestricted on Hellas, and could the cards be banned on Hellas instead?
ruling: Hellas has no volcanic sites, so the cards are unrestricted there by official rule. Fryxen agrees disallowing them would be more thematic and consistent, but the official rule stays as is for convenience; players who don't mind sorting the cards out may do so.
quote: BUT it a nuisance to try to sort those cards out when changing maps. That is why we chose the official rule. If you don't mind going through all the cards to sort them out, I think that is a more thematic solution.
author: Fryxen
heading: Noctis City

question: How were placement restrictions handled for earlier maps when the restricted feature was unavailable?
ruling: When Hellas & Elysium was released, Noctis City lost its placement restriction because it made the card unplayable, and on Hellas all cards restricted to volcanic areas lost that restriction so they remain playable. This avoids removing cards from the deck.
quote: Noctis City lost its placement restriction since it made the card unplayable, and on Hellas all cards restricted to volcanic areas lost that restriction to make them playable.
author: Fryxen
heading: Noctis City

topic: Phobos Space Haven on new maps
question: Does Phobos Space Haven keep its reserved placement area on the Hellas and Elysium maps?
ruling: Yes. Phobos Space Haven still has its reserved area in space; it is not freed to be placed anywhere on the new maps.
quote: Phobos Space Haven still has its reserved area in space, though.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Phobos Space Haven

topic: Poseidon first action with no legal colony placement
question: How should Poseidon's mandatory first-action colony be resolved when it cannot legally be placed on any colony tile?
ruling: No fixed official rule; use a house ruling that does not disadvantage the player too much. For the case where only Miranda is unavailable he would allow the colony on Miranda, since the alternatives (doubling up, fizzling, a 4th colony) are more intrusive or give an unfair advantage. An official ruling was not given.
quote: If you come across an edge case like this, do a house ruling that doesn't disadvantage the player too much (in this case I would allow a colony on Miranda
author: Fryxen
heading: Poseidon

question: What is the solo player's starting TR on the Amazonis Planitia board (13 generations with Prelude, 15 without)?
ruling: Starting TR is the normal 14.
quote: Starting TR is the normal 14.
author: Fryxen
heading: Amazonis Planitia

question: Is the Amazonis Planitia map playable with the MarsBot automa?
ruling: No. The automa does not support Amazonis Planitia: it was tuned for the pace of the standard-sized maps and can only simulate a 2 player game.
quote: No, the automa doesn't support that map, as it would have required massive changes to how it operated
author: njshaw2
heading: Amazonis Planitia

topic: Neoprene vs cardboard maps and M&A balance
question: Why do the milestones and awards differ between the neoprene maps, the cardboard maps and the Milestones & Awards tiles, and which are official?
ruling: The neoprene versions of the fan-made maps are the original fan-made versions; the cardboard maps are the official, FryxGames-rebalanced versions (the older maps and Amazonis are identical in both). Milestones and awards printed on a map are balanced only for that map, while the M&A tiles were balanced against each other, which caused a few changes; none were big enough to change the official maps.
quote: So when comparing the neoprene to the cardboard versions, the neoprene are the original fan-made ones, and the cardboard maps are the official ones.
author: Fryxen
heading: Cardboard maps and neoprene mats

topic: Cardboard maps vs neoprene mats differences
question: Why do the cardboard maps differ from the neoprene mats (names of milestones/awards, placement bonuses, region names, milestone balance)?
ruling: The cardboard maps are official and were changed from the fan-made neoprene mats: milestone/award names were changed to avoid duplicates with existing ones, the Mars projection differs so a couple of placement bonuses moved one step and some region names shifted, and milestones/awards were rebalanced so sets can be randomized. The neoprene mats were left unchanged as the fan community creation; they are not updated to the cardboard versions.
quote: We have one set of milestones and awards specifically balanced to be randomized, each map has its own set of milestones and award to balanced against each other, and the neoprene mats are the result of our wonderful fan community.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Cardboard maps and neoprene mats

question: If Mining Rights is placed on a space that gives both steel and titanium, do you get both production types?
ruling: No, you choose one of them.
quote: No, you choose one.
author: Fryxen
heading: Mining Rights

question: Is the 'or' between steel and titanium on a Mining Rights space inclusive, so both can be claimed?
ruling: No. Since you do not get 2 production for placing on a 2-steel area, it would be unreasonable to get both resources when they are different.
quote: Since you don't get 2 production for placing on a 2 steel area, it would be quite unreasonable to get both if they were different.
author: Fryxen
heading: Mining Rights

question: If Colonies is not used, how is the Terra Cimmeria MSL Curiosity placement bonus handled (ignore it, or pay the 5 M€)?
ruling: There is no official way to play without Colonies, but the intent is for products to be modular. When a map gives a bonus that does not apply to your setup, skip that entire bonus: the whole area loses both the colony bonus and the -5 M€ placement cost. (The statement that some awards and milestones may be removed was followed by a later post saying such awards and milestones are used normally.)
quote: when a map gives you a bonus or other feature that is not applicable to your setup, just skip that entire bonus. So some awards and milestones may be removed, and some placement bonuses may be blank.
author: Fryxen
heading: MSL Curiosity

question: With Colonies, if you have no valid spot to place a colony, can you still place a tile on the Terra Cimmeria MSL Curiosity space and pay 5 M€ for nothing?
ruling: No. If you cannot perform the placement effect (place a colony), you cannot place a tile on that space.
quote: If you can't perform the effect, you can't place a tile there.
author: Fryxen
heading: MSL Curiosity

topic: Constructor award and Planetologist milestone without Colonies/Venus
question: If playing Amazonis without Colonies, what happens to the Constructor award (cities and colonies), and likewise the Terra Cimmeria Planetologist milestone without Venus?
ruling: In both cases the number of colonies / Venus tags is 0 and the award or milestone is used normally; it is not removed. The Milestones & Awards product can be used to randomise goals and exclude the ones that do not fit.
quote: In both cases the number of colonies / Venus tags is 0 and the award / milestone can be used normally.
author: Fryxen
heading: Playing without Colonies or Venus

question: How do the 2v2 milestones and awards work, and can they be combined with the modular Milestones/Awards expansion?
ruling: They come on two double-sided tiles, one with 5 milestones per side and one with 5 awards per side, giving 4 combinations. They are balanced for 2v2 with higher demands and some are tailored to team play, so they cannot be combined with the modular Milestones/Awards.
quote: The milestones are balanced specifically for 2v2 with higher demands since it is easier to specialize in 2v2, and some of the milestones and awards are uniquely tailored to teamplay, so no, they can't be combined with the modular Milestones/Awards.
author: Fryxen
heading: 2v2 milestones and awards

question: If a corporation makes newly revealed milestones cost 0 to claim, does the Briber milestone still cost its extra 12 M€?
ruling: Yes, the Briber milestone's extra 12 M€ is still paid on top of the (reduced) claim cost. The corporation referred to is not named in the post.
quote: Yes.
author: Fryxen
heading: Briber (milestone)

question: Why are some map-printed milestones and awards, such as Polar Explorer, not included as tiles in the Milestones & Awards product?
ruling: Milestones and awards tied to a specific map feature (e.g. Polar Explorer and the south pole) were left out because they would be unthematic on other maps; a few may also have been too similar to others. New ones were added instead.
quote: Some milestones and awards are tied to features of their specific map, such as Polar Explorer being tied to the south pole. It would be unthematic on other maps, which is why it wasn't included.
author: Fryxen
heading: Map-specific milestones and awards

topic: Mixing map competitions with Milestones & Awards
question: Can the normal milestones and awards printed on a map (such as Polar Explorer) be used together with the Milestones & Awards tiles?
ruling: Yes, the pre-printed competitions can be combined with the M&A tiles. Fryxen describes a game where the M&A tiles were randomized, a couple that clashed were removed, and a couple of the pre-printed competitions on the board were used instead. The M&A tiles are balanced against each other so that competitions are equally attractive.
quote: Sure you can use normal competitions in conjunction with the M&A product.
author: Fryxen
heading: Map-specific milestones and awards

question: Why do some milestones in the new products have different requirements (Builder 7 tags, Terraformer 29 TR) than the original ones?
ruling: The new milestones were deliberately rebalanced against each other across maps (some maps had earlier milestones than others), with some extra general tweaks guided by data and feedback. The post does not say whether the originals must be replaced on existing maps.
quote: They were rebalanced to each other; some maps had generally earlier milestones than other maps etc, but these should all be competitive with each other.
author: Fryxen
heading: Milestone requirements

question: If a player holds the leader of the dominant party at game end, does that leader count 1 or 2 toward the Politician award (most Party Leaders and influence combined)?
ruling: It counts 2: one for being a party leader and one for the influence the dominant party leader grants.
quote: Yes, the dominant party leader would contribute 2 to the total.
author: Fryxen
heading: Politician (award)

question: Is a new chairman appointed at the end of the game before the Politician award is counted?
ruling: No. The game ends before the Turmoil step, so no new chairman is appointed at the end of the game.
quote: Game end is before the Turmoil step, so no new chairman is appointed at the end of the game (just clarifying).
author: Fryxen
heading: Politician (award)

question: Do space events count toward the space-tag milestone in Milestones & Awards?
ruling: No: space events do not count for the space tag milestone.
quote: For the space tag milestone, remember that space events don't count.
author: Fryxen
heading: Space tag milestone

question: Why are there no Hoverlord and Venuphile tiles in Milestones & Awards, and when are they used?
ruling: Venus needs those goals to be relevant enough, so the Venus award and milestone are always included when you use Venus Next.
quote: Yes, Venus requires those goals to make it relevant enough. That's why they're always in if you use Venus Next.
author: Fryxen
heading: Venus milestone and award

question: Must Arcadian Communities' first community (placed in the Prelude phase) be adjacent to the player's tiles?
ruling: No. The first community does not have the adjacency restriction.
quote: The first community doesn't have that restriction.
author: Fryxen
heading: Arcadian Communities

topic: Choosing and playing preludes in setup
question: When are Prelude cards chosen: in step 6 with corporations and project cards, or when preludes are played?
ruling: Step 7 starts with everyone examining their starting options (corporations, projects, preludes, colony tiles in solo), then players make all choices and discard unchosen cards (1 corporation, x project cards and 2 preludes). Then corporations are revealed and projects paid for, then preludes are processed. Preludes cannot be chosen during the play-your-preludes round; the Prelude rules should have said preludes are discarded together with the other cards.
quote: Then players make all their choices and discard their unchosen cards (1 corp, x projects and 2 preludes). Then corps are revealed and projects paid for, Then Preludes are processed.
author: Fryxen
heading: Choosing preludes

question: When do you choose your preludes: before any corporations or preludes are played, or in step 7b?
ruling: You choose your preludes (and other cards) before any corporations or preludes are played. The rulebook's discard wording did not foresee the fizzle rule; a more correct text would discard unchosen preludes at the same time as unchosen project cards and corporations.
quote: You still choose your preludes (and other cards) before any corps or preludes are played.
author: Fryxen
heading: Choosing preludes

question: Can players keep their options open and decide which preludes to play only after seeing others' choices?
ruling: No. The choice is made before revealing so it is not influenced by what others choose; no 'wiggle room' (e.g. against Recession). A fizzled prelude still gives 15 MC.
quote: The point of choosing before revealing is that the choice should NOT be influenced by what the others choose.
author: Fryxen
heading: Choosing preludes

question: Which step do the rules say the prelude choice is made in?
ruling: Step 6 is where you choose your cards, including preludes; step 7b says to play your PICKED preludes and discard the others, so the choice is made in step 6, not 7b.
quote: Step 6: Choose your cards, including preludes. Step 7b: Play your PICKED preludes and discard the others.
author: Fryxen
heading: Choosing preludes

question: If the discard in step 7b leaves room to change your choice unnoticed, is that allowed?
ruling: No. In 7b you play the 2 preludes that you picked in step 6, even if no one can tell whether you cheated. The discard should have been in step 6.
quote: The rule is that in 7b you play the 2 preludes that you picked (in step 6).
author: Fryxen
heading: Choosing preludes

question: Why is the prelude choice made in step 6, and may groups change it?
ruling: The reason is to make setup smooth and leave reacting to the action phase; the first player advantage is not considered significant. Groups can use a house rule if they prefer.
quote: But that is a matter of taste and you can go with a house rule if you prefer that.
author: Fryxen
heading: Choosing preludes

question: With Prelude and Venus Next, is the Solar Phase still needed?
ruling: The expansions are completely modular and can be used together, but the World Government Terraforming step can optionally be skipped.
quote: Completely modular, so yes, they can be used together. But the World Government Terraforming step can optionally be skipped.
author: Fryxen
heading: Combining Prelude with other rules

question: Is the starting TR reduced with Prelude, including in solo?
ruling: No. The Prelude bonuses are a replacement for the +1 production of each resource in the standard game; starting TR is unchanged. Solo play with Prelude lowers the limit to 12 generations, but you still start at 14 TR.
quote: Playing solo with Prelude lowers the time limit to 12 generations, but you still start at 14 TR.
author: Fryxen
heading: Combining Prelude with other rules

question: Should the basic game (no Corporate Era) be combined with Prelude?
ruling: Not recommended since Prelude in part simulates the basic game's fast start, but combining is allowed.
quote: Note that the basic game is in part also simulated by the Prelude expansion, so you shouldn't combine those (though you can).
author: Fryxen
heading: Combining Prelude with other rules

question: Does Prelude with Corporate Era make the game as long as a standard game, and what was Prelude meant to replace?
ruling: Prelude was meant as a replacement for the +1 production of each resource in the standard (non-Corporate-Era) game, but it doesn't focus the game on terraforming like removing the Corporate Era cards does, so play time is reduced less (about 15 minutes).
quote: it was meant as a replacement for the +1 production in the standard game, but it still doesn't focus the game on terraforming like removing the CE cards does.
author: Fryxen
heading: Combining Prelude with other rules

question: Does Eccentric Sponsor's 25 M€ reduction stack with other discounts and corporation effects, and can it play multiple cards?
ruling: It lets you play ONE card for 25 cheaper: a card costing 25 or less is free, a more expensive one costs the difference. Corporation effects are active when preludes are played, so discounts such as Teractor's apply (Large Convoy for 8 M€: 36 - 25 - 3). You cannot play multiple cards with it.
quote: It allows you to play ONE card for 25 cheaper. You can play a card for 25 or less for free, or a more expensive one paying the difference.
author: Fryxen
heading: Eccentric Sponsor

question: Can you play your two prelude cards in any order, e.g. a production prelude before Eccentric Sponsor to play Strip Mine?
ruling: Yes, preludes can be played in any order, even one that draws cards first to look for a better card for Eccentric Sponsor.
quote: You can even play one that draws cards to see if you can find better candidates for your Eccentric Sponsor (the real name of the card).
author: Fryxen
heading: Eccentric Sponsor

question: When is Eccentric Sponsor's card played: later in the game or immediately?
ruling: You play the card immediately when playing Eccentric Sponsor, as part of the prelude phase.
quote: You play it immediately when playing Eccentric Sponsor.
author: Fryxen
heading: Eccentric Sponsor

question: Must the card played with Eccentric Sponsor still satisfy its production decreases and global requirements?
ruling: Correct: the card played via Eccentric Sponsor still has to satisfy the cost of its production box (e.g. Domed Crater's -1 energy production) and its global requirements; only 25 M€ of its cost is reduced.
quote: Correct in both cases.
author: Fryxen
heading: Eccentric Sponsor

question: Can Eccentric Sponsor and Ecology Experts both apply to the same project card?
ruling: No. They cannot be combined to play the same card; each is played individually.
quote: They can not be combined to play the same card, no. They are played individually.
author: Fryxen
heading: Eccentric Sponsor

question: With Ecology Experts, do you still pay for the card played while ignoring its global requirements?
ruling: Correct: Ecology Experts only ignores global requirements; the card must still be paid for. Corporations are revealed after prelude cards are chosen, so the player must gamble on the corporation's effects.
quote: Correct in both cases. The Corporations are revealed after the prelude cards have been chosen
author: Fryxen
heading: Ecology Experts

topic: Tags and triggers in the same action
question: If Ecology Experts is used to play Decomposers, do Ecology Experts' tags trigger Decomposers?
ruling: Yes. Tags being played trigger every appropriate ability during the same action they are played. Worms counts old tags and its own tag still being played; Decomposers counts later tags and its own. If Decomposers is played with Ecology Experts it is all one action, and each Ecology Experts tag triggers Decomposers.
quote: If Decomposers is played with the help of Ecology Experts, is is all done in the same action and the EE tags each trigger Decomposers.
author: Fryxen
heading: Ecology Experts

question: Must the card chosen with Ecology Experts have a global requirement to be playable?
ruling: No. Ecology Experts lets you play any card you could otherwise play, ignoring global requirements; you must still be able to perform all its effects and fulfil any other requirements.
quote: It does not have to have a global requirement to play; you can play any card that you could otherwise play (must still be able to perform all effects and fulfill any other requirements).
author: Fryxen
heading: Ecology Experts

question: When a prelude (Ecology Experts) plays another card (Decomposers), do the prelude's own tags trigger Decomposers?
ruling: Yes. Order: check requirements and pay cost, tags come into play, then resolve the card's effects and anything the tags or effects trigger, in any order that does not apply an effect before its cause. The prelude's tags are considered played during the whole action, so Ecology Experts' plant and microbe tags trigger Decomposers. The app picks the order that gives the maximum benefit.
quote: Correct, although the tags are considered being played during the whole action, which is why the prelude tags could trigger the Decomposers.
author: Fryxen
heading: Ecology Experts

question: Why does Lava Tube Settlement refer to Lava Flows for its placement?
ruling: Lava Tube Settlement is meant to have the same placement as Lava Flows: the 4 unique volcanic spots on the base board, different spots on Elysium, and free placement on Hellas. It refers to Lava Flows because the Hellas & Elysium rules cannot be changed to mention the new card.
quote: This card should be have the same placement, but we can't go back and change the H&E rules to also refer to this card.
author: Fryxen
heading: Lava Tube Settlement

question: On Hellas, does Lava Tube Settlement's 'regardless of adjacent cities' apply, and where can the city go?
ruling: Official intent: on Hellas the city may be placed anywhere but must follow the standard city restrictions, i.e. it cannot be adjacent to another city. The 'regardless of adjacent cities' part only applies when placed on a volcanic area.
quote: the official intent is that on Hellas, you can place this city anywhere, but must follow standard city restrictions, i.e. no city adjacency.
author: Fryxen
heading: Lava Tube Settlement

question: On the base board and Elysium, once all four volcanic areas are covered, can Lava Tube Settlement still be played and placed on a non-volcanic area with normal city rules?
ruling: No. On those maps Lava Flows and Lava Tube Settlement are only playable if you can place on one of the volcanic areas.
quote: On those maps, the cards Lava Flows and Lava Tube Settlement are only playable if you can place on one of the volcanic areas.
author: Fryxen
heading: Lava Tube Settlement

topic: Pharmacy Union starting MC and microbe tag penalty
question: Can Pharmacy Union's player pay the 8 MC penalty for its two microbe tags before receiving the 54 MC starting money, i.e. start the game with 46 MC?
ruling: No. The 54 MC is starting money the corporation immediately starts with, not something gained after it is played, so the 8 MC penalty must be paid from the starting MC.
quote: Q1: No, you must pay from your starting MC.
author: Fryxen
heading: Pharmacy Union

question: When Pharmacy Union is played as the second corporation via the Merger prelude, can the player resolve the microbe tag penalty before receiving the 54 MC?
ruling: No. Merger does not change that the 54 MC are Pharmacy Union's starting money, so the player gains it immediately and therefore has the money to pay the Pharmacy Union penalty. Merger costs 42 MC, but 54 - 42 = 12 MC still covers the 8 MC penalty; if another way to lose MC at that time exists, this could change.
quote: Merger doesn't change that the 54 MC are PU's starting money, so they would gain that immediately and therefore have money to pay the PU effect penalty.
author: Fryxen
heading: Pharmacy Union

question: Are prelude cards project cards, can they get discounts, and do their tags trigger effects?
ruling: Preludes work like ordinary projects except for how you choose them and when you play them. They have no cost, so discounts don't help, but their tags can trigger other effects (e.g. a Jovian tag with Saturn Systems). You must be able to perform the effect in order to choose and play the prelude.
quote: Preludes work like ordinary projects except for how you choose them and when you play them. They have no cost, so you can't benefit fromm any discount
author: Fryxen
heading: Prelude cards as project cards

question: Do Prelude cards that add oceans or raise oxygen/temperature increase TR as normal?
ruling: Yes, all other rules apply to Prelude cards, so they raise TR as normal.
quote: Yes, all other rules do apply.
author: evilone
heading: Prelude cards as project cards

question: Do prelude cards count for the Tycoon milestone (15 blue and green cards)?
ruling: No. Even though they work similarly to green cards, preludes are not considered green.
quote: No, it's not counted for Tycoon. Even if they work similarly to green cards, they are not considered to be green.
author: EagleEye80
heading: Prelude cards as project cards

question: What happens if a prelude card turns out to be unplayable?
ruling: You must prove it to your opponents, discard it back to the box, and gain 15 M€.
quote: If you try to play a prelude card and it turns out to be unplayable for any reason, you must prove this to your opponents, discard it back to the box, and gain 15 MC.
author: Fryxen
heading: Prelude fizzle rule

question: What happens if a prelude cannot be played (fizzles)?
ruling: When playing a prelude, if it fizzles it is discarded back to the box and you gain 15 MC. You must show/prove to the other players that you indeed cannot play it, so this is not optional. The rule will enter future Prelude rulebooks and the FAQ.
quote: When playing a prelude, if it fizzles, it is discarded back to the box instead and you gain 15 MC. You must show/prove to the other players that you indeed cannot play the prelude, so this is not an optional thing.
author: Fryxen
heading: Prelude fizzle rule

question: How does the prelude fizzle rule apply to Ecological Experts, Merger, Business Empire and Donation?
ruling: Ecological Experts must still be played if you can afford any card in hand; only by showing a hand of unplayable cards can you discard it and take 15 MC. Merger is safer: if you can't play any drawn corporation (shown as proof) you get 15 MC. Business Empire with too little money fizzles for 15 MC. You can intentionally fizzle a first prelude and play Donation second; you still choose which prelude to play first.
quote: Only by showing the other players a hand full of cards that are too expensive or otherwise unplayable, only in that case can you avoid playing Ecological Experts, discard it, and get 15 MC.
author: Fryxen
heading: Prelude fizzle rule

question: When proving a prelude can't be played, must you show that another prelude could pay for it first?
ruling: No. You still choose when to play a prelude, so you only need to prove it can't be played at that time; other preludes are irrelevant. The rule does not affect your ability to choose preludes or their order.
quote: You still choose when to play a prelude, so you only need to prove it can't be played AT THAT TIME. No need to show the other preludes since they are irrelevant.
author: Fryxen
heading: Prelude fizzle rule

question: What is the Prelude setup order?
ruling: 1) Normal setup. 2) Choose starting projects, preludes and corporation, discarding the rest. 3) Play corporations in turn order and pay for the starting hand. 4) Play your 2 preludes in any order, then the next player, and so on. 5) Start the action phase; some corporations have a fixed first action. A prelude that draws cards may be worth playing before Eccentric Sponsor.
quote: Play your 2 preludes in any order, then next player and so on.
author: Fryxen
heading: Prelude setup and order

question: How are corporations and Prelude cards dealt and chosen, and can the draft be adapted?
ruling: As stated in the rules: deal 2 corporations and 4 Prelude cards to each player; players select the 1 corporation and 2 Prelude cards they want. Groups may adapt it to their style.
quote: Deal 2 Corps and 4 Prelude cards to each player. Players select the 1 Corp and 2 Prelude cards they want.
author: evilone
heading: Prelude setup and order

question: What is the exact order for Prelude setup: choosing, revealing, paying and playing preludes?
ruling: Everyone picks corporation, cards and preludes simultaneously; unchosen corporations, preludes and projects are discarded face down (corporations and preludes to the box, projects to the common discard pile). In turn order players reveal their corporation and pay for cards bought, resolving corporation effects that trigger on themselves (e.g. Splice). Then in turn order each player plays both preludes, one at a time, following all normal rules; tags on preludes apply when played and stay in play. Then generation 1 starts with the first player taking the first action.
quote: Player 1 plays both preludes, one at a time. Then next player goes and so on, following all normal rules for playing cards. Any tag on the preludes apply as normal when played, and then stay in play.
author: Fryxen
heading: Prelude setup and order

question: In what order should corporations and Preludes be revealed at the start?
ruling: Reveal all corporations before playing any Preludes.
quote: It is also important to reveal all corporations before playing preludes.
author: Fryxen
heading: Prelude setup and order

question: When playing Prelude, should Prelude corporations be shuffled in with the others, or should each player get one base/promo and one Prelude corporation?
ruling: Nick would say it's up to you: he shuffles all corporations together and deals, and says seeding one Prelude corporation into the deal per player would also be perfectly valid.
quote: I would say it's up to you really. I just shuffle the lot together and deal out. But seeding one prelude corp into the deal per person would also be perfectly valid.
author: njshaw2
heading: Prelude setup and order

question: Why is Research Coordination (wild tag) an automated card rather than a blue effect card if it works for multiple actions?
ruling: As an effect it would allow triggers outside the action phase and make duration hard to define; keeping the wild tag to the action phase also avoids it going out of hand when combined with Turmoil (ruling bonus, global events) and end-game scoring (jovians, awards).
quote: Having it as an effect opens up the possibility of triggers outside the action phase, and then it becomes much harder to define duration.
author: Fryxen
heading: Research Coordination

topic: Robotic Workforce with preludes and corporations
question: Does Robotic Workforce work on prelude cards with building symbols and on a building-tagged corporation?
ruling: Yes, it works with prelude cards that have a building tag and also with a building-tagged corporation.
quote: Yes, it works with the prelude cards as well :) ... It works with a building-tagged Corporation as well
author: Fryxen
heading: Robotic Workforce

question: Can Robotic Workforce copy the production of a Prelude card?
ruling: Yes, Robotic Workforce can copy the production of a prelude or a corporation. A few preludes were adjusted during development to avoid overly strong combos.
quote: Yes, Robotic Workforce can copy the priduction of a prelude or a corporation.
author: Fryxen
heading: Robotic Workforce

question: Can Robotic Workforce copy the production of Research Network (a wild-tag card)?
ruling: Yes. A 'building card' is a card with a building tag and when playing Robotic Workforce you can count the wild tag as a building tag; the digital version not allowing it was an overlooked case.
quote: It should work. A 'building card' is a card with a building tag, and when playing RW, you can count it as a building tag.
author: Fryxen
heading: Robotic Workforce

question: Does a card with a wild tag count as a tag-less card for Sagitta Frontier Services?
ruling: Yes, it counts for Sagitta, both for getting the resource when taking a tag-less card and when playing it. It does not count as playing a card with one tag.
quote: Yes, it counts for Sagitta, both for getting it when taking a tag-less card, and when playing it. It does not count as playing a card with one tag.
author: Fryxen
heading: Sagitta Frontier Services

question: How many generations does a solo game with Prelude last?
ruling: Solo play with Prelude involves fewer generations: 12.
quote: Solo play indeed involves fewer generagions. 12 to be specific.
author: Fryxen
heading: Solo game

question: Can Preludes be used in solo play, and does the generation limit change?
ruling: Preludes can be used in solo, but then you only play 12 generations, not 14.
quote: Preludes can be used in solo but then you only play 12 generations, not 14.
author: Fryxen
heading: Solo game

topic: Solo with Prelude and TR Solo
question: How does Prelude change the solo game, and what is the TR Solo variant?
ruling: With Prelude in solo you get 2 Prelude cards but only 12 generations instead of 14. TR Solo variant: the goal becomes reaching a TR of at least 63 in the allotted time, all other solo rules (e.g. Corporate Era) unchanged.
quote: Prelude gives you 2 powerful Prelude cards to jumpstart the game, but the allotted time is now 12 generations instead of 14.
author: Fryxen
heading: Solo game

question: What do Prelude and the TR solo variant change in solo play, and can they be combined?
ruling: Using Prelude cards lowers the time limit to 12 generations. Using the TR solo version changes the goal to 63 TR. Both modules can be combined with other solo constellations and with each other.
quote: Using prelude cards will lower the time to 12 generations. Using the TR solo version changes the goal to 63 TR.
author: Fryxen
heading: Solo game

question: Is solo play without Prelude cards legitimate?
ruling: Yes: solo without the Prelude cards is fine, with the standard 14 generations.
quote: Playing solo without the prelude cards is totally legit, just go 14 generations.
author: Fryxen
heading: Solo game

question: Does TR Solo have a way to raise TR directly?
ruling: Yes. TR Solo includes a standard project that gives 1 TR for 16 megacredits.
quote: Maybe I should clarify that the TR solo includes a standard project to get 1 TR for 16 megacredits.
author: Fryxen
heading: Solo TR63 mode

question: In solo with the 63 TR win option, if I already have 63 TR in the final round, do further actions such as placing a greenery still raise oxygen and TR?
ruling: Yes. Placing a greenery still raises oxygen (if not maxed) and TR, and its cascading bonuses still apply; the extra TR and board points still count for the score.
quote: An extreme case woul be placing a greenery increasing oxygen, gaining plants from placement, oxygen triggering the temperature bonus, which in turn triggers the bonus ocean, which gives even more plants from placement and triggering Arctic Algae.
author: Fryxen
heading: Solo TR63 mode

question: In the 63 TR solo variant with Prelude, when is the win checked and does end-of-game greenery placement count?
ruling: Directly after production is the solar phase, and at the start of it you check whether you have won with 63 TR. In final scoring you may place greeneries as normal; any oxygen increase and TR from those counts only towards your final score, not towards the win condition.
quote: those TR steps are not counted towards winning, only towards your final score.
author: Fryxen
heading: Solo TR63 mode

question: Why does Prelude solo use a TR goal instead of a VP goal?
ruling: Intent: the TR goal keeps the tension between terraforming and reaching a good score, opening new strategies and making more cards interesting.
quote: To keep the tension between terraforming and reaching a good score.
author: Fryxen
heading: Solo TR63 mode

question: In the final plant conversion of a TR Solo game, do greeneries raise oxygen (and TR)?
ruling: Not as the solo rules are written: greeneries placed in the final plant conversion do not give oxygen, because the rules were written for the terraform-all scenario where parameters are maxed; the designers did not want to complicate TR solo.
quote: we let it stand as it was, meaning that greeneries don't give oxygen in the final plant conversion.
author: Fryxen
heading: Solo TR63 mode

topic: TR Solo final conversion house rule
question: Is it fine to let the final conversion in TR Solo work normally (oxygen, TR, and heat conversion)?
ruling: The designer says an earlier comment saying otherwise was mistaken. He would logically have the final conversion work normally (greeneries giving oxygen and TR when possible, and heat conversion too), but this is his unofficial preference, not the rule as printed.
quote: Yeah, that was a mistaken comment in that I hadn't recently read the rules.
author: Fryxen
heading: Solo TR63 mode

question: Can the Prelude solo TR 63 goal be used without the Prelude expansion?
ruling: Yes; the TR 63 solo from Prelude can easily be played without Prelude as well.
quote: TR63 solo from Prelude (can easily be played without Prelude as well) makes quite a few cards more relevant (which was the point of designing it).
author: Fryxen
heading: Solo TR63 mode

question: Can the TR63 mode be used without Prelude?
ruling: Yes; the TR63 mode can be used whether or not you own Prelude. Its rules are not given in the post.
quote: the TR63 mode (which you can use whether you get Prelude or not)
author: Fryxen
heading: Solo TR63 mode

topic: United Nations Mars Initiative with Prelude
question: Does TR gained from Prelude cards count for unlocking UNMI's action in the first generation?
ruling: Yes. The whole setup counts as part of generation 1, so any Prelude card that gains TR also enables UNMI's 3 M€-for-TR action.
quote: Yes, so any Prelude cards gaining TR for UNMI, also unlocks their 3MC-TR action as well...
author: EagleEye80
heading: United Nations Mars Initiative

question: With Valley Trust, is Research 4 M€ cheaper because it has two science tags?
ruling: Yes. Confirmed: with the Valley Trust corporation, Research is 4 M€ cheaper (each of its two science tags counts).
quote: All very correct. :)
author: Fryxen
heading: Valley Trust

question: Is there an endorsed beginner analog to the Beginner Corporation for Prelude cards, such as +1 to all productions?
ruling: The designer says +1 production on all resources sounds good as a beginner substitute for preludes (slightly more worth than 2 preludes, offsetting less synergy potential). It may be used even with the Generalist milestone, since preludes could let another player claim it on the first turn anyway.
quote: +1 on all sounds good. It's only slightly more worth than 2 preludes, offsetting the fact that you get less potential for synergy.
author: Fryxen
heading: Variants and game balance

question: What official suggestions exist for reducing runaway leaders in 2-player games?
ruling: Suggestions: draft; limit game length (use normal WGT terraforming, or start with more preludes, e.g. draw 6 preludes and take 4); or try a merger variant where each draws 4-5 corporations and plays with 2.
quote: So how about drawing 6 preludes and taking 4 of them?
author: Fryxen
heading: Variants and game balance

question: What does 'including this' mean in Vitor's effect, and where can the VP icon be?
ruling: Vitor's effect also triggers on Vitor itself, in the same way other corporations and cards trigger on their own tags or effects. The VP icon that counts is any non-negative VP icon on the card, not only the one in the lower right corner.
quote: Vitor also makes it clear that you're looking for the VP icon, not necessarily in the lower right corner, but also if it would ever occur elsewhere on the card.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Vitor

question: What does 'VP icon' mean in Vitor's effect and why 'including this'?
ruling: 'VP icon' refers to the graphic element on the card, not to its function: this includes cards whose VP is '1 per X resources' (no VP yet when played) and excludes negative VP cards. Vitor's own effect counts itself (cards trigger their own effects), just as only the top-right jovian tag of Saturn Systems counts as an actual tag so it triggers itself once; Celestic's 'floater icon' is a precedent for referring to icons.
quote: The wording 'VP icon' refers to the graphc element on the cards, not to their function, which allows us to unabigously explain how it works.
author: Fryxen
heading: Vitor

question: How does Vitor's award funding ability work in solo play?
ruling: The award effect is not used in solo. Vitor's VP rebate still works and makes many more cards viable in solo.
quote: The Award effect is not used in solo, but that is a very minor part of its worth.
author: Fryxen
heading: Vitor

question: Is Vitor's funded award a fourth award, and what if all three awards are already funded?
ruling: It is one of the 3 normal awards, not a fourth. In the very unlikely case all three are funded before Vitor's first action, Vitor probably still wins because the others wasted money; it does not get to fund one. (The thread's original question about Vitor and fractional VP cards is not answered in this post.)
quote: No, it's one of the 3 normal awards.
author: Fryxen
heading: Vitor

question: Does Vitor's corporation effect trigger on itself even though the corporation card has no VP icon?
ruling: Yes. Cards, including this corporation, always trigger themselves if applicable (as Saturn Systems and Splice do).
