The wording demonstrates that the icon itself, not its value, is what counts: it triggers on animal cards even though they have no VP yet when played. Celestic is another example: it looks for the icon whether it refers to resources, an effect, VP or a requirement.
quote: Cards, including this corporation, always trigger themselves if applicable.
author: Fryxen
heading: Vitor

question: Does Vitor refer to the graphic VP icon (any VP icon on the card) rather than the operative VP symbol?
ruling: Yes: Vitor refers to the graphic VP icon wherever the VP icon appears, and in keeping with cards triggering their own effect it applies to Vitor itself. Celestic is the precedent: it looks for the floater resource icon regardless of where it is found on a card.
quote: And since we went for the graphic element with Vitor, wording it as we did makes it most clear.
author: Fryxen
heading: Vitor

question: If three awards are already funded, can Vitor's first action fund a fourth award?
ruling: Yes: it is an extreme corner case, but Vitor funds a 4th award since card functions overrule game rules when explicit.
quote: Vitor funds a 4th award, since card functions overrule game rules when explicit.
author: Fryxen
heading: Vitor

question: How does the wild tag work: is its type set once or does it change by action?
ruling: At any point during an action you may choose one tag type for the wild tag; it keeps that type for the whole action, and afterwards it has no type again. You can do this only once per action. Outside this time the wild tag has no type (counts as no tag). It can be used for milestones, tag requirements and cards that count tags.
quote: At any point during an action, you may choose a tag type (one, not two, and certainly not 3) for the wild tag. The wild tag continues to have that type for the whole duration of that action.
author: Fryxen
heading: Wild tag

question: Does choosing a type for the wild tag count as playing that tag (e.g. triggering Olympus Conference)?
ruling: No. Choosing a tag type for the wild tag does not count as playing that tag, and does not count as getting a new tag into play; it simply 'is' there for the duration of that action.
quote: choosing a tag type for the wild tag does not count as playing that tag (so you can't trigger Olympus Conference for example), and it doesn't count as getting a new tag into play.
author: Fryxen
heading: Wild tag

topic: Wild tag and Media Archives / Legend
question: Does a wild tag count towards Media Archives and the Legend milestone as an event tag?
ruling: No. Event tags are only counted while being played, since afterwards they are face down and not active; choosing what the wild tag is does not count as playing the tag. Media Archives and Legend use the event tag icon for simplicity but count event cards, not event tags.
quote: Media Archives and the Legend milestone use the event tag in the iconography, but this is only for simplicity and readability. They count event cards, not event tags
author: Fryxen
heading: Wild tag

question: Can Toll Station or Galilean Waystation count other players' wild tags, and when does a wild tag count as a specific tag?
ruling: No. The wild tag can only be chosen by the owning player, during the owner's action, if it is already in play. At all other times it counts as no tag (and can thus trigger Community Services). It does not apply to Toll Station/Galilean Waystation for opponents, to end-game scoring (awards, jovian multipliers), or during the action in which the wild-tag card itself is played.
quote: The wild tag can only be chosen - by the owning player - during the owner's action - if it is already in play
author: Fryxen
heading: Wild tag

question: Can the owner use their wild tag as a Jovian tag when playing Galilean Waystation, and does playing a wild tag trigger Aridor?
ruling: Yes, if the owner plays Galilean Waystation the wild tag can be chosen as a Jovian, as it would benefit Satellites. No, Aridor does not benefit from playing a wild tag.
quote: Aridor does not benefit from playing a wild tag, no.
author: Fryxen
heading: Wild tag

question: Does a wild tag count for the Diversifier and Ecologist milestones, and does playing a wild-tag card trigger anything?
ruling: It counts for milestones, since you claim a milestone in the action phase. Playing the card with the wild tag does not trigger anything, because the wild tag cannot be chosen while it is being played.
quote: It does count, since you claim the milestone in the action phase. Playing the card with the wild tag does not trigger anything though
author: Fryxen
heading: Wild tag

question: Does the wild tag (e.g. on Research Network) count as a tag of the player's choice while playing prelude cards during setup?
ruling: No. The wild tag only counts during the player's action in the action phase; during the prelude (setup) stage Research Network counts as a prelude card with no tag. It was limited to the action phase deliberately, to avoid problems with awards and Turmoil tag mechanics.
quote: Correct. Our first idea was that it would always count, but we quickly realized that this wouldn't work.
author: Fryxen
heading: Wild tag

question: Why does the wild tag not count when playing preludes, even though it would rarely matter?
ruling: Intent: the wild tag counting only in the action phase is a deliberate simplification. The designer prefers a rule that is straightforward almost always over one with a special case for preludes.
quote: I'd rather have a rule that is straightforward 99.9% of the time and counterintuitive 0.1% of the time than a rule that is intuitive 100% of the time
author: Fryxen
heading: Wild tag

question: Can Research Network's wild tag, used when performing an action, count as an animal or plant tag to trigger Arklight's effect?
ruling: No. Using the wild tag is not the same as playing a tag. Research Network's wild tag can increase the tag count, for example for requirements and milestones or to improve cards such as Cartel and Insects, but it cannot trigger effects such as Arklight's or Viral Enhancers'.
quote: Using the wild tag is not the same as playing a tag. It can be used to increase the count of tags for example to fulfill requirements/milestones, or to improve cards such as Cartel and Insects. It can not be used to trigger effects like Arklight, Viral Enhancers etc.
author: Fryxen
heading: Wild tag

question: If you play a different card, can your wild tag count as a plant tag and trigger Ecological Zone?
ruling: You can count your wild tag as any existing tag during an action, but you did not play that tag, so it does not trigger effects such as Ecological Zone. Only the tags on the card played that action are played. The wild tag also cannot be used while it is being played. It is good for requirements, milestones and cards that count tags (like Satellites).
quote: the wild tag can't be used while being played, so it wouldn't trigger even when it was played. The wild tags are good for requirements, milestones, and cards that count certain tags
author: Fryxen
heading: Wild tag

question: If Applied Science is your only card with a resource and has exactly 1, is the option to move a resource to another card invalid?
ruling: Correct: after paying the action cost Applied Science has 0 resources and there is no valid target, so the only choice is to gain a standard resource. Fryxen adds that trying to put the resource back on Applied Science would be a very fringe use.
quote: Correct. Although trying to put is back to Applied Science would be a very fringe use.
author: Fryxen
heading: Applied Science

topic: Applied Science and Board of Directors combo
question: Can Applied Science add a resource to Board of Directors, which is then used to draw a prelude in the same generation?
ruling: Yes. The Board of Directors resources are resources, so the combo works.
quote: Correct. That is a very fun combo indeed.
author: Fryxen
heading: Applied Science

question: If you pay 12 MC for the Board of Directors action and cannot play the prelude, do you discard it and get 15 MC?
ruling: No. If you do not actually play the prelude, the option to play it for 12 MC is invalid.
quote: No. If you don't actually play the prelude, then the option to play it for 12 MC is invalid.
author: Fryxen
heading: Board of Directors

topic: Board of Directors: trying an unplayable prelude
question: Can you try to play an unplayable prelude with Board of Directors and fizzle it?
ruling: His current ruling is that you cannot try to play a prelude that is unplayable, but he calls it a tricky rules situation. It is rarely relevant since you would waste a director resource for just 3 MC.
quote: my current ruling is you can't try and play a prelude that is unplayable, but it is indeed a tricky rules situation.
author: Fryxen
heading: Board of Directors

topic: Board of Directors: commitment and payment
question: When using Board of Directors to play a drawn prelude, when are the 12 MC and the director resource committed, and what if the prelude (e.g. Merger) then fails?
ruling: You can change your mind about playing the prelude until you have new information. Once you play it (e.g. Merger) you are committed; if it then fails the prelude fizzles and you get 15 MC for the 12 MC and director resource already paid.
quote: I would say you can change your mind about playing the prelude until you have new information. Once you play Merger, you're committed, and you can choose any of the corps.
author: Fryxen
heading: Board of Directors

topic: Board of Directors: playing a prelude known to fizzle
question: May a player use Board of Directors to play a prelude they know will fizzle?
ruling: Yes, you can choose to play a prelude you know will fizzle.
quote: You can even choose to play a prelude you know will fizzle.
author: Fryxen
heading: Board of Directors

topic: Board of Directors: preludes fizzle rather than bounce
question: Can a player be forced not to play a prelude with Board of Directors because it will not be possible to resolve it?
ruling: No. The game does not know what the player knows, and preludes fizzle (the player gets compensation) instead of bouncing back like other actions that cannot be resolved. Fryxen notes this is a tricky area with edge cases.
quote: Well, the game doesn't know what you know. And preludes don't bounce like other actions when they don't work out, they fizzle.
author: Fryxen
heading: Board of Directors

topic: Board of Directors: one prelude per generation
question: How many preludes can you take with Board of Directors per generation?
ruling: Only 1 prelude each generation, and taking it costs 12 MC.
quote: you only get 1 prelude each generation, and if you take it, it costs 12 MC.
author: Fryxen
heading: Board of Directors

question: Can you let players choose from more than 2 corporations?
ruling: The official rule is 2 corporations, to make people try weaker corps. There is a common house rule to choose from 3, which Fryxen thinks is fine, especially with the many corporations now. He thinks 4 is probably too many.
quote: there is a common house rule to choose from 3, and I think that's fine too
author: Fryxen
heading: Choosing from more corporations and preludes

topic: Optional rule: choose from 6 preludes and 3 corporations
question: What new optional rule does Prelude 2 add for selecting preludes and corporations?
ruling: Prelude 2 has a new optional rule to choose from 6 preludes (and 3 corporations). The exact dealing procedure is not described in this post. He also says there are new ways to get extra preludes and that some of the new preludes are expansion dependent.
quote: there is a new optional rule to choose from 6 preludes (and 3 corps).
author: Fryxen
heading: Choosing from more corporations and preludes

question: What is the intended starting selection with the Prelude 2 optional rule?
ruling: He considers 10 project cards, 6 preludes and 3 corporations a suitable selection for the current state of the game; 4 corps would be too much choice.
quote: I think 10 + 6 + 3 is a suitable selection for the current state of TM.
author: Fryxen
heading: Choosing from more corporations and preludes

question: What optional rule does Prelude 2 add for the starting choice of corporations and preludes, and can it combine with the Focus variant?
ruling: Prelude 2 adds an optional rule to choose from 3 corporations (and 6 preludes). It can be combined with the Focus variant: draw 1 corporation from the select pool and 2 from the general pool. The development team advises against more than 3 corporations.
quote: With Prelude 2, there will be a new optional rule to choose from 3 corps (and 6 preludes). It can be combined with the Focus variant to draw 1 from a select pool and 2 from the general pool of corps.
author: Fryxen
heading: Choosing from more corporations and preludes

topic: Optional rule: choose from 6 preludes and 3 corporations
question: What is the new optional rule in Prelude 2 about the starting selection?
ruling: A new optional rule allows you to choose from 6 preludes and 3 corporations, making it easier to find good situations for situational preludes.
quote: the new optional rule allowing you to choose from 6 preludes and 3 corporations
author: Fryxen
heading: Choosing from more corporations and preludes

question: How does the Prelude 2 'choose from more' option apply to the solo game?
ruling: Optionally choose your corporation from 3 instead of 2, and choose your 2 preludes (never 3) from 6 instead of 4. This makes solo a little easier and is suggested when using many extra cards.
quote: Prelude 2 added an option to choose your corp from 3 instead of 2, and choosing your 2 (never 3!) preludes from 6 instead of from 4.
author: Fryxen
heading: Choosing from more corporations and preludes

question: What is the new optional setup rule from Prelude 2?
ruling: Optional rule: during setup choose from 3 corporations and 6 preludes (rather than 2 corporations and 4 preludes), to make it easier to find a corporation and 2 preludes that suit your starting hand.
quote: This is also the main reason for the new optional rule from Prelude 2: Choose from 3 corps and 6 preludes during setup.
author: Fryxen
heading: Choosing from more corporations and preludes

question: Can the 3 corporations / 6 preludes setup be used without Prelude 2?
ruling: Yes, it can be used, but Fryxen would not use it with only base + Prelude, since it is designed for a larger card and corporation pool; choosing from 2 was meant to push players out of their comfort zone.
quote: Sure you can use it. But if you only play base + prelude, I wouldn't. It's designed to fit a larger card pool (and corp pool).
author: Fryxen
heading: Choosing from more corporations and preludes

topic: 'Including this card' counts its own tag
question: Does a Prelude 2 card whose effect counts tags 'including this card' count its own tag?
ruling: Fryxen answered 'Mostly correct' to a list in which this was answered yes: a card always includes its own tag (and possibly tags of other cards played in the same action) even when the text does not remind you. His reply only comments on points 3 to 7. The specific card is not named in the post (image).
quote: Mostly correct.
author: Fryxen
heading: Counting a card's own tag

topic: Double Down on Board of Directors
question: If Double Down copies Board of Directors, do you get 4 more director resources?
ruling: No. Double Down copies only the direct effect, which would put 4 directors on Double Down itself; since Double Down defines no use for them they cannot be collected, so you get none.
quote: Double Down copies only the direct effect, which means it tries to put 4 directors on ITSELF.
author: Fryxen
heading: Double Down

question: Can Double Down copy Preservation Program?
ruling: Yes: he saw it used at FryxCon to copy Preservation Program and get 5 TR without that prelude's negative ability.
quote: One cool use of Double Down I saw at FryxCon was when someone copied Preservation Program to get 5 TR without that prelude's negative ability
author: Fryxen
heading: Double Down

topic: Double Down copies only the direct effect
question: Can Double Down copy a prelude's ongoing (blue) ability such as Terraforming Deal's?
ruling: No. Double Down only copies the direct effect, not any 'blue' ability.
quote: Double Down only copies the direct effect, not any 'blue' ability.
author: Fryxen
heading: Double Down

topic: Double Down copying a prelude that fizzles
question: If you play Double Down to copy Merger and Merger cannot be resolved, what happens?
ruling: Double Down fizzles and you gain 15 MC instead. You cannot change the target once you have new information.
quote: If you Double Down on Merger and it fizzles, then Double Down fizzles and you gain 15 MC instead. You can not change target once you have new information.
author: Fryxen
heading: Double Down

question: If you cannot raise all colony tracks 2 steps, can you not play that prelude?
ruling: Correct: you need to be able to increase the colony tracks. Colony tiles that have not been activated yet (for example Miranda without any animal cards) count as having no tracks and do not block you from playing Early Colonization.
quote: Caveat mentioned already that colony tiles that have not been activated yet (e.g. Miranda without any animal cards) count as having no tracks, and so they don't block you from playing Early Colonization.
author: Fryxen
heading: Early Colonization

question: How much does Established Methods give and how must it be spent?
ruling: Fryxen thinks it was settled at 30 MC, and that you must then buy standard projects costing at least 30 MC.
quote: I think we settled on 30 MC, and that you MUST then buy standard projects costing at least 30 MC.
author: Fryxen
heading: Established Methods

question: Must the Established Methods money be spent right away in the Prelude phase?
ruling: Yes, spend it immediately during the Prelude phase.
quote: Yes.
author: Fryxen
heading: Established Methods

question: Why does the card say 'pay and perform' a standard project instead of just 'perform'?
ruling: The wording is there to emphasize that you cannot just sell patents. The post does not spell out further consequences.
quote: Yeah, the wording is to emphasize that you can't just sell patents.
author: Fryxen
heading: Established Methods

question: Can Cyberia Systems or Robotic Workforce copy Industrial Complex's production box, and what does it do?
ruling: Yes with both. You do not pay the 18 MC again, since it is not part of the production box. Copying it repeats the production effect: increase every production lower than 1 to 1 (not +1 in total). The production box includes any special rules attached to that production.
quote: Correct. The production box is not only the icons, but including any special rules attached to that production.
author: Fryxen
heading: Industrial Complex

question: When Kaguya Tech places a city, does Philares trigger?
ruling: Yes, Philares triggers since a tile is placed (it can be a big payout). The card was not yet published at the time and the wording may change.
quote: 1) Yes, Philares triggers since you place a tile (and it can actually be a quite big payout!).
author: Fryxen
heading: Kaguya Tech

question: If you play Kaguya Tech as Philares, do you get your Philares adjacency bonuses a second time?
ruling: Yes, you get your adjacency bonuses a second time. To get maximum use you would need a greenery tile completely surrounded by opponents' tiles, though 3 adjacencies is easily reached.
quote: Yep.
author: Fryxen
heading: Kaguya Tech

question: Do expansion-specific placement bonuses and restrictions apply on maps when you play without that expansion?
ruling: No. Bonuses and restrictions such as colonies, delegates and volcanic areas only matter in games with the corresponding expansions and maps; without them you can ignore them. The same goes for Noctis City: you can place it normally if there is no reserved area for it.
quote: If you play without those, you can ignore these bonuses / restrictions. Same with Noctis City; you can place it normally if there isn't a reserved area for it.
author: Fryxen
heading: Maps and expansion-coupled bonuses

question: Can a map's placement bonus tied to an expansion be ignored without that expansion?
ruling: Yes. If you play on a map with placement bonuses coupled to certain expansions, you can ignore the whole bonus if you do not play with that expansion.
quote: If you play on a map with placement bonuses coupled to certain expansions, you can ignore that (whole) bonus if you don't play with that expansion.
author: Fryxen
heading: Maps and expansion-coupled bonuses

question: Can the Nomads cube move back to an area it has already been in, or stay in its current area?
ruling: It can move back to an area it was in before, but it cannot 'move' to the area it currently stands in.
quote: 2) Yes, you can move back to a place you've already been, but you can't 'move' to the same area you're already standing in.
author: Fryxen
heading: Mars Nomads

question: Do the Nomads get ocean adjacency bonuses?
ruling: Yes, they get ocean adjacency bonuses as well as the placement bonus.
quote: 3) Yes, ocean adjacency too.
author: Fryxen
heading: Mars Nomads

question: Does the Nomads cube interact with Arcadian Communities markers (can the AC action be used where the Nomads are)?
ruling: The Nomads do not block Arcadian Communities placement. Since Arcadian Communities reserves areas, the Nomads cannot move there; the Nomads do not reserve their area, they only block tile placement there. The card was unpublished, so wording could change.
quote: Edit: Since AC reserves areas, the Nomads can not go there. In contrast, the Nomads doesn't 'reserve' its area, just blocks placement there.
author: Fryxen
heading: Mars Nomads

question: Do Land Claim and Arcadian Communities reservations block the Nomads?
ruling: Yes. The Nomads can only move to unreserved areas, so areas reserved by Arcadian Communities or Land Claim block them (with the wording at the time).
quote: Since they can only move to unreserved areas, both AC and Land Claim block it. With the current wording anyway.
author: Fryxen
heading: Mars Nomads

question: Do the Nomads get the placement bonus when the cube is first placed?
ruling: No, not when first placed. But the cube can be moved in the same generation to gain the bonus.
quote: And no, they don't get the bonus when first placing the cube. But they can move it to gain the bonus on the same generation.
author: Fryxen
heading: Mars Nomads

question: As Arcadian Communities, may you move the Nomads onto a hex with your own marker, or put multiple markers on one area?
ruling: No. Arcadian Communities reserves areas, so the Nomads cannot go there even if reserved for you, and Arcadian Communities cannot place multiple markers on the same area since the first one reserves it.
quote: No. AC reserves areas, so the Nomads can't go there, even if they are reserved for you.
author: Fryxen
heading: Mars Nomads

question: Which tile-placement triggers fire off the Nomads moving?
ruling: Mining Guild triggers off placement bonuses, not tile placement, so it triggers off the Nomads. Philares, Mars First and similar cards trigger off tile placement, which the Nomads do not do.
quote: Mining Guild triggers off placement bonuses, not tile placement (unless we changed the wording and I don't remember doing that), so Mining Guild does trigger off the Nomads.
author: Fryxen
heading: Mars Nomads

question: Does the answer for Mining Guild depend on the card's printed wording (older text referred to steel/titanium from placement bonuses)?
ruling: Fryxen concedes the Mining Guild text was changed in the third edition, so the outcome depends on which edition's wording a player has. No further resolution is stated.
quote: So then it depends on which edition you're playing with
author: Fryxen
heading: Mars Nomads

question: Can the Nomads be moved onto a space whose placement bonus you cannot fulfil (cannot pay the MC cost, no delegate or colony to place)?
ruling: Confirmed as correct: if you still cannot pay after gaining MC from other trigger effects you cannot move there. Delegates and colonies are not covered by the three exceptions (only global parameters at max, resources you cannot collect, and removing resources from any player), so if you cannot place a delegate or colony you cannot place on or move to a hex with that bonus. Oceans, temperature and oxygen at max do not block.
quote: Correct. With the caveat that expansion-specific bonuses like colonies, delegates, and volcanic areas (bold names) are only relevant in games with the corresponding expansions and maps.
author: Fryxen
heading: Mars Nomads

question: What counts as an empty area for placing Mars Nomads: not having a tile, or also no placement bonus?
ruling: An empty area means not having a tile. Fryxen confirmed an answer to this ('Correct').
quote: Correct, with just 1 exception: If you play on a map with placement bonuses coupled to certain expansions, you can ignore that (whole) bonus if you don't play with that expansion.
author: Fryxen
heading: Mars Nomads

question: When Recession makes opponents lose MC and decrease production while you own Mons Insurance, how much do you pay each victim?
ruling: 6 MC to each victim, since Recession's two parts (indicated by 'OR') are two different abilities that trigger independently on Mons Insurance.
quote: 6) 6 MC to each victim since it is actually two different abilities (as indicated by the 'OR') that trigger independently on Mons Insurance.
author: Fryxen
heading: Mons Insurance

question: When you cannot pay Mons Insurance claims in full after Recession, in what order are the payouts resolved?
ruling: The first player chooses the order of all effects (for example resolving their own refund first and then Mons Insurance to limit payouts to others). Which of the proposed splits applies is left open.
quote: The first player chooses the order of all effects
author: Fryxen
heading: Mons Insurance

topic: Recession with Mons Insurance: pay twice
question: If you play Recession while owning Mons Insurance, do you pay your opponents one claim fee or two?
ruling: You pay twice, because the 'OR' on Recession signifies two different effects, one for resources and one for production.
quote: You need to pay twice. The 'OR' signifies that it is 2 different effects; one for resources and one for production.
author: Fryxen
heading: Mons Insurance

topic: Discarding the card from the Venus track bonus
question: After receiving the Venus track 1-card bonus, can you discard that card for an effect such as 'Discard 1 card to terraform Venus 1 step'?
ruling: Yes ('Mostly correct'): the two icons are separate and the text does not require the discard to come before the Venus increase.
quote: Mostly correct.
author: Fryxen
heading: Order of effects

topic: Order of effects without an asterisk
question: Does 'Discard 1 card to terraform Venus 1 step' require discarding first?
ruling: No: without an asterisk the icons take precedence over the wording and the order of effects is up to you.
quote: Good point, but without an asterisk, the icons take precedence and the order of effects is up to you.
author: Fryxen
heading: Order of effects

question: Is the original Prelude required to play Prelude 2?
ruling: Officially yes, Prelude is required, because Prelude 2 alone does not provide enough preludes with 5 players and no other expansion. In most cases it would work without.
quote: Officially, Prelude is required, because it will not be enough with 5 players and no other expansion. In most cases it would work though.
author: Fryxen
heading: Prelude 2 requirements and contents

topic: Prelude 2 contents by expansion in play
question: How many Prelude 2 corporations, preludes and project cards are usable depending on which expansions are in play?
ruling: Prelude 2 has 54 cards. With Venus, Colonies and Turmoil all in play: 5 corporations, 25 preludes, 24 project cards. Venus only: 5 corporations, 19 preludes, 7 project cards. Colonies only: 5, 19, 3. Turmoil only: 5, 19, 8. None of those expansions: 5 corporations, 16 preludes, 0 project cards. Six project cards require two of the expansions. He notes the numbers may shift slightly in final card adjustments.
quote: If you don't use any of those expansions: 5 corporations, 16 preludes, and 0 project cards.
author: Fryxen
heading: Prelude 2 requirements and contents

question: Can any Prelude 2 project cards be used without Venus, Colonies or Turmoil, and are preludes tied to expansions?
ruling: None of the Prelude 2 project cards are suitable for play without expansions, so the number of usable project cards is zero. Each expansion has 3 preludes tied to its mechanics; some neutral preludes also reference them (for example one referencing planet tags and one using floaters) but not enough to upset balance.
quote: None of the project cards in Prelude 2 are suitable for play without expansions.
author: Fryxen
heading: Prelude 2 requirements and contents

topic: Removing Prelude 2 cards for a missing expansion
question: If you play with all expansions except Turmoil, which Prelude 2 cards must be removed?
ruling: Remove the 3 Turmoil-tied preludes and the 8 Turmoil project cards, plus a few cards that require Turmoil and another expansion. All cards are marked with any expansion they require.
quote: Yes, plus a few that require Turmoil and another expansion. All cards are marked with any expansion they require, so they will be easy to sort out.
author: Fryxen
heading: Prelude 2 requirements and contents

question: Are Prelude 2 corporations tied to expansions?
ruling: No. All the Prelude 2 corporations are independent and can be played with or without any expansions.
quote: All the corporations are independent and can be played with/without any expansions.
author: Fryxen
heading: Prelude 2 requirements and contents

question: Can Prelude 2 be played without the original Prelude?
ruling: Omitting the original preludes means lacking all the ordinary preludes, so they are meant to be played together. You can try Prelude 2 alone, but the designer does not want to be responsible for problems that might arise.
quote: But you can certainly try with only Prelude 2 if you want. I just don't want to be responsible for problems that might arise.
author: Fryxen
heading: Prelude 2 requirements and contents

question: Can Prelude 2 be used with only the base game?
ruling: Officially it requires the base game and Prelude. In theory you could use the 5 corporations and 15 of the 25 preludes (and none of the 24 project cards), but you really need Prelude 1 for it to be any good except for the corps; having at least one of Venus/Colonies/Turmoil is recommended, preferably two. Using the cards not dependent on those expansions does no harm.
quote: You really need Prelude 1 for it to be any good (except for the corps).
author: Fryxen
heading: Prelude 2 requirements and contents

question: Does the prelude refund (reveal and discard an unplayable prelude for 15 MC) apply only when Prelude 2 is included?
ruling: No. The rule is universal for preludes. They should have had it before Prelude 2, but the need was extremely rare.
quote: The rule is universal for preludes. We should have had it before Prelude 2, but the need was extremely rare.
author: Fryxen
heading: Prelude fizzle rule

question: When can the prelude fizzle rule apply, e.g. for secret prelude choices?
ruling: The fizzle rule is for mistakes and mishaps. Whenever you make a secret choice of preludes, one can be or become unplayable and then the fizzle rule applies. The WG Project action falls in this category since opponents are not shown your options.
quote: Basically, the fizzle rule is for mistakes and mishaps.
author: Fryxen
heading: Prelude fizzle rule

topic: Preservation Program played via Board of Directors
question: If Preservation Program is played in the action phase, is its 'skip the FIRST TR you gain' effect applied when you already gained TR that generation?
ruling: No. The effect is immediately active, but if you already gained a TR during that action phase, the Preservation Program opportunity (skipping the first TR) has already passed.
quote: Correct. If you already got a TR during that action phase, then the PP 'opportunity' has already passed.
author: Fryxen
heading: Preservation Program

topic: Recession: up to 5 MC and mandatory production decrease
question: Is Recession's MC loss up to 5 or exactly 5, and what if production cannot be decreased?
ruling: Up to 5 MC. The -1 MC production is mandatory, so if someone already has -5 MC production, Recession fizzles (discard it and get 15 MC instead).
quote: Up to 5 MC. But note that the -1 MC production is mandatory
author: Fryxen
heading: Recession

topic: Sagitta Frontier Services and event tags
question: Does Sagitta treat a card with only an event tag (such as Flooding) as a card with no tags?
ruling: No. An event tag is a tag, so playing a card with only an event tag gives 1 MC back (the one-tag amount), not the no-tag amount.
quote: An event tag is a tag. So playing a card with only an event tag would give you 1 MC back.
author: Fryxen
heading: Sagitta Frontier Services

topic: Sagitta with Merger and Head Start
question: Starting with Viron, Board of Directors and Head Start, how much does Sagitta give when Merger and Sagitta are played via Head Start?
ruling: Head Start's actions are separate actions performed while the Head Start action is suspended. Sagitta triggers on itself, on Merger played along with it, and on Head Start still being played (not twice). The total benefit is 12 MC plus what the other extra action of Head Start may give.
quote: Total benefit is 12 MC + what you may get from the other extra action.
author: Fryxen
heading: Sagitta Frontier Services

question: Do you have to be able to place the 2 delegates to play Sponsoring Nation?
ruling: Yes, you cannot play it otherwise. Delegates and colonies are not covered by the three exceptions (global parameter at max, collecting resources you cannot collect, removing resources from any player), so you must be able to perform them.
quote: Correct, with just 1 exception
author: Fryxen
heading: Sponsoring Nation

question: With a maxed temperature, can Kuiper Cooperative spend asteroids to raise the temperature to trigger Standard Technology?
ruling: Yes. Standard Technology triggers off using a standard project, even if it 'fails'. The rules for playing cards apply to any action: you pay for it and its effects must all be performed, with the 3 notable exceptions (e.g. raising a maxed global parameter).
quote: You can indeed do that. Standard Technology triggers off using a standard project, and you do that even if it 'fails'.
author: Fryxen
heading: Standard Technology

topic: Suitable Infrastructure triggers in Head Start chain
question: How often can Suitable Infrastructure trigger during a Head Start sequence?
ruling: It has 3 chances to trigger during that action, although the Head Start action itself might find it difficult to increase production.
quote: it has 3 chances to trigger during this 'action'
author: Fryxen
heading: Suitable Infrastructure

question: Is Terraforming Deal active outside the action phase, e.g. in the solar phase or for UNMI's action?
ruling: Yes, Terraforming Deal is always active, whoever's turn it is, so it triggers in the solar phase too.
quote: Terraforming Deal is always activated, so yes.
author: Fryxen
heading: Terraforming Deal

question: Is Terraforming Deal always active?
ruling: Yes: Terraforming Deal is always active; he had confused it with Suitable Infrastructure and edited the earlier post.
quote: Sorry, you are completely right, TD it is always active. I confused it with Suitable Infrastructure.
author: Fryxen
heading: Terraforming Deal

question: Can a prelude chosen with Valley Trust fizzle for 15 MC?
ruling: Yes. The Valley Trust action is initiated before you know you have a playable alternative, so it could fizzle and give 15 MC. In that case it is also allowed to choose an unplayable prelude even when you have playable alternatives.
quote: It is also allowed to choose an unplayable prelude in that case even when you have playable alternatives.
author: Fryxen
heading: Valley Trust

topic: Playing corporation and preludes at setup counts as actions
question: Does Suitable Infrastructure trigger during the prelude phase / setup?
ruling: Not quite as framed: playing your corporation and preludes during setup also count as actions outside the action phase, so effects tied to actions can apply there.
quote: Playing your corp and preludes during setup also count as actions I think, outside the action phase.
author: Fryxen
heading: What counts as an action

question: What counts as an action in the rules, e.g. for preludes, Head Start and final greenery conversion?
ruling: Everything that uses action mechanics counts as an action: playing your corporation and each prelude, and any card that lets you play another card creates a new action that suspends the original. Head Start creates new actions while its action is suspended. Even final greenery conversions count since they use a normal action mechanic. He frames this as a provisional ruling ('we'll see how long this holds').
quote: Everything that uses action mechanics are counted as actions.
author: Fryxen
heading: What counts as an action

topic: 'As your first action' means in the action phase
question: What does 'as your first action' mean now that preludes count as actions?
ruling: Effects like 'as your first action' must now mean 'as your first action in the action phase', so as not to interfere with the playing of preludes; this matches the original intent.
quote: effects like 'as your first action' must now mean 'as your first action in the action phase' in order to not mess with the playing of preludes.
author: Fryxen
heading: What counts as an action

topic: Wild tags outside the action phase
question: Can wild tags work outside the action phase, e.g. in preludes or final scoring?
ruling: Wild tags can work outside the action phase in quite rare cases, but not for final scoring. This applies to other effects that refer to actions as well.
quote: So wild tags can work outside the action phase, but the cases are quite rare, and it doesn't apply to final scoring.
author: Fryxen
heading: Wild tag

topic: Wild tag limited to the action phase no longer valid
question: Is the earlier ruling that wild tags only work in the action phase still valid?
ruling: No. That ruling was meant to exclude the solar phase and end-game scoring. Because cards now create actions outside the action phase, limiting wild tags to the action phase is no longer valid, though uses during setup are expected to be very rare. Things that behave like actions should be considered actions unless there is a special reason.
quote: Now it just seems to me that things that behave like actions should also be considered actions, unless there is a special reason for it not to.
author: Fryxen
heading: Wild tag

topic: Wild tag is a function reminder
question: Does a card with a wild tag count as a tag type or as no tag for awards such as Administrator (most cards with no tag)?
ruling: Fryxen says a wild tag is not a tag type but a reminder of its function, being able to count as any tag type. He does not state directly how it counts for Administrator or Highlander; he agrees with the poster that it does not count as an actual tag during award counting.
quote: Snake is right, a wild tag is not a tag type but a reminder of its function - tobe able to count as any tag type.
author: Fryxen
heading: Wild tag

question: When World Government Advisor raises a parameter, do you get the benefits, and do effects that trigger on another player's action still trigger?
ruling: WG Advisor and WG Terraforming simulate the World Government doing the work, not you, so the WG gets the associated benefits, not you. All effects that trigger when another player acts do trigger, including Arctic Algae and the like (Lakefront Resorts and Aphrodite were named in the question).
quote: Both WG Advisor and WG Terraforming simulates the WG doing the work, not you, so they 'get' all the associated benefits.
author: Fryxen
heading: World Government Advisor

topic: World Government Advisor and milestone counters
question: Does a global parameter raised by World Government Advisor count towards milestones that place a counter when you raise it?
ruling: No. It is the WG acting, not you.
quote: 1) No, it's the WG acting, not you.
author: Fryxen
heading: World Government Advisor

topic: World Government Advisor, Hydrologist and Homeostasis Bureau
question: Do oceans placed by World Government Advisor count for the Hydrologist milestone, and does raising the temperature with it give Homeostasis Bureau's 3 MC?
ruling: No to both. It is not you raising it but the World Government; you just advise them.
quote: In both cases, no. In principle, it's not you that do the raising but the WG. You just advise them.
author: Fryxen
heading: World Government Advisor

question: Does raising the temperature with World Government Advisor count towards the Thawer milestone?
ruling: No, that play was wrong. WG Advisor works like WG Terraforming from Venus Next: it is the WG that terraforms, not you, which is why you get no bonuses for it.
quote: It was wrong. WG advisor works like WG terraforming from Venus Next - it is not actually you who do the terraforming, it's the WG.
author: Fryxen
heading: World Government Advisor

topic: Arcadian Communities on a full board
question: What happens with Arcadian Communities when the board is otherwise full?
ruling: If the board is otherwise full, only Arcadian can place tiles, since it can reserve areas in advance with its communities.
quote: If the board is otherwise full, only Arcadian can place tiles.
author: Fryxen
heading: Arcadian Communities

topic: Arcadian Communities in the first generation
question: Can Arcadian Communities use its action in the first generation?
ruling: Yes. It can use its ability in the first generation, giving 2 communities in the first generation (including the one from its first action).
quote: Arcadian Communities can use its ability the first generation, yes, resulting in 2 communities the first generation (including the 1st action one).
author: Fryxen
heading: Arcadian Communities

question: Does Arcadian Communities get 3 MC for placing a tile on an area marked by the Land Claim event?
ruling: Yes. For Arcadian Communities a Land Claim marker works like any other area marked with their player marker: they can spread from it and gain the 3 MC when placing a tile on it.
quote: For Arcadian Communities, Land Claim works just like any other area marked with their player marker. They can use the Land Claim marker to spread from, and they get 3 MC refund for placing tiles on it.
author: EagleEye80
heading: Arcadian Communities

question: After a tile is placed on an area reserved by Arcadian Communities, does the reservation remain (e.g. 3 MC again when Kaguya Tech places a city there)?
ruling: Intent: you replace your reservation with the tile, and from then on it behaves like a normal tile/area again, so the reservation does not persist.
quote: The intent of Arcadian Communities is that you replace your reservation with the tile. So from that point, it behaves like a normal tile/area again.
author: Fryxen
heading: Arcadian Communities

question: If Directed Impactors places an asteroid on Asteroid Hollowing, do you also get Asteroid Hollowing's increase of MC by 1?
ruling: No. Placing an asteroid on Asteroid Hollowing via Directed Impactors only puts an asteroid resource there (worth 1/2 VP); it does not also give the MC increase of 1 that the question asked about.
quote: No. It just puts an asteroid there (worth 1/2 VP)
author: Fryxen
heading: Asteroid Hollowing

question: Can Bactoviral Research be played if you have no card that can hold microbes?
ruling: Yes. Not being able to collect resources you gain is one of the 3 exceptions to the rule that all effects must be carried out.
quote: Yes, it can. Not being able to collect resources you gain is one of the 3 exceptions to the rule that all effects must be carried out.
author: Fryxen
heading: Bactoviral Research

question: Does Crash Site Cleanup require that some player actually removed another player's plants this generation?
ruling: Fryxen confirms ('correct') the reading that the requirement is that any player has removed another player's plants this generation, and that at least one plant must actually have been removed (merely being able to remove some does not count).
quote: correct.
author: Fryxen
heading: Crash Site Cleanup

question: In solo, does removing plants from the invisible opponent (e.g. with Virus) enable Crash Site Cleanup?
ruling: Yes ('correct'): trashing plants from the invisible opponent counts as something actually happening, as with Mons Insurance in solo, so playing a card like Virus enables Crash Site Cleanup.
quote: correct.
author: Fryxen
heading: Crash Site Cleanup

question: Which resources count towards the 9 different resource types required by Diversity Support, and do standard resources count?
ruling: It requires 9 different types of resources, which can be MC, plants, heat, microbes, floaters etc.: the standard resources count as well as card resources.
quote: Yes, it requires 9 different types of resources, which can be MC, plants, heat, microbes, floaters etc.
author: Fryxen
heading: Diversity Support

question: Do resources placed by Self-Replicating Robots count as a type for Diversity Support or for the Eccentric milestone?
ruling: No. The resources placed by Self-Replicating Robots have no type, so they are not applicable to playing Diversity Support or counting for Eccentric. They are also on a card that is not in play, which disqualifies them for Eccentric as well.
quote: The resources placed by Self-replicating Robots have no type, and are thus not applicable to playing Diversity Support or counting for Excentric.
author: Fryxen
heading: Diversity Support

question: Does Double Down copy a prelude's tags, so that copying an Earth-tag prelude triggers Point Luna?
ruling: No. Double Down copies just the direct effects of the prelude card, not its tags, so it does not trigger Point Luna.
quote: No, just the direct effects of the prelude card, so no tag and therefore no trigger of Point Luna.
author: Fryxen
heading: Double Down

topic: Merger: first actions of two corporations
question: If both corporations a player has (via Merger) have a first action, how do they work?
ruling: Both are part of your first action, just like playing a card with multiple effects.
quote: If both corporations have a '1st action', then they are both part of your first action, just like playing a card with multiple effects.
author: Fryxen
heading: First actions

question: If Merger gives two corporations with a 'first action', how are they handled?
ruling: If you have two 'first actions' they are both done during your first action. If you play Merger during your first action, the new corporation's first action is also performed immediately.
quote: If you now have 2 'first actions', they are both done during your first action. If you play Merger during your first action, any 'first action' on the new corp is also immediately performed
author: Fryxen
heading: First actions

question: If a first-action effect (Valley Trust) leads to Merger and a new corporation with its own first action (Philares), is that one action or two?
ruling: The first action is still just one action; many things can happen in it, just as when playing a card with multiple effects.
quote: The first action is still just one action, but many things can happen in that action, just as when you play a card with multiple effects.
author: Fryxen
heading: First actions

topic: First action of the game: multiple sources
question: What happens when several cards give a 'first action' (e.g. two corporations via Merger, or Head Start)?
ruling: Multiple first actions are performed during the same first action. If you get more first actions through Merger, just do them before other actions.
quote: No, multiple first actions are performed during the same first action. And if you get more first actions through Merger, just do them before other actions.
author: Fryxen
heading: First actions

question: How should '1st action' be read when a corporation is played after the first action has already passed (Merger via Board of Directors or a WG Project)?
ruling: Interpret '1st action' as 'next available action'. If you have two, Fryxen's ruling is that they stack up and are done together right away; the alternative is to let them occupy the first two actions.
quote: following the intended effect would be to interpret '1st action'¨as 'next available action', and, if you have 2, either have them stack up (my ruling), or let them occupy the first 2 actions.
author: Fryxen
heading: First actions

question: Is Floyd Continuum an official card?
ruling: No. It was made for the Dutch Open tournament in collaboration with FryxGames, but it is unofficial and has never been printed in the same material as the other cards.
quote: It was made for the Dutch Open tournament, it is an inofficial card, but it was made in collaboration with us at FryxGames for the tournament. So it is not official
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Floyd Continuum

question: Do the 2021 Season Promo printings of Harvest ('Gasin 12 M€') and Bio Printing Facility ('Speciese') really contain typos?
ruling: Yes, the latest printing of the 2021 Season Promo Cards has these typos: Harvest should read 'Gain 12 M€' and Bio Printing Facility's flavour text 'Species'. They are only typos, not game-changing text, and the cards will not be reprinted.
quote: I can confirm that the latest printing of 2021 Season Promo Cards do have these typos, unfortunately.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Harvest

question: Is the first action of Head Start the first action of the game, and what does 'immediately' mean?
ruling: The first action of Head Start is indeed the first action, triggering Inventrix and the like. 'Immediately' stresses that it happens before the action phase. You still get the 2 actions even if you have a corporation-defined first action; that first action is just defined.
quote: The first action of Head Start is indeed the first action, triggering Inventrix and the like. We wrote 'immediately' to stress that this was before the action phase.
author: Fryxen
heading: Head Start

question: Can you combo Tharsis Republic's first-action city with Rover Construction using Head Start's actions?
ruling: No: you can't combo Tharsis with Rover Construction before the first-action city. You could do it with Excentric Sponsor or Ecological Experts, since those don't count as regular actions.
quote: This does however mean that you can't combo Tharsis with Rover Construction before the first action city. But you could do it with Excentric Sponsor or Ecological Experts, since these don't count as regular actions.
author: Fryxen
heading: Head Start

question: Can the effects and the two actions of Head Start be resolved in any order, and can they be separated or skipped?
ruling: Under the 'bag of effects' principle, playing Head Start leaves 4 separate effects (2 MC per hand card, gain 2 steel, take 1 action, take 1 action) to resolve in any order, including triggered effects. The two actions can be separated, but cannot be interrupted by other effects. He also said the actions may be skipped, which he retracted on 2023-01-20.
quote: you can skip these actions if you like, and also that you can't interrupt these actions with other effects since they are themselves each a separate effect.
author: Fryxen
heading: Head Start

question: Are the actions or card plays of Head Start, Excentric Sponsor and Ecological Experts optional?
ruling: No. None of these preludes say you can skip their action/card play, so they are all mandatory. Worst case for Head Start is having only the sell patents action available.
quote: None of the Preludes Head Start, Excentric Sponsor and Ecological Experts say that you can skip their action/card play, so they are all mandatory.
author: Fryxen
heading: Head Start

question: Can you skip Head Start's two actions if your only possible action is selling patents?
ruling: No, you cannot skip the actions since the card doesn't say so; the earlier statement that they could be skipped was wrong.
quote: No, you can not skip the actions since the card doesn't say so. The cited comment was wrong in this regard.
author: Fryxen
heading: Head Start

question: With Head Start, must you perform a corporation-specific first action (Tharsis, VITOR, Poseidon, MSI, etc.)?
ruling: Yes, you must perform it if your corporation has one. The idea is that you start 2 actions earlier, whether or not you have a fixed first action.
quote: Yes, you must if you have one. The idea is that you start 2 actions earlier, whether you have a fixed first action or not.
author: Fryxen
heading: Head Start

question: Can Helion and Stormcraft Incorporated be combined so floaters pay as 2 MC each?
ruling: Yes. Helion works together with Stormcraft, so Stormcraft's floaters can be used as 2 MC each.
quote: Helion works together with Stormcraft so you can use Stormcraft's floaters as 2 MC each.
author: Fryxen
heading: Helion

question: Does Homeostasis Bureau's 3 MC apply per temperature step, so a 2-step increase from Giant Ice Asteroid gives 6 MC?
ruling: Yes. The extra 3 MC is gained per temperature step raised.
quote: Yes.
author: Fryxen
heading: Homeostasis Bureau

question: Is 'desease' in the Hospitals card text a misprint?
ruling: Yes, the card text misspells 'disease'; it was printed in a hurry. It is only a typo.
quote: Yes, unfortunately we were in too much of a hurry when we needed to print these :(
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Hospitals

question: Is the Lawsuit promo playable in solo, given the neutral player cannot attack you?
ruling: Not playable.
quote: Not playable.
author: Fryxen
heading: Law Suit

question: If Lawsuit is drawn in solo, may you remove or redraw it?
ruling: No, there is no rule allowing that, and no rule to sort cards out of the deck for solo play. Fryxen adds that promo cards are optional material, so a group can pretend it is not there or not play with it.
quote: No, there is no rule allowing that.
author: Fryxen
heading: Law Suit

question: If a player plays Mons Insurance, can another player play Law Suit against that player because of the production decrease?
ruling: No. Law Suit requires that an opponent decreased your production, but Mons Insurance has an asterisk and bold text saying you decrease your own production yourself, so no opponent decreased it.
quote: Law Suit is not applicable anyway, since it requires that an opponent decreased your production, but Mons Insurance specifies with an asterisk and bold text that you do it yourself.
author: Fryxen
heading: Law Suit

question: When Merger says 'Then pay 42 MC', can the new corporation's starting steel or titanium be used toward the payment as if playing a card?
ruling: No. Merger says pay 42 MC, so it must be paid in MC only; steel and titanium cannot be used. Paying first and then getting the effect matches the normal order of playing cards and actions.
quote: No, it is not a correct interpretation since it doesn't say so. It says pay 42 MC. Period.
author: Fryxen
heading: Merger

question: What happens if you cannot pay the 42 MC for Merger?
ruling: Formally it is the same as any prelude you can't afford (e.g. Business Empire after spending all your money on cards): the card can't be played and is taken back, and since there is no other chance to play preludes, its benefit is lost.
quote: Formally, this is the same as when you play another prelude that you can't afford, for example Business Empire when you've spent all your money on cards: The card can't be played and is taken back.
author: Fryxen
heading: Merger

question: If no drawn corporation lets you afford Merger's 42 MC, is there an official fix?
ruling: No general or house rule is given. Fryxen would improvise a temporary exception in the rare case, for example drawing corporations until you can play one, and would allow retroactively buying fewer cards if Business Empire is unaffordable.
quote: Rather than having a general rule or even house rule for this, I'd make up some temporary exception in the rare case this should happen.
author: Fryxen
heading: Merger

topic: Merger when the new corporation cannot be paid
question: What happens if after drawing corporations with Merger the player cannot pay the 42 MC?
ruling: Strictly speaking Merger fails and you get nothing. As a house rule Fryxen would personally continue to draw corporations until one can be played, and advises saving a little MC (about 7) so the risk is practically zero.
quote: If it should happen, strictly speaking, the Merger fails and you get nothing. If it happened in my group, I think I would personally house-rule that you continue to draw corps until you can play one.
author: Fryxen
heading: Merger

topic: Merger when the new corporation cannot be paid
question: How likely is it that Merger fails for lack of MC, and what would Fryxen do in a casual game when it does?
ruling: Fryxen calculates the failure risk as very low when saving some MC (saving 7 MC gives 0 percent risk in base plus Prelude and with all corporations) and worst when the other prelude is Business Empire played after Merger. In casual play he would simply allow the player to draw more corporations until they get one they can play.
quote: If it happened in my group during casual play, I'd simply allow them to draw more corps until they get one they can play.
author: Fryxen
heading: Merger

question: Do you really get the effects of both corporations when using Merger (e.g. Ecoline and Tharsis Republic)?
ruling: Yes, you get all the effects and resources from both corporations.
quote: Yes, you get all the effects and resources from both corporations.
author: Fryxen
heading: Merger

question: Are there limitations on the timing of buying cards and paying for Merger?
ruling: Two limitations: you must buy your project cards with the cash of the first corporation before seeing and choosing your second one, and you must be able to pay the 42 MC after playing the second corporation.
quote: You must buy your project cards from the cash of the first corp, before seeing & choosing your second one. And you must be able to pay the 42 MC after playing the second corp.
author: Fryxen
heading: Merger

topic: Mons Insurance production decrease and replacement effects
question: When another player plays Mons Insurance, could a player with an effect letting them decrease a different production instead (hypothetical 'weird Helion') choose that alternative?
ruling: Yes: a hypothetical corporation that lets you decrease heat production instead of M€ production would let its owner choose that when Mons Insurance is played, because each affected player performs the decrease themselves.
quote: 1) yes, a 'weird Helion' would work.
author: Fryxen
heading: Mons Insurance

question: Can Helion pay Mons Insurance payouts with heat, and what does the receiver get?
ruling: Helion may be used to pay Mons Insurance payouts, but the receiver gets MC: you pay an amount and the other player receives the same amount, and Helion only affects what you pay. The receiver cannot force you to use heat even if you lack MC, because using heat as MC is your optional ability.
quote: Helion may be used to pay for Mons Insurance payouts, but the receiver gets MC [...]. The receiver can not force you to use heat, even if you don't have enough money, since it is your optional ability, not theirs.
author: Fryxen
heading: Mons Insurance

topic: Mons Insurance with Stormcraft and Helion
question: With Mons Insurance, Stormcraft Incorporated and Helion together, can floaters be used to pay Mons Insurance payouts?
ruling: Yes, you can use floaters for the Mons payment and the receiving player gets the corresponding MC. The active player still determines when you do the payout. (This point 6 was edited after the first version.)
quote: In a hypothetical scenario of combining Mons + Stormcraft + Helion [...] you can use floaters for Mons payment, the player receiving the corresponding MC. The active player still determines when you do the payout however.
author: Fryxen
heading: Mons Insurance

topic: Mons Insurance with Stormcraft and Helion
question: When a Mons Insurance payout is paid with Helion heat or Stormcraft floaters, does the receiver get heat or a floater instead of MC?
ruling: Fryxen admits he got it wrong in the first version of point 6 (which had the receiver getting a floater): the receiver gets MC, and the post was corrected.
quote: Yeah, sorry, got that wrong. It is corrected now. Tricky, these cases...
author: Fryxen
heading: Mons Insurance

question: Mons Insurance plays Flooding with its last money: in what order do the ocean, attack and insurance payout resolve?
ruling: The ocean must be placed first (to determine the victim); its TR, adjacency and placement bonuses go into the pool. The player may resolve the attack before those; it triggers the Mons Insurance payout, which is added to the pool and may be resolved even if the player cannot afford it (allowed by that effect). Only then the ocean bonuses are resolved.
quote: The player resolves the insurance payout but has no money for it (which is ok according to that effect). Only then does the player continue with the ocean bonuses, gaining TR, MC and whatnot.
author: Fryxen
heading: Mons Insurance

topic: Pharmacy Union starting card draw timing
question: When does Pharmacy Union's draw of a science-tag card happen, and how does it work?
ruling: It works like previous examples (reveal cards until a science tag card is found, take it, discard the rest) but is done when the corporation is revealed, not on the first turn, just like the timing of similar preludes.
quote: Yes, it works the same as previous examples, but is done when it is revealed instead of the first turn (just like the timing of similar preludes).
author: Fryxen
heading: Pharmacy Union

topic: Pharmacy Union: microbe and science tag order
question: If you play a card with both a microbe tag and a science tag while Pharmacy Union has no disease, and you resolve the science tag first to flip the corporation, what happens to the microbe tag?
ruling: Both tags trigger at the same time and may be resolved in the order of your choice, but all must be resolved. If you resolve science first and flip Pharmacy Union, the microbe trigger still resolves: the disease is not added (a resource you cannot collect is ignored, one of the three exceptions) but you still lose 4 MC (or as much as you can).
quote: you can ignore effects collecting resources you can't collect (one of the famous 3 exceptions), so the microbe trigger is resolved by you losing 4 MC and NOT getting a dicease resource.
author: Fryxen
heading: Pharmacy Union

topic: Pharmacy Union: flipping does not cancel triggered effects
question: Does flipping Pharmacy Union face down remove effects of tags that already triggered but are not yet resolved?
ruling: No. Both tags trigger together and no tag takes precedence. Flipping the corporation prevents further triggerings but does not remove effects that have already been triggered and are waiting to be resolved.
quote: The corp flipping is preventing further triggerings, but does not remove effects already triggered.
author: Fryxen
heading: Pharmacy Union

topic: Pharmacy Union: triggered text is stored until resolved
question: When a card triggers two Pharmacy Union effects, is the triggered effect's text or its outcome fixed at trigger time?
ruling: The triggering text itself is stored until resolved, not its result or choice. Resolving the microbe tag first adds a disease and costs 4 MC, after which the science tag must remove that disease for 1 TR (the flip option is no longer available). Resolving science first with no disease flips the corporation, and the waiting microbe trigger still resolves: the disease is skipped and you lose 4 MC or as much as possible. Likewise a pending 3 TR would not fizzle because the corporation flipped.
quote: It is not the result or choice of the trigger that is stored, but the triggered text itself.
author: Fryxen
heading: Pharmacy Union

topic: Pharmacy Union: Research with no diseases
question: If you play Research (two science tags) while Pharmacy Union has no diseases, is the play legal?
ruling: Yes. Both science tags trigger and the first resolves normally; because Pharmacy Union's flip effect says 'may', the effect is allowed to be ignored, so the play is legal. (Fryxen edited this post after realising an earlier version of the card without 'may' was being discussed.)
quote: Because it says 'may' on the effect, this effect is allowed to be ignored, so the play is legal.
author: Fryxen
heading: Pharmacy Union

topic: Tag icon with a text explanation (draw a card with a tag)
question: Does the iconography on Pharmacy Union's starting draw imply it happens as a first action like other corporations' draws?
ruling: No. The timing is not part of the iconography. The tag shown on the icon acts as a kind of asterisk and is explained in the text; corporations and preludes have used the same iconography with different timing before, and the procedure to get the card is always the same.
quote: the timing is not part of the iconography
author: Fryxen
heading: Pharmacy Union

topic: Pharmacy Union: science plus microbe ruling stands
question: Does removing Pharmacy Union from play (flipping it) let you fizzle a microbe trigger that is waiting to be resolved?
ruling: No. In the case of a science tag plus a microbe tag the earlier ruling stands: removing Pharmacy Union from play changes the game state, but does not allow you to fizzle effects that are waiting to be resolved.
quote: Removing PU from play does change the game state, but it does not allow you to fizzle effects that are waiting to be resolved.
author: Fryxen
heading: Pharmacy Union

topic: Pharmacy Union: placed in event pile
question: In its final version, what happens to Pharmacy Union when it is flipped, and does it count as playing an event?
ruling: The final version of Pharmacy Union is put in the event pile when flipped, so it counts as a played event for Media Archive and the event milestone. It does not trigger Media Group or Interplanetary Cinematics because it does not count as PLAYING an event tag.
quote: the final version of PU actually puts PU in the event pile (to count as a played event). This is useful for Media Archive and taking the event milestone.
author: Fryxen
heading: Pharmacy Union

topic: Pharmacy Union: scope of 'may' on the flip option
question: With one disease on Pharmacy Union, you play Research. How do the two science triggers resolve, and what does 'may' cover?
ruling: Resolving the first trigger removes the disease and gains 1 TR; resolving the second, with no disease left, you may place Pharmacy Union in the event pile and gain 3 TR. The 'may' covers the whole 'remove + 3 TR' option, so you may not gain 3 TR without removing Pharmacy Union, nor remove it without gaining 3 TR.
quote: The 'may' refers to the whole 'remove + 3 TR', so you may not gain 3 TR without removing PU, and you may not remove PU without gaining 3 TR.
author: Fryxen
heading: Pharmacy Union

topic: Pharmacy Union: scope of 'may' on the flip option (confirmation)
question: Does the 'may' on Pharmacy Union's flip effect cover only the 3 TR or the whole option including removing the corporation?
ruling: The 'may' refers to the whole option, both removing Pharmacy Union (flipping it) and gaining 3 TR: you can do both or skip both. Playing Research with no diseases is therefore fine, since the second science trigger can be skipped.
quote: The 'may' refers to that whole option, i.e. both removing PU and gaining 3 TR, so you can do both or skip both.
author: Fryxen
heading: Pharmacy Union

topic: Pharmacy Union: resolution uses current game state
question: When two science tags trigger Pharmacy Union at once, are their outcomes fixed when triggered?
ruling: No. Both tags trigger and wait to be resolved with their outcome not yet determined; the first resolution changes the game state so the other resolution must respond to the current game state (for example Research with 1 disease: the first removes the disease for 1 TR, the second then finds none and has a different outcome). Fryxen notes this does not settle whether the trigger happens at once or on resolution.
quote: the first resolution changes the game state so that the other resolution must have another outcome.
author: Fryxen
heading: Pharmacy Union

topic: Pharmacy Union: microbe trigger already triggered
question: If the science tag flips Pharmacy Union first, does the microbe tag effect still apply?
ruling: Yes. The ability was already triggered, so changing the game state does not change that. What changed is that you can no longer place diseases on Pharmacy Union; since gaining a resource you cannot collect is one of the three allowed exceptions, the play stays valid and you do the rest, losing 4 MC.
quote: The ABILITY has already been triggered, so changing the game state does not change that.
author: Fryxen
heading: Pharmacy Union

question: What does 'the ability' that is triggered by a microbe tag consist of on Pharmacy Union?
ruling: The ability is everything after the colon, i.e. for the microbe trigger 'add 1 disease here and lose 4 MC or as much as possible'.
quote: by 'the ability', I mean everything after the colon, so in this case 'add 1 disease here and lose 4 MC or as much as possible'.
author: Fryxen
heading: Pharmacy Union

topic: Pharmacy Union with Reds ruling: Trans-Neptune Probe
question: With Reds ruling, Pharmacy Union with 1 disease and only 6 MC, can you play Trans-Neptune Probe (a science tag card)?
ruling: No. Trans-Neptune Probe is not playable, because the Pharmacy Union effect (remove the disease and raise TR) cannot be skipped here and the 3 MC Reds tax cannot be paid; all effects must be performed to play the card. The explicit 'Correct, TNP is not playable' sits in text Fryxen struck through; his edit only reverses point 2 (Research), so point 1 stands.
quote: my mistake again, looking at an older version which doesn't have 'may'.
author: Fryxen
heading: Pharmacy Union

topic: Pharmacy Union with Reds ruling: Research
question: With Reds ruling and Pharmacy Union with 1 disease, can you play Research if you can pay the Reds tax for only the first science tag?
ruling: Yes, Research is playable: after the first tag removes the disease the second effect is optional (no diseases left, 'may'), so it can be ignored, not fizzled. (Fryxen first ruled Research unplayable, then corrected himself because he was reading an older card version without 'may'.)
quote: the effect is optional when you have no diseases on PU, so the second one can be ignored (not fizzled!).
author: Fryxen
heading: Pharmacy Union

question: With an empty Pharmacy Union, if I play a card with a science and a microbe tag, can I flip the corporation first to gain 3 TR and avoid the microbe effect?
ruling: You may choose to flip first, but both effects still trigger and the microbe penalty still applies; adding the disease is skipped because it can no longer be added (the exception for resources you can't collect). If you resolve the microbe trigger first, a disease is added and the science trigger then must remove it for 1 TR instead of 3.
quote: So in the case of Pharmacy Union playing a science microbe card, both effects trigger and you still have to pay the microbe penalty even if you choose to flip the corp first.
author: Fryxen
heading: Pharmacy Union

question: Does playing Vermin (animal and microbe tag) trigger Pharmacy Union?
ruling: Yes. Pharmacy Union gives diseases when anyone plays microbe tags, so Vermin triggers it.
quote: Well, Pharmacy Union gives you diseases when anyone is playing microbe tags, so Vermin would trigger that
author: Fryxen
heading: Pharmacy Union

question: What does Project Inspection allow?
ruling: It allows using the action of one of your own cards again; it works exactly like the Viron ability.
quote: Project Inspection allows you to make a motivating visit to one of YOUR projects. It works exactly like the Viron ability.
author: Fryxen
heading: Project Inspection

question: How many copies of the identical promo card from the pre-launch kit are added to the deck?
ruling: Only 1 promo card per game; all cards in the game are unique and the promo cards were meant to raise interest in the game.
quote: Only 1 promo card per game.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Promo cards

question: Can two copies of a promo card be mixed into the deck?
ruling: No. Every card is supposed to be unique, so the deck contains only one copy of each card.
quote: Every card is supposed to be unique, so only one copy in the deck.
author: Fryxen
heading: Promo cards

question: Should you play with both copies of the three Colonies alt-art promo cards?
ruling: No. Each card should be unique: do not put both the promo copy and the Colonies copy in the deck.
quote: No, each card should be unique :)
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Promo cards

question: Are the Colonies alternate-art promo cards identical in stats to the final Colonies cards?
ruling: No. They were created before final adjustments (one card lost its space tag and its cost went from 21 to 20), so they aren't really official, but you can play with them.
quote: Yeah, so the alternate art promos aren't even really official. They were created before final adjustments. But you can play with them, it's no big deal.
author: Fryxen
heading: Promo cards

question: Can the 2025 WSBG promo Public Plans (which involves showing a card to an opponent) be resolved in a solo game?
ruling: Yes. Solo has a neutral opponent, so the card works.
quote: Good question. There is a neutral opponent in solo, so it would work.
author: Fryxen
heading: Public Plans

question: Does Saturn Surfing require the Venus or Colonies expansion to be played?
ruling: No. Floaters are a resource like animals or microbes, and the card can be played in any combination of expansions.
quote: Yeah, it can be played in any combination of expansions, but works best in an earth tag strategy
author: Fryxen
heading: Saturn Surfing

topic: Self-Replicating Robots: discount resources stay on the card
question: Can the discount resources collected on Self-Replicating Robots be shifted to a different card placed on it?
ruling: No. The resources are put on the card to receive the discount, so a previously collected discount cannot be moved to a new card.
quote: You put the resources on the card to receive the discount, so you can't shift the previously collected discount to a new card.
author: Fryxen
heading: Self-replicating Robots

question: Can several cards be placed on Self-Replicating Robots?
ruling: Yes. You can place several cards on SRR, using 1 action for each new card (with 2 resources), so you choose which card to work on each generation.
quote: You can, on the other hand, place several cards on SRR (using 1 action for each new card with 2 resources)
author: Fryxen
heading: Self-replicating Robots

topic: Self-Replicating Robots: play in the same generation
question: Can a card be played in the same generation that it was placed on Self-Replicating Robots?
ruling: Yes. Playing it in the same generation it was placed gets just a 2 M€ discount.
quote: You can of course also play the card on the same generation that you placed it on SRR, getting just 2 MC discount
author: Fryxen
heading: Self-replicating Robots

topic: CEO's Favorite Project and Self-Replicating Robots
question: Can CEO's Favorite Project put a resource on a card being worked on by Self-Replicating Robots?
ruling: No. CEO's Favorite Project cannot be used on Self-Replicating Robots. SRR resources are not real resources and the corresponding card is not in play, so they generally do not interact with other parts of the game.
quote: CEO's Favirote Project can not be used on Self-Replicating Robots.
author: Fryxen
heading: Self-replicating Robots

topic: Self-Replicating Robots and the Eccentric award
question: Do resources on cards under Self-Replicating Robots count for the Eccentric award?
ruling: No. Resources on cards held under Self-Replicating Robots are not real resources and the card is not in play, so they do not interact with other parts of the game such as the Eccentric award.
quote: SRR resources are not real resources, and the corresponding card is not in play, so they generally do not interact with other parts of the game (such as the Eccentric award or CEO's Favorite Project).
author: Fryxen
heading: Self-replicating Robots

question: How often can Self-Replicating Robots be used?
ruling: Self-Replicating Robots can be used once per generation, like all other blue cards with actions.
quote: Self Replicating Robits (SRR) can only be used once per generation (like all other blue cards with actions).
author: Fryxen
heading: Self-replicating Robots

question: What can the Self-Replicating Robots action do?
ruling: Each use does either of two things: add a new Space or Building card from hand onto SRR with 2 generic resources on it, or double the resources on one of the cards on SRR.
quote: SRR can then EITHER add a new Space or Building card there from hand with 2 generic resources on OR double the resources on one of the cards on SRR.
author: Fryxen
heading: Self-replicating Robots

question: Can several cards sit on Self-Replicating Robots?
ruling: Yes. There can be several cards on SRR, and each of them has its own resources.
quote: There can be several cards on SRR. Each of those cards have their own resources.
author: Fryxen
heading: Self-replicating Robots

question: Do cards on Self-Replicating Robots count as cards in hand (for example for the Planner milestone)?
ruling: No. Cards on SRR can be played as if from hand, but they are not actually in hand, so they don't count for the Planner milestone.
quote: Cards on SRR can be played AS IF from hand - they are not actually in hand, and so they don't count for the Planner milestone.
author: Fryxen
heading: Self-replicating Robots

question: Do resources on cards held on Self-Replicating Robots count for the Excentric award?
ruling: No. Cards on SRR are not in play, and the Excentric award only counts resources on cards in play.
quote: Cards on SRR are not in play either, so their resources don't count for the Excentric award, because that award only counts resources on cards IN PLAY.
author: Fryxen
heading: Self-replicating Robots

question: Can CEO's Favorite Project add a resource to a card held on Self-Replicating Robots?
ruling: Yes. CEO's Favorite Project can add one resource to a card on SRR, because it doesn't require the card to be in play, only to have resources on it.
quote: CEO's Favorite Project can be played to add one resource to a card on SRR, because it doesn't specify that the card has to be in play, only that it has resources on it.
author: Fryxen
heading: Self-replicating Robots

question: Does Viron interact with Self-Replicating Robots?
