ruling: Yes. Viron can use SRR an extra time each generation if SRR is the action chosen for Viron.
quote: Viron can use SRR an extra time each generation if that's the action you choose for Viron.
author: Fryxen
heading: Self-replicating Robots

question: How is the cost of a card played from Self-Replicating Robots calculated?
ruling: When playing a card from SRR (as if from hand), its cost is reduced by the number of resources on it, and the cost cannot go below zero.
quote: When playing a card from SRR (as if from hand), the cost is reduced by the number of resources. The cost can not be below zero.
author: Fryxen
heading: Self-replicating Robots

question: What type are the resources placed on cards held on Self-Replicating Robots?
ruling: They have no particular type. They only measure how far the robots have progressed the project.
quote: These resources have no particular type, because they don't represent anything we'd associate with resources - they are only a measure of how much the robots have progressed the project.
author: Fryxen
heading: Self-replicating Robots

question: Can other cards (such as Corroder Suits, which adds a resource to any Venus card) add resources to cards held on Self-Replicating Robots, contrary to the earlier FAQ?
ruling: Yes. The FAQ was updated: other cards can add resources to cards on SRR, so Corroder Suits can combo with it. Excentric is still unaffected because it specifies cards in play (errata).
quote: Cards can add resources to SRR. So corroder Suits could also combo with it. Excentrc is still off though since it specifies in play (errata).
author: Fryxen
heading: Self-replicating Robots

question: Can a card with an unmet global requirement (temperature, oxygen, ocean limit) be placed on Self-Replicating Robots?
ruling: Yes. The restrictions only apply when the card is actually played from SRR, so it can be hosted there until the limit is met.
quote: Yes you can, because the restrictions only apply when you play the card (from SRR).
author: Fryxen
heading: Self-replicating Robots

question: What happens to the resources on a card placed on Self-Replicating Robots when it is played?
ruling: The resources are on the card that sits on Self-Replicating Robots and are discarded when that card is played.
quote: The resources are on the card that is on SRR, and they are discarded when the card is played.
author: Fryxen
heading: Self-replicating Robots

question: Can several cards be on Self-Replicating Robots, and which one is doubled?
ruling: Yes, several cards can sit on it, each with its own resources; if you have more than one you choose which one to double.
quote: SRR can have several cards on it, each with their own resources.
author: Fryxen
heading: Self-replicating Robots

question: How many resources does a newly placed card start with on Self-Replicating Robots?
ruling: Always 2 resources when a new card comes onto the Robots.
quote: Yes, you always start at 2 resources when a new card comes onto SRR.
author: Fryxen
heading: Self-replicating Robots

question: What is the erratum on Small Asteroid?
ruling: 1st edition erratum: there should be a '-' before the plant icons on this card; the text is correct. It is a promo card not in the base game.
quote: There should be a ‘-‘ before the plant icons on this card. The text is correct.
author: Fryxen
heading: Small Asteroid

question: How does the Splice corporation trigger?
ruling: If another player plays a microbe tag (including a corporation after you revealed Splice) that player gains 2 M€ or a microbe on that card, while Splice gains 2 M€. If Splice plays a microbe card (including Splice itself) it gains 4 M€, or 1 microbe to that card plus 2 M€.
quote: If another player plays a microbe tag (including a corp after you revealed Splice), that player gains 2 MC or a microbe on that card, while Splice gains 2 MC.
author: Fryxen
heading: Splice

question: Is the cathedral (silver cube) on a city from St. Joseph of Cupertino Mission a resource?
ruling: No. Cathedrals are not resources, they are a new type of marker.
quote: No, they are not resources. They are a new type of marker.
author: Fryxen
heading: St. Joseph of Cupertino Mission

question: Does the Stanford Torus city count as a city for cards that count cities?
ruling: Yes for cards counting cities anywhere (Immigration Shuttles, Pets, Landlord award), no for cards that count cities on Mars (Zeppelins, Martian Rails) because the Torus is not on Mars.
quote: Yes, Stanford Torus counts for Immigration Shuttles, Pets, Landlord etc. and does not count for Zeppelins and Martian Rails (because it's not on Mars).
author: Fryxen
heading: Stanford Torus

question: Can Stanford Torus be placed so it counts as adjacent to other tiles (for example next to Ganymede Colony) and trigger Philares?
ruling: No. Stanford Torus is separate from all other tiles and can have no adjacencies, so it cannot trigger Philares' adjacency bonus.
quote: Stanford Torus is separate from all other tiles and can have no adjacencies.
author: Fryxen
heading: Stanford Torus

question: Do tags on a revealed corporation trigger other corporations' effects (e.g. Splice with Recyclon's microbe tag)?
ruling: Yes, corporation tags trigger normally like any card, also for Saturn Systems and Stormcraft, so strict player order matters when revealing. The same applies to Prelude cards and the first turn (e.g. Immigrant City before Tharsis Republic places its first city). All starting cards are chosen before any are revealed.
quote: Yes, it triggers normally, just like all cards. This is also true with Saturn Systems and Stormcraft. The same can be said about Prelude cards and first turn of the game. Player order matters.
author: Fryxen
heading: Starting corporation tags

question: Why does Supermarkets have no building tag?
ruling: By design: it was meant as a 'society' card, a theme that often has no tags, and supermarkets are housed inside other buildings rather than being big buildings. It has no building tag.
quote: We wanted it to be a 'society' card, a theme that oftentimes has no tags.
author: Fryxen
heading: Supermarkets

topic: Merger with Terralabs Research and Polyphemos
question: What happens when a player has both Terralabs Research and Polyphemos through Merger?
ruling: The only corporation conflict Fryxen sees is Terralabs Research and Polyphemos, which cancel each other. He says that had they anticipated this promo they would have worded them as reducing/increasing the cost of buying cards by 2.
quote: The only conflict I see is Terralabs/Polyphemos, in which case they cancel each other.
author: Fryxen
heading: TerraLabs Research

topic: Merger with Terralabs Research and Polyphemos
question: How do Terralabs Research and Polyphemos combine when both are in play through Merger?
ruling: They average out to 3 MC per card bought.
quote: Terralabs and Polyphemos average out to 3 per card bought.
author: Fryxen
heading: TerraLabs Research

topic: Merger with Terralabs Research and Polyphemos
question: Do Terralabs Research and Polyphemos conflict when a player has both?
ruling: They cancel each other.
quote: Terralabs and Polyphemos cancel each other.
author: Fryxen
heading: TerraLabs Research

question: How much do you pay for project cards if you hold both Polyphemos and Terralabs through Merger?
ruling: Their card-buying effects cancel each other out. The exact resulting price per card was not stated. The combo costs you the unique play style of both corporations.
quote: They cancel each other. There is a specific downside to playing this combo in that you can't utilize either corp's unique play style.
author: Fryxen
heading: TerraLabs Research

topic: Merger with Polyphemos and Terralabs Research
question: How do Polyphemos and Terralabs Research interact when you hold both (e.g. via Merger) regarding the card purchase cost?
ruling: They cancel each other out. Note that you choose and pay for your starting hand before playing Merger: starting with Terralabs and then merging with Polyphemos gets cards for 1 MC each, while starting with Polyphemos makes the starting hand very expensive.
quote: Yes, they cancel out.
author: Fryxen
heading: TerraLabs Research

question: Does Topsoil Contract pay per resource gained or per gaining event (e.g. gaining 4 microbes at once)?
ruling: It is for each resource, not each occurrence: gaining several plants or microbes at once triggers Topsoil Contract for every resource gained.
quote: It is for each resource, not each occurence.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Topsoil Contract

question: Can Viron activate the action of the player's other corporation?
ruling: Yes, Viron can activate the action of your other corporation.
quote: Viron can activate the action of your other corporation.
author: Fryxen
heading: Viron

question: Can Viron reuse a corporation's action (e.g. Septem Tribus) when you hold two corporations via Merger?
ruling: Yes. Officially, Viron can reuse corporation actions.
quote: Official stance: yes you can!
author: Fryxen
heading: Viron

question: Can Banned Delegate target your own Chairman, e.g. to avoid a Revolution penalty?
ruling: Follow the theme when in doubt: the card represents the Chairman kicking out an opponent, not a weird way of resigning, and resigning is for those who have already lost real power. By implication it should not be used to escape a Revolution.
quote: The card is obviously meant to represent the chairman (your guy) kicking out an opponent, not as a very weird way of resigning.
author: Fryxen
heading: Banned Delegate

question: When a party becomes ruling its delegates are removed and dominance shifts; so is the chairman usually left with no delegates in that party?
ruling: Correct. The ruling party will shift most of the time. The chairman is worth 1 TR plus 1 influence, so pursuing it can be worthwhile, and ruling parties can be anticipated.
quote: Correct. But the chairman is worth 1 TR plus 1 influence, so it can definitely be worth pursuing.
author: Fryxen
heading: Chairman and dominant party

question: Does the Chairman still count as a delegate of a party for determining the dominant party?
ruling: No. The Chairman is not in a party anymore, so it doesn't count towards dominance.
quote: The chairman is not in a party anymore, so it doesn't count towards dominance.
author: Fryxen
heading: Chairman and dominant party

question: Are ruling and dominant party mutually exclusive?
ruling: No. The dominant party is marked by the dominance marker and the ruling party by its policy tile being displayed. A party can be both, although it is unlikely, since the dominant party is emptied when it becomes ruling and would have to gain enough new delegates to surpass all other parties.
quote: A party CAN be both ruling and dominant at the same time, although it is unlikely
author: Fryxen
heading: Chairman and dominant party

question: Can a player reach 4 influence with a card that gives +1 influence?
ruling: Yes: with the card, plus being chairman, dominant party leader and another delegate in the dominant party, a player can reach 4 influence.
quote: you can indeed reach an influence of 4 if you also have the chairman, the dominant party leader and another delegate in the dominant party.
author: Fryxen
heading: Delegates and influence

question: Is each party limited to 7 delegates?
ruling: No. Each player is limited to the 7 delegate pieces in the game, but each party has unlimited space. The 6 seats behind the party leader seat are decorative; delegates can be placed anywhere in the party's area.
quote: Each player is limited to the 7 delegate pieces given in the game, but each party has unlimited space.
author: Fryxen
heading: Delegates and influence

question: How do neutral delegates accumulate in Turmoil, and how often do you need an extra lobbyist?
ruling: There are 2 new neutral delegates every generation and they stack up over time; to become chairman you often need to place an extra delegate.
quote: In order to be chairman, you often need to place an extra delegate. There are 2 new neutral delegates every generation, and over time, it stacks up.
author: Fryxen
heading: Delegates and influence

question: Does a delegate in the lobby count as being in the reserve for cards that place delegates from the reserve?
ruling: Yes, the lobby is considered part of the reserve for supply purposes. The different wording between cards amounts to the same. You normally never take delegates from parties.
quote: Yes, the lobby is considered part of the reserve for supply purposes.
author: Fryxen
heading: Delegates and influence

question: In the Diversity global event (10 MC with 9 or more different tags), how does Influence count?
ruling: Each Influence counts as a different, unique, imaginary tag: 2 Influence equals 2 different tags. So 7 different tags plus 2 Influence qualifies. Event tags are not face up so they don't count.
quote: 2 influence = 2 different, unique and imaginary tags.
author: Fryxen
heading: Diversity (global event)

question: If two players tie for first in the Election global event, does the third player get second place rewards?
ruling: No. Global events like this work like awards: if 2+ players already won, there is no 2nd place.
quote: They work like awards. If 2+ players already won, there is no 2nd place.
author: Fryxen
heading: Election (global event)

question: Does Factorum's second step (spend 3 MC to draw a building card) involve revealing cards one by one until a building tag is revealed and kept?
ruling: Correct: it involves revealing cards until a building tag is revealed and kept, so all players know which building card was drawn.
quote: Correct on all points.
author: Fryxen
heading: Factorum

question: Why doesn't Factorum say 'reveal' like other reveal-until effects?
ruling: Design intent: Factorum's ability uses the same reveal-until mechanic, but the card avoids the long explanation, assuming players are familiar with the mechanic.
quote: Because it requires such a long explanation, and we figured players picking this up would already be familiar with the mechanic.
author: Fryxen
heading: Factorum

question: With only Stratospheric Birds in play, can you choose to receive microbes instead of animals with Freyja Biodomes, even though they can't be placed?
ruling: Yes, you can choose that (players may choose any legal option).
quote: Yes, you can choose that.
author: Fryxen
heading: Freyja Biodomes

question: Why is the Influence icon on Generous Funds shown with a plus, and how is it counted?
ruling: Influence does not change the count but adds to it. With 28 TR and 2 Influence you have 2 sets of 5 TR over 15, not 3, then Influence is added for 4 payouts total; each Influence gives one payout (equal to a set of 5 TR). In Energy Templates, by contrast, each Influence counts like a power tag (half a payout).
quote: In these few particular cases however, the influence doesn't affect the count itself, but adds to it.
author: Fryxen
heading: Generous Funds

question: Where does an ocean tile removed by a Turmoil event go?
ruling: It goes back to the pile and has to be placed again.
quote: It goes back to the pile and has to be placed again.
author: Fryxen
heading: Global events

question: Do global event effects on parameters apply once or per player, and do effects on players apply to all?
ruling: Parameter changes are one-off effects as written on the card (not per player). The parts that affect players (resources, production, TR) affect all players, with the amount depending on game state and influence.
quote: Those changes are of course one-off effects, just as described on the cards. The part affecting the players (easily identified because they affect player-related stuff like resources, production and TR) are affecting all players
author: Fryxen
heading: Global events

question: In a global event, can players choose the order of effects, e.g. Helion paying for building tags with heat before Great Dust Storm removes all heat?
ruling: No. The choose-the-order rule applies on your turn, and a global event is nobody's turn. The ruling is that things are done in the written order, with triggered effects done immediately and the first player deciding ties. So players lose all heat before paying for their buildings.
quote: My current ruling is that things are done in the written order, with any triggered effects done immediately, the first player deciding any ties.
author: Fryxen
heading: Global events

question: Does the player who removes an ocean tile lose TR?
ruling: No. They do nothing except decide which ocean is removed.
quote: No, they don't actually do anything, they just decide what ocean is removed.
author: Fryxen
heading: Global events

topic: Global event ranking ties and resources
question: For the global events described (resources on every card that uses resources; ranking Earth tags; ranking Building tags plus cities), do corporations with resources get one, and are ties handled so that multiple first ranks leave no second rank?
ruling: Correct on all three: resources are added even to corporations that collect resources, and when there are several first ranks they all get the first-rank penalty/reward and there is no second rank (ties are friendly).
quote: That is all correct.
author: Fryxen
heading: Global events

topic: Maxed global parameters in global events
question: If a global parameter is maxed, are the corresponding steps in global events like Dry Deserts and Snow Cover ignored?
ruling: Correct: if the parameter is at its maximum it may not be affected again, so the first part of Dry Deserts (remove an ocean) and Snow Cover (reduce temperature) would be ignored.
quote: Correct on all points.
author: Fryxen
heading: Global events

topic: Global event standard resources per Influence
question: When a global event gives a standard resource per Influence, can the resources be different?
ruling: Yes, you can choose different resources.
quote: 3) You can choose different resources.
author: Fryxen
heading: Global events

question: Can a wild tag count as a theoretical extra tag for Interplanetary Trade when you already have all distinct tags?
ruling: No. The wild tag can only be a tag that could normally be face up in your game, so it can't be an event tag, and it can't be a Venus tag unless you play with Venus Next.
quote: The wild tag can only be a tag that could normally be face up in your game.
author: Fryxen
heading: Interplanetary Trade

question: Does Interplanetary Trade count its own tag among the different tags?
ruling: Yes, it also counts its own tag, if you don't already have a space tag in play.
quote: It also counts its own tag, if you don't already have a space tag in play.
author: Fryxen
heading: Interplanetary Trade

question: Can Law Suit be played in a solo game?
ruling: No: in solo your neutral opponent never harms you, so you can never meet the Law Suit condition (and it has no discard pile to archive it).
quote: In solo, you have a very nice and neutral opponent, that will never do you harm. So you'll never win (play) a Law Suit against them.
author: Fryxen
heading: Law Suit

question: Does Mons Insurance pay each player 3 MC for its own starting -2 MC production on opponents?
ruling: No. Although it would follow the normal working of cards, it would be unthematic to compensate for charging for the insurance; the final wording will make this clear.
quote: No, you don't. Although it would follow the normal working of cards, it would be unthematic to compensate for charging for the insurance.
author: Fryxen
heading: Mons Insurance

question: Can Mons Insurance play a card that harms others when it cannot afford the 3 MC payouts?
ruling: Yes, because it can always pay 'as much as possible'. Any player can invoke triggers, so the hit player asks for the payout, but the active player chooses the order of effects and can pay when out of money, paying as much as possible.
quote: The active player can indeed play the card because you can always pay 'as much as possible'.
author: Fryxen
heading: Mons Insurance

question: In solo, must Mons Insurance pay the neutral player when reducing production?
ruling: Yes. Production reduction is mandatory so compensation must be made; the reduction is made but not tracked, and the neutral player counts as a player.
quote: Production is mandatory, so compensation must be made. The reduction is made but not kept track of. The neutral player counts as a player.
author: Fryxen
heading: Mons Insurance

topic: Mons Insurance in solo: resource destruction
question: In solo, must Mons Insurance pay when a card removes resources?
ruling: Resource destruction is optional, so it does not have to be performed and compensated.
quote: Resource destruction is optional, so doesn't have to be 'performed' and compensated.
author: Fryxen
heading: Mons Insurance

question: In solo, must Mons Insurance pay when stealing resources?
ruling: Yes. Stealing removes resources from a player and so must be compensated.
quote: Stealing removes resources from a player, and so must be compensated.
author: Fryxen
heading: Mons Insurance

question: When Mons Insurance is involved and a card steals resources (e.g. MC), can the insurance trigger between removing from the opponent and adding to yourself?
ruling: No. Stealing is a single effect, so the removal and the gain cannot be separated or interrupted by Mons Insurance. Had it been worded as remove + gain, the remove part could be omitted under the rules exception for such effects, which would be unthematic.
quote: B) is correct. Stealing is one effect.
author: Fryxen
heading: Mons Insurance

question: As Mons Insurance, playing Deimos Down with your last MC and destroying plants while Optimal Aerobraking would give you MC, may you pay the insurance before taking the Aerobraking MC?
ruling: Yes. You decide the order of effects, so you can do the plant destruction and the insurance payout before taking the Optimal Aerobraking bonus.
quote: If you are Mons Insurance doing that, you can choose to do plant destruction and insurance payout before taking Aerobreaking bonus. You decide the order of effects.
author: Fryxen
heading: Mons Insurance

question: Playing Giant Ice Asteroid against a player with 4 plants and Arctic Algae, may you place one ocean, activate Arctic Algae, destroy 6 plants, trigger Mons Insurance to pay 3 MC you don't have, and only then place the second ocean next to ocean(s) and collect its bonus?
ruling: Yes. Effects and triggers can be resolved in any order you choose, so Mons Insurance can use the order to avoid paying before the second ocean placement.
quote: Yes. Mons can be very sneaky as long as they follow the written rules...
author: Fryxen
heading: Mons Insurance

question: How does Mons Insurance' compensation work when a player is hit, and what if the payer has less than 3 MC?
ruling: Whenever someone gets hit by anyone, the Mons Insurance player must compensate them by giving 3 MC or all they have if less. If Mons Insurance itself gets hit, it pays itself. With only 2 MC, it pays 2 MC.
quote: Whenever someone gets hit by anyone, you have to compensate, and choose to either give them 3 MC or all you have.
author: Fryxen
heading: Mons Insurance

question: When another player plays a microbe-tag card and Pharmacy Union loses 4 MC, does Mons Insurance have to pay Pharmacy Union 3 MC?
ruling: No. The loss is caused by Pharmacy Union's own ability, not by the player who played the microbe card, so Mons Insurance's payout is not triggered.
quote: No. It is not the microbe player that causes the loss, but Pharmacy Union's own ability.
author: Fryxen
heading: Mons Insurance

question: If a player uses Ants to take a microbe from their own Tardigrades, does that count as stealing from 'another player' for Mons Insurance?
ruling: No. Taking your own resources does not count; the loss has to be inflicted on a player other than the one dealing the hurt. (If Mons itself were hurt, it would pay the insurance to itself, a net zero.)
quote: Taking your own stuff doesn't count. it has to be from another player than the one dealing the hurt.
author: Fryxen
heading: Mons Insurance

question: In what order may triggered effects be performed?
ruling: Triggers can be performed in any chosen order but do not exist until the thing that triggers them has occurred.
quote: The triggers can be performed in any chosen order, but of course don't exist until the thing that trigger them has occurred.
author: Fryxen
heading: Order of effects

question: How does Philares' 'each new adjacency' trigger work?
ruling: It works like ocean adjacency bonuses: each new stretch of border created between Philares' tile and another player's tile gives a resource of choice, so a tile touching 2 opposing tiles gives 2 resources (can be different). Philares also benefits when other players create the border.
quote: Each new stretch of border created between Philares and another player's tiles gives Philares a resource of their choice on the player board.
author: Fryxen
heading: Philares

question: Does Philares' ability trigger when an ocean is placed next to a tile?
ruling: No. Oceans are not owned, so they don't count. Creating a new adjacency means establishing a new permanent border between your land and that of an opponent; it refers to the result, not to what you do.
quote: Oceans are not owned, so they don't count.
author: Fryxen
heading: Philares

question: If you place a tile next to two opposing tiles, or an opponent places a tile adjacent to two of your tiles, does Philares gain two resources?
ruling: Yes to both. Each time a non-ocean tile is placed, adjacencies are checked; if the new tile creates a new border between your tiles and an opponent's, the effect triggers separately for each stretch of border created, so the resources can be different. Philares also gets the bonus when other players create these borders.
quote: it triggers separately for each stretch of border created, so placing your tile next to 3 opposing tiles will give you 3 opportunities to take a standard resource
author: Fryxen
heading: Philares

question: If Pristar plays a Prelude that gives TR (UNMI Contractor), does it count as terraforming in generation 1 and block Pristar's ability?
ruling: Yes. Setup (playing corporations and Preludes) is included in generation 1, so gaining TR from such a Prelude blocks Pristar's ability for generation 1.
quote: Setup (playing corporations and preludes) is included in generation 1, so no, that would block Pristar's ability for generation 1.
author: Fryxen
heading: Pristar

question: Can the Turmoil corporations Pristar and Terralabs be played without the Turmoil expansion?
ruling: They should not be played without Turmoil: their effects are balanced against the TR revision rule in Turmoil, and Pristar has a hard time getting TR back.
quote: Turmoil Corporations like Pristar and Terralabs should not be played without Turmoil expansion, really.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Pristar

question: Can Pristar and Terralabs be used without Turmoil, and do they under-perform?
ruling: Pristar and Terralabs are designed to take advantage of the Reds ruling bonus (+1 TR if you are last in TR), so without Turmoil you may want to buff them a bit.
quote: Pristar and Terralabs are both designed to take advantage of the Reds ruling bonus (+1 TR if you're last in TR), so you might want to buff them a bit if playing without Turmoil.
author: Fryxen
heading: Pristar

question: Does Protected Habitats protect your plants, animals and microbes from global events?
ruling: No. Global events still affect you; Protected Habitats only stops opponents from removing them.
quote: Exactly. Global events still affect you.
author: Fryxen
heading: Protected Habitats

question: How does Red Tourism Wave count empty areas adjacent to your tiles?
ruling: It counts all empty areas (hexagons without tiles) adjacent to all your tiles. It counts hexes, not adjacencies, so a hex bordering two of your tiles counts once.
quote: It counts all empty areas (=hexagons without tiles on) adjacent to all your tiles. Note that it counts hexes, not adjacencies
author: Fryxen
heading: Red Tourism Wave

question: For Red Tourism Wave, do empty reserved ocean areas count, do cities not on Mars have zero adjacent empty areas, and do spaces beyond the board edge count?
ruling: Correct on all points: empty ocean/reserved areas count, cities not on Mars have zero adjacent empty areas, and spaces beyond the edge of the board do not count as empty areas.
quote: Correct on all points.
author: Fryxen
heading: Red Tourism Wave

question: How does the Reds policy apply to actions that raise TR?
ruling: Reds require paying 3 M€ when you get TR, so you can't take any action that increases your TR unless you pay the Reds 3 M€ during that action.
quote: This means that you can't take any action that would increase your TR unless you pay the Reds 3 MC during that action.
author: Fryxen
heading: Reds

question: If the Reds are ruling and you cannot pay 3 MC, can you still perform an action that raises TR?
ruling: No. The Reds' tax must be paid to raise TR; effects chain (parameter increase adds TR, TR adds the -3 MC), losing resources is not ignorable, and if you cannot pay you cannot perform the action at all. You may gain the MC during the action (e.g. via an ocean adjacency bonus) to pay.
quote: When TR is taken, Reds adds a -3 MC to the list of effects. Losing resources is not something that can be ignored, so this effect must also be performed. If you can't do it, then you can't perform the action at all.
author: Fryxen
heading: Reds

question: If the Reds rule and you lack 3 MC, can you play the card/action that raises a global parameter and just not raise TR?
ruling: No. All actions follow the same principles as playing a card: pay cost, meet requirements, and be able to perform all effects and triggers (excluding maxed parameters, removing opposing resources, and taking card resources you can't collect). You cannot do the action that would raise your TR if you can't pay the Reds.
quote: For this particular case, it is a matter of how to play an action, and it follows the same rules as playing a card, so you can't do the action that would raise your TR at all if you can't pay the Reds.
author: Fryxen
heading: Reds

question: With Reds ruling and not enough MC, can you play Big Asteroid (raising temperature two steps) using MC from the ocean bonus to pay the Reds TR tax?
ruling: Yes. You choose the order of effects, and as long as you can find a way to perform all effects you can play the card. Each temperature step, TR step and MC cost is a separate effect; the Reds payment is not in the pile of waiting effects until you take the TR.
quote: Summary: You choose the order of effects, and as long as you can find a way to perform all effects, you can play the card/action.
author: Fryxen
heading: Reds

topic: Choosing between legal options with Reds
question: With Reds ruling and Venus maxed, can the player choose to raise Venus with Atmoscoop to avoid paying the Reds tax?
ruling: Yes, you can choose Venus; it is your only option if you can't pay the Reds for the temperature TR. Players may choose any legal option, and both are legal if you can pay the Reds.
quote: Players may choose any legal option, and both are legal if you can pay the Reds.
author: Fryxen
heading: Reds

question: Under Reds ruling, can you take an action that raises TR if you cannot pay for it?
ruling: No. Reds require you to pay for your TR, and gaining TR is not one of the exceptions to performing all effects, so you cannot take actions that would raise your TR if you cannot pay the Reds. This can also block greenery placement when the greenery would raise the oxygen level.
quote: you can't take actions that would raise your TR if you can't pay the Reds.
author: Fryxen
heading: Reds

question: Is the Ruling Bonus, or becoming Chairman, affected by the Ruling Policy (e.g. Reds)?
ruling: No. Ruling policies are only active during the action phase, so the Reds do not punish TR gained from the party's ruling bonus or from the new chairman.
quote: The ruling policies are only active during the action phase, so Reds will not punish the one getting its policy TR or the new chairman.
author: Fryxen
heading: Ruling policies

question: Do the Greens and Mars First policies trigger during end game scoring?
ruling: No; neither Greens nor Mars First trigger during end game scoring.
quote: Likewise, neither Greens nor Mars First will trigger during end game scoring.
author: Fryxen
heading: Ruling policies

question: Could the game start with the Scientists as ruling party instead of the Greens?
ruling: Yes, you could indeed start with Scientists if you like, but they prefer Greens and the rules are shorter without a choice. Greens were chosen for thematic reasons and because several parties (Kelvinists, Mars First, Reds, Unity) would unbalance the game start.
quote: So to conclude, you could indeed start with Scientists if you like, but we prefer Greens, and the rules are shorter if you don't have a choice. Do as you wish.
author: Fryxen
heading: Ruling policies

topic: Game end check and global events
question: If a global event (e.g. Volcanic Eruptions) completes the last global parameter during the Turmoil phase, does the game end that generation?
ruling: No. In the solar phase the game end check occurs before the global event triggers, so you play another generation until the next end game check.
quote: Correct. You play another generation until you make the next end game check.
author: Fryxen
heading: Solar phase

question: What is the order of the production phase, research and solar phase in a game with expansions?
ruling: Researching new cards happens at the start of the next generation; after production comes the solar phase. The solar phase begins with the end-game check and then administers the expansions in release order: Venus Next (World Government Terraforming), Colonies (colony production and reset of trade fleets), Turmoil (several steps).
quote: Researching new cards is at the start of the next generation, after production comes the solar phase. It begins with the end game check and goes on to administer the expansions in release order
author: Fryxen
heading: Solar phase

question: How does solo play work with Turmoil?
ruling: Use the normal Turmoil rules in solo: goal is complete terraforming, or 63 TR (which adds a Buffer Gas standard project). The player loses 1 TR every generation, neutral delegates make controlling the Terraforming Committee harder, and combining with other expansions just adds their rules and solo rules.
quote: Goal: complete terraforming or 63 TR (which adds a Buffer Gas standard project). Use the normal Turmoil rules in solo.
author: Fryxen
heading: Solo game

question: In solo with Turmoil, must you play the TFALL (end of generation 14) objective?
ruling: No. You can also play the TR63 objective with Turmoil in solo; it is more difficult but far from impossible, and being chairman and getting the Reds in power early helps.
quote: You can play TR63 as well, and it is more difficult, but far from impossible.
author: Fryxen
heading: Solo game

question: Does the neutral player compete in global events like Revolution?
ruling: Yes, the neutral player competes (e.g. counting influence) and will take the penalty.
quote: The neutral player competes, and will take a 'hit' in this case.
author: Fryxen
heading: Solo game

question: Does the Sponsored Projects global event add a resource to Self-Replicating Robots?
ruling: Yes, confirmed with 'Correct on all points'.
quote: Correct on all points.
author: Fryxen
heading: Sponsored Projects (global event)

question: Can the Turmoil TR revision (lose 1 TR per generation) be dropped?
ruling: The designers tried without it and the engines went bananas with runaway leaders winning with 50+ points; players may try without it but should not expect a balanced game.
quote: Try without it if you like, but don't expect a balanced game.
author: Fryxen
heading: TR revision

question: What is the TR revision for in Turmoil?
ruling: Design intent: it is not aimed at the leader specifically but slows the overall exponential escalation caused by party bonuses, policies, chairman TR, influence and global events, giving players more time to win by other means. Reds act as the specific catch-up mechanic.
quote: So the TR revision doesn't specifically hit the leader, like you said, but it slows down the overall escalation, giving players more time to win by other means.
author: Fryxen
heading: TR revision

question: Can Atmoscoop's 'raise temperature or Venus' be played choosing temperature when it is maxed or one step from max while Venus is not?
ruling: Yes. The exception for maxed parameters is valid for the Venus scale too, so you can play either effect, deciding which: choose, then do as much as you can of that choice.
quote: The exception for maxed parameters is valid for the Venus scale, so you can play either effect - you decide.
author: Fryxen
heading: Atmoscoop

question: Does Celestic's initial card reveal for floater icons apply to Stratospheric Birds, which requires paying a floater?
ruling: Yes, Stratospheric Birds is definitely a target since it has a floater icon.
quote: Yes, Stratospheric Birds are definitely a target since it has a floater icon.
author: Fryxen
heading: Celestic

question: Does the requirement of 5 floaters on Aerosport Tournament count as a floater icon for Celestic?
ruling: Yes, it does.
quote: Yes it does.
author: Fryxen
heading: Celestic

question: Does Hydrogen to Venus add 1 floater per Jovian tag to a single Venus card, or one floater to a Venus card for each Jovian tag (possibly different cards)?
ruling: All floaters go to the same card: add one floater per Jovian tag you have to a single Venus card.
quote: Correct. All floaters go to the same card.
author: Fryxen
heading: Hydrogen to Venus

question: With Manutech, can you play Nitrophilic Moss by raising plant production first, gaining the plants from Manutech, then paying the plant loss?
ruling: Yes. After declaring the card, checking the requirement and paying, the waiting effects are +2 plant production and -2 plant. Choosing production first makes Manutech add a +2 plant effect to the waiting effects, which you can then resolve before the -2 plant effect.
quote: If you choose the +2 production first, then Manutech will add a +2 plant effect to the waiting effects. You can then choose that effect before the -2 plant effect.
author: Fryxen
heading: Nitrophilic Moss

question: Is losing 2 plants on Nitrophilic Moss a requirement, so that it cannot be played without 2 plants?
ruling: The loss of 2 plants is part of the effects (shown among the lower-panel icons), not a requirement; the text is only a reminder. Effects can be chosen in any order but none can be ignored (apart from the three exceptions); if you cannot complete all effects in your chosen order, you take the card back.
quote: But losing 2 plant is part of the effect, as its icons are depicted in the lower panel among other effects of the card.
author: Fryxen
heading: Nitrophilic Moss

question: With Manutech you can play Nitrophilic Moss with no plants, since production gives plants that are then lost; is that correct?
ruling: Confirmed ('All correct'): this works. The same reasoning is confirmed for a Tharsis Republic player paying the 6 MC ocean cost on a Hellas ocean space after the city's income, and for placing an ocean and then removing plants from an Arctic Algae owner who just gained them.
quote: All correct.
author: Fryxen
heading: Nitrophilic Moss

question: Can Predators take animals from Venusian Animals?
ruling: Yes (answered in thematic terms): Predators can attack animals on Venusian Animals, since predators may be brought to the other planet.
quote: Yes, if someone brings them in a shuttle to the other planet.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Predators

question: Are Predators limited to Martian animals, i.e. can they not attack Venusian Animals?
ruling: Implied no restriction: Predators are not all Martian, so they can attack Venusian animals as well. Answered only as a rhetorical question.
quote: Who said the Predators are all Martian?
author: Fryxen
heading: Predators

topic: Predators and Ants with Venus resources
question: Can Predators remove animals from Venus-based animal cards, and Ants microbes from Venus microbe cards?
ruling: Not stated outright. The designer explains that existing cards could not be changed and new wording would have been complicated, so Predators/Ants work on Venus animal and microbe cards as printed ('hawks' flying over Venus).
quote: Those predators are hawks... Yeah, we couldn't change existing cards, and rewording the new new ones would have required quite complicated text and iconography.
author: Fryxen
heading: Predators

question: Can Predators remove an animal from an opponent's Stratospheric Birds (a Venus card)?
ruling: Implied yes: the answer is that Predators can be seen as a multitude of species, e.g. Venusian hawks; no restriction to Mars cards is stated. This is a thematic interpretation.
quote: you could also see Predators as a multitude of species, like Venusian hawks for example...
author: Fryxen
heading: Predators

question: Can standard-deck cards that add microbes to 'any card' (and Venus cards like Maxwell Base and Corroder Suits) put microbes on Thermophiles?
ruling: Yes. Maxwell Base and Corroder Suits can put microbes on Thermophiles, and Extreme-Cold Fungus can as well since the card wording allows it, even though some such combos are non-thematic. It was left that way for simplicity and playability.
quote: Yes, you can use Maxwell Base and Corroder Suits to put microbes on Thermophiles.
author: Fryxen
heading: Resources on Venus cards

question: Which Venus cards restrict where resources can be added?
ruling: Stratopolis can only add floaters to a Venus card, while Floating Habs can add floaters to any card, not restricted to Venus. Maxwell Base and Corroder Suits can only add resources to Venus cards.
quote: Stratopolis (on Venus) can only add floaters to a Venus card, while Floating Habs (on Venus but could be elsewhere as well) can add floaters to any card
author: Fryxen
heading: Resources on Venus cards

question: What does the Venus icon next to a resource icon mean, and why do some cards say 'another Venus card' and Thermophiles 'any Venus card'?
ruling: The Venus icon is meant as an asterisk (restricting the target to Venus cards), like the steel icon on Aquifer Pumping's action cost. The four cards have the same mechanism of adding microbes, but only Thermophiles can collect them, hence 'another' versus 'any' wording.
quote: The Venus icon IS meant as an asterisk.
author: Fryxen
heading: Resources on Venus cards

question: Should Venus Next be played with Corporate Era?
ruling: Venus Next is playable without Corporate Era, but for optimal experience and balance Corporate Era should be included; it is primarily balanced with it (e.g. science tag requirements are hard to satisfy without it).
quote: Well, Venus Next is certainly playable even without CE, but for optimal experience and balance, CE should be included.
author: Fryxen
heading: Setup and expansion combinations

question: When the Solar Cycle (world government terraforming) variant is used, should the game end if the last parameter is completed by the world government step?
ruling: No. The Solar Phase follows the Production Phase: Step 1 is to check end-game conditions; if not met, play another generation after this phase, and if met go immediately to end-game scoring including final greenery placement. Step 2 is World Government Terraforming: the first player raises 1 global parameter without getting any bonus. It is an official rule from Venus Next that can be used as a variant in any game.
quote: Step 1 - Check end game conditions. If not met, like in your case, continue to play another round after this Solar Phase. If met, immediatelt go to end game scoring including final greenery placement.
author: Fryxen
heading: Solar phase

question: If the World Government's terraforming in the Solar Phase raises the last Mars parameter step, does the game end that generation?
ruling: No. The end game check (step 1 of the Solar Phase) happens before the World Government raises the last step, so another generation is played. That is the official rule; the order is so the upkeep phase is not performed when the game is ending. Players may house rule differently.
quote: The end game check is before the World Government raises the last step and therefore another generation is played. That is the official rule.
author: EagleEye80
heading: Solar phase

question: How does the Solar Phase work and what does it contain?
ruling: There is a new phase after the Production Phase, the Solar Phase. Step 1: check whether Mars is completely terraformed; if so the game ends as in the normal rules and the rest of the Solar Phase is skipped. Step 2: World Government Terraforming (used with Venus Next): the first player raises one global parameter (temperature, oxygen, ocean or Venus scale) without getting any bonus. More steps will be added by future expansions.
quote: The first step is to check if Mars is completely terraformed and if so, the game ends, just like in the normal rules, and the rest of the Solar Phase is skipped.
author: Fryxen
heading: Solar phase

question: If the start player (World Government) maxes the last Mars parameter in the Solar phase, does the game end?
ruling: Correct about the timing: you play another generation, because the game end check happens before the parameter is raised.
quote: Correct about the tim7ng of game end.
author: Fryxen
heading: Solar phase

question: Will the summer 2017 expansion be allowed in the Solo Terraformer Challenge?
ruling: Yes. The expansion for that summer will be allowed in the challenge because it does not change the conditions for solo play in any major way.
quote: Yes, the expansion for this summer will be allowed in this challenge, because it doesn't change the conditions for solo play in any major way.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Solo game

question: Is World Government Terraforming used in the solo game?
ruling: It is used in solo with the Venus Next expansion, where Venus must also be terraformed (another 15 steps) within the 14 generations. It cannot be used for solo without Venus.
quote: World Government Terraforming can not be used for solo without Venus.
author: Fryxen
heading: Solo game

question: Is World Government Terraforming optional in solo play with Venus Next?
ruling: No. It is always mandatory for solo play with Venus Next, because you must max the Venus scale as well as the 3 Mars parameters to win.
quote: World Government Terraforming is always mandatory for solo play with Venus Next
author: Fryxen
heading: Solo game

question: How does Venus Next work in solo?
ruling: In solo with Venus Next you must also terraform Venus in the allotted time, and you get the help of World Government Terraforming; skipping WG Terraforming is not allowed.
quote: Skipping WG Terraforming is not allowed.
author: Fryxen
heading: Solo game

question: In TR63 solo with Venus Next, is the Venus terraforming requirement still needed, and is World Government Terraforming used?
ruling: In the TR63 solo variant the Venus terraforming requirement is completely ignored, but World Government Terraforming (WGT) still helps you reach bonuses on the tracks.
quote: you could try the TR63 solo, where the Venus terraforming requirement is completely ignored, but the WGT still helps you reach yummy bonuses on the tracks.
author: Fryxen
heading: Solo game

question: In solo with Venus Next, does the game end when the global parameters are maxed before generation 14?
ruling: The solo rules override the normal multiplayer rules. The solo game ends at generation 14 regardless of the global parameters (generation 12 with Prelude), so if you complete the parameters earlier you keep playing to score more points.
quote: The solo game ends at generation 14 no matter what the global parameters are, or generation 12 if using Prelude.
author: Fryxen
heading: Solo game

question: In solo with Venus Next, is completing the Venus scale required to win?
ruling: Yes: completing the Venus scale is required to win the solo game along with the other 3 parameters on Mars, unless you are using the TR63 variant introduced in Prelude.
quote: Completing the Venus scale is required to win the solo game, along with the other 3 parameters on Mars.
author: Fryxen
heading: Solo game

topic: Solo World Government in last generation
question: In generation 14 of a solo game, does World Government Terraforming fire when a Mars parameter remains?
ruling: No. In generation 14, World Government Terraforming will not fire, since the game ends in the end game step right before it.
quote: In generation 14, the World Government Terraforming will not fire, since the game ends in the End game step right before that.
author: Fryxen
heading: Solo game

topic: World Government Terraforming in TR63 solo
question: In solo TR63 with Venus Next, should World Government Terraforming be used?
ruling: Yes, use WGT. It makes TR63 slightly harder since parameters fill faster, but helps reach requirements and bonus steps faster.
quote: You do use it, yes. It doesn't help very much in TR63, in fact it makes it a little harder since the parameters fill up faster.
author: Fryxen
heading: Solo game

question: Can Sulphur-Eating Bacteria's microbes be spent for MC as a stand-alone action, or only when paying for another card?
ruling: Sulphur-Eating Bacteria's action spends any number of its microbes to gain triple the MC as an effect of the action itself, not as payment for playing a card. Only Dirigibles works like steel or titanium, with floaters usable solely as payment for Venus cards.
quote: Dirigibles is the kind of effect your friend was thinking about, analogous to the use of steel and titanium. [...] Sulphur Eating Bacteria is formulated like Titanium Shuttles, and a multitude of microbe- and floater cards, which spend their resources to do something, not as part of the action of playing a card.
author: Fryxen
heading: Sulphur-Eating Bacteria

topic: Unexpected Application and text vs icons
question: Must the discard in Unexpected Application (and Mars University) be paid before the rest of the card resolves, e.g. can Venus be raised first so the 8% bonus card is the one discarded?
ruling: The intent of both cards was to pay (discard) first. Strictly, however, icons take precedence and 'do X to get Y' does not necessarily imply order, so the card can be paid later during the action. Fryxen's advice: play it as intended, but if someone insists, allow paying later; a printing may add an asterisk.
quote: In summary, play it as intended, but if someone insists, allow paying later.
author: Fryxen
heading: Unexpected Application

question: Is the Venus scale an end game condition?
ruling: No. The Venus scale is a global parameter that can be increased, including by the World Government, but it is not an end game condition.
quote: remember that Venus scale is also a parameter that can be increased, but Venus scale is not an end game condition!
author: EagleEye80
heading: Venus track

question: Do Adaptation Technology, Special Design and Inventrix work on Venus requirements?
ruling: Yes. The Venus track is considered a global parameter, and the Venus rules clarify these cards work on the Venus scale as well. Morning Star Inc., on the other hand, only affects the Venus scale.
quote: The Venus track is considered a global parameter, and the Venus rules clarify that Adaptation Technology, Special Design and Inventrix do indeed work on the Venus scale as well.
author: Fryxen
heading: Venus track

question: Does the +2/-2 global requirement adjustment (card and corporation) also apply to the Venus track?
ruling: Yes. The Venus track counts as a global parameter, as clarified in the Venus rules, so the +/-2 adjustment applies to it too.
quote: Yes, the Venus track also counts. This was clarified in the Venus rules.
author: Fryxen
heading: Venus track

question: Can Viron's action be used on an opponent's blue card that has already been used this generation?
ruling: No. Like all cards, effects affect only you unless specified otherwise (usually a red border around an icon, and always stated in the text), so Viron cannot use other players' actions.
quote: So no, Viron cannot use other players' actions.
author: Lord_Aethan
heading: Viron

question: If a blue card offers action A or action B and you used A this turn, can Viron's action be used to do B?
ruling: Yes. You can choose either; Viron simply lets you use the card again.
quote: You can choose either. Viron simply lets you use the card again.
author: Fryxen
heading: Viron

question: Can Viron use an opponent's blue card action?
ruling: No. Viron can only use your own blue card action (one of your blue cards with a red arrow signifying an action).
quote: Viron can only use your own blue card action (one of your blue cards with a red arrow signifying an action).
author: Fryxen
heading: Viron

question: Who receives placement and track bonuses, and TR, when the world government raises a parameter in the Solar Phase?
ruling: The track and placement bonuses are triggered but go to the world government, not to the player: ocean placement bonuses go to the WG, the WG's extra heat production at -24 and -20 C is nullified since nobody plays the WG, and if the WG's raise reaches a threshold that places an ocean or raises another parameter, the WG gets the TR, not the player.
quote: the track bonuses are triggered, but to the world government, not to the player.
author: Fryxen
heading: World Government Terraforming

question: In the Solar Phase (world government terraforming), who gets bonus steps and placement bonuses when the parameter is raised?
ruling: Bonus steps are triggered but go to the world government (WG), which is treated as a player controlled by the first player; all normal rules apply. Example: the WG raises temperature to 0 C and gets 1 TR, which triggers an ocean placed by the WG (first player) for 1 TR plus placement bonuses (nothing happens); another player with Arctic Algae gets 2 plants because the WG is considered a player.
quote: Bonus steps are triggered too, but goes to the WG (controlled by the first player. Basically the WG is a player that does nothing else than this, and is controlled by the first player. All normal rules apply.
author: Fryxen
heading: World Government Terraforming

question: Does the world government have resources or production that can be targeted?
ruling: No. Unlike the neutral player in the solo variant, the WG is not considered to have any resources or production to mess with.
quote: In contrast to the neutral 'player' in the solo variant, the WG is not considered to have any resources or production to mess with.
author: Fryxen
heading: World Government Terraforming

topic: Solar Phase and World Government Terraforming status
question: Is the Solar Phase / World Government Terraforming mandatory?
ruling: The Solar Phase becomes an integral part of the game from Venus Next on, and World Government Terraforming (a step of it) is the norm with Venus Next. Using it without Venus Next, or playing Venus Next without it, are non-standard variants. New expansions will add more steps to the Solar Phase.
quote: The Solar phase will become an integral part of the game from Venus Next and on.
author: Fryxen
heading: World Government Terraforming

question: Can Venus Next be played without World Government Terraforming, and WGT used without Venus Next?
ruling: Playing Venus Next without WGT is an official variant. Using WGT without Venus Next is not an official variant; it can be done, but then Venus Next will feel longer, which was not intended. For solo, WGT is only included when playing with Venus Next.
quote: You can play Venus Next without WGT as an official variant.
author: Fryxen
heading: World Government Terraforming

question: When the World Government terraforms, are bonus steps (temperature at 0 C, oxygen at 8%) and placement bonuses performed?
ruling: All placement bonuses and other bonuses are performed, but the benefits go to the WG, not the first player. The first player raises the bonus temperature and decides where to place the bonus ocean on behalf of the WG. The WG does not keep track of resources, so placement bonuses are irrelevant.
quote: All placement bonuses and other bonuses are performed, but the benefits go to the WG, not to the first player.
author: Isaac Fryxelius
heading: World Government Terraforming

question: Is the World Government Terraforming step needed when playing Venus Next, with or without Corporate Era?
ruling: The Solar Phase is mandatory (it includes the end of game step), but there is an optional rule not to use the World Government Terraforming step. It is meant to speed up the game a bit when using Venus Next and is not intended for play without Venus Next (though many people do).
quote: The Solar Phase is mandatory (it includes the end of game step), but there is an optional rule not to use the World Government Terraforming step.
author: Fryxen
heading: World Government Terraforming

question: May World Government Terraforming be skipped in a multiplayer Venus Next game?
ruling: Venus Next adds the Venus parameter, a 6th milestone and award, and World Government Terraforming in the Solar phase after production. It can be skipped in multiplayer if you want a longer game.
quote: Skip VN:World Government Terraforming if you want a longer game
author: Fryxen
heading: World Government Terraforming

question: Must the World Government player choose Venus when raising a parameter?
ruling: The player must choose a non-maxed parameter, so if Venus was the only one left it would have to be chosen (but then the game would already have ended from the other parameters being maxed).
quote: But the player has to choose a non-maxed parameter, so if Venus was the only one left you would have to choose it.
author: Fryxen
heading: World Government Terraforming

question: When the World Government terraforms and hits a bonus (temperature bonus on the oxygen track, ocean bonus on the temperature track), do the bonuses occur?
ruling: Yes. Treat it as a neutral player (the WG) taking the action following the first player's suggestions. They even get the heat production bonus on the temperature track, although that has no game effect.
quote: Yes. Think of it as a neutral player (the WG) doing the action, follówing the suggestions of the first player.
author: Fryxen
heading: World Government Terraforming

topic: World Government Terraforming as a speed-up
question: Can the Venus Next World Government Terraforming rule be added to speed up a game?
ruling: Suggested as an optional speed-up: add the World Government terraforming rule from Venus Next if the game is still too slow.
quote: Add world government terraforming rule from Venus Next if it is still too slow.
author: Fryxen
heading: World Government Terraforming
